title: Great Headphones
text: I had been looking for earbuds that wouldn't continually fall out of my ears and started researching here on Amazon and was immediately drawn to these "earhook" headphones.  I was a little worried that they might be uncomfortable because I have very sensitive ears but I was pleasantly surprised by how comfortable these are.  I would have thought that after wearing them for a while, they would start to feel heavy wrapped around my ears but they don't!  I just love the fact that I can wear them on my walks and while running around town and not have to worry about my earbuds falling out every few minutes.  The sound quality is very good and it blocks out other noises because they fit (and stay) in your ears so well.  There are three different size rubber ear tips to help you find the perfect fit and I've found myself listening to more music than ever because they are so easy to put on and take off that I've even started using them while working in the yard and cleaning around the house too. I would definitely recommend these earhook headphones for anyone who is tired of having their earbuds fall out of their ears all the time.

title: Good Overall
text:
I use these for work, 8 hours a day in a work from home call center. I have a large head and am a big guy. The sound is fantastic for voice communication, I would never use these for gaming, music or multimedia. The audio range is not good enough for those applications, it is great for voice. The microphone works beautifully and others can hear me clearly and crisply.

To say that these are "passive" noise cancelling is laughable. There is really no such thing as passive noise cancelling, it's just how much noise is blocked out by wearing the headphone. Do not take that into consideration when buying headphones, unless they totally cover the ear. You can hear everything going on around you.

The ear pads are pretty comfortable, much more than a foam ear pad on standard headphones. I do need to pull these away from my ears every now and then to restore circulation and reduce soreness. Durability of the pad itself is in question, but I have not had these long enough to figure that out. First impression is the pad might last 6-12 months using 5 days a week for work. To me the pads seem to be a weak spot durability speaking.

Overall a great headphone for work. If these had active noise cancelling and a more comfortable/durable ear pad, they would be perfect. I have no experience with microphone filtering yet.

text:
I have owned/purchased several different types of headphones in the past ….Beats, Koss, Sony, Sennheiser, even wired V-moda’s, and I would say these are in my top two.

These headphones are attractive...I received these in gunmetal black. If you’d like to customize your look, you can order different colored metal shields and ear cushions.

The earmuffs have soft cushions and surround the entire ear. More importantly, these muffs allow for several hours of comfort if worn for extended periods of time. The volume control and mic are integrated on the right side of the headset. And while these can be worn for several activities, I wouldn’t really suggest working out in them, they are too nice (or expensive), but it can be done.

The headset comes with their own case, a USB charging cord, a 3.5mm 45’ degree plug with 24k gold tips and a clip to hang them from your bag or jeans. Bluetooth connection is fairly easy, there is a switch that you push on the back of the right earpiece. Once activated it gives a tone that lets you know it is trying to connect. Once you activate bluetooth on your device, it is ready.That’s right, these headphones provide great sound and are WIRELESS. What a fantastic feature. And you even have the option of not using the wireless feature by connecting to various portable devices (i.e., smartphone, laptop, tablets, etc) with the provided “mic 1 speakeasy cable”.

And finally, when I listened to different genres of music (i.e., jazz, rock, rap, classical) , the sound was clear and the quality is among the best. The frequency response listed is 5Hz-30kHz and that appears to be accurate. The sound wasn’t muted or distorted.

Overall, I would give these headsets 5 stars. These are definitely worth the money.

But base on how it worked with the A/C, I expect these will do a great job. Just don't expect it to wipe out outside noise. I could still hear the TV going and my husband talking. Just no A/C loud rumbling noise. Now if only I could sleep in these to kill the sound of my husband's fan.

I did get these free in exchange for my honest opinion. What is funny is a just bought a new pair of noise cancelling headphones because my old ones just died and I like these better so far....

title: Weak bass but best headphones at this price, especially for iPhone.
text:
These are around the same price as all the junky Chinese wireless earbud brands on Amazon but sound much better, are much more reliable, and are made by a company with good customer service that stands behind their products.

Ankers has several wireless earbuds with the cords that go behind the neck but only these, the spirit, the spirit pro, and the spirit x are worth considering for purchase. Their other earbuds are older models that cost just as much but have less features and weaker specs.

The bass on these is weak but I use these mostly for working out and for that it is fine.

I already have a pair of Apple EarPods but I wanted another wireless pair of headphones as well so I could switch back and forth while the other pair was charging.

These do not work with Apples w1 chip Bluetooth protocol, only apple and beats headphones work with that standard right now so those wireless headphones brands will sound better than anything other wireless headphones will with Apple products.

They also do not have aptx, which is the best sounding Bluetooth standard for anything other than Apple.

Ankers spirit pro headphones do support the aptx standard and supposedly have better bass than these so those are that models advantages.

However the spirit pro cost twice as much as these and only supports Bluetooth protocol 4.1 while these headphones support Bluetooth protocol 5.0.

Why is that important? Because the 5.0 protocol is the new “low energy” Bluetooth standard. Meaning that if you have both a device and headphones that support it you will get much more play time out of the same size battery.

Ankers other most recent model of earbuds, the spirit x headphones, have the same specs as these headphones in terms of the protocols they support but have a different form factor, obviously, and have 10mm drivers while these have 6mm. They also have a little more battery life.

I think I might buy the spirit x headphones as well in order to have a backup and to compare their sound.

As an Apple user the spirit pro headphones are just not worth the extra cost for me since I will never use the aptx protocol and they do not even support the Bluetooth 5.0 protocol.
If they were Bluetooth 5.0 compatible I might consider spending the extra 25 bucks in order to get that extra bass.

While these don’t sound spectacular they will get great battery life when I use them with devices that support 5.0 Bluetooth and they are very affordable.

I want to quickly rant about amazons policies and the flood of cheap Chinese products on here.

If you search for “wireless earbuds” or “Bluetooth earbuds” or any similar terms ankers products will not even show up on the first several pages of results.
Nor will Aukeys headphones, which I think are the second best option for wireless headphones in this price range.

Why is this?
Because the Chinese brands pay “click farms” to leave hundreds or even thousands of 5 star reviews.

The fraud is so obvious. What do you think is happening when a product has more than a thousand 5 star reviews all left on the same day or within the same few days and almost none of those reviews are from verified buyers?
The fact that many of them say the same things over and over and that many of them are written in broken English are other obvious clues.

I reported a few of them but Amazon does not take them down because Amazon cares about money and absolutely nothing else and having millions of people purchase this Chinese junk off their website makes them a lot of money.

It really sucks because good products, like these anker headphones, are barely visible in amazon search results because reputable brands don’t pay click farms to manipulate amazon search results.

It’s the consumers that lose in the end when their headphones, or other cheap Chinese products, break a few weeks after use or maybe never even work to begin with.
And you can bet that half of the time the companies selling this junk on amazon will simply disappear in order to avoid accepting returns and then reappear later under a new seller account to sell more junk through click farm manipulated amazon search results.

Of course amazon will find itself on the hook for some of these costs but apparently the money they make off of allowing all of this Chinese junk to be sold on their website under false practices is much more than any costs they incur.

These practices that amazon allows, and this one issue about manipulated search results is just the tip of the iceberg, hurts not just American consumers it also hurts American companies.

Rant over.

text:
Been using Gumy head phones for several years, always like a good pair of Gumys.
Only have a few small complaints.

For the most part Gumys are VERY comfortable, they're light and thin and easy to stick in your pocket, they don't pull on your ears or cause major discomfort like a lot of other small earbuds do.
However, after extended use (over an hour -say a full length movie, or using it for music while working on your next exam) it does seem to cause a bit of discomfort in my ears. BUT!! That may just be the shape of my ear, and it doesn't apply to everyone. ;)

I purchased this specific earbud (coconut white) because I LOVE coconuts and thought a creamy white would be an awesome color to have next! But I was disappointed in the color, it actually looks dirty and cheap, like something my grandma would have picked up at the Dollar Store.

The only other small complaint I would have is that if you use these headphones often (like I do), they slowly start to short out right below one of the earbuds. I generally find that these earbuds last me anywhere from 3-6 months at a time.
Sadly though, it's not just Gumy's, because I have tried different brands, and they all have done the same. (Even Apple's earbuds, though they lasted closer to 9 months, but I still had the same problem with the shortage right below the earbud itself.)

I still choose Gumy though because of the comfort compared to other brands, and the colors. I mean really... who doesn't love a bright colored pair of headphones? ;)

title: Solid Headset, maybe not for every application
text:
Edit/Update:Within 24 hours of the below review which put the headset at 4/5 stars, I was contacted by an Anker customer support rep to find out what they could do to resolve the situation. While any individual product might not be perfect for every person, I've never seen a company so dedicated to CUSTOMER SERVICE. That's why anytime I buy any charger, headset, cable, or anything that Anker makes, I buy from them. You get consistent quality and outstanding service.

If you'd like to see the original review to see if this headset is best for you, read below.
---------------------------
ORIGINAL REVIEW
---------------------------
Application: I wear lightweight BT headphones when working outside on my farm, working out, or while driving. I like to be able to leave one or both hanging freely until a call comes in.

I purchased these to replace my Anker SoundBuds Lite Bluetooth Headphones that got destroyed (new dog, chewed them up). The only complaint I had with the Soundbuds with the neckband was that sometimes when working on my back that they'd slide off my neck, so I thought these would be better. Bottom line: It depends on your application

Application: General wear: Outside work rating: (2/5)
When in my ear, they are much more secure than the neckband Soundbuds, but if I take one out to allow myself to be more aware of my surroundings, it ends up pulling on the other ear.
Also, when my neck gets all sweaty and I have to turn my head back to look at what is happening behind my tractor, they tend to pull on my neck.

Application: working out (5/5)
So long as I have both in (as I typically do when working out), these stay great. The sound is outstanding and they're very solid since I don't typically do much head turning when working out.

Application: driving (3/5)
When driving, it's hard to work the controls because they're on the right side, whereas the soundbuds lite had controls on the left. With the controls on the right, it's hard to turn them on, change volume, answer or end calls while changing gears (manual transmission). If I put one under my shirt so I'm only using one, then it ends up resting right under my seat belt.

I'd like to point out that I feel that the failings of the headset are only because I use them in unconventional ways. For standard use of "normal" people, they are great earbuds. For me, I'm trying to decide if I want to return them and go back to my comfort zone.

title: Decent passive sound cancelling, bad bluetooth range, good sound, thin pads, hopefully durable.
text:
I bought these to wear while working at my metal lathe - not exactly machine shop levels of noise since it's just me and one lathe, but some passive noise cancelling is important. Active NC would be nice but I'm not popping $300+ on head phones. $185 was more than enough. I have some Sony Mega Bass whatever number it is from Best Buy, and those sound better I think, but they're plastic, and they've already broken three times (repaired with string and epoxy, and paper towel and epoxy), so I had to replace them before they were totally unusable. So here comes the V Moda. Reviews suggest the metal frame should be quite durable if I drop it on a concrete floor. Hopefully I won't drop them, but accidents happen.

The pads are super thin, so if you get these go ahead and get the XL pads. The pads on my Sony phones are twice as thick as the V Moda pads. It makes a HUGE difference. They're pretty tight, too. The Sony phones I could wear all day long and not even feel them. These are a bit rough on my ears after a few minutes, but I'll deal with it if it means they'll not break as easily as the plastic frame Sony phones, and I've ordered the XL pads so that should make a big difference in comfort when those get here.

How do they sound? I listen to podcasts 90% of the time, so they sound fine for that, and they do block out enough of the machine noise so that I don't have to turn the volume up super loud. I guess they sound fine, bass and treble and all that stuff, I don't care. Helen Zaltzman and Roman Mars and NPR all sound fine on it. :)

Would I recommend them? Meh. If you're not a clutz like me, and aren't worried about breaking them, get the Sony ones. They're on sale all over for $100 or so right now. Or they were last week (May 2018). I almost got another pair instead of the V Moda, but I need the durability.

Bluetooth range sucks bad. The Sony's would work across the house, 30 foot in a straight line, but around corners and through walls and doors, before they'd crack out. These crack out after 5 foot if there's a door or a single wall in the way. The buttons click nicely, which some reviews said they wouldn't. The bluetooth/on switch has a good click feel, too. At least to my hand. The volume and pause buttons are nice, but a skip forward/backwards button would be SO nice. I'm going to miss that from my Sony. I skip ads in podcasts all the time, and it's going to be a pain in my backside to walk over to my phone from my lathe to do that, stopping whatever I'm working on to skip 10 minutes of mattress or shaving ads.

They connect very easily to bluetooth on my android phone, too.

The headband part is comfy though. I don't notice it at all. The adjustment is also really nice. Really the thin thin pads and lack of skip buttons are the biggest downer, bluetooth reach being terrible isn't that big of a deal, I just gotta pause before I go across the house to pee.

I feel like I'm leaving a bunch out, but I've only had them a couple days. Hopefully they'll last a few years. (May 21 2018)

Edit - 5 22 2018 - used it with my phone a few times and works really well for that. I can hear them, they can hear me (or at least they didn't complain if they couldn't hear me well). No complaints there.

Edit - 5 24 2018 - Got new XL ear pads in today. Much better. I had been using the Sony pads between the slim pads and my head and that was pretty nice actually. The V Moda pads aren't as nice as the Sony's, but much better than those thin sad excuses of ear pads it came with. Boo V Moda for supplying your phones with lousy thin pads.

EDIT!!! 7-13-2018 - So I finally read the directions that came with these b/c I accidentally skipped ahead once. If you double click the play button it speeds or skips, and if you triple skip it reverses or goes back. So much better. I've also masking taped the original thin ear pads on top of the thicker pads to make it even more comfortable. The battery lasts from about 8 in the morning till 6 or 7 at night with nonstop podcasting in my ears. Except for lunch and a couple potty breaks.
And I would say it's pretty dang durable so far. Very glad I picked these for use in my shop. When the battery dies I go to my Sonys as backup and DANG they feel so flimsy in comparison.

title: Everything solid, except for comfort
text:
Coming from a sound enthusiast (not quite audiophile) and classical musician.

Sound Quality: 8.5/10

The most important part of a pair of headphones, right? After burning in for a couple hours (whether or not you believe in burning in) these sound great. They have a very warm sound, better for more modern genres.
Bass - While the bass is very tight and controlled, its just slightly too prominent for some. Sub-bass is almost painful..I had to equalize it so I wouldn't get a headache after listening for more than an hour. It does not overpower the mids and highs, but it still feels too heavy. That being said, I do like being able to hear individual bass guitar plucks clearly on these. It also does wonders for genres like EDM and rap/trap.
Mids - Comes through nicely; clear and articulated. Doesn't get covered up by the bass too badly, vocals and everything sound like what you'd expect. Probably the most recessed range on these headphones, but by no means too quiet. Not much else to say here.
Treble - Crystal clear, maybe very slightly rolled off towards the top. Not harsh on the ears even in the scratchiest of violin solos (in fact, any fatigue I experienced while listening was from the bass). I was able to hear tiny stray string-crossing sounds in live orchestral pieces, which is...good, I suppose?

The sound quality as a whole is great. Nothing is muffled or mushed together, and everything is present and well separated. With the V-shaped sound signature, these are better for genres like EDM, Pop or Hip-hop. Bass heads will most likely be satisfied, unless you're talking like, OG Beats Studios tier. If you want a balanced sound, DO NOT purchase these. I wouldn't use these to listen to classical for my life. Equalization helps, but I still prefer my ATH-M50x's. As for wired vs wireless, I haven't had too much time to test this yet (everything said above is based on wireless performance), but from my brief listens with the wire, it seems to have marginal differences. The bass is perhaps slightly reeled in; and stays nice and punchy.

Build Quality: 10/10

These are sturdiest headphones I've ever owned, and they market them as such too. Lots and lots of metal in the construction. Nothing creaks when twisted/moved. Everything just feels like you can drop these a dozen times without a worry. Heavy, which is probably good for the durability, but not for comfort...

Comfort: 2/10 (5/10 with XL earpads, but costs extra)

This is where the V-Moda Crossfade Wireless really falls short. I'm not expecting it to match Bose's QC line in comfort..but its just ridiculously uncomfortable, especially in this price range. Uncomfortable enough to ruin the experience, and almost blur out the pros. It clamps really tightly around your head (my head is average sized, I promise). This can somewhat be fixed by clamping it around a box or something to loosen it up a little, but takes time. The earcups can't swivel, which is not a dealbreaker, but definitely uncommon nowadays. The earpads it comes with are outrageously bad for its high-end price. Literally all of my other headphones at this price range have softer, thicker, and larger cushions. In under an hour, I had to take them off because my ears were in a dull pain. For 20 more bucks you can get the XL earpads, which are significantly more comfortable, but thats 20 more dollars for something that I think should have been in the box in the first place. Even with the XL earpads I can't leave them on for more than around 3 hours - something I could do even with the notoriously uncomfortable M50x's. All this combined with its heavy weight means you can forget about just leaving them on throughout the day.

Final Thoughts:
Overall they're a decent set of cans for what you're paying. Some other pros include: pretty good battery life, looks cool (subjective), swappable earcup designs, and good bluetooth range/connectivity. Some cons might be: the lack of AptX codec support, not foldable for portability, and very minor latency issues(not noticeable for vast majority of things, but if you wanted to, say, play competitive games on bluetooth audio, these do have a small delay).

title: Best headphones for the price.
text:
I'm a bit of an audiophile and have a decent collection of headphones. I got these off of V-Moda's website (I had a coupon) and I have been blown away. The sound is incredibly crisp. The range in the highs is very good. However, bass is where these shine. I didn't think unamped headphones at this price point could deliver such a full spectrum of lows and provide as much a kick as these do.

Comparisons:
Beats Studio - In my opinion there's no contest, the V-Moda's take it. The Beats have a bass that over powers the highs and have a smaller spectrum than the V-Modas. The V-Modas have more detail across all spectrums. They also have phenomenal build quality and a much more impressive and portable case than the Beats.

Sennheiser Momentums - these were my previous go-to's. The Sennheisers are definitely better general purpose headphones. They have cleaner highs (which is saying something), but have noticeably weaker bass. The V-Moda's are better for all music except genres like jazz and classical. Also, I prefer the styling and build of the V-Modas. I should note two things: the V-Moda's are incredibly more comfortable than the Sennheisers and the V-Moda's are over ear, not on ear, which the Sennheisers are. My head begins to hurt after a couple of hours of wearing the Sennheisers because they are so tight and I have a slightly larger head.

Sony MDX wireless - I think the V-Moda's are superior in every category. The Sonys are lighter and have pivoting ear pieces, but that's it.

Audio Techinica - (I don't have these any more and can't remember the model, but they come in around the 100 price point). Again, not a contest. The Audio Technicas feel and sound cheap by comparison.

Reservations:
The price can be off putting for some and I couldn't disagree more. These are an incredible value and V-Moda's warranty is quite good.

The bass may over power the highs. For most listening, this won't make a difference, but if I'm going to listen to jazz, spoken word, a TV show, I'm going to grab my Sennheisers.

title: A couple issues but overall a great option for casual/moderate users
text:
I've had and been using these earphones for about 10 days now. I bought them at full price [$39.99] but I see now they have a $6 coupon :(. Ultimately, they are pretty good for the price.
Here's a breakdown of my thoughts on this product so far.

EarTips: These are very comfortable. I really love the shape of them, which makes them very secure but also, compared to the common hook shape of other sports earphones, makes it almost feel like you aren't wearing them.

Audio: The audio quality is decent; however, when it's connected to a device that isn't playing audio, the earphones often emit a sort of low droning static noise. I actually don't mind that part so much, because it can act as a minor active noise cancellation--in addition to the passive noise cancellation that is advertised and performs really well with snug (default for me) ear tips--which is helpful for when I'm in a focused studying mode.

Battery: I haven't actively timed how long these earphones last on a single charge continuously playing audio. However, I find myself having to charge these every night as, personally, I'm a heavy-user and use these (as my only pair of ear/headphones) constantly throughout the day. It'd be really nice if the earphones are useable while they are connected to the usb cable and charging, but they're not. [Please Anker R&D team make this happen for future versions!]

Bluetooth Connectivity: I do have an issue with its connectivity despite its Bluetooth 5.0. I haven't isolated any possible reason as of yet, but sometimes when I'm just outside the room of the connected device, 5-7+ feet away, the audio will sporadically fade-out for up to a few seconds before fading back in. It's a little frustrating.
** Edit: Customer support told me that "some Bluetooth signal obstacles will interfere the Bluetoooth range, such as walls, home appliances, wifi modem"; the fact that my connected device (Macbook Pro mid-2012) was a foot away from the wifi modem and I was testing the range from the laptop through a wall, lined with a fridge and oven, into the kitchen makes this issue understandable haha.

I really want to try out the Soundcore Spirit X and compare. Personally, I definitely would have benefited from the 4-hour extra battery life for the same price. I only hesitated and chose this Spirit Sports one because of the eartip shape since I wear glasses and thought it might feel weird having both hooks around the ear.

* Edit: Added a star because Anker has such fantastic customer support. Shout out to Emily who is simply amazing and very patient with me! They reached out to me really quickly and were willing to replace a possibly defective product, as well as answered any questions/issues I had. Then there is the issue of calls lagging when moving a few feet away from my phone. It's kind of annoying to just a bit from my phone only to find that the other person is hearing me lag in the call. The mic is also at a pretty low volume when I talk to people. Also another problem is watching videos and listening to music. For some reason, if I start listening to anything when the buds are coming from a state of not playing anything, sound will not play at full volume at first but instead, gradually gain volume until they reach the volume that it was set to last. I never had earbuds do that to me and I found that weird when I first experienced it.

So overall, the buds are built well and are very comfortable, but sound quality is a bit lackluster considering I spent more money for these than the Soundbuds slim. The other issues definitely does not help as the lag in calls and the gradually gain when I start listening to anything add to the annoyance of using these. These buds are built well and the magnets are great, but the other issues are what make these earbuds harder to use for me.

Update: Anker's customer support is one of the best in the business. I contacted support after they messaged me to reach out to them after my review and they decided to send me their upgraded version the Soundcore Spirit Pros. title: Small flaws in design and overall experience mar an otherwise fantastic product
text:
I love Anker products and they have a reputation for solid construction and quality, hence I bought these and honestly these live up to that standard. So why the negative review? Well, there's a few things.

First off, and maybe my main gripe is the fit. These simply aren't comfortable to me and may be one of the less comfortable headphones I've used, bluetooth or otherwise. Every possible combination of the provided tips and ear hooks just didnt feel like a tight or sealed fit, and as a result the headphones always felt kind of loose. i took these to the gym once and I can assure you that these stayed on and weren't loose in the slightest, so I was wrong on it being ACTUALLY loose, but that uncomfortableness was always there. After 5 days with these I gotta say I'm 50-50 on these and the fit hasn't gotten any better. Of course, that is 100% subjective and people's ears will vary greatly so make of that what you will.

Soundwise, these are decent. Bass, while not overbearing is tight and punchy and I noticed how clean drums sounded in most songs. Of course, much of the sound depends on a song's production but the sound was good or exceeding what was expected of the price point. That being said, I was getting a tunnel effect, especially on video content that made things sound "echo-y". Not a deal-breaker in of itself, but definitely a contributing factor to what soured me on these headphones. For reference, I'm using these with a Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge.

Moving on, Battery. The description says 8 hours of battery and having looked at laptops and all sorts of tech for years on end, I know that battery life always depends on how you use it and even what volume you listen at. So, I deducted an hour from the description and expected about 7 hours of battery life, which is about what I got. I got exactly what I expected walking in and came to the realization that it was a bit short for my preferences.

Finally, let's talk about the actual user experience. Pairing is nice and fast on this device and the little control dock or whatever you would call it on the headset is easy to use. 3 buttons, long press + for skip, tap for volume up. Long press - for replaying/ going back a song, and tap for volume down. Long press middle button for power, tap for pause. Oh, by the way, with the design of these, expect the headset to lean heavily to the right instead of the wire being evenly distributed towards both sides. All of these buttons worked great and it was such a relief to use a bluetooth headset with buttons that actually did what they were supposed to most of the time (looking at you JBL Everest). Range is fine but when I was out of range or at the very limit, the headset had an annoying tendency to fade in and out. Which brings us to the fading. The engineers or designers on this headset were apparently a little too fond of the fade in/out sound effect and used it for almost everything possible. Press volume up when the headset volume is maxed? Your music will now fade out, play a soft beep, and fade back in. It's kind of annoying. When the device's battery is low, it will fade out and beep every so often, enough to kind of get on my nerves.

And that's ultimately how I would describe these headphones, aggravating. They're a great pair for the price if you can get over these little grievances, and I have to admit that some of my problems listed above might seem petty or inconsequential. However, the poor fit is what did me in. You can have the most expensive headphones with 300000000000000000mm drivers or whatever but at the end of the day if they're not pleasant to wear then it's a bad experience. All of the other issues I possibly could have lived with but when added to the fit issue, I had to give these ones a pass.

EDIT/REVISIT- While the fit was initially terrible, it has grown on me and I would say that after forcing yourself to use these for a period, these may prove to be a decently comfortable set.

I also forgot to mention another thing and that is how heavily the set leans to the right. This is not noticeable at all if you use both ears but if you want to keep one ear in and the other out, you'll want to keep the right ear in since that's the side with the button panel. Not a big issue, but something that might be worth noting.

One HUGE thing worth bringing up is Anker's customer support. Those folks are beyond fantastic and would often reply to emails within an hour of me sending them. They were more than willing to work with me in any way possible and make my experience as pleasant as possible. One thing I can say is that if you;re unsure of a product but leaning towards trying it out, I'd say go for it. Their customer service is completely hassle-free and if you don't like it they'll be more than happy to help. Kudos to the folks over at Anker for the help.

title: Reliability Issues (updated three times)
text:
Well, I wasn't expecting a terrific sound quality. You couldn't expect that from a $40 bluetooth earphones. I just wanted reasonable sound. Let's face it, most people buy it for gym/running and only want/need some background. I believe you should be less picky about sound quality for such a purpose and save some money, but maybe it is just me. I did expect it to work though. After about 7-8 uses the right earphone became too weak and with a very poor sound quality. I made sure it wasn't clogged, tested my phone settings, tested it on another device, tested my right ear hearing capability (seriously) and tried reset the device (read somewhere it sometimes help connecting it to a power source while pressing the power button). Nothing helped. It is just a hardware failure.
Amazon is great though. Got a full refund for the purchase. Not sure what to do next. Should I buy it again? I don't want to spend $$$ for an expensive pair, just for gym/running. Buying expensive pair also doesn't promise reliability and it would have been angrier had I paid $$$ for a faulty unit.

Update 09/17/18 - I was contacted by the company representative. They offered sending me a replacement pair free of charge and supplied me with a shipping label to ship back the defective unit (for investigation). So far, the replacement unit is operating properly, the sound quality is as expected - naturally far of being audiophile level, but for my ear it serves the purpose just fine (gym, running). I’m hoping this pair will last for a long while and that the former incident was just a glitch. If it will, these earphone are defiantly good bang for the buck.

Update 01/05/19 - another reliability issue. The battery stopped holding its charge. I used to charge the battery every four usages or so, then storing it (off) until the next usage. About a week ago, after charging and storing it, I tried turning it on with no success. I initially thought I might have left it on, so I recharged, made sure that it is turned off and stored it again. Sadly few days later it didn’t turn on again. I said, OK, maybe there’s something wrong with the charger, which made little sense because the led turned from red to blue after the charge, so I tried a different one. After this charge, I turned the headphones on, played music for 20-30 minutes, to make sure it works and then turned it off and stored it. Today, about 60 hours after this charge (with the earphones off) it won’t turn on again.
Although this time it’s a completely different for last time, I suspect the QA of this product is not at the highest levels.

02/04/2019 - The customer service of this company deserve 5 stars. They sent me a new replacement unit. I hope The other two units were a glitch and this one will last.

title: Great At First, Bound To Fail
text:
I have narrow ear canals and struggle to find comfortable earbuds. The default inserts fit perfectly, and it was nice to know that other sizes were included in case my taste changed.

The sound was surprisingly full and hit a decent volume. The passive noise cancelling was so impressive that these became my go-to for flying, replacing active noise cancelling over-the-ear headphones. It also helped that the battery life was every but as good as advertised.

Notice that everything so far is in past tense...

After a few months of regular use, the battery life started to drop off. No big deal, I thought. Even if I only got 5 hours of playtime, that was impressive for such an impossibly small battery.

Then, six months in, it stopped taking a charge at all. The LED blinked red when plugged in. Fortunately the RMA process was fairly painless (Keep your documentation!) And I had a replacement in about two weeks, with no need to send in the original.

The replacement lasted nine months before dying in the exact same way. I'm not going to bother with an RMA again. It's not worth it.

If you're not sure whether wireless earbuds are for you or you want something cheap that you won't be devastated to lose, you can't beat the price of these - for a while. Now that I know how much I like good wireless earbuds, I'll look for something a bit more reliable.

UPDATE 09/10/18: Anker did reach out to me in response to the review and I've updated to 4 stars. I would probably say the product itself is around a 3.5 but the solid support pushes it to a 4. Anker sent me a replacement pair of Spirits which did not have issues with the screeching sound, however they did still seem low on volume and didn't really fit too well - though I've had that complaint with other headphones too so maybe that's not an issue for everyone. Anker then replaced them with the Spirit X, which are similar and have the same price but are a bit bulkier and have ear hooks. Initially I thought I'd dislike them since I wear bulky plastic frames which tend not to mix with ear hooks but as it turns out, the ear hooks are so light that it hasn't been an issue. Additionally, the in-ear fit is a LOT better, the volume is probably 30% louder or so, and the overall sound profile is a lot better (though a lot of that probably has to do with the fact that the in-ear seal is much better now). I'd honestly advise most prospective buyers to check out the Spirit X even if you think they look bulky - they don't feel any heavier in your ear, the fit is much better, they'll stay in your ears very well due to the hooks and you also get a couple more hours of battery life too. Also, the Spirit X come with a clamshell case which I appreciate a lot more than the little pouch the regular Spirits come with. Much better for the same price IMO. title: Definitely a great purchase if you’re on a budget.
text:
Before I begin the review, I want to note that I was planning on returning these earbuds if they didn’t meet my expectations and instead buying a pair of Jaybird x3’s. But, these met my expectations and exceeded them in some aspects.

When I first tried the earbuds I did notice that it sounded very flat and the sound quality lacked vibrance. Thankfully, there are built in eq’s into most streaming apps such as Spotify and Apple Music so I was able to adjust the sound to my liking. After doing so, I was pleasantly surprised with the amount of deep, rich base that was produced. Seriously, I wasn’t expecting it at all. The mids sounded pretty good and the highs were crisp and clear. To compare these to a common pair of earbuds, I would say that these produce much better base and highs than Apple earbuds, but the mids are just about the same if not a tad bit better. I would even go so far as to say these are just as good as the powerbeats which are $160. On the contrary, one thing that I did notice is that with certain songs, the mids lost a bit of clarity and the bass became somewhat overpowering. The sound will not blow you away, but it will definitely pleasantly surprise you. I mean after all these are $40 earbuds. Also, I wouldn’t call myself an audiophile, but I do have a great appreciation for sound quality.

The build quality exceeded my expectations. They have a nice, rugged feel to them. The magnets at the ends of the buds also provide a sercure hold. Also these buds come with an excess of accessories, so finding the right fit for you will not be a problem and they’re surprisingly comfortable. After 3 hours of usage my ears felt a little fatigue, but it wasn’t anything too terrible. One thing to note is that if you do not have the correct sized ear tips, there will be a great deal of audio quality lost. So even if the tips which come preinstalled seem to fit I would suggest trying other sizes just in case.

These are definitely sweatproof as I have used them in the gym and I sweat a good amount. They continue to work just as well as they did when I first tried them.

The battery life lasts for around 7-8 hours when the volume is 2 bars away from max. I havnt put that to the test yet, but I used these buds for about 3 1/2 hours and afterward they were just above 50%.

Bluetooth connectivity is also seamless and I heard no distortion from up to about 100ft away. I did not test this any further than that.

Overall, I would definitely recommend these earbuds to people who do not mind using Apple earbuds or other earbuds around and slightly above that sound quility range.

If there are any other aspects of this product that anyone wants me to review, feel free to ask. I will update this review after a week of usage.

title: Great value wireless earbuds.
text:
Today I am reviewing the Soundcore Spirit wireless bluetooth headphones by Anker. I have used a ton of budget bluetooth headphones over the years, and these earbuds include everything I'm looking for. They are basically my perfect pair of budget earbuds.

Design: They in ear portion is small with controls on a separate in line controller. I GREATLY prefer this to around the ear or around the neck earbuds with controls built into the ear portion or around the neck. So these are perfect for me in the design. Next up is build quality. Better than expected for the price. Not quite premium, but far better than "good enough". Also in regards to design is "fit". With 3 different sizes of tips and the rounded nub, these fit great and don't fall out.

Sound Quality and Mic: Listen, these aren't $500 Bose earbuds. That said for the current listed price of $40 on Amazon, these sound better than you would expect. They fall somewhere between "good enough" and "pretty good". Easily in the same quality range as name brand earbuds in the $70 to $100 range. Next and most important is mic quality. A lot of ear buds just use the worst mic they can find. This set however has an average mic and that's a big deal to me. No one complained about audio quality to me while on the phone.

SweatGuard: These earbuds include SweatGuard technology for sweat proofing. Now Anker reached out to me suggesting a salt water mixture to use to simulate sweat to test this. However, I personally don't care about test results and care WAY more about real world results. Thankfully for the purpose of this particular review, I sweat A LOT. So I had to do some yard work this past weekend and figured, this will be the perfect test. After a few hours of yard work with me absolutely drenched in sweat the headphones were still going strong. The sound was a little distorted until I wiped off the speaker part but then boom, back to normal. Couldn't be happier with how well they held up.

Other notes: Battery life is great so far. After a full charge I've probably used them for about 6 hours and they are still going. The box claims 8 hours, so at the very least that seems at least mostly accurate. The box doesn't claim any IPX raiting, yet on Amazon the listing title says IPX7, but the description then claims better than any IPX rating. If that's the case and it's better why not just get the rating and put it on the box? So something seems fishy there, but from a real world use I can tell you sweating profusely didn't damage them, and their simulated test method suggested I fully immerse them in the solution, so do seem to be actually waterproof despite no clear rating indicated.

Overall, at a current price of $40 these seem to hit the sweet spot. You can save a little but get a much worse product, or you can spend a little more and get a similar product just a different brand. You'd have to spend a good amount more to get an actually better product. I would definitely consider giving these a look if you are in the market.

title: Basic Bluethooth headphones that are waterproof, so far.
text:
This is now my third set of Bluetooth headphones in less than two years. I use them at least 1.5 hours each day commuting by bike in all weather. I will be comparing all three headphones -- Soundcore Spirit, Aukey Latitude, and Phaiser Tecton BHS-730 -- as part of this review.

Sound: All three headphones offer decent quality sound. They work for listening to a podcast on my commute or when preparing a meal in the kitchen, but none of them would suffice for critical listening. I use my Etymotic in-ear monitors or Grado SR80i headphones for that.

Comfort/Fit: The Phaiser Tectons came in first. The flanges did a good job with my large ears, and I ended up using the eartips on the Soundcore headphones. Both the Aukey and Soundcore headphones angle the speaker from the main body of the headphone, which means that there is a definite right and left. The Aukey has the microphone/controller on the left side, which I didn't particularly like. If I'm in the bike lane and traffic is on my left, I want that ear free. The Soundcore controller is on the right side.

Controls: They are all pretty similar, with buttons to power one, change the volume and skip forward or backward. They each operate differently with my iPhone's music and podcast apps. For example, holding the up button may skip to the next podcast but only fast-forward music. Another headphone would do the opposite. The Aukey headphones have three equalizer settings, but only the middle one sounded OK, with the others either too tinny or too much bass. The Phaisers do have one really neat feature: when you power them up, they give a verbal prompt on remaining battery time. With the others, you have to remember to check the tiny display in the corner of your screen.

Durability: The Phaisers were my first set and starting experiencing shorter battery life before the right earpiece got a very loose connection. At the beginning, they were good for 3 days of commuting, but by the end I had to recharge them almost every day. The Aukeys were showing more promising battery life before they gave up the ghost after getting caught in a downpour. They may be sweat-resistant, but they aren't waterproof. So far, the Soundcores are holding up, but we're still early in the game. They can get me through a solid 3 days of commuting (> 1.5 hours each day), and they lasted through a 5 hour bike ride recently with charge to spare. I also wore them recently during a torrential downpour, and they kept going.

title: Great sound, fit and value
text: I’ve been using these for a week and really like them. They fit my ears very well which most earphones don’t. The sound is incredible especially given their small size. I now own a number of Anker earphones and the quality improves with each pair.  Anker (Soundcore) have found the sweet spot of making quality earphones at an affordable price. I’ve used these for moderate exercise and they stay in my ears without a problem. I also use them for quiet listening. They are light and I hardly know they are in. Can’t beat these for around $30. They come with a variety of wings and ear tips. I also like the storage pouch. It’s much less bulky than the hard pod. I highly recommend these earphones.

title: Good bang for your buck
text:
These are $30 headphones so you shouldn't be expecting a top of the line product. With that said, these are a great value. The sound quality is good with punchy bass, clear treble, and a relatively balanced middle. Battery life is pretty good at ~8-10 hours on a charge as well which is useful for someone semi-forgetful like myself.

My main complaint is in the overall fit of the headphones, both in ear and around the neck. Anker includes various earbud sizes, but none of them fit my ear particularly well. This means that the seal on the headphone is either not tight or muffled when the speaker is pushed against the side of my ear rather than directly into the canal. With a little maneuvering, I can typically get the headphones into the right place. However, coming from a $10 wired set of headphones that fit perfectly and didn't have this problem, it's pretty annoying to deal with. The behind the neck wire material also tends to get stuck upon contact with skin making it frustrating trying to turn your head during use.

Despite these annoyances, I'm happy with my purchase and would recommend them at this price point.

title: Spirit > Spirit X
text:
The Soundcore Spirit is more of a 4.5 stars, but the Anker customer service earned the 5 stars. When I received the Soundcore Spirit, I can’t help but to compare it to the Spirit X. The box was slim and rectangular, whereas, the Spirit X was a cube. When I unboxed the contents of thr Spirit, we have similar accessories inside. A charging cable, various sized eartips and earwings as well as a small pouch for the earphones. The pouch feels like a high quality felt material. Also, I thought the snap close is a genius idea for a pouch. I have had other earphones that came with pouches, but all of them were closed by drawstrings. The Soundcore Spirit pouch requires the pinching of both ends of the opening to open and then it snaps back into place to close. So how does the Soundcore Spirit breakdown? Let’s see.

Sound:
One issue I had with the Spirit X model was that there was a hiss when connected to a source and music was playing. This hissing is most noticeable when the music is soft, which offen happens in classical music. When the music is pumping like say a dance track, the hissing gets drowned out. I was prepared for the Spirit earphones to have the same exact hissing issue. I powered it on, put on some music and kept listening for that hiss. It never surfaced. That’s good news.

Now for the sound, these earphones sound amazing for the price. The sound is clear and the BassUp technology works. I test my earphones with no equalizers and on a track like The Weeknd’s Starboy, the bass thumps. Look, I’m not one of those bass heads that need my earphones to dish out jaw jarring, core vibrating bass. I just want my earbuds to sound alive and these earphones does just that. I also switched over to Labrinth’s Jealous to listen to whether these earphones push the clarity and emotion of Labrinth’s vocals; it certainly does. Every type of music I threw at the Spirit, it passed the tests.

Let’s move onto noise isolation. It is decent on the NYC subway. While listening to podcasts I can hear the dialogue clearly with minimal external noises seeping in. I attribute the great noise isolation to the nice silicone eartips and the way the earphones sit pretty deep in the ear canal. You can probably improve the noise isolation even more if you purchase some Comply noise isolation foam tips… but honestly, you really don’t need to spend that money.

Comfort:
The Soundcore Spirit is small and light. Unlike the larger counterpart, I had no trouble putting these on. The earwings does a great job at keeping the earphones in place, which is needed for people working out with these buds.

Design:
The small profile of the earbuds with 8 hours play time is impressive. I still don’t like the wiring that runs behind the neck though, it still rubs on the collar of my dress shirt. Of course it wouldn’t be an issue if I used the Spirit with a t-shirt. The earbuds itself look good. The color way and the materials used, they all give off a high quality feel. The controls are simple to figure out. With bluetooth 5.0 and what Anker calls “sweat guard,” you can be sure these earphones will be able to handle the abuse you throw at it during your workouts.

Price:
The Anker Soundcore Spirit is priced the same MSRP as the Spirit X at $39.99. At MSRP, I will pick the Spirit over the Spirit X. Why? Because it is smaller, sounds the same and without the hiss, looks nicer and easy to put on.

I will look to get it returned if possible.

I love Anker products and their Soundcore line is promising but this specific product is kinda dangerous and I can't recommend it to others. Keep an eye on the reviews and make sure they've fixed the issue in new versions before you buy a pair.

title: One of the best bluetooth earbuds for heavy workouts
text:
These are my favorite and most reliable BT earbuds for working out; I sweat a lot more than most people when I work out/run, and these are the only IPX7 earbuds I've used that DON'T short-circuit and become unusable from ion build-up.

Sound quality is excellent for this price range. The highs and mids are pretty good, and the bass is surprisingly good. The overall sound is very slightly muffled, but better than the other waterproof BT earbuds I've used in this range ($20-$60).

Fit-wise, these stay in my ears extremely well (I know this is dependent on ear-shape, though). They form a snug, air-tight seal and don't fall out unless they're tugged on. When tugged, some sweat can leak into the ear, making it easier to slip out, but this rarely happens. Showering with these is fine too.

Battery life is as-advertised, right around 6-8 hours of constant use. And Anker's customer service is top-notch: I bought a pair that unexpectedly quit working, and they were extremely helpful with quickly replacing them.

I would highly recommend these; they're reliable, sound good, and are relatively inexpensive, and I plan to buy them again (I expect that will be several years from now :) )

title: Some minor issues
text: I like these headphones and was delighted with the sound when I first heard them, it was really nice for portable headphones that were priced where I wouldn't be too upset if I lost them.  Issues: 1.  Grippy cord: the cord sticks to my sweaty neck at my gym and tugs.  I have to grip the cord and loosen it.  A lot.  I tried the button with the 3 slots to adjust it up tight and off my neck but that didn't help.  I ended up with it still sticking to the skin just under my ears and then with the cord out of the button thing.  I couldn't get the cord back into the slots in the button with just my fingers.  I needed a tool to push it into the slot without putting too much tension of the wire.  Now, I've loosened the wire completely so it hangs down in back and I find it grips and tugs less and is easier to quickly reach and pull it loose than it was with the shortener button.  Recently, I've noticed that it grips when dry, too.  It's really annoying as I sometimes pull one side out to speak with people and the cord grips and tightens up on the remaining side.  The cord also transmits shock from heel strikes to my ears if I walk at a good pace (I wear heavy soled boots so there's more shock than foam shoes.)  2. Range: The bluetooth 5 range is improved but nothing like I'd hoped. Maybe my phone is at fault, it is BT 5 but without comparisons to eliminate the source I don't know.  I get maybe 10 to 20 feet more range than bluetooth 4.2, not the 4x range the standard is promoted to have.  3. Watertightness:  I tried these in the shower.  I shielded them with my hand from a spray that could hydraulically forced its way inside them but I definitly let them get wet.  The first tiem I used them in the shower they lost their charge afterwards. They had been fully charged and used for an hour when they lost the charge.  I recharged them and they worked fine until a week or so later I tried the shower again, this time they lost volume permanently, I could hear the sound but at a low volume.  Both times, the rubber plug for the micro usb port was fully inserted and water ran across the phones but was not sprayed on them.  I replaced them and have not gotten the replacement pair wet beyond sweat and misty rain.

title: Great product, but seems to have a critical defect
text:
*EDIT* Customer service addressed the issue I experienced by promptly shipping me a replacement product. It works perfectly with no issues so far. Will update if the replacement starts acting funny.

This has been my first bluetooth headphone set, and after being a loyal Sennheiser user for years, I decided to give this Anker model a try. I use them mainly for exercise, and they stay in and out of the way perfectly. Sound quality is good, commensurate with the price. Bluetooth range is great and they pair to all my devices without a hitch.

One critical failure I've experienced is that every 100-200 minutes of listening or so, the headphones emit a full-spectrum static-like chirp/screech sound. After about two months of use, it seems to be proportional to the set volume level. When set to about 50% max volume, the sound is so bad the headphones have to be removed immediately. A few times the chirping persisted indefinitely, and the headphones disconnected from the device and had to be turned off and re-paired. I have seen a few others report this issue as well.

Overall, good headphones if you can get lucky with a properly functioning pair?

title: Average at best.
text:
I have Apple Airpods but I wanted something else for use at the gym. The price and reviews on the Anker Soundcore Spirit Sports Earbuds were great, so I thought I'd give them a try. In spite of the glowing reviews, these Anker headphones were disappointing.

build quality: Good. I liked the magnetic connection between the two earbuds. Included case was nice.

sound quality: Average. I realize these are much cheaper than Apple Airpods, but the Airpods have spoiled me for good sound in a lightweight construction. I wanted headphones with more noise isolation. While the noise isolation is a little better than the Airpods, it wasn't by much.

comfort: The poor comfort was the main reason why I returned these. I wanted a pair of earbuds I could put on and forget I was wearing them. Even though they include three different size ear cups and hooks, I couldn't find a combination of cups & hooks that felt completely secure. This is because of the cord. Maybe your ears and head will be a better fit for these than mine.

Update below

text:
First let me say, impressive product considering the cost, there is really nothing I do not like about it.
1. Sound, for the low cost, its surprisingly good. Not really for the purist but for the general public that likes a nice bass punch and exaggerated highs, all in all, most will love it.
2. Construction is impressive to me, including a case to store them in.
3. Fit is comfortable and an assortment of different sized plugs provided.
4. Bluetooth connection and controls are rock solid

Summary, at this price point and if you aren't looking for a 12+ hour battery life I dont see how you can go wrong with these. Nice packaging, nice construction, sound as good as any earpiece at almost any price where the response is curved (almost everything now days) for more bass and treble as this is what the average consumer wants.
They are a LITTLE bit on the larger size, but a wide assortment of plugs comes with it.

My disappointment was battery life, I think to claim a 8 hour battery is a bit exaggerated. I was closer to 6+
Since I already have 12+ hour earpieces I did not want to go back in "time" and I am returning them.
If your ok with 6 to 7 hours add one more star to my review for 4 stars.

At this price point I think they are one of the best "in class" and I am feeling like Soundcore by Anker are turning out some pretty good stuff.
The sound coming from these earplugs are truly fantastic and I would be glad to recommend them to any of my family or friends as I have now become a fan of the Anker Soundcore Series so if you are good with the 6+ battery add a Star for Sure.

+++I did at the same time I bought the Spirit Sports above I bought the Soundcore Spirit X with a claimed 18 hour battery, I am keeping those. They are fantastic, GREAT Soundcore Sound, ROCK SOLID BLUETOOTH CONNECTION, comfort and the Spirit X gives me that nice, secure, comfortable fit as a bonus. I will be reviewing them in the coming week as I further test them.

text:

The included eartips come in a good variety of sizes, and the wingtip piece is removable. The isolation these provide is good enough to hear audio on streets and trains. Also, the included magnetic carrying pouch is a nice touch.

The call quality on the other end isn't the best in noisy environments, but I don't use these much for calls.

The pairing process is straightforward, and they pair pretty quickly with my OnePlus 3T when I turn the headphones on. The connection with my phone isn't as reliable as it is with iOS devices, however, so the headphones sometimes cut out. They have this annoying feature of fading in sounds, so each time the connection is lost, the audio fades back rather than coming in all at once, so you miss a few seconds of audio each time this happens. Luckily, it's not too often for me, so it's not a major issue.

Their "free" replacement policy is great, as long as you don't place any value on your time...***

These were suggested to me by Anker as a replacement for my previous pair of their headphone, the Soundcore Curve (which died after a month). They upsold me on the idea these the Spirits are better for running.

They're not.

I just took these on an initial outing, a five mile run. First, there's substantial wind noise even in a light breeze. Second, even the smallest tips seal too tightly in my ears. This causes two problems: (a) impact noise from your feet on pavement is omnipresent and (b) even at low volumes it's hard to hear, say, a cyclist letting you know they're coming up behind you. (c) there's weird suction noises as the phones move in and out of your increasingly sweaty ears. Third, the buttons are too close together to distinguish by feel while you're in motion. IMO, hooks over your ears is the way to go -- which is what my first Anker headphones had.

As far as sound goes, I listen to podcasts and books when I run, and they seem fine for that. I think the bass line of EDM along with the thump and whistle combo of my feet and the wind would drive me nuts.

On the upside -- and this is not nothing, and the basis for a 2nd star -- Anker's customer support was helpful and responsive. So, when these die in 30 days I'm sure I'll continue checking out their product line.

I got these at a pretty good price, under $30 with a coupon from Amazon. These are my very first set of Bluetooth earbuds ever so this is my first impression as a new user.

First off, packaging is nice, short manual that's clear to understand, everything good here. Accessories are great. Comes with a small pouch self closing opening that works great. My issues with this product are: latency with video, volume problems.

I've used these with a Pixel 3 and a laptop with Bluetooth but both experiences have identical problems with these headphones. The latency between the video and the audio makes the video nearly unwatchable. I can kind of get used to it after a bit, but as soon as someone in the video starts to talk, it's pretty off. Another weird problem is that if I'm watching a video, both on my phone or computer, and I scrub through the timeline the headphones have an audible click like they disconnected, and then click again and slow fade into the video audio. Like really slow fade in. I unfortunately can't really use these to watch videos because of those problems.

The volume on these seem very quiet too. I'm nearly up to 3 ticks before full volume when they feel like they're a nice comfortable level. This isn't really a problem, I hadn't needed to go louder, but it's still weird and unlike any other headphones I've had.

Overall, for music on the move, these are 10/10. For main headphones for everything including video, I can't reccomend these unfortunately. I'm still happy with them considering the price I paid.

title: BEWARE iPhone 7 Plus users...
text:
I've had these pair of headphones for a little less than a year already. When I received them and immediately tried them out, I was pretty blown away by how surprisingly good they are. I currently go to school, so whenever I'm on campus, I leave these around my neck and whenever I want to listen, I just easily put them on. But after some careful listening, there were some issues that I had with these headphones...

In terms of sound quality, I thought there was some sort of inconsistency regarding the "highs" of the music. When I listened to these with my iPhone 7 Plus, there were times where it sounded like there was a very small "low-pass filter fuzziness" that was turned on for 5 seconds, making the music I was listening to sound as if it were below 128 kbps quality. Then, all of a sudden, it went back to normal. This pretty much never stopped happening, even after resetting it, re-pairing it to my phone, you name it. I called Anker's customer support and they were happy to send in another pair, so I tried them out again and the same thing was happening. I figured at that point, I give up because it was just whatever, I can still use them fine.

As I kept using them, I tried connecting them to my 2015 Macbook Pro and immediately found out the issue wasn't happening anymore, but that it would only happen if it was connected to my iPhone. I was a bit more satisfied because at least I found out when this issue would happen, so I continued using them with my iPhone despite the quality sounding low periodically until I found another issue that I ran into.

One day, I put these on and headed out to school. As I was walking, all of a sudden, the music cut off and there was a MASSIVE, continuous static noise that just blasted at full volume, which made me jump as I was walking (people probably thought I was crazy or something). Even when I took these out, you could probably hear it from far away because it sounded like they were about to explode. I didn't know what to do, even when I tried to turn it off, disconnect it from my phone, etc. It wouldn't stop spazzing out to the point where I considered stepping on it to make it shut up but eventually, it stopped. So then that day, I just continued on my day at school not using these earbuds.

I decided to not use them for a while because 1) I didn't want to look like a fool getting "shocked" by this static hiccup and 2) I just hated that feeling of something suddenly blasting into your ears (like a sudden gunshot or balloon pop that would throw you out of your chair). However, a couple of months later, I decided to try these on again with my phone because I was actually just using them with my laptop perfectly fine. Everything was pretty much fine (the "low-pass filter" issue was still present with my phone) until the SAME static issue happened as I was sitting in class listening to music with these. Here, I literally jumped out of my desk this time (because how could something so loud not shock someone). People around me probably thought it was going to explode or something, so I tried my best to cover both earbud grills with my fingers and just went outside the classroom. At that point, I stopped using them, because I wasn't going to take another chance using them.

Fast forward less than half a year later, I upgraded my phone to an iPhone XS. I didn't think of using the pair of headphones again until today (right before I wrote this review) because I totally forgot that I had them after discovering they were hidden inside my backpack. I tried them on again and they sounded completely fine this time. I didn't hear any drops in quality (specifically the low-pass filter issue mentioned previously) and everything else sounded fine. I'm probably prematurely saying these are completely bug-free now that I'm using a different phone, but I think I've come to the conclusion that these headphones are buggy WITH the IPHONE 7 PLUS (at least mine). I'm not sure if it had to do with the Bluetooth connectivity/compatibility between my phone and the headphones, but I feel like the low-pass filter quality issue was related to the massive static noise that prevented me from using them again. Overall though, I'll be giving updates if I do experience this same issue again (crossing my fingers) and I think I'll continue using these a lot again.

title: Fails to deliver on the audio
text:
EDIT 08/15/2018
Anker product support remained determined to ensure I was satisfied. They reached out and offered to send me the Soundcore Spirit X at no cost but I refused since not the form factor I was looking for (larger size, over ear hooks). They then offered to send me a Soundcore Spirit Pro to which I agreed. The Soundcore Spirit Pro basically fixes what was wrong with the Soundcore Spirit Sports and is a fantastic product which I can highly recommend. I have reviewed it separately under its own product reviews.

I can't praise Anker's product support enough, in general. The company makes truly excellent products. In our household, through subsequent IPhone upgrades, we've stopped using Apple's own included charger/lightning cable. Anker makes far superior alternatives on both counts. Occasionally, where products are defective or sub-par the company is eager to help resolve quickly, with sole focus on customer satisfaction. They absolutely nail it when it comes to generating brand loyalty!!

( I can't seem to find the review breakup which allows me to rate individual aspects separately as well as overall). I have also added some more details relevant to the headset.

REVIEW

Unfortunately, these failed to deliver on the audio. In short, the sound is simply flat and at full volume, not as loud as you would expect earphones to be. I got almost no bass response out of these despite testing adequately. I had returned my initial set for a replacement hoping that would solve the problem but same issue on the replacement as well so leads me to believe is a general issue.

Otherwise, it ticks all the right boxes. They're still good for watching shows on Netflix for e.g. where bass is not such a prerequisite. They have more heft than the soundbud series so relatively rugged build + IPX7 waterproofing and as always, accompanied by Anker's outstanding warranty/customer service.

title: Moving away from the BeatsX
text:
I needed to replace my BeatsX with something that sounded comparable. I’m not a fan of heavy bass earbuds such as the Anker Spirit X. I like my music balanced and not muddied by excessive bass. The BeatsX’s sound quality was clean and well balanced. Unfortunately they were made with absolutely zero water resistance.

I just received these Anker Spirits. One day shipping was nice. The sound is comparable to the BeatsX. Bass isn’t over powered. Though a little tinny. The form factor is slightly larger than the BeatsX but isn’t noticeable when wearing when correctly fitted. I went with the largest wings. They’ll do the job at a fraction of the cost with the added benefit of water resilience. Now to put them to the test.

I purchase four sets of Soundcore earbuds.

Soundcore Curve. The bass was too overwhelming, bringing the bass to the forefront of the sound stage. These were the least expensive of the four. For the price they are acceptable given the battery life and water resistance.

Soundcore Spirit X. Bass is punchy, but a little too over powered for my taste. Over all these had the clearest and best sound.

Soundcore Spirit Pro. These sounded the worst. Way too much bass which sounded muddied even with the EQ turned off. The EQ made it sound worse.

In the end I prefer the Soundcore Spirit. They may not have the longest battery life of the four but the sounded suited my tastes.

Update April 24 2019

These things suck for phone calls. The sound quality is terrible. I had to switch over to speaker phone they were so bad.

title: Threw them away. Incredibly irritating headphones.
text:
let me first say this is the second pair of Anker headphones I have had. The first pair was terrific. So the issues I had with these headphones were unique to this model.

These headphones, acoustically, are perfectly fine. For $24, they're a decent bargain even. However, they have a couple of features that are truly annoying, to the point where I have thrown these headphones away.

The cord between the two earbuds is too long, leaving way too much weight tugging on the earbud. Their solution to this? A wee bit of plastic you can use to tangle the cord up into a knot. That knot will then get caught on everything; your gym bag, your shirt, your neck, the person next to you, magnets, whatever...

The control panel is far too large and heavy. It is located on the cord on the right side. This leave the headphones completely lopsided in terms of weight. Your right ear bud is going to fall out every time you move, pick up a weight, take another stride on the treadmill, whatever...

The microphone is trash. Do not call people on these headphones unless you truly hate them and wish to deafen them. Calling someone using this microphone is akin to putting a microphone up to a hurricane and hoping you can shout over it. Either way, your listener is going to hate you and not hear a thing.

Overall, these headphones are perfectly fine if you are planning on sitting completely still and only using them for audiobooks. Beyond that, I can see no use for this product.

title: You won't find anything better than this for the price.
text:
I wanted some wireless headphones that I could do a lot of bodyweight exercise, mountain biking, and any amount of moving around in. These headphones absolutely fit the bill.

The most important thing I looked for was fit. These headphones had consistent reviews saying that you don't need to adjust ever once you have these in, and they are absolutely right. Once you figure out how much slack to have and get both earpieces in, you won't have to touch them. The only issue I have had with fit is when I have only one earpiece in, the other becomes very easy to pull out. Since this isn't what I use these headphones for, I'm not upset about that.

As someone with schooling in audio engineering, I cant say that the sound quality is amazing. It makes me miss my $30 monoprice over-ear headphones. That being said, even for wired earbuds, there aren't many buds that will give you much more for the price. The sound quality isn't bad, and no bluetooth earbuds have amazing sound quality yet, but these aren't a "hi-fi" pick. Bass is emphasized if you're into that.

The cables dont feel too flimsy, they're light enough to not get any the way or move around too much, and sturdy enough to where I dont worry about tearing the cable if an earbud is caught in my bag or something.

I charge them every couple of days, but I only use them for an hour and a half to 3 hours a day. I haven't run them completely out of battery, but the charging is fast enough to where I dont feel like I need to push that limit.

Even if these broke within a month or two, I'd probably buy them again. Very much passing sound for the gym, isolates better than I expected, and very comfortable.

text:

I'm using these on a Bluetooth 5.0 compatible phone (essential PH-1) and have had some issues with the headphones dropping out with the sound gradually fading back to full volume over the span of about a second. I haven't had a problem with any of my other Bluetooth headphones, although they're all Bluetooth 4.x... could be that my phone doesn't like 5.0, or there's just a one-off issue with my particular pair of headphones. I contacted Anker and with zero fuss they refunded my money and let me keep the headphones. I really appreciated how simple and frustration free their customer service was.

Oh, and the Bluetooth range on these is great - I think the 5.0 standard allows for a much higher range, and it shows with these. I can leave my phone in the kitchen and go anywhere in the house without losing connection.

title: Audio is delayed! Videos/gaming will be out of sync with audio!
text:
AUDIO DELAY
There's a major bummer with these affordable buds: Bluetooth delay. For the record, I have a Google Pixel 3 phone. When I watch any streaming video (regardless of app --it could be YouTube or Netflix or whatever), the audio is out of sync with the video. It's really annoying.

OVERALL
You get what you pay for. For a lovely low price, you get okay sound quality, decent build quality, and iffy comfort. What's nice is that the battery life seems good (seems to live up to the marketing).

COMFORT
The buds have mediocre comfort. I've tried the different ear tips that come with the buds, and it doesn't feel that good. When I move my head around (e.g., looking down at my phone, then back up), there's a decent chance that the ear buds will lose the tight seal in my ear canals that allows for the buds to reach their highest potential sound quality. I imagine the buds will feel a lot better if you get Comply foam tips, but that adds a big percentage to the cost of using these.

SOUND QUALITY
There's a bit too much bass in my opinion. Those who say the bass is weak probably aren't getting a proper seal with the ear tips. But more importantly, the bass is somewhat muddy. In the end, it's not terrible, and most people probably won't care. I was using the 1MORE Triple Driver wired earbuds for a couple years before I got the Soundcore Spirit buds. The 1MORE earbuds cost 4x more (back when I got them --now they're only about 2x). So I'm used to better sound quality. That said, I'm fine with sacrificing the sound quality given the super low price of these Spirit buds.

Sadly, the audio delay/syncing problem is way too big of a deal for me. I need to find another brand to buy.
