They feel kinda cheap, if I'm being honest in comparison to my BeatsX that these replace. The wire containing the controls that connects the ear buds is surprisingly thin, which I think, in combination with the cheap plastic control box (again, coming from the machined aluminum of my BeatsX) is what makes up my impression of chintz.
Pairing was simple with my iPhone 7, power button for 3 seconds and bingo, there they are. They also show up in Control Center's battery section, which is nice.
Fit is very comfortable in my ears with the medium sized tips & small wings. I haven't used them other than sitting at my desk thus far so how they stay put while I'm moving around / running / etc remains to be seen. The body of these ear buds is more significant than my BeatsX and therefore they stick out of my ears about twice as far as the BeatsX, which I was able to wear under my full face motorcycle helmet comfortably (and get the helmet on without displacing the headphones), I seriously doubt that will be the case with these. No big deal as I really should be using my wired sound attenuating ear buds that are attached to my SENA blue tooth headset.
Sound Attenuation. This is important to me as I travel a lot and easily get annoyed by the inane conversations that I over hear while moving through the world. These seal into your ears nicely to produce a natural attenuation that feels similar to hearing protection I've used rated at -20db. Your mileage may vary as attenuation levels come down to how they fit in your ear a lot of the time.
Microphonics (the sound a cord transmits when bouncing around or rubbing against things) are very minimal, I put this down to the very slim cord.
Sound quality is pretty bass heavy. Even coming from BeatsX which are well understood to be bass-heavy. I used the "flat" eq setting on my iPhone with my BeatsX and enjoyed the slightly bass heavy sound. With the Anker / Soundcore Spirit Sports, I listened to Run The Jewels & Radiohead songs while messing with EQ settings to see where the sweet spot is for these. Many of the settings like R&B or Lounge are unpleasantly muffled and / or bass heavy. Flat EQ for music is slightly more bass heavy than I'd like - so I'll continue to play around here no doubt. I also tested the sound with one of my favorite podcasts, Do By Friday. Merlin's voice sounds great and overall, voices are clear and sound profile is good...Alex Cox's laugh is slightly less annoying through these headphones, somehow. Shrug.
Phone calls. Call quality overall is good. There is a more pronounced lag between invoking Siri or voice dictation for text messages than my BeatsX had - I'm assuming this is down to the W1 chip's magic.
Overall, like many Anker products, these headphones are excellent value for money.

title: Great budget wireless headphones
text:

I only have two minor gripes so far: (1) the maximum volume level could be a peg or two louder. I'll admit I listen to music loud, and the maximum volume of the earbuds combined with my phones maximum volume is JUST loud enough for me when I'm using these in a noisy environment like cutting grass or on a plane. (2) I haven't quite figured out how to adjust the cord binders so that it doesn't tug on the buds when I turn my head all the way left or right. Too slack, and they will grab the collar of my shirt; too tight and they stick to my neck.

That said, I am finding that the little rubber "fingers" that fit in your outer ear do a much better job of keeping the buds secure than the behind-the-ear clips like Beats "Powerbeats" earbuds I have. Speaking of the Beats earbuds, I prefer the Anker buds to the Powerbeats (which cost ~3x more) in almost every way except for max volume level. The Ankers are more compact, fit my ears better, have better battery life (on paper anyways), and are more balanced than the ridiculously bassy Beats.

One improvement I think could be made is to have the cable made of a slicker material (fabric sheath?) that does not catch on skin or clothes as easily. For the price, though, I am completely satisfied with these.

title: Sound frequently fades in and out
text:
=== The Good ===

These are very comfortable, and while the battery life is lower than I'm used to, it is on par with or greater than most headsets currently being sold.

There are many tips included so you can find the perfect fit.

=== The Bad ===

My previous bluetooth headset was the LG HBS 750. Now I am no audiophile, but I could not tell any difference between the HBS 750 and my wired headset. The Soundcore, on the other hand, is noticeably worse. The sound is airy, for lack of a better word. You get used to it after an hour, but every time I switch to my wired headphones and then back to the Soundcore I get annoyed all over again.

Also, the airy sound is audible as white noise when there is a pause in the sound. For example, if you listen to an audio book then you hear a static sound whenever there is a pause between sentences.

The volume when talking on the phone is insanely soft. Even with the volume cranked to max I have a hard time hearing. Perhaps I was just spoiled by the HBS 750, which had it's own volume and could boost or attenuate the volume level coming from the phone. The Soundcore's volume buttons affect the phone directly, and there doesn't appear any way to boost the sound. Perhaps there is an app which could boost the volume on phone calls when using a bluetooth headset.

The call quality issue is worth dropping a star. I find myself disconnecting the headset most of the time when I am on a call.

One final note, these are not a good option for using one ear at a time (for example, if you are riding a bike and need to pay attention to your surroundings). I've tried to use the clip included with the headset, but I just can't find a reliable position that allows me to turn my head freely from side to side without worrying about the extra weight pulling the earpiece out of my ear.

=== The Ugly ===

The sound frequently drops and fades back in.

I will set my phone on the desk, mere feet away, and listen for hours (while at work). Sometimes it will go 30 minutes without the sound dropping, but when the sound does have issues it fades in and out every 30-60 seconds until it stabilizes.

I think the issue is that the Soundcore is ultra sensitive to interference. I say this because the fading is always an issue while walking around (occurs at least 3-5 times per song), and while at my desk the problem is more common during the day (when more people are around) than in the morning (when I'm by myself at the same desk). Presumably many of the people I walk past (or at desks near me) also have bluetooth devices.

Deducting a star for the fade in issues.

=== Conclusion ===

If I can resolve the fade in issues I will bump it back up to 4.

I've had them for a week. If I can't resolve the fading issues within the next few days I am going to return them.

title: Comfortable, long lasting battery with full range of sound
text:
Like many similarly styled earbuds from Anker before, the new SoundCore series offers more of the same...which is to say a great performing set of earbuds at a fair value over.

The fit is easily customized to fit different shape and size ears. There are separate pieces for your inner ear and ear loops to help get a fit that will stay in place no matter your activity. I found a fit for me that is comfortable over long periods of time. I have used them for everything from a short bike ride to a long car ride (using only one ear while driving of course - I use the included clip to attach the loose earbud to my shirt collar).

The most important feature of any earbud is the sound quality. I found the sound to be very clear and full - almost a little heavy on the bass for my tastes. I changed the EQ on my iPhone to reflect my audio preference and its been great for me. Audiobooks/podcasts can still be a little heavy on the low end but overall its a great sound. For music, I found the default EQ to be fine for me.

Bluetooth range is excellent. I can leave the phone on my desk and make it about 50 ft to the printer in my office without any issues. The included cable clips are an improvement over previous designs with the ability to reduce the slack on the cord between earbuds without having a hanging loop hit my neck. I haven't yet been able to find how long the battery lasts and that's because the battery life lasts so long. I use them almost every day and haven't had any problems with low battery warnings so that should be more than enough for most. I also tried to test out the water resistance of the earbuds and have been out in the rain wearing them and also put them in a cup of water to see if that would have any effect. Everything sounds and works as they day I first got them.

The remote/mic on the right ear is able to pick up my voice clearly. The button arrangement is pretty standard and very responsive to key press. I do have a preference for remotes that have a little more separation between them or perhaps a more definitive bump on the middle key to make choosing the middle button a little easier on first grab. That may be me just being nit-picky.

I don't think you can go wrong with the SoundCore Spirit. Anker has made it easy to get the right fit, great sound, and long lasting battery from a lightweight design and keeping the price affordable compared to other retail premium brands.

title: Anker's Soundcore Slim earbuds are much better and cheaper. Buy those instead!
text:
These earbuds are functional, but Anker's Soundcore Slim earbuds are cheaper and way better.

Things I hate about these earbuds:
- The sound fades in when you start playing something. That means if you un-paused a podcast or are starting to watch a quick video on instagram, in addition to the short delay due to the bluetooth connection, you'll hear an additional delay as the sound goes from very quiet to normal volume.
- If I have them connected and receive a phone call, they mess with the phone call on my phone (Galaxy S9). If I click the bluetooth button on the call to opt to use the regular handset speakers instead, my phone switches back to bluetooth randomly during the call, meaning I think I've been disconnected from the person on the other end of the call.
- The sound quality is BAD. I use exclusively bluetooth earbuds and I don't usually care about sound quality but the Anker Soundcore Slim earbuds have much better quality, and they're $5 cheaper that these ones!
- This is probably just my preference: I think the cord is way too long, and the loop system they use to shorten it at the back doesn't stay at the place you shortened it to. Much better just to buy earbuds that have a shorter cable in the first place.

Things I like (all of these things can also be said about Anker's other earbuds, Soundcore Slim, so, as I've stated multiple times, buy the Slims instead):
- Magnetic backs, so you can keep the earbuds around your neck when you're not using them.
- They're really light and you often forget you're wearing them.
- The battery lasts most of the day.
- They're cheap enough that you don't need to worry about losing or breaking them, and you can buy five pairs of these for the price of one set of airpods.

text:
Most of the headphones I have dealt with in the past always have had a huge annoyance lurking somewhere. These Anker Spirits seems to have finally solved that. I think the most common annoyance I have had is fit and this is where these shine. Usually with a connected pair(wire between the two buds), the wire works its way to the left or right on my neck and tugs because it is too long or sits in the wrong spot. One of the best things about these is the small rubber chunk in the middle of the wire that allows the user to shorten the wire to any length of their choosing.(See Picture) Other buds after an hour or so make my ears throb and ache due to them putting pressure on some wrong part of my ear. These allows for the perfect adjustment of the wire prevent pull or discomfort. With the huge selection of included buds, I think anyone can find a good fit with these. For me personally, the default included buds with the little wrap-around piece fit PERFECT. I mostly use these outside doing yard work and I am blown away every time I use them at just how comfortable they are. After being outside for 3 hours, it is almost like they don't exist! Now that the comfort has been addressed lets get to the rest.

Sound quality: No these are not Sh*re monitors ($300-$500) but man are they awesome for what they are. There isn't a hint of muddiness in the highs and the bass is perfectly adequate for some gentle yard work listening. I would say 9/10 on sound comparing them to other ear buds in the same price range.

Battery Life: Honestly I don't know because they seem to never go dead. I have worked three 2-3 hour days in the yard without a charge and they just keep going and going and going... like this bunny I know... They seem to fully charge in a few hours at a charge rate of .25 amps and any sort of 30 min top up will give you plenty of juice for the rest of the day.

Durability: These are advertised as Ipx7 and boy do they live up to the hype. Even if you are doing hot yoga or some sweet Kung Fu in India at the height of Summer, these will hold up perfectly fine. As my pictures show I have no fears of submerging the entire device in a cup of water. The oleophobic coating (guessing oleophobic) keeps the water off and makes these seemingly impervious to the elements. The flap over the micro USB slot fits snugly and FINALLY has a pull tab so I don't need to get a knife to pop it off.

Overall for the price you pay, these are some of the best headphones in this category as far as I am concerned. 7/5 with rice, would recommend again.

title: Surprisingly good bluetooth headphones
text:

Then I came across the Soundcore Spirit Sports earphones by Anker. It had very good reviews especially for such a great price, so I took the chance and ordered a pair. I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the material used and how easy it was to pair them to my iPhone. The sound is pretty amazing for a pair of bluetooth headphones at this price. Sure, you won't have the deep bass or high ends, but it that is what you're looking for, you would buy a pair of Bose or Beats. It all depends on what you want. I needed a solid pair of bluetooth headphones to listen to music when I ride my bike run, so extremes in bass or highs are not top priority to me, just something that sounds good. These headphones do the job.

Since the earbuds fit tight in the ear, it was a bit strange getting used to when I wore them and tried to talk to someone; it just sounded weird me talking and hearing how I sound, but a few days and you're used to it.

As for the battery life, they say 8 hours. I can't verify that since I haven't listened to them for 8 hours straight. Although, I have listened to them for an hour at a time on my commute over 4-5 days so I can safely say I'm getting at least 6 hours out of them.

Overall, a very pleasant experience. I'm very pleased with these headphones and for $39.99 you simply can not go wrong. Don't spend $300 on Bose or Beats unless you have money to burn or want to look cool, or if deep base and high ends are priority to you. These headphones do the job, and do it nicely. I highly recommend them.

title: Static Noise Present That Is Hard to Ignore.
text:
When I went to listen to these headphones for the first time I was excited because I have bought many Anker products in the past and have been happy with them. I turned them on straight from the box no issues they connected nice and quick to my iPhone XR and had a good connection range. BUT.

As I turned them on and the initial start up sound went through, I noticed that there was a faint TV static noise in the background while the headphones were only set at about half volume. As I turned the volume up the sound got louder and was fairly hard to ignore. It seems that the headphones will sometimes have this noise and sometime they won't. More so than not. When music is playing the fuzzy sound is definitely there and ruins the quiet parts of music. Thoroughly disappointed at this fact.

As for Sound quality (from the one or two times where the fuzzy noise wasn't there) it was just okay. Nothing to boast about. I was expecting more bass from the comments that said it had a clean punchy bass. These headphones aren't balanced as they definitely focus on the upper end of the music. Even after altering the EQ on my iPhone with the Bass Booster option, the bass was not really there compared to other earphones I have listened to. Another small note is that they don't get very loud like I prefer. If you have Apple EarPods the max volume is equivalent to about 75% UP. It would be wise to invest the extra bit for the Soundcore Spirit Pro's I am guessing. Wish I would have picked those up instead. My bet is that they have better bass as they have larger 6mm drivers. I am no audiophile but these things definitely did bother me.

Coming to a conclusion with my complaints I will touch on some of the more positive things about the Soundcore Spirit.

Pros:
-The build quality is solid with a metal construction and a tangle free wire design
-They come with a good variety of ear tips which is nice
-The wire length is adjustable due to a management clip for the wires which was very good for my workouts in the gym.
-The Earbuds stay in very well and batter life has been very good in my testing. I got at least 3 hours right out of the box after I took them out of the box and an hour or so the next day on full volume.
-The waterproofing is exceptional and definitely works. I wore them in the shower to test their claims and as far as I can tell, the coating they put on the electronic components inside does exactly what it should, keep water out.
-Rather comfortable despite their bulky size
-Solid Bluetooth range. I can get ~15ft with my phone around a corner without any signal being dropped.

Cons:
-A fuzzy tone that is present during silence and can get louder as music plays. For me it is hard to ignore but you might be able to tune it out. It's hard to though especially during quieter parts of songs.
-They have a rather bulky design that make you feel like you have black marshmallows in your ear
-Minimal Bass. Clearly focuses on the upper range of Music.
-Can be hard to fit into my ear due to the large form factor compared to headphones like Bose Soundsport wireless or AirPods.
-Not very loud when set at max volume (Equivalent to 75% EarPods max volume)
-The fade in and out tones when you hit max volume or play a new YouTube can get annoying.

Conclusion:
I guess for $25 they got a few things right (Battery life, Range, Waterproofing) But that is NOT going without saying that the atrocious static noise in the background is very annoying. I have been a fan of Anker and have suggested their products to my friends and family, many of whom have bought their products as per my recommendation. I am not saying that this is a smudge on Anker as a brand but after having tried their bluetooth speakers and charging pads, I was disappointed to have had a bad experience with this product.

Save your money. Would not recommend this product.

I would like to suggest investing your money into the Soundcore Spirit Pro's but I haven't tried them. They advertise them as having Clear Sound and Deeper Bass so that sounds like your best bet. I would gladly try the Spirit Pro's because I feel they would fix these issues, but after this experience I wish I could just trade in for them.

Battery life is good and I average around 5-6 hours at higher volumes, which allows me to listen to them at work in the morning before lunch, but them to charge during lunch and have enough battery life to last me the rest of the work day. Call quality is good and have not had any complaints with my voice sounding far away as long as the mic/in-line controller is hanging down and not pulled behind my neck. Fit is good and I do not have any problems with them falling out during workouts or while working, I did have to swap the curved pieces with the smaller size as they did fell a little uncomfortable with the medium sized curved tips. The medium sized actual tips do a good job a noise canceling and I do have to remove at least one earbud to be able to listen around me. Battery charge times are a little slow, so you may have to plan your charging cycles if you do plan on using them most of the day. Having a form of fast charge would've been nice. But other than the left earbud concern and the charging time, these are very good headphones and the in-line features are great if you have your phone away fr.you and the Bluetooth 5.0 does seem to hold it's connection well if you do not have any obstacles in between the phone and the headphones. I work in a shop and feel comfortable walking around with the headphones and my phone charging next to a computer.

Overall, I do believe these are some of the better headphones in their price range and possibly even better than other higher prices earbuds.

title: These have ZERO noise canceling for calls.
text:
Listening to music on these is actually quite pleasant, especially considering the relatively low cost.

Pros:
- There is decent bass, sound isolation, and battery life.
- The water and sweat resistance is also a nice feature, again for a product that is so affordable.
- Standard variety of earbuds provide a good fit and sound isolation for my ears.
Cons:
- There is absolutely NO noise canceling for phone calls. This is so bad that it's the equivalent to putting the call on speakerphone for the person on the other end. I've even been told that the caller could hear conversations between people standing 10 ft away from me more clearly than they could hear my own voice right next to the mic. I find myself turning off the Bluetooth and switching to my phone whenever I need to make or receive a call.
- There is a necessary, but annoying, plastic clip that is used to keep the cord connecting the two earbuds centered behind your neck, by clipping to your shirt. For this to work the cable must first be wound through a rubberized disc, with channels in it, to create loops in the cable. These loops prevent the cable from sliding through the eyelet on the plastic clip and rendering it useless. Unfortunately, these loops constantly come free from the rubberized disc, and have to be painstakingly reset (the channels are made to hold the cable in place using pressure and friction, requiring a fair amount of force to get the cable in, and the cable has a tacky rubberized coating -- think of flossing using a rubber band!)

Conclusion:
For the price it's hard to complain about the foibles of these earbuds, but only if your primary use-case is for music or podcasts -- making phone calls is practically a no-go. While you will hear the caller quite well, they will not likely hear you, unless you're in a quiet room by yourself.

title: Great fit, long battery life
text:
Fit well, and charge very quickly. The battery survives a day of heavy use. There can be some interference, but I think that's from ambient signal interference and not from the headset itself.

Cable is comfortable, adjusts fairly easily and isn't too slick or grippy. Having a variety of earpiece adjustments is very useful for finding a secure fit that can survive a run.

*update 1/22/19*
Dropping 2 stars - After a few months of trying these with two different cell phones (Nexus 6P, Essential PH-1 on VZW) and a VOIP base station (Yealink SIP-T54S), I've given up using these for calls. There's omnipresent noise, whether out on the sidewalk, on a train, in a car, or in a quiet office environment. Noone can hear me clearly, and everyone complains about noise on the line.
Additionally, signal interference is pretty bad in NYC, especially around other cars or dense areas where other people are bluetooth. The signal will not break, but volume will drop out while it tries to recover and resume. It doesn't register as a disconnect, so audio doesn't pause, but it's very noticeable.

As mentioned by other reviewers, the fade-in for notifications is extremely irritating - why does a notification ping need to fade-in? I miss 3/4 of the short sounds because the volume does not have time to fade in.

Battery life and sound quality are still fine after 6 months - no complaints there when signal isn't dropping - but these are my go-to for wireless listening only, and not for making calls. I actively disable bluetooth when I need to talk to someone. I would not buy these again.

*2nd update 1/27/19*
After leaving the update above, Anker reached out and offered to replace the headset under warranty. I declined, since they're fine for my current use case, but still I want to give back a star for standing by their product and extending the offer even though I hadn't asked for warranty replacement.

title: Great value entry in quality noise cancelling headphones
text:
These are some great headphones. Are they perfect audiophile quality "cans"? No, but they get so much right that I think they earn a 5 star rating for they offer. So what's that?

* Sound quality? Very nice sound signature that biases mids over highs and lows. This give music a "full" feeling without that very popular bass forward sound that's all the rage right now. Highs are good but again, these are hyper articulate cans, they provide a nice a full sound that is easy to approach with being tailored to bassheads. I can see some calling this signature "bloated" but in my opinion, the treble is just there enough to keep from earning that description. As I said, I think this is a very approachable sounding headphone.
* Affordable noise cancelling. It seems to get into quality noise cancelling headphones you're looking at high end 'phones that are easily over $200 - Sony's big brother to these come to mind. But these, with street prices that can be much lower than $200 offer some really good noise cancellation.
* 35 hours on a full charge. Add in quick-charge capacity and this should easily last start to finish on the most grueling day(s) of travel. And if you forget you should be able to get you to your next connection with a quick pit stop at a charging booth in the terminal.
* Comfortable. Earpads are vinyl but they are comfortable (that said these closed back headphones can get hot if you're prone to that)
* Bluetooth 5.0 support
* Wired option. Yes, these are Bluetooth headphones but they include a headphone jack in case you prefer of need that wired connection.
* Volume, play/pause, and NC controls. Easy to reach and use buttons on the headphones for these critical functions.
* Decently stylish. Obviously personal opinion but the navy version while not flashy looks pretty decent in my humble opinion. Uncluttered is how I'd describe them.
* USB C charging port. Cable included but something to note if you've got a bunch of USB micro cables (maybe of a longer length) lying around you were hoping to use with these.
* No carrying case or tote bag. This is my biggest gripe with these actually; would have been really nice to have at least a fabric carrying tote.
* Alexa compatibility. I know I'm behind the times but I have yet to jump on that bandwagon so I can't comment on how well they integrate into Amazon's voice recognition ecosystem.

In summary, I think this is a very nice package (minus the tote bag I'd have liked to see) especially if you can get them below the $200 MSRP. Highly recommended.

Note: 700 vs 710
* 710 is apparently a little lighter, looks to have a bit better build quality (less squeaky), and is upgraded to BT 5.0. Earpads seem to be a bit of a downgrade though I felt they were decent.

title: Plantronics Backbeat Pro I can honestly say the V-Moda's are my favorite of them all
text:
Let me begin by listing (no particular order) the wireless headphones I've purchased over the past few months:
1. Beats Studio Wireless
2. Beats Solo 2 Wireless
3. Bose Wireless Soundlink On-Ear
4. Bose Wireless Soundlink Over-Ear
5. Sony Extra Bass
6. Plantronics Backbeat Pro
I can honestly say the V-Moda's are my favorite of them all. First of all, the headphones are absolutely beautiful! I've always thought the Beats Studios were attractive but the Crossfades make the Studio's look plain in comparison. Even the box/packaging it came in is attractive. And I thought Beats did a great job in packaging their headphones...V-Moda does it even better! As for sound quality, the Wireless Studio's are the only headset on my list that compares with the Crossfades. I believe the Beats are a little louder but the clarity of the Crossfades is better. The Beats "might" have a tad more thump in regards to bass. However, when the Beats are cranked up to full volume the bass becomes distorted. Not so with the Crossfades! Even at full volume the bass and sound is crystal clear. The other headphones on my list are a step or two below the Studio's and the Crossfades. The Solo's are nice but not quite loud enough for me. Nor do they have enough bass. The Bose headsets are also nice but not meant for bass heavy music. No disrespect but they are headphones made for older music lovers, in my opinion. And they don't get very loud either. In fact, I'd buy the Beats Solo 2's before I would buy either of the Bose headphones. The Sony's are the most affordable of the headsets on my list but they just don't sound as good as my top two. I must add, the Sony's do have outstanding bass, probably the best bass on this list. The Plantronics sound pretty good but they are unattractive and have an industrial look. And they weigh a ton! The Crossfades, in one word, are AWESOME! I love everything about them. Plus, I got them on sale for $264 taxes included, so I'm very pleased with my purchase. I ordered the blue shields but honestly, mine are even beautiful with the gun metal shields they came with. I haven't tried any other headphones past the $300 range but if you're looking for a set of headphones that won't leave you broke, sound excellent, look fantastic, and are built to last, buy the V-Moda Wireless Crossfades!!! All the above mentioned headphones were returned...with the exception of the Crossfades.

title: Excellent for the money, but over-hyped and need a 3rd-party cable
text:
I bought these as an inexpensive alternative to the ATH-MR7 headphones, which I bought a few months ago. As much as I love the MR7s, I'm not sure I'd want to ride the New York subway with them on. In addition to being much less expensive, the ATH-M50x has a much more flexible design that allows them to be folded into a more compact form for travel. That said, they use a non-standard locking 2.5mm headphone jack that requires use of the proprietary cords that come with the headphones. Designed as a studio monitor, these phones were not intended for use with a smart phone and the supplied cords lack even a microphone, let alone controls. Suitable replacement cords are available from third parties, however, so that is not a significant issue.

My quibble with these cans, however, is in sound quality. Although I would agree that the sound is exceptional for the price, There are other headphones in the price range that are nearly as good, and with a frequency response that is more to my taste. The high end of these is much better than most of the competition, but it's not in the same league as the ATH-MR7s. I find the bass response of the ATH-M50x, however, to be excessive and boomy - not something I was expecting from a studio monitor. Don't get me wrong - these are excellent headphones, but not nearly as exceptional as all the reviews would lead you to believe.

title: A decent pair of headphones at a reasonable price

The price point of these ear buds is very attractive at sub $40, but don't expect the same level of sound quality or functionality that you'll get with more premium models from other well known brands. That said, these are pretty good! the sound quality was impressive, especially on the low end, and probably just fine for 75-80% of casual music listeners.

The overall design is quite attractive, the ear bud themselves as well as the charging case look high quality. I did have some trouble keeping them tightly secure in my ear when running and beginning to sweat a bit. When walking around the house I didn't have this issue at all. They fit my ears better than my wife's, and without any customization of the tips I imagine it's a bit variable in terms of different ear shapes. There is no rubber on the tips, just the same plastic as the rest of the ear bud, but I still found then to be adequately comfortable. In terms of noise cancelation, these leave quite a bit to be desired. Ambient noise from the environment can still be heard fairly well at mid volume on the earphones.

While I haven't used then enough to throughly gauge the battery life, I can say that I listened to these on a full charge for several hours and still had plenty of battery left.

Overall I believe these headphones are a great product if you're not wanting to spend heaps of money for a more premium product. Again, you get what you pay for.

title: Review from a non-tech guy
text:
I wanted to provide a review, without using technical jargon, for the average person to understand. This is my first pair of quality headphones. For years I have just been using the free earphones that come with my phones. After using these, I’ve realized what I’ve been missing all these years.

Unboxing:
There weren’t too many highlights with unboxing these headphones. It comes in very basic packaging. The headphones are wrapped in a thin layer of foam and come with a headphone cable and usb type c cable for charging. Also in the box was a quick setup guide and an instruction booklet. Keep in mind, these do not come with a case or carrying pouch, so you may want to invest in one if you play on traveling with these.

Set-up/Pairing/Navigation:
After charging the headphones, pairing them with my phone and laptop were simple via bluetooth. No issues here. It took less than 30 seconds.

The headphones have multiple navigation buttons to turn the volume up or down and to skip songs. This takes a day to get used to since you have to feel around for the buttons while they are on your head. Since I am always on my phone, I found it easier to just use my phone to control these settings.

Sound quality:
For years I just used the free earphones that came with my phones. I never really understood why someone would want bulky headphones. However, after using these, I was amazed by the sound quality. It was as if all the songs I’ve been listening to over the years suddenly became more vibrant and clear. I loved the experience of using the headphones to listen to my music. I was able to hear parts of songs I’ve listened to hundreds of times and never noticed before.

For voice calls, the headphones were crystal clear.

Noise Cancelling:
The smart noise cancelling feature seemed to be hit or miss for me. It did a great job with background noises like white noises (vacuum, dryer, street noise, bus, etc). However, I found that it didn’t cancel the conversations people around me were having. I was hoping to use these in the office, but I don’t think they would be ideal for a talkative office environment.

Overall:
Overall, I would definitely recommend these headphones. I have been wearing these non-stop since I got them, even when I’m alone in the house, because the audio quality is much better than any headphone or speakers I have used in the past.

text:
Headphone sound is a very personal thing. How do you tell whether the AT's are the best for the price? Youtube! Lots of videos on independent tests and a user blind test. Electronics articles. AT's are rated among the top choices by almost all audio writers and professionals. So, I took the plunge, looking to upgrade from MMElectronics open headphones to a closed system to block out extraneous noise. Frankly, the MME's have very good sound for a reasonable price ($40) and I will continue to use them when outdoors or using an iPhone. But the AT's are an order of magnitude above these entry level phones.

The M50x sound quality is superb. Clear sound over all frequencies. Perhaps a bit bright in the HF's, but most of us like brightness. The bass is full but not booming. These aren't Beat Studios with their bass attenuation.

Overall, I don't think you could ask for a set of headphones in this range that will do any better. They reproduce what is recorded very accurately.

My favorite test is Faltemeyer's "Axel F". About 50 seconds in, there are small clicks that have a tendency to get lost with less responsive headphones. The AT's provided clear definition.

title: You Have To Be An Objectively Bad Person To Have A Problem With The Way These Sound
text:
I'm a snobby, elitist audiophile. I'm broke, but that doesn't change the fact that I try so hard to enjoy myself that I can't actually enjoy myself. I have to police my thoughts in order to focus on the music and not the equipment playing it. I have really high standards and to cope with this purchase I kept my expectations very low. And I have been humbled.

Sound:
These sound good. Very good. Frustratingly good. I bought these because I already have some other iems and headphones (Fiio F5, Tin T4, SHP 9500's recently) but I needed something with a mic for use on PS4. I never actually intended to use them for music listening, I just needed something with a decent mic that didn't sound horrible. And I knew the KZ earphones have been getting cheaper and better for years, so I figured "why not."

Now I won't kid you, there are flaws in these *cough* $13 earphones. They're pretty V-shaped, and I noticed that some vocals were recessed (though the mids are still good. Perhaps it's right at the crossover point and only noticible in some songs. Regardless, my wife Lana Del Rey sounds good through them). Bass is excellent, punchy without being boomy, and I mean it! And the treble is bright but smooth. I'd say it's like a fine wine, but I don't drink, so I just have to assume it sounds like what wine tastes like.

Look, I know my review may not help you much, but that's the point. You don't NEED my help to know these sound good, you just NEED to buy them so you have an extra pair for quality earphones around the house. Granted, my Tin T4's are 10-20% better in key areas that make them worth spending $80 (honestly worth more imo), but the KZ ATE's are half way there! And they cost as much as two Starbucks orders!

So just do it. Pull the trigger. If it can make a no-fun snob like myself shut up, you're bound to like them too. 10/10, cannot believe they actually pulled off something this good for such an absurdly low price.

Oh, and the cable is alright too. Cheers.

title: Buyer beware....
text:
I usually don't leave reviews unless I can remain positive for the most part but I really feel like I need to voice my opinion about this product. I am one of those people who think they can read all the negative reviews and then think it will be better for me because I am really good with this stuff. I was dead wrong.

I have wanted a pair of these for a very long time now but after only a week with these things I have had nothing but problems,

-Half the 'felt' from the headband is already falling off. It's all over my head every night and very annoying and makes the product look terribly cheap.

-The cheesy fold to power off/ power on is a complete joke and the hinges feel extremely fragile to me and likely to last less than a few months at most. This means there is no way to wear them around your neck if out and about with no other way to hold them and wish to have them turned off. And it also means you have to fold them in order to charge with out interfering with your backup bluetooth headset. I found this to be a very annoying problem becuase I wanted to avoid hinging them as much as possible because of the cheap hinge feel.

-The charging indicator works nothing like advised in the manual. You plug it in and the battery blinks red for 2 hours and then just turns off. It never turns to green like it is supposed to and unless it does it wont turn on. The first charge took over 4 hours, 2 hours blinking red and then turned green after another 2 hours of no indication light at all. The second charge I had it plugged in for 5 hours, it blinked red for the first 2 hours and then did nothing for the next 3 hours and when I went to use them the battery was still dead!

-Terrible, uncomfortable fit that will have your ears throbbing within the hour and a design that in no way attempts to stay flat against your ears or stay even remotely positioned on your head in an active environment.

-Constant clicking and static sounds heard during silent periods between songs/during pause time.

-It is not possible to initiate voice commands with the headset. Long pressing the center button only puts it in pairing mode to pair with multiple devices at the same time. Seriously a bluetooth hands free headset that cannot initiate voice commands so I can make a call?

-Jabras customer support declined to respond to my emails or call me despite their *STOP DO NOT RETURN TO STORE* labeling. I gave them a fair chance to support their product and they declined.

+On the bright side when they did work the phone calls were crystal clear and music sounded amazing with deep rich lows and crisp vibrant highs with plenty of volume even when working in noisy environments with power tools. No call complaints what so ever.

+Volume controls worked very well, precise and consistent for me. EVEN with my work gloves on.

Promptly returned. BUYER BEWARE.

They are comfortable to wear but the loops over the ears are a little big and floppy so they don't sit as securely in my ears as I would like.  Finally, I used these for a month in February.  It was cold and I would wear a light fleece hat.  I like that the headphones are slim enough to wear comfortably with a hat in cold weather (I have worn other headphones where it was uncomfortable to pull the hat over your ears) however, I noticed a repeatable problem.  Everytime (and I mean everytime - it was repeatable) I turned my head to the right to look over my shoulder the sound would crackle like it was losing bluetooth.  It never occurred when I turned to the right.  (phone was in my pocket - less than 3 feet away - and other than my head - nothing blocking the signal.  I tried resetting the settings and again - totally repeatable.  Then as the weather warmed up and the hat went away - the problem disappeared.  So I think it has something to do with a hat pressing down against the ear pieces.  I do like the way the bluetooth synchs in that caller id numbers are sent through the headset - my other headphones did not do that.  On the whole - not bad - but a few fine tweaks would help.

title: Bye Bye Bluetooth - ISOtunes brings the fire
text:
Wow ... where do I begin? Should I start with the beautiful packaging or just get straight down to the meat and potatoes of the BEST headphones that have ever graced my ears.

I'd heard about ISOtunes before on social media (specifically Instagram) when a friend recommended I'd follow them. As someone who loves headphones and traveling, I'm always looking for the best new way to drown out the sound of airplane engines so I can rock out to my favorite tunes or hear every word of my Netflix shows. One problem with the previous ISOtunes headphones, I'm not a fan of bluetooth!

As someone who is old school in ways, I prefer to have the wires dangling around. That way there's a better chance I don't lose them and I don't have to connect them to bluetooth and hurt my phone battery. Anyway, back to the headphones at hand. When I saw ISOtunes come out with Wired Earplugs (for under $40, might I add), I sprung at the opportunity to purchase a pair, and boy did I make the right decision.

Wrapped up nice and neat when I took them out of the packaging, I properly followed the instruction manual (for once) to make sure I put the foam tips on properly without any problems. I went for the medium size but ISOtunes offers a large and a small so that it fits all ear shapes and sizes. Foam tips: check. Plugged in: check - It's time to test these babies out!

These aren't headphones if you're trying to blow out your ear drum. OSHA certified (which I googled, meaning they are safe to use at the workplace) make sure that the volume never gets too loud and hurt your ear. The sound was crystal clear, and the noise isolation was everything I expected and more. I powered up the TV in the other room to full volume, put the ISOtunes wired earplugs in my ears and seriously couldn't hear a word the TV was saying.

If you've made it this far, you're interested, so I'll keep the rest short. If you travel, work in loud places or simply need a solid pair of headphones for the morning commute, but hate bluetooth headphones, then these are worth every penny.

text:
This is my first set of wireless ear buds. I was nervous to try inexpensive ones and couldn’t spend the money on fancy name brand ones. But so far these work very well! I can’t really attest to the sound quality, they sound the same as every pair of wired ear buds I’ve owned over the years and I’m not really picky as long as the sound is clear.

They seem to hold a charge for quite a while. I only use them to listen to music or videos for 1-2 hours a day and I’ve only had to charge them a couple of times over the last month. And i only charged them because I thought it was time, not that they ran out of power. There are 3 little lights on the front of the case that I think indicate the level of charge, though I haven’t noticed them changing at all yet. When you pair these with your device there is no indicator to tell you their charge level. I use apple products, so I’m not sure if that has anything to do with that.

While they have been simple to pair with my devices, it seems that they will only pair to one device at a time, whether that device is being used or not. For instance, if I pair them to my computer, then log off the computer, they will not pair to my phone. I have to remember to unpair them before I log off and leave the office. I’m not sure if this is typical? It’s kind of annoying that they won’t connect to other devices even if they aren’t currently connected to the paired device. And there is no way to disconnect them from the device when you don’t have the device on hand. Like I said, I don’t know if this is just how these things work since this is my first time using wireless ear buds. I suppose I will get used to it.

Their range seems okay, I was able to walk to the bathroom which is maybe 40-50ft from my computer where they began to cut in and out. So, not too bad but I certainly couldn’t walk around the house listening to a podcast or something.

So overall, not bad for inexpensive wireless ear buds!

title: Love these!!
text:
I already had a couple of V-Moda headphones [[ASIN:B00GO4GMHQ V-MODA XS On-Ear Folding Design Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone (White Silver)]] and [[ASIN:B003BYRGKE V-MODA Crossfade LP Over-Ear Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone (Rouge)]] both of which I have been satisfied with, but honestly I haven't been using them that much lately because they were not wireless and when I go to the gym or listen to music before I go to sleep, the wire just got in the way. Luckily I also had the [[ASIN:B00KGGK71A Samsung Level Over-Ear Bluetooth Headphone - Retail Packaging - Black]] which are an excellent set of headphones that I used in the gym as well as occasionally before I go to sleep. The downside to these otherwise great headphones is that they are huge and tend to get hot with prolonged use. I attempted to use the Bluetooth adapter with my wired VModa headphones, but they were too tacky and too cumbersome to use.

Introducing the WIRELESS V-Moda Crossfade over the head headphones!!! In short these headphones are excellent in almost every way. They combine the great sound from my wired V-Moda headphones with the convenience of wireless capability of my Samsung level over set. Comparing these with the Samsungs which sound excellent I would say these sound slightly better with a little deeper bass and fuller sound. A big advantage of these over the Samsungs is that they are more comfortable to wear. They do not get hot and because they are so light weight I can wear them for an extended period of time without them being uncomfortable. They also look great and offer customizable choices of ear plates ranging from $20 to well over $400 for the precious metal options.

Connecting these to your Bluetooth enabled devices is a snap, just set follow the easy to read instructions included in the packaging and you'll be connected to your phone, tablet, or music device in seconds. Another great option (which are also on the Samsungs) is if your battery is low or don't want to use Bluetooth, then you can plug in a standard earphone wire (included) into the side and these immediately turn into a wired set of headphones. This is also convenient for gaming because while they are wireless, my PS4 does not recognize these headphones when trying to connect them to my console via Bluetooth. I wish I could use the wireless option for my PS4, but that is not the fault of these headphones.

These headphones have many of the same features as the Samsungs, but there is one thing the Samsungs do a little better. On the Level Overs, volume control and track skipping are controlled by a integrated touch pad embedded in the right earpiece. So simply running your finger up over the side of these headphones would instantly turn the volume up, and running your finger down, will turn the volume down. Track skipping/backtracking is controlled by forward and backwards motions with your finger. To pause you just simply tap your finger and to resume tap your finger again. While the V-Moda can do the same thing, these functions are controlled by physical buttons. There are two buttons for volume up and volume down, and a single button that controls track skipping as well as pausing/resuming. To pause just tap the button once, to skip to the next track tap the button twice, but your timing has to be just right or it will just pause the song. In addition there doesn't seem to be a way to go back to the previous track.

Other than the downside I mentioned these are excellent high quality comfortable headphones that should leave you satisfied for a long time.

title: Great headset and comfortable.  Glad I purchased!
text:
So when this whole Covid thing occurred I began to work from home. I was using a company issued headset and by the end of the day, my head would hurt from the pressure on it all day. I basically felt sick because of it. The headset was an over the ears USB one. After I had enough of this for about a month, I looked for something better and decided on this one due to the price, form-factor and ratings.

This thing is great. No longer do I get headaches from being on work calls all day. It is reversible so you can switch ears if you'd like. It has a pretty good distance away from my computer, maybe about 20-25 feet before it starts cutting out. It was recognized right away as a Bluetooth device. I think the sound for those on the other end went down a slight bit, but not too much of a difference. This was mostly a volume change since the other headset had a mic right by my mouth.

The battery life lasts for maybe 7 hours talk time, don't think I ever got anything more than 8. I recharge it every night and it lasts all day. If I only talk for a few hours, it can last almost 2 days with standby.

One last tip that might help others, if I don't shut down my computer and restart it every day, the headset isn't recognized or if it does, it has problems. Your best bet is to power down every day to avoid problems. Once I figured this out I was golden.

Overall this was a great purchase and the money was worth it, even with me being a cheapo.

title: Excellent Headphones with relatively weak battery life!!
text:
Disclaimer: This product is NOT given to me as a gift to share my "Honest Review" :) . I have purchased the product with my own money.

The Good Things:
Sound:
For any headphone the sound quality is the foremost thing. Since this headphone is operating over Bluetooth the quality of sound becomes more crucial here. I have been using this headphone for a week now. The sound quality to a person varies with his taste of music. To me, the sound from this pair is bass heavy and little muddled (lack of clarity) when using no equalizer. I have downloaded app from play store and adjusted the sound to my need and now the quality is excellent given the price range. I tried this pair with a wide range of songs from heavy bass to metal, from classic to pop, from folk songs to vocal and most of the times I have found the sound reproduce pretty accurate with the equalizer settings.

While playing music the sound do not leak out to disturb others near by even at high volumes.

Phone calls:
I have joined conference calls and personal calls with this headset. The voice is absolutely clear when I am speaking or listening to others.

Noise Cancellation:
Noise cancellation is passive and based on the type of the ear plugs you choose from the set. I use the largest pair in the set. It does not hurt at all and blocks lot of the outside noise. I mostly use it indoors so have not encountered lot of noise like in subways.

Accessories:
The small hard case is a bonus to keep the pair safe while not in use. Its small enough to carry around.

Charging time:
The headset gets fully charged in less than 2 hours.

Build:
The headset build quality is very good. The material used gives a soft rubbery feeling to the fingers. The cables do not tangle. The headset stays in the ears properly and do not hurt from prolonged usage. The max volume and low battery prompt are very useful.

Now the Not-so-Good things:
Connectivity:
The Bluetooth connectivity is excellent as long as the device and the headphone are in close range (within 2-3 ft). But as soon as I try to move to an adjacent room the Bluetooth starts to cut on and off, barely catching the music. Even in a straight line of vision there are disturbances in connectivity while moving over 5 ft from the phone.
I have other Bluetooth devices which plays just fine irrespective of the location of my phone in the house.

Battery Life:
One of the factor for considering this product was its long battery life as advertised. The description says the headset will stay charged for up to NINE hours. Well, its technically correct. But the expectation is that it would run for at least 8 hours. My head set gets exhausted in less than 5 hours with normal usage. I have not used it for straight hours (more than 2 hours at a time) but I have noted how long I have used it after each full charge until it gets exhausted. It seems to consume battery even though it is not in use.

Overall its a good product given the sound quality and price range but the connectivity and battery life is something that cannot be ignored.

text:
First impressions: These are nicely made headphones. Comes with its own hard case which is great since my other headphones that cost 4 times more came with soft cases.

Build quality:
Excellent mix of metal plastic and leather. These look and feel like premium headphones. It doesn't fold flat either and the clamping force is not too much that it hurts you ears. It's not as light as my Sony MDR-1A but less heavier than my master & Dynamic MW50.
You can order custom face plates for them from VModa.com at $25 a set to over $300 and even more if you decide you want exotic metals. But at that point it's better to get better headphones. You can use in in wireless mode or wired mode which Is great. The only negative is the use of micro USB for charging instead of USB-C. It even comes with a carabiner but I doubt anyone would want to hang the case from the bag.

Sound:
Wireless Mode :
Pairing is also quick and easy. And if you have paired other BT devices before you won't even need to read the manual in order to pair it. Soundstage it typical for this kind of headphones. These headphones have enough bass to satisfy people who like EDM or techno music. It does sound bloated at times. Midrange is ok if a bit forward with a bit of sibilance with male voices and the highs are not fatiguing at all. I’d say this is geared for mobile users rather than people looking for accuracy. Since it doesn’t have noise canceling the choice for a slightly boosted bass is a good decision so your music still sounds lively even in a noisy environment.

The controls are located on top on the right side ear cup while useful it feel is oddly placed since the ear cups will tilt towards your head. I have managed to pause the music more often than change the volume as i had planned as the controls are hard to differentiate by touch other than one is on the back middle and front top of the ear cup.

These are not neutral sounding headphones. These are fun head[hones to listen to. You can probably even out the overall response by using some equalization but as is, I like the sound signature so far. It’s similar to my Sony MDR-1A.

Wired mode: Similar sound signature but everything tightens up a bit which is a good thing.

They haven't completely broken it yet but they should sound even better once they do.

If you can find one on a good discount, I would recommend getting one for sure.

title: Hate For No Reason
text:
I'm not sure why so many reviewers have knocked these headphones. I paid about $45 for a Like New pair and they are more than adequate for my needs. I bought these to use at work when I return to the office. I wasn't looking for Bose level sound quality, just a decent pair of noise cancelling headphones. I saw reviewers mention these aren't loud enough. Unless you are hard of hearing, or want to become hard of hearing later in life, the volume is more than enough. I also saw reviewers mention how uncomfortable they are. I, admittedly, have a large head. I didn't find these uncomfortable to use at all.

I gave these headphones a 4 out of 5 for two reasons:
1. Build Quality - As many have mentioned, they are plastic. They definitely feel flimsy. A carrying case of some sort would have put me at ease. For now, I will keep them in the box they came in.
2. Noise Cancellation/Ambiance Mode - The Noise Cancelling works fine on these. Not the best, but they do a fine job if you have music going plus the NC mode. Ambiance Mode is where they lose me. Both are tied to the same button. From the description, the headphones are supposed to be able to detect what is going on around you and auto adjust accordingly. I didn't find this mode to work very well at all and it certainly made my music sound worse.

Overall, I'm happy with these headphones. If you've ever owned a pair of Sony headphones, you know what you are getting. They aren't going to blow other headphones out the water, but they will sound serviceable for most people's needs. The main draw is the noise cancellation feature, which it does well. I can't recommend these at $198, but if you see a pair for $50 or less via Amazon Warehouse, they are worth taking a chance on.

title: Personal Preferences
text:
I don't often use earbuds, and if sound quality isn't the biggest priority. It's not like I don't care, it's more that if I am aiming for max HiFi sound, I just go with enclosed over-ear headphones. More important to me is how they handle voice. So here is my takeaway after using these for a few weeks:
- I prefer rubber ear pieces. IMHO the sound better and it feels more secure on/in my ear. The hard design JVC sports on these has the advantage of being easy to clean. Also rubber caps tend to fall off at the most inconvenience time
- The design is simple and well done. The buttons are not touch. JVC decided to use micro switches that are enclosed under the rubber skin or the outer case. Less sophisticated but easier to use and provides a tactile feedback.
- Wireless earbuds are still massive compared to cable in-ears. These are no exception.
- The case is solid but also not small.
- Pairing is easy by keeping the button on the headphones pressed
All in all these are good headphones. If the brand-image (or the lag off) isn't an issue, these are a good alternative to more expensive earbuds. Music sounds okay. The noise cancelling is more of a box feature, and not really comparable to higher priced headphones. Still five stars, especially considering the price. Recommended for those who want the comfort of wireless, but don't need a high end product.

title: All you need to know about a great set headphones...
text:
This is a first day review of the headphones right out of the box. First let me say that the packaging is very appropriate for how the company promotes their product. Nothing about the packaging is cheap, as a matter of fact first impression was that you were getting your money’s worth. The box is secured with a ribbon that you must cut to show it’s straight from the manufacture. Out of the box everything was neat and protected. The headphones came with a nice molded case and all the accessories as promised on the box. The shields even had protective wrapping to prevent scratches and such. Giving the headphones a quick look over, you’ll see the quality of the build and especially the metal arms which the earpieces swivel on. Not a solid plastic arm like most of the other brands that I’ve looked at and tested, in which could be prone to split and crack at some point with excessive use. When you see these in person, you’ll know that pics doesn’t do it any justice. At this price point you get a very professional looking headphone and one that you can use in the gym (my main reason). Pairing was simple, didn’t even need the directions. Had a charge right out the box. Put them on and the fit was comfortable and being that my hat size is 7 3/8, it sat well on my dome. I believe that the metal arms and the swivel capability help with that. Even if you have a smaller head, it will be a good fit. They are a little heavier that some of the others out there, but nothing that’s intolerable, I think it makes them sit and feel better. Now turning them on and listening to music (using Spotify and tracks saved to my phone) was a nice mix of mids and highs. The bass was moderate and not overbearing or under-achieving. I’m sure you can use your device’s or a 3rd party equalizer to make some adjustments. But for me it was fine. I’m not an audiophile by any means, just a guy who likes his music crisp, clear and lively. That is what these will deliver. I wore them for 30 minutes and had no issues with discomfort (I wear glasses). The memory foam cushions kept the right amount of pressure.
Now for those wondering about wearing them in the gym, wonder no more. I started off on the elliptical and there were no issues with the headphones moving around (I have a somewhat of a bald head with a little fuzz). I did notice that it was getting a little warm around the ears after the first 10 minutes or so, but that’s to be expected with over-the-ear headphones. I did buy the XL ear cushions like allot of folks suggested but didn’t swap them out yet. Once I started to sweat, the headphones remained in place 30 minutes later. I tried the incline bench and nautilus equipment with no issues even using overhead movements and the headphones not getting in the way. I cannot say how well they would stay in place for flat bench or decline, but I would suspect that you wouldn’t have an issue unless you have allot of hair, in which you’d have the same issue with most other headphones. The volume on the headphones will get loud if you set the volume all the way up on your device and then use the headphones to control. When the volume is low, you can still pick up noise around you, which is good and turned up, will even drown out the music the gym plays. I have not tested taking a call with these, but should you be on the phone in the gym anyway???? I received compliments maybe because I wasn’t wearing the run of the mill black headphones that all look alike. I have the shiny red shielded, slimmer than most stylish, V-Modas!

title: Finally broke. Still love them.
text:
First of all let me just state that I've had these headphones for over a year and that they finally broke on me. The hinge broke. That seems to be where they will fail judging by other reviews and my experience. I don't always leave a positive review for things after they break but I really loved these headphones. I originally was introduced to mee audio with the AF32 which is now branded the Runaway. I loved their ear cushions and found them to be the most comfortable on ear headphones I own. Being a basshead I wanted a little more and got a pair of the rumbles. They sound great in my opinion. I am an audiophile and in the past i had used wired headphones with headphone amps to get headphones to really drive bass. That is a pain. Bluetooth headphones have their own power source so they have the power to push larger drivers that corded headphones just can't do from a phone or iPod. These have fairly big drivers and they supply the power to push them. They even have enough power that i can use equalizers and actually mix down (for less distortion). So they actually seem like they have more bass even though I own headphones that have frequency responses that get 10 hz or more under these.

For the price and comfort these are really hard to beat. They are very light and the vented ear pad things are super comfortable. Also, the battery life is amazing. These are all day headphones. For over a year I have used them all day long. Like really all day at work and in the evening I use a bluetooth transmitter to watch tv with the same pair at night.

Even though they are broken now, I don't think the durability of the rumble was that bad. I wasn't super careful with them and as I mentioned earlier, they were used all day every day and in the evening. They broke in my backpack. I've probably had close to 8,000 hours on these things so I don't feel like they owe me anything. If I had the sense to buy a hard shell case for them I'd still be enjoying them.

I'm looking at replacing them and knowing how much I used them I was thinking it'd be worth a much more significant investment but to be honest I'm not finding much with specs that look a whole lot better in a lightweight on-ear style. I keep coming back to this page while using my trusty Runaways despite giving myself a $400 budget. I'm not 100% sure what I'll end up with but it is very clear to me that I will have to spend a lot of money or go up in size to over-ear headphones at about double the weight to get any any improvement in specs over the Rumble.

title: V-MODA Crossfade
text:
These headphones are excellent. Their frequency response & features (relating to cell phone use as well as volume control & song selection control) are great. They seem to be made to last. Quality materials are used everywhere I can see. They were rather tight at first but as it specifies in the directions, simply pull them open slightly past their normal bend and the metal part of the headband (call it the spine) will bend slightly which will make it more comfortable with less pressure. Be careful not to bend it TOO much all at once; simply do your "bend" fitting in small increments.
I have one small issue but I like these so much I don't feel it deducts more than a quarter star - which still makes this a 5-star review. I have another, lesser quality set of wireless Bluetooth headphones which have about 6 feet more range. Not a real biggie, but these V-MODAs drop the connection closer to the broadcast source than my less-expensive 'phones. I no longer can make it back to my storage room fridge to pick up a cold Pepsi or other cold adult drink. LoL!
These are NOT inexpensive, nor are the accessories one can buy to change the colors & looks, but if you want top-shelf Bluetooth enabled 'phones that can be worn for hours, these are a great choice.

PROS:
Sound quality is excellent
Controls are very usable & nice to have
They are comfortable for over-the-ear types that seal around the ears. I've worn mine regularly (4-5 nights per week) in excess of 6 hours
They can withstand a lot of volume. I'm hard-of-hearing & need them loud, but they don't "overdrive" & distort even at my needed volume level
They charge quickly - if I had to guess, I'd say fully discharged to fully charged in less than 3 hours - I haven't actually timed it
Top-quality construction & materials
Easy-to-use instructions

CON:
Their range is less than other B/T enabled wireless headphones (by 5-6 feet or so) I own which cost about one quarter (1/4th) the V-MODA's purchase price.

I will & have recommended these to friends.

title: Great bass for headphones.  Microphone is nice for phone calls.  Fairly comfortable.
text:
These Altec Lansing Comfort Q+ headphones came with a nice large, round clamshell case that has a zipper. Inside is a bag that is attached to the case to store the 3.5mm cable, the charging cable, and a splitter. (use the splitter to connect it to a PC that doesn't have Bluetooth) The case is decent and holds the headphones when they are folded up. They do not fold up very tight so the case is a little larger than I would have expected.

The sound quality is pretty good. The bass is actually very good. I always play a bass test song that has very low tones and most of the time headphones cannot even reproduce those sounds. These actually did a pretty good job of reproducing even the lowest of lows. Doing this for a long time will probably hurt your ears though so I only did it on low volume.

The highs and mids sounded pretty good as well. For a minute, I thought they might sound as good as my studio-quality Audio Technica ATH-40 headphones. I did a comparison and the studio cans sound better. (The studio headphones cost more, are wired only and are not very portable though)

So as far as Bluetooth headphones go, they sound pretty darn good. I also used these with Skype for a few meetings. Everyone said I sounded fine. The only thing that is a bit strange about using them for Skype is that they do block out background sounds even when the noise canceling is off. I can't hear my own voice which may take a bit of getting used to.

The passive noise cancellation is great. (the earcups keep outside sound out) The active noise cancellation doesn't seem to improve the noise cancellation done by the ear cups much. In fact, I couldn't really tell the difference between having the active noise cancellation on or off. If there is a difference, it is not much of a difference. I have just been leaving it off.

The headphones do talk to you when you turn them on and off which is nice. The ear cups are soft and nice. The headband feels good and has a soft cushion at the top. They do put some pressure on the ears but not too much.

Left and right are not marked but it is pretty obvious which way they go. (the way they fit ears) They feel funny if you put them on backward.

Most of the materials feel like they are of good quality. If anything is going to break, I would guess it would be the headband.

Overall, I really like them. I keep them paired with my computer for Skype meetings and they can go with me when I travel. The case is a bonus.

title: Freedom of cordless beats out the need for EQ
text:
I own a lot of headphones. I am somewhat of a headphone junkie. I own several pairs of V-MODA headphones including the older wired pair of the over the ear Crossfades. They are excellent headphones but they are not my first choice for everyday use. I have been using my Audio technica ATM-M50's as my daily headphones for probably over a year now. Sometimes I switch it up to get a different sound signature but the M50's are just so well balanced that I have a difficult time finding something that can compete in this proce range.

But...enter wireless headphones. I have a few sets including a nice pair of senheiser active noise cancelling ones but I haven't found a great set that was free of soem issue (the Senheisers volume is too low for me). When I was offered as et of these I jumped at the chance because I have had good luck with V-MODA.

Design and comfort - Like the older Crossfades I have, these are some of the most comfortable headphones I own. I can wear these for hours. The design is beautiful and you don;t feel silly wearing them like I do with my M50's. having no crod flying around makes these very easy to use while cutting the lawn, on a train or just lounging around the house.

Pairing - I had no issues pairing this to my Iphone 5S. Following the included instaruction, I was up and running within a minute or so.

Battery life - This is one area that I am hoping I will see improvements. The first 2 charges have not lasted very long. I have gotten about 6 hours per charge so far and I believe these are supposed to last more like 12. I know some batteries improve with a few uses so I am hoping that is the case here. Or it is possible that the rated battery life is based on lower volumes or something. I tend to listen loud so maybe that is killing my battery.

Sound - These headphones were a bit disappointing at first. Coming off the M50's and having my ears trained to hear those, I found these headphones a bit flat and a bit too bass heavy at first. I tend to listen to music with no EQ with my M50's but I find I need to EQ these headphones a bit. I have been playing around with various settings (on Spotify) and find that a treble boost seems to take away some of the "muddy" lowe end sound. It is not perfect but it helps a lot. I think these are just designed to push the bass a bit more since people think that equals quality. As far as soundstage, I find these to be very up front with little soundstage. Great for heavy rock music that I listen to. However, I do get some separation at times wich makes them feel a bit more full. But not a wide soundsatage by any means. If you are listebing to orchestra type music, I would try these before you buy to make sure they work well for that environment.

Cord vs Cordless - the great news so far is that I haven't heard any difference between the two with quality of the music. Running cordless, these are LOUD headphones with my 5S. I am running them at about 75% volume which is in line with my M50's. I find they run the same with the cord. I have had no dropped sound running wireless. These just work well.

Overall these are going to be with me for the near term. I love the fact that I am no longer restricted by a cord to get great sound. I can live with the need to EQ to deal with the low end issue (although this does not work with amazon music) . These are definitley worth considering if you are in the market for quality cordless headphones

title: Tight-fitting, high quality cables and no guess work. Winner!
text:
We live in a 1950's home that only has two outlets in the bedroom. With a Samsung Tab 2 tablet, Samsung Note 10.1 2014 edition tablet, two Samsung Note 3 phablets and a Kindle Paperwhite to charge, we have a lot of wall plugs and cords at the bedside. I also have a CPAP machine and a bluetooth speaker plugged in. Sick and tired of multiple surge strips and constantly having to borrow wall chargers for use in our livingroom, I looked up alternative options on Amazon. Anker's multi-port chargers had great reviews and I've had excellent experiences with other products from this company. Since some of our cables have become finicky, I decided to get this combo pack which included 5 cables of varying lengths (three 1', one 3' and one 6' cable).

Now, understand, I don't normally get excited about electronics unless they're sexy, sleek things with screens -- I DO oggle and wax poetic about stuff like new smartphones, laptops, TV's or tablets. However, THIS accessory is as sleek and beautiful as it is functional. From the packaging on down, Anker screams quality. So impressed was I with the packaging and the slick little sliding card advertising insert, I half wish I'd done an unboxing video -- Yes, on a charger.

The charging unit itself is solid, nothing hollow, rattling around or plasticy feeling. It has a matte finish that's easy to grip and pleasing to look at. I was impressed with how well-engineered the microUSB cables were, too. The USB ends fit super-snugly into the ports with amazing precision. The cables are pliant, but don't feel cheap. Best, the plastic overmolding housing the microUSB plug is no larger than need be to immobilize the plug. If you've ever had microUSB cables with big, clunky overmolding around the plugs, you're in for a great surprise. I can't imagine a device into which these microUSB plugs won't fit, even while in the case. From what Anker says, these cables are also durable and charge faster than OEM cables. I can't vouch for this, but if the quality is any indicator, I believe it.

I plugged all the cables into the unit and tested them -- check! My Note 10.1 and Note 3 are charging up just fine. I have not seen the dreaded "Battery charges more quickly if you use original charger" or "Charger incompatible" error messages. This charger will charge devices at the maximum allowable rate without overcharging them. Unlike some other chargers I've seen and used, you don't have to pick between 1.8A, 2.4A or other designated ports. Just plug devices into those suckers willy-nilly and Anker has you covered. I know from personal experience with Anker that they also have terrific customer service. That's one of the main reasons I bought from them.

It's safe to say I love this thing. I will post an update to my review a few months hence -- remind me if I don't!

I bought my red crossfades in 2016 as a replacement to the wired only crossfades I had from 2011.

After 6 years these headphones still hold up. Given that most devices are switching to bluetooth only, you may want to consider aux to usb or aux to lightening cable. The battery itself has dropped from 12 hours of advertised play time to about 3 to 4 hours.

These headphones are NOT noise cancelling, and do not expect them to work this way. If there is a loud tv in the background, you will be turning up the volume on this headset. I would say some noise is dampened out, but that is the best you're getting from this.

If you are looking for a good bluetooth set, consider the newer models. If you need something cheaper and/or looking for aux only, then these are fine and will last years.
