title: Great, comfortable, affordable workout earbuds as long as you keep your phone close with no obstructions.
text:
A good value and comfortable set of headphones that have good sound. In most ways I love them.

PROS:
They're incredibly light and comfortable and they stay on really well even if I'm running stadium steps or doing violent moves like box jumps in my workouts or hitting/kicking a heavy bag. The battery life is insanely good. I simply recharge them every once in a while when I think about it, but they've never come close to running out of battery even when I use them for multiple workouts over a few days along with some listening time while I'm running errands, etc. Also, they have pretty good sound. I'd say like a 90 out of 100 for me, but I'm comparing them to my much more expensive Jaybird Freedom set. The Freedom has better sound, but it also cost me 4 times as much money and they were close enough in the sound that it was probably only worth a 10% premium for the Freedom sound. My opinion to my untrained ear.

CONS:
If you plan to use them for working out, you MUST have your phone in an arm band, on the RIGHT side (within a foot or two of the right side earbud) or you will constantly lose the signal. Even putting it in your pocket will make it skip and god forbid you set it down and walk 20 feet away. Terrible connectivity over distance or with obstructions. I could literally set my Samsung S6 on desk, walk 15 feet away and lose the signal if my head was turned in the wrong direction. By contrast, my Jaybird Freedom earbuds allowed me to walk nearly 75 feet away before it started having issues. I almost wonder if my XR100 is defective because every other aspect of the Treblab XR100 is so good???

Comparing the two: Treblab XR100 and the Jaybird Freedom:
The Treblab XR100 is a much better value for the money. But the Freedom does sound a bit better and does a better job of blocking out background noise. The freedom has 3-4 times the range, but they're not as comfortable as the Treblab and again, the Freedom cost me 4 times as much money.

If you can only afford one set, I'd probably go with the XR100 and just make sure my phone is close to me and unobstructed.

title: Top notch charger, but included cables are not up to typical Anker cable quality.
text:
This charger is as amazing as you would hope. It performs great at charging tablets, phablets, phones, wireless mice, and any other device that wants USB for charging. Really a great product as I've always received from Anker.

My only complaint with this charger is the cables that come with it. I have ordered a lot of Anker USB cables and found through testing that even their 6ft cables can support 2+ amps of current. This indicates their quality through a thicker gauge wire. Other cables, while still pretty good, can only manage 1A of current over 6ft (i.e. Amazon Basics brand). Not a deal killer, but devices will charge slower using those cables. So, I was excited to get more Anker cables for a small premium with this charger.

However, the included cables were visibly different from opening the box. You can tell by holding them next to my existing Anker cables that they are thinner (see included pictures, cables with this charger on top, Anker cables bought separately on bottom). The 1ft and 3ft cables will still push 2A. Unfortunately, the included 6ft cable is too thin and maxes out at 1.5A. Not, bad, but not what I've come to expect from Anker and is fairly disappointing to be included in a charger that offers up to 2.4A.

Overall I love Anker products. Their customer service is great as well. However, I do feel I've been jipped with the included cables. They're not terrible cables, but they're not what I've come to expect from my Anker cables. I would say I'd rate this overall combo a 3.5 star rating, but since there is no 3.5 star option and I don't want to penalize the charger too much since it's awesome, I will stick to four stars (5 star chager, 3 star cables).

Edit: Within the warranty, I contacted Anker because one of the ports stopped charging. They sent me a newer model no questions asked. Excellent service. I always buy Anker and I don't plan on changing!

title: A great item to have in your gym bag
text:
I bought the Treblab XR100 almost two weeks ago now and overall I think it is a great product. My primary use of these headphones is lifting weights and going on runs. The product has its pros and its cons.

PRO: Great sound for the price and actually pretty decent noise cancelling. I go to a gym where people overly grunt or they bring speakers to the gym. YES SPEAKERS. The headphones block out the inconsiderate people and I can listen to my own music while I lift. After sound my next biggest concern is comfort. I actually have no problem with the headphones while in my ear. The longest I have worn them in the gym or running was about two and a half hours and they were great. Lastly, I like the range of the headphones, I would say its about 30 - 40 feet from the device the headphone is connected. Once you go out of that range, the headphones start to go on and off, sorta. I love that because I sometimes forget my device and just walk away to get to my next exercise and this reminds me I forgot my device.

CONS: I have two con's with these headphones. First, the on and off switch, okay so my routine is connect the headphone to the device, turn on my music then put it into my ears. Every time no matter what i push the button which will pause the music. Sometimes during my workout I have to adjust it in my ear and I always press the button. Now not a big of a deal but it gets annoying. Last thing I do not like about the product is the cord behind your head. It is just way to long and when I am running I feel it bouncing up and down or when I am squatting or benching the wire will get snagged on the bench or barbell. Shortening the wire will help deal with this problem a bit.

Overall great product like I said. Also if people are wondering their is a next and back button. You just have to press the volume up and down button for like a full second and you hear it change songs.

UPDATE 3 Dec 16

So a few weeks ago my headphones died on me while at the gym. I thought it was the battery but nope the product died. I contacted customer service, which they were pretty decent.

Then today again while at the gym, it just started to disconnect and reconnect with my phone. Again maybe it was the battery, NOPE, this time the headphone component is acting weird. I am over the headphones, at first it was great, but now I am done. Don't buy it if you are looking for a long term headphones, good for a few months, but after that you'll be lucky. Time to invest in some good headphones.

title: Excellent excellent build and sound quality for the cost.
text:
I'm by no means an audiophile but I have tried a bunch of low to mid range headphones and use a pair of Shure 215's as my daily drivers.
These headphones are amazing for the cost. Plain and simple.
Sound profile: The highs can be a bit tinny, a little TOO warm. The mids aren't the most robust and the bass is too much and kind of muddy.
All that being said, I'm comparing them to $100 IEMs so.. the fact I can even make that comparison with a $15 is fantastic.
If using with some kind of software EQ I'm sure you could tweak these to be excellent.

As for the physical quality of them they're very nice. The cable doesn't transfer sound when brushing against your clothes and such. It has small weights on each cable to allow you to hang them behind your ears which helps with them not falling out and lets you run with them and such. The cable itself isn't very long and the With Mic version doesn't have that lil' slidey part to bring the two cables together more.

I will say the cable is a bit short when compared to other IEMs I've used.
Also the Mic button is very flaky on my Nexus 6P. It seems to change what functionality it has based on the foreground app and is kind of inconsistent. I've pressed it and it's: Paused the music. Gone back 10 seconds on a podcast. Launched Google Now. Etc.
Haven't tested functionality of the Mic itself. Giving these to a friend and just burning them in/testing out.

I mean really any negatives I can say would just be nit picking and frankly for $15 the overall quality of the sound and build quality for that cost hugely outweigh any downsides.

As I'd mentioned these are a gift and I'm glad they turned out to be pretty damn good lil IEMs for the cost so much so down the road I'll probably snag a second pair (though without the mic) for a backup to keep at the office if I ever forget my Shures at home.

title: Currently no app support for WHCH710N, so sound quality is questionable
text:
### Summary ###

The positive: I really like the build quality, design, and feel. The headset is extremely comfortable and lightweight. The buttons are easy to feel for with your fingers once you train your brain which is which (they each have their own unique feel). I also like the ability to speak voice commands so I can make calls, set timers, and whatnot without having to pull my phone out. Uses the more modern USB Type C for charging, which is a plus. Comes with a 6” USB-C cable. Also comes with a cable (3.5mm) to plug the headset in as an alternative to Bluetooth. The cable is a generous 4-feet long, but note it only works for audio, not phone calls. NC is good at blocking white noise. Great battery life.

The negative: Phone calls over Bluetooth are quiet, and call-voice quality is poor. I wish the headset boosted volume rather than just synchronized with the device volume. Does not come with a wall charger. Uses HD audio: AAC, but the sound quality is more middling than I’d have wished for at this price range. It’s good, but not great. Hopefully Sony eventually adds 710N to the app so I can adjust the EQ to get better bass and treble. NC isn’t good at blocking voices. This headset isn’t the best option if you wear eyeglasses and not good for outdoor or sports activities. Voice guidance is accented, English only, and cannot be disabled.

### Full Review ###

-- Sound Quality --

I test all my headsets by listening to Some Chords by Deadmau5. It provides a good sampling of the full spectrum—from the highs to the midrange to the bass. The overall quality is good assuming you have a good seal around your ears (see section below about wearing glasses). The bass sounds rich and midrange is clear. The treble isn’t the best, though. You may have heard the term “crisp” when referring to high notes. These lack that. The high notes are more muffled and muddied. But, they are not the worst, either. I’ve had other headsets with worse treble. To compare, I tossed in my pair of Jabra Elite 75t and swapped back to the Sony headset. The Jabra sounded way better IMO. Clearer high notes and richer bass. The sound quality on the Sony is good, but for the price, I personally feel it should be better.

Other reviews mention that you can improve bass and treble in the Sony Headphones Connect app, but as of this review (July 2020), the app would not register the 710N version. So I searched Sony’s “List of compatible devices” and WH-CH710N isn’t listed. The closest I could find was for the WH-CH700N, but that doesn’t work on these. So for now, I have to review the default sound settings that I’m stuck with.

If you listen to voice, such as audiobooks and podcasts, that is fine. Voices weren’t too boomy or too flat. Slightly muffled perhaps, but only slightly.

-- Volume --

Pressing the volume up and down on the headset synchronizes the volume with your connected device rather than adding its own boost. That means you are at the mercy of your device for the loudness factor. On my OnePlus 7 Pro smartphone, the music volume got plenty loud enough. However, there are times when voices (e.g. podcasts) may be too quiet. Such as when mowing your lawn or vacuuming (even with NC on). Also, it’s pretty low when on a phone call (more on that below).

-- Calling --

This was the most disappointing feature. Even with volume maxed, the person on the other end is quiet. In general, I find that volume for calls is best when the headset boosts beyond the phone’s max, but this one doesn’t. As mentioned above, it’s locked to the phone volume. On top of that, the voice quality is low. It sounded muffled/muddy. And that’s calling mobile to landline on a 4G-LTE network. Mobile to mobile or to VOIP would likely fare worse. If you make a lot of phone calls and rely on your headset, you may want to look elsewhere. That said, the person on the other end did say they could hear me clearly, so at least the mic seems good.

-- Wearing --

This headset is super lightweight. I weighed it in at 220.2 grams. Whereas a similar pair of headphones I have is 335.5 grams. Feels good even when worn over long periods of time. Padding on the band adds to the comfort. The earcups rotate and headband has a good range of adjustability—could even fit it over a baseball cap.

The sides grip my head well enough so that the headset stays on when rotating my head downward, or violently shaking from left to right. But it doesn’t grip so tightly that it causes discomfort.

That said, when putting them in a resting position around my neck (not on my ears), the headset did feel a little tight. Not painfully so or even uncomfortably, just annoyingly. It was best when the earcups were vertical rather than horizontal. I'm getting more used to the feeling over time.

-- Wearing with eyeglasses --

I tried the headset with both my computer glasses and sunglasses. While it wasn’t uncomfortable per se, the temples on the glasses push against the earcups and create a gap in the material. Thus breaking the seal and allowing more outside noises in, and fewer sounds to stay put. For example, sound leakage causes a big drop in the quality and richness of the bass. Was flatter and weaker. The gripping of the band with eyeglasses isn’t as effective, either. While the headset doesn’t fall off with glasses on and lowering my head, they do slip a bit depending on how quickly I do it.

I find this headset isn’t the best if you need to wear glasses with them, but not the worst, either (for instance, the temples don’t dig uncomfortably into your head or ears as some headsets do).

-- NC / AMB --

I tested the noise cancellation (NC) and Ambient Sound mode (AMB). With all modes turned off, and no music playing, I sat on my couch in the living room while my wife and daughter played a card game in the dining room. I could easily hear them. Turning NC on, the sound of my refrigerator faded, but I could still hear their voices. With NC off and AMB on, their voices sounded about the same, but the fridge was louder. Also, there was a whooshing / white noise coming from the headphones when AMB was on. Sort of like the sound you’d hear back in the day when playing cassette tapes. This can distract from the quality of music when on a lower volume (and can be annoying when listening to voice).

With music playing in the headset and NC turned on, I couldn’t hear their voices anymore. That said, I really couldn’t hear them with AMB on (or off). Since these are Over-Ear Headphones, music playing pretty much stays inside and masks outside noises depending on how loud your volume is.

-- Using Outdoors / Exercising --

This headset wasn’t made to be used outdoors or for sports. While AMB (Ambient Sound mode) is supposed to help you hear your surroundings better (such as nearby traffic), it’s not super useful when music is actively playing. Even the manual states, “Do not use the unit while walking, driving or cycling. Doing so may cause traffic accidents.” Also, I found that the sound of wind blowing gets amplified when using both NC and AMB. It’s particularly loud and annoying with AMB on. This is likely due to wind hitting the sensor since it’s less noticeable when turned off.

Another factor that hurts it’s outdoor and active usability is the lack of waterproofing. This headset has zero waterproofing, and the manual warns that rain and sweat could damage it. Even says damp hands are bad.

-- Voice Guidance --

Voice guidance is a feature (a voice) that tells you things like battery level, connection state, and sound mode. I’ve owned many different headsets and have experienced both male and female voices with varying degrees of quality. On this headset, the voice is feminine and has a slight foreign accent. While I can clearly understand what the voice is saying, the Chinese accent does knock the quality down slightly. If only because cheaper off-brand headsets I’ve owned had similar accents whereas higher-end ones like Jabra sound more native. It’s not about being picky, since I’m honestly fine with the voice, but for the price of this headset I’d have expected something higher quality . . . less knock-off sounding.

Even though the manual has instructions in Espanol and Francais, the voice guidance is only available in English. I also didn’t see a way to disable the voice guidance for those who find it irritating. While both these things don’t matter to me, it may be of concern for some.

title: Surprisingly good!
text:
I bought these headphones out of sheer desperation while in Target, so I could listen to music on my iPhone while shopping (too many distractions, I am not what one would call a "people person"), and was shocked at more than a few features:

1. Comfort. I have always been skeptical of ear bud headphones, because all others hurt my ears after a short time. These, however, fit perfectly right out of the box. They do come with different size ear pieces (small, medium, large). The over-the-ear construction is flexible enough to allow for some movement, unlike the ear buds that come with the iPhone/iPod, so they are about a thousand times more comfortable - a huge plus in my book.

2. Sound quality. I own a great number of Bose/higher end equipment, and while these headphones definitely aren't on that level of sound, they are incredibly good! Great bass, crystal clear high tones, and no distortion at all at high volumes. I was pleasantly shocked, to say the least. They are also pretty good at blocking noise, although these are not noise-reduction headphones.

3. Ease of use. As stated, I bought these at Target, tore them out of the box in the parking lot, and wore them into the next store - they stayed in place, and when I needed to I could simply pop out the ear buds and leave the earpieces just over my ears. The length of the cord is also just right for an iPhone or iPod - not so long it gets caught on things, and not too short where you feel restricted in movement.

Overall, for $30, these were a great buy! I'm very impressed.

title: Sound Good, But Button Design is Frustrating!
text:
Bluetooth headphones are one of those items that have finally started to become less expensive for the unwashed masses. Sure, Bluetooth earpieces have been available for cell phone use for years, but a set of nice cordless headphones with a solid connection (earlier Bluetooth versions didn't always transmit sound reliably) that don't require breaking the bank are being released in droves.

So MEElectronics® provided me with a sample of their Rumble Bluetooth Headphone set, and after a couple of weeks of use, I can comment below:

Construction

The MEElectronics® Rumble headset (aka MRH) comes in at 5.3oz (146g), with thick, leather-wrapped, soft ear pads and a plastic frame. The headset allows each earpiece to fold up, enabling the entire set to become compact enough to fit inside of a felt drawstring bag (included). Unfortunately, while these metal hinges do "lock", there is still a tendency for the sides to fold inward when manipulating the headset. In one instance I pinched my finger, but I attribute that more to my own clumsiness than a design flaw. That being said, exercise caution if you are adjusting the fit so that you don't accidentally pinch your own skin.

There are three buttons on the left earpiece which control volume, play/pause, and track forward/back. There is no dedicated power button; you simply press the play/pause button to turn on the headset, as well as initiating the sync mode. The microphone and audio jack port are also on the left side, with the right side having the micro-USB port used for charging the unit.

Function

First and foremost, the headset packs good sound. The bass is pronounced while still keeping the vocals of each song clear. While all of the songs that I listened to, ranging from Mozart, classic rock, modern rock, punk, & reggae to the crooning of broken-hearted country ballads, sounded good, I couldn't shake the feeling that the quality was only a step or two better than a basic car stereo. While that within itself is not an especially bad thing, the MRH should sound much better than it does. All of this being said, 95% of the time the headset sounds great and plays songs with a drum and guitar track much more pronounced. The other 5%, however, especially if there is a really strong bass to a song, makes it sound like you are missing some of the music.

The only other issue that I have is in regard to the operation of the headset buttons. While it is not unusual for buttons on a smaller device to do double duty, the programming of the MRH is frustrating. Each button that controls the track selection is also used to adjust the volume. Where most headsets would require you to hold down a button to adjust the volume while allowing a quick press to change the song, the Rumble is the exact opposite. As such you are forced to hold down the buttons to change the tracks, making it next to impossible to 1) not adjust the volume, and 2) jump to the next song since the button is inexact. As a result, it was easier to use my iPod to change songs and only use the MRH for volume control.

My last issue concerns the buttons and general control of the headset. Whenever you manually advance a song and/or adjust the volume, the headset makes a beeping noise. While the beep is not too annoying when you are selecting a song, the volume control is downright aggravating when you use a slide bar (such as on an iPod). The MRH will beep continuously until you remove your finger from the volume control; using the buttons on the headset prevents the annoying sound from being nonstop, if nothing else.

Final Say

While the sound quality and aesthetic design of the MEElectronics® Rumble is pretty good, there are still several features of the headset that range from annoying to just a plain bad design. Most of the issues that I have with the MEElectronics® Rumble are easily rectified, however, so I am hoping that MEElectronics® will be able to incorporate some of the feedback into improving their next Bluetooth headset. Until then, I think that there are too many flaws for me to give this product a strong recommendation.

title: This is a great pair of headphones for everyday use
text:
This is not the flagship Sony noise cancelling headphones for sure. When I first open the box and took the WH710N out, I thought it felt cheap, The plastic body is well made, but still felt cheap. But after using the headphones for three days straight, I really appreciate the light weight construction of the headphone. The clamping force is not high. I find that I reached for it more than I normally would (since I own the higher end 1000XM3 and the Bose 700 as well).

The sound signature of the 710N is reasonably flat — the base is not boosted like many of the other popular sony headphones. That is just fine with me. The driver is only 30mm in size but the sound is good. The noise cancelling is fair. This would not be my first choice of headphones for flying. But to cut out noise at a cafe? It does a fair job. I only tested it with a simulated sound source during these stay-at-home times.’

Bluetooth range is good. I walked 40 ft away from the source with walls and doors in between before the connection drops. However — the 710N does NOT support multi-point connections. I have to manually switch off the Bluetooth on my iPad to (re) connect the 710N to my laptop. I do not know why Sony do this in 2020.

I think Sony is pricing this headphones wrong. Either keep the price and throw in some goodies like a good carrying case, or price it lower and make this a per of great affordable headset. At the list price I think it is over priced, but at a discounted price, this is a great deal. Think of this as the affordable version of their flagship 1000XM3 if you can find this on a discount.

title: Intermittent Power Drops
text:
I have owned a pair of MEE Runaway headphones for a couple of years and absolutely loved them. I purchased a pair for all of my family for Christmas and they also thoroughly enjoyed them. Unfortunately, the band on my pair was recently accidentally broken, which spurred me to look at this newer model, which my son also already owned. His pair was not working in one ear, but I took that as a measure of his handling, as he had also subsequently broken his Runaway model by dropping them. Thus, I proceeded to purchased this model and was initially very pleased. They look very well designed and are beautiful. After a week, I noticed the unit would simply power off on its own (Yes, fully charged). This problem became more prominent over time, so I requested a replacement pair from Amazon.

In the meantime, I took this opportunity to look at my son's broken pair. I am extremely adept at fixing electronics, so I carefully disassembled the pair and discovered that the one of the wires had disconnected from its post. I re soldered it and it now works.

I have been using my replacement pair for a week now and as always, have been extremely gentle with handling them. Today, they also began shutting off for no reason. I can also hear something rattling inside. Taking everything into account, I now have experience with 3 pair of this model and all seem to have a problem with the quality of the soldering. This is disconcerting because my previous experience with this companies products has been excellent. I expect to return this model for the Runaway, which sound the same anyway. My only other explanation for the issue I am seeing is that the wire that runs through the band may not have enough slack to allow for the extra pull that is caused by collapsing the unit to fit in its cloth case. It may be cause a ratcheting effect where opening and closing the unit causes the wire to exert more and more force on the wire and thus its connection to the post.

text:
EDIT UPDATE- 2020 May 19: Left channel is intermittently dropping out on Bluetooth. I am a few months beyond warranty and V-MODA will not repair or replace. Their "lifetime" trade-up warranty only gives you 20% off a new set. In my case, the cost of the headphones is now over $50 higher than when I bought them so with the 20% discount, I am still losing money. Not happy. They may be physically robust, but I'm having my doubts about the electronics. Should not have to trash a good set of headphones fifteen months after purchase.
ORIGINAL REVIEW:
After years of messing around with earbuds,it was time to step up to decent headphones. I'm a musician but use these for listening to music at work and for movies at night. I'm probably using these for 3-4 hours a day on average.

I was looking at various models from AudioTechnica, Sony, Senheiser, etc. Durability to me is just as important as sound quality. My resources are not unlimited and having something break and not be repairable a couple years later is something I refuse to accept. The reviews here helped me decide on these VModa Crossfades. I got the optional deeper earpads.

Comfort. for my coconut, they are REALLY good. Earpads and headband pressure just firm enough to seal outside noise . I can wear these for hours and not feel uncomfortable.
Sound quality: first of all, I have always felt that Bluetooth degraded sound quality. Plugging in directly has always been the way to go. but I knew I needed the convenience of moving around as I worked and was prepared to accept some degradation in sound quality. Additionally my phone (LG V20) has a pretty high quality DAC (Digital Audio converter) that is only active when the 3.5mm headphone jack is used. i figured that between the Bluetooth and not taking advantage of the high quality settings on my phone, I would be listening at a mediocre level. Not so!

Yes, I can tell a little bit of a difference when I plug in directly but it is really not that significant. The quality on the bluetooth here is remarkable,. The things sound fantastic hour after hour. Great neutral signature...not bass-heavy like the kids seem to go for. I listen to a lot of jazz, alt rock and classic stuff like Steely Dan.. anyone familiar with Steely Dan's music knows they put incredible effort into their production and the recordings that are issued have detail that really carries over from their mastering. These headphones let me hear detail in therir music that I've never heard before.

Durability. This is what made me buy these. They were reviewed as being extremely well built and they are indeed solid without being bulky or heavy. Very very impressive. And if you're into that sort of thiing, you can get various colors of outer shells to look cool.

Design/Aesthetics: As a designer, it's fairly important to like the visuals of products I care about. I think these are very contemporary and sleek without being overly techy or crazy retro like some of the high end stuff (looking like World War II Air force stuff)

I noticed the price has dropped significantly on these since I bought them a year ago...at the current price, it's just a complete almost unparalleled value. Nowhere will you get this quality for such a low price. And no, I'm not being paid for this review in any way.

An additionally, the company stands behind their products. I believe that if you want to upgrade, they have a very good package that credits you the value of your current headphones.

Don't believe the hype about noise-cancelling headphones. If you get a good seal between the earpads and your noggin, you will really reduce outside noise. Noise cancellation does not work that well on varying sounds, like random conversation or noises in your environment although it works quite well on constant noise sources like jet engines. I have to believe that messing around with phase cancelling and so forth in these noise-cancelling circuits HAS to have a deleterious effect on sound quality. It certainly adds a hundred or two to the price. I'm not rich.

Overall, I honestly don't have a single bad thing to say about these. Which is kind of amazing fro me, being a picky designer-type...really for ANY product. So...10/10 right here. Go for it.

title: EXCELLENT VALUE
text:
A few days ago I received my new Philips SH8100/28 ear hook in-ear headphones. I spent quite a long time researching these and other lower-priced headphones before making this purchase. As so many other reviewers say, "I'm not an audiophile," but so far, I am quite pleased with these headphones. I learned that many in-ear "cans" require a break-in period, maybe 100 hours. If so, these can only get even better.

PROS: Very good price, considering the quality and performance--balanced range of sound, not super heavy in the bass, nice, clear midrange and treble sounds. These phones are quite comfortable. I had them in for a couple hours straight on the first day, and I've never even worn in-ear phones before! They stayed in place very securely, even when I was heading down a trail on a very warm day hike!

The ear hooks even allow me to semi-remove the phones to talk with other people, while the headphones stay in place hooked on my ears. I was concerned about whether the hooks would interfere with the ear temples on my sunglasses, but not a problem at all.

As for the cable itself, it is a perfect length, and is well-fastened and supported where the wires enter the headphones. Also, I have NOT noticed any noise transmitted to my ears when the cable rubs on my shirt, something I've heard can be a problem with headphones from other companies.

CONS: My only complaints: (1) No storage pouch or case (a Zip Lock baggy does the trick). (2) Providing a clip to hold the cable on my shirt would be nice. (Maybe I can use an old tie clip or alligator clip). (3) As mentioned by others, the cable is VERY tangle-prone, until I straighten it out and put the phones on. A nuisance, but not a deal breaker.

Anyway, so far, after a few uses, these Philips phones are proving to be a wise choice.

text: These Palovue SportSounds were my first experience with Bluetooth ear buds, so I did have a bit of a learning curve with their set-up, but it wasn’t too difficult (hint:  install the app earlier than later & use its Quick Start feature, which is more complete and clearly written than the manual).  I had to experiment with different sized tips and it took a couple weeks of practice, but now it’s quick and easy to put the ear buds on and get them comfortably and securely positioned.  The SportSounds allow you to start, stop and advance tracks by tapping on either bud.  This is a very handy feature, but occasionally I still inadvertently trigger it while I’m putting them on.  Not surprisingly, it is liberating to be able to listen without being tethered to my phone via a cable.  I mostly use ear buds to listen to French lessons during dog walks, and the SportSounds are perfect for that or for podcasts or audiobooks.  The app does include an equalizer, which is a cool feature and it does help with music.  I can’t compare SportSounds with other Bluetooth ear buds, but their fidelity for music, while OK, definitely does not measure up to my wired Palovue SoundFlow ear buds.  To test the microphone I called a friend.  He rated the voice quality as “excellent” and said he couldn’t really hear any difference when I used the phone with or without ear buds.  He must have been pretty impressed because he ordered his own pair the next day.  SportSounds appear to be well constructed and built to last.  The case is compact and solid and keeps them handy, well protected and charged for weeks at a time. I admit I was skeptical about Bluetooth and resisted it for years, but these SportSounds have won me over and now I would really hate to be without them.

title: Not worth it, poor sound quality
text:
If I had nobody else to help me review these, I'd give them one star, but after giving them to a few friends and having them say "its not that bad," I've settled on 3 stars.

The key points: Subpar sound, cheap material feel, okay build quality, comfortable enough, acceptable noise cancelling

I've tried a lot of headphones, from $5-$500, and these sound a whole lot closer to the $20 headphones I've tried than anything else. The mids are extremely muffled, almost as if the drivers are blocked by something, or if wires somewhere are crossed. The highs are rolled off and the bass gets a bit boomy, which themselves aren't dealbreakers at all, but the mids definitely are for me. The friends that've also tried this said that they could see someone liking it, but that they didn't exactly prefer it. To me, however, they are almost painful. If I paid full price for this ($130-$200!?), I would return it, potentially the same day. I've tried Mpow H10s at $40 that sound much better and have noise cancelling just about as good.

Onto the build, its made of very rough/loud plastic, and plasticy/polyestery headband and earpads. It feels like its put together solid and will last a while, but it doesn't feel like $200. It's not the most comfortable pair in the world, but its not uncomfortable. If these were a bit cheaper and weren't severely lacking in the sound department, I wouldn't take a star away or anything for it.

The noise cancelling works, but it's not amazing. I'm not sure if its up to par for a $200 pair of headphones, but if you're listening to music with it on, most outside sounds will be muffled enough to no longer be distracting.

In the end, I would recommend against them. From what I've tried/seen, there isn't a large jump in quality from a good $50 noise cancelling headphone until you get to around $250, so these aren't really worth it. The price of these looks like its been jumping around from $130-$200, but everything I've said still stands, I don't think its worth $130. If you can't afford the jump up to a WH-1000XM3 or anything, get a Mpow H10 and save a good chunk of money.

title: Good headphones with a lot of bass.
text:
The TREBLAB Z7 PRO headphones are really good headphones, but they may have a bit too much bass for some people. The highs and mids are well balanced and sound great, but the bass is overly heavy and can drown out some of the higher sounds. I know there are many people who like that though, and if you like heavy bass, these may be perfect for you.

I've had the TREBLAB Z7 PRO headphones for around a month and haven't had many issues. They pair quickly to my phone and are comfortable for me to wear for hours. They can also last for me for the day, which is really nice.

The buttons on the headphones are easy to feel and use, unlike many others I've tested. There is a clear voice prompt that isn't overpowering either. I did find the capacitive touch gestures a little unresponsive at times though.

The TREBLAB Z7 PRO also fold up nice and flat. This allows a small profile and allows for them to have a smaller case. The fit and finish on the TREBLAB Z7 PRO is decent. They have a quality feel, yet still have a bit more plastic than some others.

All-in-all, the TREBLAB Z7 PRO are decent headphones for their price, for those that really enjoy a heavy bass sound. They aren't for everyone though.

title: Don't Even Bother for PC (or Anything that Needs to Sync to Video for that Matter)
text:
I know what you're thinking. You're sick of ppl tripping over the cable running from your PC to your comfy spot on the couch; you're sick of abusing your limited USB connections. You want to upgrade your sound. You want something good for gaming and music and movies. These will literally fulfill none of those needs. Because they are BT. Windows 10 and BT don't play well. At least it doesn't with the BT on these phones. Don't even bother trying. And I know now you're thinking "yea this dude is just too stupid to figure it out". But... no. It will pair but not connect. It will connect but have no sound. It will connect and have sound but only choppy BS; it will then promptly disconnect. Just look it up you will see countless threads and no real resolutions aside from the standard "run troublehsooter" (LOL) and "reinstall drivers", i.e. the standard answers to everything that usually don't do anything, especially in this case.

The best I could do was connect these to my Display.... and the lag is so bad you cant even watch movies with them without having your brain fragment from the disjunction. No idea if the lag would be bad if connected straight to PC, cause like I said after a couple weeks trying to get it to work, no dice. Seems to me if it's connected to the display and the display is, you know, displaying the video presently, that the audio should be synced, but the lag is God Awful, upwards of 50ms easily. Clearly noticeable. Clearly due to the BT connection.

And now you're wondering what higher-end wireless audio set you should get for your PC. And I have no clue - seems anything with decent sound is strictly BT, which is demented given how small the bandwidth is for BT to begin with. BT can't even transmit voice from a mic and play HD audio at the same time, even if it is connecting properly. I was willing to overlook that, but I mean just as a point of contention: why the f^ck only BT? Make a damn version with a dedicated 2.4ghz usb adapter so that ppl with PCs or just gamers in general can use these. Our market is 100% not served.

These are going back. These are designed for someone who wants to walk around with their phone listening to music.

Sound is good. Very clear. Bass is weak af.

title: Just what I wanted, great customer support
text:
I originally bought the $99 Acoustic Sheep bluetooth setup, which worked fine, but having to disconnect and reconnect the battery every day was a pain. I talked to support about it, and they referred me to the Effortless, and I upgraded right away, no hassle and they refunded my original purchase gladly. I would have bought the Effortless originally, but despite doing a lot of product research on Amazon I didn't realize they existed.

Anyway, this product does exactly what I want.

First, the mechanical aspect. The speakers are flat, thin, and flexible. You can lie your head down directly on your side on a pillow and the speakers still work. You might notice that they are present, but they aren't uncomfortable.

Second, the sound. Well mostly I am using them for noise blocking, which means I usually have my white noise app playing. Sound quality doesn't matter too much. When I do play music it sounds fine. You're not going to get any bass out of a speaker this size, and that's not their fault, it's the laws of physics.

Third, the convenience. The charger is very easy to use, you just line it up on the charging base until the magnet grabs it and the light starts blinking, walk away and forget about it.

Fourth, the Bluetooth controls. I'm able to change the volume with relative ease while lying down, I don' t need to fumble around and find my phone. I do think this is on area for potential product improvement - it would be great to have external controls in a fixed position. As it is you have to find them through the fabric of the headband. No big deal.

All in all, this product is exactly what I wanted and it performs exactly as I hoped.

title: Nice Headphones with Good Sound.
text: I liked these.  Easy enough to charge, pair to my phone (or TV) and use.  I've used them several times now for listening to my TV, and to music on my phone, and they sound great.  No outside noise can be heard, and extremely comfortable to wear.  I'm not an expert at what makes headphones better or worse than one another, I'm just looking at if I can set them up easily and use, and how good they sound, that's it.  I've had other headphones that after months I'm still trying to pair them to something, these I had paired to my phone on the first try.  Different colored lights on the bottom of one of the ear pieces tell you when pairing is complete.  The parts that fit over your ears are padded nicely, and extremely comfortable to wear.  All you need is located on these including the charging port, on/off pairing button, noise cancelling button, and a 3.5mm jack for plugging into listening devices not equipped with Bluetooth.  The only thing that took me a little getting used to was the on/off button being so close to the volume up/down button.  They are right next to each other, and although they are shaped differently so your touch can tell them apart, my old fingers still kept turning the headphones on/off by mistake when i tried adjusting the volume with the headphones still on.  Young people will most likely have no problem with this, for old(er) people like me, having on/off on one ear and volume on the other side would have worked better, but this is hardly a deal breaker on these because they sound great once adjusted right.  I can't say if the treble or bass could be this or that, but I've been to over a 100 rock concerts back in the 70's, and have heard all the great rock bands live that you still hear today in movies and commercials, and know what good music sounds like.  Without being nerdy technical, this sound good enough to me.  Very happy with how easy they are to use and how good they sound.  Well worth the money.

title: I'm in love with these headphones. Comfortable for hours, amazing sound quality, beautifully made.
text:
I'm in love with these headphones. I'm a huge headphone nerd and have probably a dozen pairs of varying styles and brands -- I have an old pair of M100 Crossfades that've served me well, and the new wireless option caught my attention.

V-MODA over-the-hear Crossfades are a huge win: they look beautiful, with quality craftsmanship and design, and sound even better. The slick design is comfortable for hours of wear - usually 6-8/day for me - without any issues. They aren't isolating or active sound-blocking, but the enclosed memory foam earcup keeps sound from leaking and lets me enjoy my music without having to crank it up.

Bass kicks without drowning out mids; trebels are tight and sound great without being flat or tinny. The sound quality between wired and Bluetooth is essentially the exact same - a relief, given some BT headphones are kind of lossy.

The wired/wireless dual option is so convenient: the included cable is thoughtfully and well-designed, too, making it prepared for any and all uses without fraying or falling apart. The cable also has controls for volume built-in, which is handy when your phone or iPod is in your bag/pocket. The battery life is at least ten hours over BlueTooth, and it's a godsend when I'm working or at the gym. Pairing is quick and painless, taking just a second.

My main comparison headphones are my regular office headphones, Beyerdynamic DT770's and my home phones, a pair of Sennheiser HD-600's. The Crushers can't touch my Sennheisers, but they're not far off the Beyerdynamics at less than half the price. title: Fantastic Headphones but a little overhyped
text:
So I gave these headphones a 4 out of 5. Let's start with why it's a 4. I've purchased two sets of headphones from Amazon besides these, those are 1) Philips Flexible Earhook Headphones SHS3200/28 (Replaces SHS3200/37), and 2) JVC HAEBX85Z. Hence my comparison will be against both of these as well.

The Philips SHS8100/28 are a great pair of headphones that go into the ear and isolate (not cancel) noise. The standard ear caps are a one size fits all making and fit snug into my ear as compared to the SHS3200 which just sits atop the ear canal. The JVC were a similar fit but the ear cap needed to be changed out and the ones that cap with it didn't quite fit as well as the SHS8100/28 does.

Ear Hooks: The ear hook on the SHS8100/28 is smaller and much more firm than the other two. In fact the ear hook completely wraps around and encases the wire. On the JVC there is a slit in the loop of the hook which allows you to pull it out. Both the JVC and the SHS8100/28 ear hooks take abuse as in me nawing at them when I'm not using them or buried deep in my work or study. The SHS3200 ear hooks were flimsy and absolute rubbish. Between the JVC and the SHS8100 both can stand up to abuse and sports, including basketball much less running. I've had both pairs hook onto branches and they handle pretty well while I'm trail running.

Sound Quality: Philips SHS3200 isn't even worth mentioning since it sits atop the ear canal and not in it. Between the JVC and the SHS8100 not much can be distinguished between someone who isn't an audiophile. The turbo bass is noticeably different in the SHS8100 as opposed to the JVC but it's not like I'm expecting superb quality. In terms of symphony but are on if not near equal footing. The SHS8100/28 definetely doesn't go as loud as the JVC but you won't punish the SHS8100 for these. Any louder and your not really trying to drown out the world your just trying to drown the world in your music. I listen to white noise at work to drown out the background noise and I think the JVC are just a bit crisper in the different ranges but when it comes to rock or heavy rap the SHS8100 takes the edge.

Build Quality: You'll need super glue at some point on the JVC and the SHS3200 (especially the 3200 since the speaker has a plastic rim which falls off). The JVC have been through several spin cycles, courteousy of me leaving the headphones in my jeans and they stood up to the abuse so maybe they aren't that bad. I need to glue back the shell and it wasn't a problem since. I haven't had the SHS8100 long enough to comment but it looks pretty solid.

Why the SHS8100 got 4 instead of 5 stars. From the images it looks like the headphone swivels on the ear hook, it doesn't. It just bends, that's it. The turbo bass thing is a little marketing with perception. Nothing over the top. In the end you can pay half the price for the JVC or you can pay (about) twice as much for the SHS8100 for a small difference. If the SHS8100 was $12 it's a no brainer but for the bang on the buck the JVC is the better option.

text:
For headphones of this price from a company like Sony I had pretty high hopes, but I was sorely disappointed. I'll start out by saying the sound quality is actually very good, but that's where the positives end.

As soon as I took them out of the box the first thing I noticed is how cheap they feel. All thin poor quality plastic, and barely any padding on the head strap. The ear pads are alright, but the head strap starts to get uncomfortable within minutes because it's hard and thin. I've had $20 Walmart headphones that are more comfortable to wear. The buttons feel cheap and flimsy as well. They honestly kind of feel like they might fall apart. Maybe the light plastic was used to reduce weight on your head, but it just left them feeling like junk.

The noise cancellation is alright, but it really only works for ambient sound. You can cycle from ambient sound to noise cancelling to nothing, but both the ambient and noise cancelling settings do about the same thing. I'm wearing them right now as I type this, set to noise cancelling, and I can't hear the sound of my heater fan, but I can hear the sound of my keyboard loud and clear, I can hear my dog chewing her bone a few feet away, I can hear the traffic outside (though it is quiet), and I can hear videos on my computer just fine (the headphones are connected to my phone). So it seems to really only be able to handle constant white noise type noise like fans and refrigerators, without doing much of anything about more dynamic sounds. It is like this on both noise cancelling and ambient sound control setting, then on the off setting of course everything comes through. I'm also now starting to notice a faint chirping like sound it's making in my left ear now that my heater turned back on and its trying to cancel the noise. I just noticed it in the middle of writing this and it's already getting very annoying. Actually, now that I'm paying attention its making a bunch of little chirps and whines in attempt to noise cancel. Probably wouldn't hear them if I were playing music, they're quiet, but when nothing is playing you can really notice.

I also downloaded Sony's headphone app hoping there'd be more controls I could access through that, like an equalizer, but they don't seem to work with it. The headphones are connected to the phone but the app doesn't recognize them, so it seems you're limited to the 4 buttons on the headphones, which is fine, it wasn't advertised any differently, but I'd hoped.

All in all, they're alright headphones, but you can definitely do better for this price. Feels like a pair of cheap headphones that got some sub par noise cancelling software uploaded onto them and then sold for 3x the price they're worth.

title: Surprisingly good
text:
I've had these for about 6 months. I did a lot of research online before buying these and was hesitant when I actually picked them up at the store--the packaging seemed kind of cheap and I was skeptical. I bought them anyway and was surprised by how well made they felt. They are gratifyingly heavy for their size and the polymer cap that fits into your ear seems durable and is very comfortable.

When I put them on, I was surprised by the sound quality and amount of noise reduction. The sound quality still amazes me. These have really good base and rich, full sound. I've had several pairs of headphones and these blow all of them away in quality. They are definitely competitive with headphones over twice the price. I didn't see any advertisement about noise reduction, but as soon as you put them in, the world becomes muffled, and once you turn on the music to a reasonable volume, nearly all outside noise is drowned out. It feels like walking around in a movie, where the scene volume is muted and the soundtrack is all that is heard. They don't amplify the sound of you breathing, either, as covering your ears would do.

The one thing it does amplify is the sound of the cord moving--it is an awful noise that becomes infuriating quickly. Any thumping at all on the cord is greatly amplified. The noise isn't as noticeable when I take them out running, especially if I wear the cord under clothes. It is most obnoxious when sitting still or walking and the cord is accidentally thumped. As annoying as I find this noise, it doesn't even come close to outweighing the pros of these headphones.

I have taken them out jogging and biking, and they are great in the wind, since most of the ear bud is in your ear canal. My old ear bud headphones forced me to crank the volume to the max to hear over the sound of wind. Not so with these. I've accidentally tugged the cord hard a few times while jogging and as a result, the sound sometimes begins to cut out if the cord is bent in just the wrong way. I am sure this would be the case with most headphones, however, so I do not fault them for it. All in all, I love these and would buy them again immediately even if they broke tomorrow. For $50, I don't think these can be beaten.

Pros:
-Outstanding sound quality
-Very good noise reduction
-Comfortable fit

Cons:
-The sound of the cord moving around is loud and annoying

UPDATE!
After accidentally yanking the cord, the metal housing of the earbud snapped apart at the seam. I was able to snap it back together, but it didn't hold very consistently and it came apart a few more times. They still worked perfectly and I'll still keep them as a backup, but it was time to buy a new pair. The first lasted well over a year, if not two years. True to my word, I bought another pair of Titans. Here's what you get with newest version:
-Fancy packaging, and now says 'Hi-definition noise isolating ear buds'
-Different cord--this time it's braided aluminum (according to the package) and has a clear plastic sheath. It looks cooler, but functionally seems just like the last version. Relatively loud thumping sounds are still transmitted through the cord when it is bumped sharply.
-Black silicone earbud fittings instead of clear. There are 3 sizes. There is a significant difference in sound quality depending on the fit--definitely try out the different sizes to make sure you've got the right one.
-Still comes with a nice case.

Bottom line: I'm still very happy with these.

title: Solid Wireless Headphone
text:
This won't be a full review yet because I just got my pair a couple of days ago from V-Moda, but so far they are awesome.(edit.. week and a half in now and still really liking these.)

Coming from using the M100 religiously, they sound equal to actually significantly better in some areas.

The M100 is great for bass while keeping everything else crystal clear. The Crossfade Wireless seems to improve on the mid clarity while tightening up the bass and keepin it punchy.
This goes for wired and wireless and I honestly can barely tell a difference in sound quality between wired and wireless.

The construction is very much like the M100 and I used my XL ear pads on the wireless. I opted for the gunmetal version and although mines has a blue tint to them I still really like them, they just seem different that I expected.

The pairing was easy enough and I know for my iPhone 6, that the notifications screen shows the battery percentage while the main screen shows a new battery bar by the phones battery bar that shows how much juice the Crossfade Wireless has left in it. I have used them wirelessly for around 5 hours so far and it shows about 60% battery left.

The controls feel good and seem sturdy and reliable. They work a lot like the three button remotes on apple headphones.

I really like that there is a wired mode that immediately shuts down wireless mode as soon as you plug it into a 3.5mm jack. This turns off the battery and allows for unlimited listening in wired mode whereas some wireless headphones always need the battery to be used.

My only issue comes from the M100. Cliqfold and the lack of it. The M100 came with an awesome feature called cliqfold that allowed the headphones to fold up really nice and compact. That feature seems to have been omitted here and I don't see a logical reason why just yet. They are still very portable so I didn't feel it enough to dock a star for.

Overall they are great wireless headphones from a company that initially never seemed like they would make wireless headphones. I feel a lot of time went into tuning and although my experience with wireless Bluetooth headphones is limited, I know these are the best I've heard. These are easy to recommend and I'll keep updating my review as I have more time with them.

Now using these for about a week and a half now, everything has held up. The battery life listening at roughly 50%-75% gets me right around 12 hours. Connectivity is typically fast and responsive and now using it to make calls, microphone clarity is good with moderate background noise and great in quieter settings.

I wanted to point out that for those who are not familiar with the V-Moda headphones, these are not audiophile headphones in the standard sense. These are not neutral headphones. In my opinion they work pretty great for every kind of music you can throw at it but they are tuned for modern music, rock, rap, hip hop, electronic, and so on. The bass is forward and punchy yet clean which takes slightly away from the mid but still sounds fairly clean. The highs are forward but not harsh and overall there is a nice and very fun balance. These are easily the best bass geared headphones I have listened to based on leaving the mids and highs intact. The soundstage is reasonable for closed headphones and while it won't compete with any open air headphones, they aren't meant to. I have listened to rock, classic rock, hip hop, rap, EDM, country, and even classical music without any issues. While they are not my preferred method of listening to classical music, they do a great job considering what these headphones are geared towards.

UPDATE 1:
Forgot to mention that comfort for the Crossfade Wireless is similar to the M100. With the stock earcups comfort is good but after a few hours it is not great. I recommend the XL Earcups if you experience a good deal of discomfort after long term use. I do have a big head so try out the standard cups first but for me the XL earcups add a lot more comfort.

*This review is for the Gunmetal Version

Coming from using the M100 religiously, they sound equal to actually significantly better in some areas.

The M100 is great for bass while keeping everything else crystal clear. The Crossfade Wireless seems to improve on the mid clarity while tightening up the bass and keepin it punchy.
This goes for wired and wireless and I honestly can barely tell a difference in sound quality between wired and wireless.

The construction is very much like the M100 and I used my XL ear pads on the wireless. I opted for the gunmetal version and although mines has a blue tint to them I still really like them, they just seem different that I expected.

The pairing was easy enough and I know for my iPhone 6, that the notifications screen shows the battery percentage while the main screen shows a new battery bar by the phones battery bar that shows how much juice the Crossfade Wireless has left in it. I have used them wirelessly for around 5 hours so far and it shows about 60% battery left.

The controls feel good and seem sturdy and reliable. They work a lot like the three button remotes on apple headphones.

I really like that there is a wired mode that immediately shuts down wireless mode as soon as you plug it into a 3.5mm jack. This turns off the battery and allows for unlimited listening in wired mode whereas some wireless headphones always need the battery to be used.

My only issue comes from the M100. Cliqfold and the lack of it. The M100 came with an awesome feature called cliqfold that allowed the headphones to fold up really nice and compact. That feature seems to have been omitted here and I don't see a logical reason why just yet. They are still very portable so I didn't feel it enough to dock a star for.

Overall they are great wireless headphones from a company that initially never seemed like they would make wireless headphones. I feel a lot of time went into tuning and although my experience with wireless Bluetooth headphones is limited, I know these are the best I've heard. These are easy to recommend and I'll keep updating my review as I have more time with them.

UPDATE 1:
Forgot to mention that comfort for the Crossfade Wireless is similar to the M100. With the stock earcups comfort is good but after a few hours it is not great. I recommend the XL Earcups if you experience a good deal of discomfort after long term use. I do have a big head so try out the standard cups first but for me the XL earcups add a lot more comfort.

title: 5 Stars for Multiple Reasons!
text:
My son suggested I try this brand of wired earbuds because I have so much trouble keeping earbuds in my ears. He was right!

In the past, when I put earbuds in my ears, I try to make the full little circular speaker face toward my ear so I can get the full benefit of everything from the treble through to the base. It just doesn't work for me. My ear is too small, and they always pop out. And the ones that have a large end to place in your ear with a small speaker sticking out of it that goes into your ear canal still fall out of my ear because I don't have enough "ear surface" to keep those from falling out of my ear and they never give me a rubber tip small enough to fit into my ear.

I hope I can explain this:
These aren't exactly round; they have a small protrusion on one end. The end of that protrusion is flat and THAT is where the speaker is located. You place the bud sideways into your ear; sort of like sliding it in with the speaker pointed toward your eardrum. The bud lays flat against your ear and stays there because the disc part of the bud is held in place by your ear on both sides of the bud as it slides toward your ear canal. All the sound goes directly toward your eardrum through the flat edge buried in your ear. The sound is so amazing.
The big surprise is you don't have to have the volume turned up so loud to hear all the music. I had to turn it down from the setting I use for my other ear buds! And I was able to enjoy really good, clear, amazing music. Although I still hear sound around me like if the A/C turns off or on, or someone says something - but it does not bother the music one little bit. To be honest, it was sort of like the ultimate club or bar experience; you get to hear all the great music and can enjoy it with friends without having to shout at each other to share it and your thoughts. Or going to one of those movie clubs with tables and being able to hear the film perfectly and talk about it with your companions at the same time.

The quality is not just fantastic for music. Works great for everything I have tried so far like phone, movies, tablet, games. And I mean a lot of different games; Terraria, Minecraft, or COC with my grandson, as well as WOW, Diablo and everything in between. We are definitely a gaming family!

I have noticed that all the controls work so far on phone, tablet, and such, but I did discover the volume control does not work on PC. But I am so happy with the quality of sound I don't mind that at all.
It is handy to control volume on the phone or tablet using the earbud control because you have to adjust controls on those things with little buttons on the sides; sometimes having to pick the device up to do so while you are trying to use it. Having it on the earbud wire is better.
I have volume and other controls readily handy on my PC as well as on my keyboard and don't even think about adjusting it on the wired earbuds, anyway.

2 thumbs up, 5 Stars, and THANK YOU. I love them.

title: A wireless headphone with excellent bass, treble, and clarity
text:
The V-Moda Crossfade Wireless headphones are an excellent choice if you are looking for punchy bass, crisp treble, and clear sound. What's great about these headphones is that they sound great even while in wireless mode. However I found the stock earpads to be a bit thin - so I upgraded those with V-Moda's XL earpads for an additional $20.

Sound Signature - Bass lovers will enjoy these!
The sound signature of these headphones is V-shaped - bass and treble are emphasized over the mids. Bass is punchy and tight while treble is also well-defined, and "sparkly" at the top. Mids are not as forward as the bass or treble, but are still very much present and clear. Unlike other bass-emphasized headphones, the mids do not sound muffled, but are still well-defined. Music such as EDM, Rap, Pop, and modern Rock music sound quite good with these.

Wired vs Wireless Sound Quality - both sound great
Whether listening to these headphones in wired, or wireless mode; the sound is nearly the same. In wireless mode the over all crispness of the sound is slightly less than wired mode. I could only tell the difference if i repeatedly plugged in and unplugged the wire - and even then, the difference is so small, that it's not an issue. I usually use these headphones wireless as a result.

Sound - Compared to other headphones
The Crossfade Wireless are headphones that I consider to be bass-heavy. Another well-known bassy headphone is the Beyerdynamic Custom One Pro. (The Custom One Pro has an adjustable bass setting but it lacks bluetooth.)The Crossfade Wireless definitely has tighter bass, and more extended treble than the Custom One Pro. But because of the extended treble, classic rock and acoustic music can sometimes have artificial sounding highs. Because of this, I prefer the Custom One Pros whenever listening to classic rock and 80s music. But for EDM and Rap, the Crossfade Wireless are amazing.

Wireless and Wired Functionality
In wireless mode, once you've paired these headphones to your bluetooth-capable device (phone, tablet, computer, etc), connection takes only a few seconds everytime the Crossfade Wireless headphones are turned on. On my phone, there is an indicator of the connection, and how much battery charge is left on the headphones. I also happen to have these headphones paired with my laptop. When both my phone and laptop are present however, the headphones default to whichever is actually putting out audio at a given moment. The range on these headphones is good. I've had the my iPhone 6 over 30 feet away from me behind a single wall and the Crossfade Wireless worked just fine. However more walls or more distance past that would easily cause spotty reception. I suppose the strength of the source of the bluetooth signal (iPhone, audio reciever, computer, etc) would also play into the equation - but in my experience, the reception is quite good.

Battery Life and Charging
It took me about 2hrs to fully charge the battery of this headphone. The battery is not user-removable. The manual states it lasts 12 hours. I've used it on and off for a few days straight without having to charge it. It should be noted that in wired mode, the headphones do not use battery power. This means when the battery goes out, you can still use these headphones wired. There is no visual battery life indicator on the headphones themselves. You would have to check the connected device for how much life is left in the current charge - this is common in a lot of bluetooth headphones.

Latency in Wireless mode - none noticable
When watching videos and youtube on my phone or ipad, I have not noticed any sort of latency issue in wireless mode. The sound of people talking matches the timing of their lip movements, and gaming seems to be work correctly - at least on my iPhone 6.

Comfort
This is where these headphones fell a bit short for me. The pads included with these headphones are somewhat thin for my tastes. What's more, the pads are not quite big enough for totally encase my ears - which means some of the padding rested directly on the outer tips of my ears. This caused a bit of soreness after an hour or so. Fortunately, V-Moda offers the memory foam XL Pad for around $20. Upgrading to the XL Pads made the fit much more comfortable. With the XL pads, my ears are fully-encased inside the pads, and no longer touch them directly. I can now wear the headphones significantly longer with a lot more comfort. Though I still have the one complaint - my ears get a bit hot after a few hours of use. It's not a huge issue, and I can put up with it. But by contrast, my Beyerdynamic Costum One Pros are much more "spacious" - allowing my ears to remain cool for longer periods of time.

Build Quality - Good, but the buttons are a bit clunky
The Crossfade Wireless headphones are made of good parts and materials. The housing of each earpiece is made of sturdy plastic with metal trim and metal shield plates. The earpieces are held in place by a metal frame and the headband is flexible but very sturdy. It all makes for a robust pair of headphones. In fact, I've accidentally stepped on them once - forcing one of the earpieces to dislodge from the frame. But since the frame itself is metal, and the fact that the plastic is well-reinforced; there was no damage - I simply just popped the earpiece back into place. However, the buttons that control volume, and play need a bit of improvement. The pressing action of these buttons feels too shallow and sometimes pressing the button doesn't actually feel like it's being pressed. The power-on button also functions as a pairing-mode button. This slides instead of being pressed-down. The sliding action is decent, but in the "off" position, the force required to slide it to "on" seems a bit too much - I sometimes find it painful to operate since it catches on my fingernail.

Bling - customizable shields
Like other V Moda headphones, the shield plates on each earpiece can be replaced for a customized look. The V-Moda website has a special service in which customized plates with different materials and surface types can be made. The materials range from simple aluminum to even precious metals that can cost as much as $40k! However, the more affordable options (such as the aluminum and standard metal) are still quite good-looking. You can even have your own initials engraved into them, as well as your own custom logo.

Conclusion
The Crossfade Wireless headphones are a great choice for someone looking for punchy bass, extended highs, and excellent clarity. The fact that these sound so great in wireless mode is perhaps the most amazing thing about them. The default ear pads do require replacing for the best comfort, and they still can get your ears hot - but it's a small gripe to an otherwise excellent pair of wireless headphones.

text: Since I got it earlier this week, so far I've used it in the weight room twice & running errands all weekend.  Fast same day delivery was a plus. This BT earphone fits better & doesn't fall off my ears unlike my first one.  I wear glasses & it doesn't bother me; only if I'm using my Samsung Gear VR.  Sound quality is good, I don't mind the bass.  I grew up on Sony H.ear earphones back then but I remember the stiff earhooks bothered me at times so when I heard that this is flexible, I considered as one of its selling points.  Initially, the problem I've had was that the earhooks were too big & too flimsy.  I noticed that the unit would some time rock up or down in my ear especially when I'm working out & sweating in the weight room.  Even though the combination of the flimsy ear hooks & the silicon eartips prevented the earphones from falling off my ears, it still feels loose not to have a secure fit.  Feels like it just sits there.  Everything got fix & got even better when I used the eartips of my old & slowly crumbling 3+ year old Monster iSport Victory earphones.  Now it fits better & doesn't move around.  The flimsy earhooks lightly holds the unit in place & if one needs to listen to the rest of the world, one can just pop it out & let it hang on your ears without the risk of losing it.  Battery life is way better than my roughly month-old Anker BT earphones as I've used it all day Friday & Saturday, charging only once each day just in case.  The usual BT range limitation applies so it's best to have your phone on you instead of walking away from it & lose the connection around the corner.  I've noticed that the rubber cord management is ineffective in holding the cables in place.  It easily pairs to my Android phone & I like that there's a voice notification when powering on & off the unit.  Buttons are responsive but I don't understand why the back button doubles as the volume up button instead of volume down (same for the Next button).  Comes with a semi-hard case, a short micro-usb charging cable & foam & silicon ear tips, each in 3 different sizes.  The manual looks nice but at times, the color of the font blends into the dark backgound so it's hard to read especially with the small font size.

title: NOT worth $144 in any world.
text:
I'm not an snobby audiophile , but I can hear the difference between headphones. I'll go to stores and just listen to them to find the best bang for your buck... I really LOVE music. I seen these headphones on Youtube various other articles and they were getting high praise, and even being compared to Beats by Dre headphone. I was in the market so I pulled the trigger and picked up a set!

When they arrived I was excited to try out this little know brand in hopes of finding a real deal in headphone... I had them boxed up and ready to return about 2 hours later.

The noise cancellation HUMS and does not really cancel anything... kind of dulls the highs in sounds. The hum is what was just the breaking point. You can hear it very well with no music playing and just a bit if you know its there.

Then there is the quality of sound. At low (with noise cancellation turned off!) and mid level volume the sound is pretty good. All ranges do fairly well overall. When you get to about 50% you start to get sound seepage to people close to you. This seepage, of course gets worse the louder you have your music. At full volume on an Iphone 7 plus, people across the room could sing along with you... but then it goes into the next con to this headset. At max volume, the mids are distorted and the bass can't keep up with the volume and are lost in the overly loud mids.

As I said In the end I listened to these headphone for about two hours until I boxed them packed up and ready to return. Here is a snap shot of why.

Pros:
1. Low to mid volume sounds good
2. Build quality is nice and the headphone are fairly comfortable on the head.

Cons:
1. ANC (active noise cancellation) simply is garbage, it slightly muffles highs in the surrounding area. I was tapping a knife on the counter and when turned on the ting went away, but I could clearly hear every tap... and ALL conversations are very audible.
2. The ANC has a hum when it is on. You can hear this in music, or just having them on your head... very annoying.
3. At high volume mid range music and speech is distorted
4. At High volume music or speech, anyone withing 20 ft. can hear exactly what you are listening to.

The most I would pay for these headphone and not feel like I was ripped off was $60... Perhaps the Ghost tek SoDrop (non noise cancellation) model would do better for the cost vs. quality.

I am not impressed with Ghost Tek at all.

Double also! it comes with some neat little velcro straps to bind your new cables up when not in use. title: Excellent build quality
text:
As the selling point of these suggest, these are in fact great when it comes to bass, they're not lying. However, the real selling point of these should be how well they're built. These headphones are the longest I've ever had a pair without them breaking. The only con in terms of build quality is the adhesive on the ear cushions started to decay, but some glue fixed that no problem. The big con, which isn't a con of the headphones themselves really, but because all these aux wires are made in China, they all fall apart absurdly fast. I go through 1 aux wire about every month or two, unless I get really lucky and get a decently made one (by China standards) that'll last a few months. I'm not being overly rough with them, I just use the headphones A LOT and the quality of the cables suck so, very easy to destroy them.

Now, over all audio quality. I'm picky about my audio quality. Picky enough where I can't stand not having an equalizer I can tweak to my liking, but I don't think it's quite fair to call myself an audiophile. That said, the over all audio quality seems fine to me. I did have a headset that was cheap, but supposed professionals were claiming they had really good audio quality despite the price. Comparing the two, I can tell a difference in audio, but not so much in quality. I couldn't tell you which ones sound better over all, I think it comes down more to preference unless you're doing super high end professional work where it's an absolute must to have sensitive headphones to pick apart audio at the seems. The main thing I seek in audio is heavy bass and these deliver, the non-bass audio sounds perfectly good too so over all I'm very happy.

I like these headphones enough that I ponied up for one of the expensive wireless upgraded versions of them, but if you're on somewhat of a low budget and these are available, I'd recommend them. Maybe I'm just lucky, but they should last a good while.
