title: Not one Bad Thing to Say
text:
I wouldn't consider myself an audiophile but a music lover. I've listened to music my entire life and enjoy all genres with the exception of most country. With that said, I've always been passionate about mid-top tier audio products and have been searching for a great sounding set of bluetooth headphones. I scoured the web and the V-Moda's came up in a couple of "best of 2015" articles.

Frankly, what initially caught my eye was their incredible and one of a kind styling. I was looking for something that sounded great but I also didn't want to be another person wearing beats out of the house. Not that I think beats are horrible, because I've owned two sets of the bluetooth sports headphones. One had some quality issues. To the point, I wanted something different and something that isn't on every walmart/target shelf.

So after reading reviews and checking out their website, I pulled the trigger. Incidentally, If you look at the reviews on Amazon only 2% are 1 star. That says something. Most of the solid quality products that I have purchased over the years at least have a 5% 1 star rating.

To be fair, I ordered them from the V-Moda website because they offer free customized ear covers. I couldn't be happier. They updated my order regularly. I ordered them on Friday and received them on Monday. The packaging is sublime and the build of the headphones is quality. They remind me of a modern and streamlined version of my father's headphones from 40 years ago. The arms click into place with a satisfying feedback and you can feel and hear the quality of the spring mechanism. Everything about them says "quality". They are comfortable and light.

I've seen some reviews that say they are a bit on the heavy side and I disagree completely. They are much lighter than my gaming headset and I've been wearing them almost all day with no ill effects or hotspots.

The sound quality is phenomenal. I've listened to music that I've heard for over 20 years and I've picked up some subtle and sometimes not so subtle nuances that I've never heard before. It's like listening to my music for the first time.

The mid range is clear, the bass full, and the treble is crisp. I can almost see the vibrating guitar string with each "pluck". It's really amazing.

My wife, who doesn't really give a rip about sound quality one way or the other, even noticed how great they were when I played her "Into the Mystic". She liked them so much I will be ordering her a customized and monogramed pair of her own soon.

They aren't noise cancelling but they do a good job of blocking out the world around us.

The carrying case is well thought out and high quality. I have absolutely nothing bad to say about this product.

The built in microphone works great. I took two calls on them today and no one mentioned anything. I didn't have to yell and they sounded clear as day.

At $300, I don't think you can go wrong with these. There are others out there in this price range, but I honestly don't think you will get better sound quality regardless of what you spend. From a design and form factor I don't think these can be beat either.

If you are remotely close to "being on the fence" about buying these, I would encourage you to pull the trigger. Obviously with Amazon's stellar return policy if there is a problem they can be quickly returned. V-Moda also offers a 60 day return policy too. Check them out, give them a listen if you can, but these are my new favorite thing.

title: This are a budget set of wireless bluetooth headphones that give good performance.
text:
I like these headphones and am planning to keep them. They can also work as a phone communication device with the mic built into the headset. They are comfortable, If you're used to getting ear aches with press against the ear small headphones these are much more comfortable as they go around the ear instead of right on top of it.

The biggest issue with these that I noticed right away was the noticeable difference in sound quality between the bluetooth wireless connection and the normal 3.5mm headphone jack cable. The wired connection was head and shoulders fuller, clearer more robust sound in my opinion. I was able to tweek the equalizer on the playback device to improve the sound to some degree, but I can't get over the sound difference between the headphone cable and the bluetooth interface.

The second issue is range. For a blue tooth device about 25-30 feet is about all the range you are likely to get. If you have a large workarea that you roam, these will start cutting out and dropping conversation when you get out to about 20 feet. It's wireless but reliably, I was only able to get about 15 feet away from the bluetooth device and not have to wory about it cutting out.

This technology is still fairly pricey so if you don't need wireless right now. I'd wait.

I would NOT recommend wearing these or any headphones while driving. The noise cancelling / ambient noise cancelling technology makes traffic very faint while you are wearing them. NOT SAFE for driving should be a prominent disclaimer.

title: Sound is good, comfort is meh, and has other issues.
text:
Received this as a headset provided to me by my work.
It has decent sound and others can hear me well in conference calls. Being noise-cancelling I do hear the typical white-noise-like sound during silence that I feel like all noise cancelling headsets do, which can be annoying/uncomfortable to some. Additionally the fit is pretty snug on your ears and I feel like that would eventually cause discomfort if continually wearing them for long, but that it likely helps with the noise cancelling part.

Jumping right to what is a huge disappointment for me:
The usb cable is really short. Going from my laptop to my head is stretched nearly full length on my desk, especially when standing. That is lame, but not as lame as the fact that the microphone wand is expected to be worn on the right side of your face (only pulls down on that side) which is coupled by the usb cable is also on that side - this conflicts with having my laptop setup on the left side corner of my desk because to be plugged into the laptop, the cable now has to cross over my keyboard to reach the right side of my head. I'll need to change where all my monitors are clamped to my standing desk to make room on the right side of my desk for the laptop now, just so the headset cables can reach me without overlapping my keyboard. Some people may have this sort of a setup positioning already, but the headset could have been made with the wand being able to be pulled down to either left or right side. Big design flaw.

I also wish that the sound controls weren't positioned at the top of earpiece and I wish they were instead located mid-usb cable. During a conference call I have to rely on touch/memory to mute or adjust sound and that doesn't make things work very smoothly.

Finally, the only included instructions for these are printed on the back of the box, which of course someone plastered a big barcode label on top of. There aren't instructions inside the box, only a many language warning and declarations booklet. I figured out it's saying go to jabra.com/manuals for the manual. You'll need to install the free software from Jabra.com/direct to really get the features on this headset working, the software does have a neat concept it enables for auto-answer by lowering the mic arm and muting when raising the mic arm. Things like skipping track that is says it supports does not work with Amazon Music app in Windows.

I would say this is not worth the price and do not recommend purchasing.

text:
...heads. Yes, that roundish thing that caps off my body does me in yet again. But I'm stuck with it so what can I do?

I picked this up at a certain big box electronics store (fact is, they're about the ONLY big box electronics store these days). The Halo paired easily with my iPod Touch, T-Mobile G1 and Sony Walkman NWZ-A829. Its sound quality was quite good, both via Bluetooth and via the corded option, although the only way I could achieve this given the size of my noggin was to use both hands to press both earpieces against my ears to get them to position correctly for the best sound. Obviously personally looking akin to something out of Edvard Munch's painting 'The Scream' really isn't a workable solution for me or anyone else with a head close to my own's physical size. Which is a shame because Jabra otherwise has created a really nice, minimalist slick-looking LITTLE headset (a fitting irony in that last bit of description) that for the bulk of the population probably won't have any fitment issues. But as I lamented earlier I'm stuck with the head I've got so alas, this particular Halo sadly isn't ever again going to find itself around my scalp.

Other observations: Its rechargeable design is a definite plus. Its volume and track advance controls are rather touchy and seem to me to have a bit of a learning curve. The hinges for collapsing the earpiece sections during storage seem rather cheapish and fragile to me; I'd tend to question how long they would last with repeated folding actions, and although the obvious workaround is to leave then unfolded and ready for use most of the time...except that the only way to shut them off is to fold them closed.

title: Good for the price
text:
So I got these headphones to have a spare pair for the gym or sometimes for use at work.
At only $25, I didn't expect much at all but was surprised at what these brought to the table.
Now, you can't go and compare a cheap pair of headphones to anything out of its ballpark price range so don't expect to be blown away.

The headphones included a USB-C charging cable and a 3.5mm TRS aux cable. The headband on these were fairly comfortable. I have what I would believe to be an average sized head for a male adult and they felt snug. Pressure on the sides was minimal but enough to keep them in place during some light jogging and sweating. The ear padding felt great but also feels cheap.

Sound quality is decent but definitely lacks bass and a good sound stage. Mids are ok, Highs are good.
Battery life seems a bit short though. When I got the headphones I gave them a full charge before first use. During my workouts, I usually do 2 hour sessions. By the fourth day I had to recharge the headphones so that was only 8 hours before they got low. I was listening to Rock style music probably at mid volume during each use.
Another full charge and battery life improved greatly but still fell short of the claimed 55 hours.
Maybe the 8 hour issue was a 1 time fluke? I don't know. But with continued use I only average about 30 to 35 hours of playtime before needing a charge.

Bluetooth connectivity was spotty at first when trying to pair with my Galaxy S9. I would have a random disconnect and it would immediately reconnect. It only happens every now and then.

During a phone call, the person on the other end said they can hear my voice clearly but that it sounded like I was at a distance. Kind of like when you have aftermarket bluetooth in a car.

Overall for a budget set of wireless headphones, they are great for what you're paying.

text:
The KZ ATE is an exceptional value. There are several key points that I considered during this purchase as I wear them several hours a day.

2. Comfort - I wear these several hours a day and they are light and comfortable. The ear piece has a gel tip that blocks out ambient noise, which contributes to the overall listening experience and is very easy on the ear. No pain points after hours of use.

3. Build quality - I don't know how they can build these units at this price. Heavier cord, beefy fasteners and connection points. Nice.

4. Microphone quality - People on the other end of the phone have commented on the quality of my transmission.

These are so inexpensive, absolutely no risk.

text: I was wanting a pair of over the ear wireless headphones for the gym so I did some research about which ones are best and saw everyone recommending the Sony XM4 or XM5. I ended up getting the XM4s since they fold up and they're a bit cheaper. To my surprise, they did not live up to the hype for me but I liked how they looked and enjoyed the touch features on the ear cup. Somehow I stumbled upon these Treblab headphones which look very similar and have the same touch features so I decided to give them a try in hopes they would replace my Sonys and I could return them and save some money. After just a few minutes of using these, that is exactly what I ended up doing! The differences are so subtle that it just wasn't worth the price difference for me. They also fit my head better and they're extremely comfortable! I really just plan on using them for air travel and the gym for the noise canceling since I am perfectly happy using airpods for day to day uses so I am thrilled to save the money and still get the things I liked about the Sony XM4s. These are definitely worth a try if you want them for casual use or you're on a budget. I also like that the noise canceling isn't quite as severe as the XM4s, that was a bit much for me and made me a bit claustrophobic.

I’m not sure why this function would be used because even though they have been powered off as soon as you remove one of them from the case they automatically start your music anyway. One last thing is that I am unable to figure out how to adjust the volume from the earbuds rather than the phone. Pairing these headphones with my Bluetooth devices is also pretty simple, although there's a noticeable difference in audio quality when using Bluetooth, so I try to avoid it unless I really don't want cables in my way. The battery life when using Bluetooth also seems really good, and I haven't ever scrambled to charge it to preserve its battery life, which is nice — it only requires a standard phone charger (USB Micro) to recharge its battery, so I don't burn through AA or AAA batteries.

It feels reasonably sturdy, although I've noticed it sometimes shifting a little bit more often where the brace meets the earphones. I sometimes sleep with these on for noise canceling and for white noise, and I do feel like they'll hold up, so that's good.

One complaint I have is that there was this incredibly sticky film on the brushed metal part of the headphones. Removing it left some residue on the side of it, which looks visually unappealing, and I don't want to risk scraping the metal trying to remove it.

text:
I give this product a 4-star rating because I do like it. Output audio is loud and crisp, noise cancellation is amazing, whereas bass levels are "okay". Unfortunately, within a month of use, my several of my colleagues have told me I cannot be heard very clearly on their end of voice calls. It seems that I sound like I'm far away or my mic input volume is too low. I've experienced this on two different Windows 10 computers. Raising the mic input only helps so much. In rare cases, others cannot hear me at all. When I originally purchased this, I also purchased [[ASIN:B073LNTQ67 Lovinstar Replacement Cable Boom mic Volume for PS4 PC Xbox One to V-MODA & most 3.5mm input headphone Aduio Cable Computer Game]] because a friend made a recommendation. My experience was the same with the included mic cable and the Lovingstar mic cable I separately purchased.

Today, for the first time, I decided to give the Bluetooth functionality a try and use the built-in mic. Pairing and connecting the headphone to my Google Pixel worked flawlessly. In my first phone call, my voice was loud and clear, as far as I can tell because there were no complaints. In a call that followed, the other person informed me more than once that they had trouble hearing me; leading me to switch from Bluetooth to phone handset in order to complete our conversation. I do like this product as mentioned before but the microphone performance has been my great disappointment. I would rate with three stars, however, I understand that the issues I face could be isolated to the particular headphone I received. I intend to return it through Amazon.

text:
These are great. Not perfect, but I don't regret them at all.

PROS:
1. Very Comfy. I have actually fallen asleep with them in place, while on a recliner. Gotten up and gone to bed without realizing I had them in, and not realized it until I later rolled over on my side.
2. Sound Isolation. My wife doesn't have to listen to my podcast while she's trying to fall asleep right next to me :) Even when I think it's pretty loud.

CONS:
1. Not very much warning when you're out of battery. I walk two blocks from my office to my car, during that time, it went from the first low battery warning to shutting itself completely off because of no battery.
2. The volume up/down buttons are just a little too close together, and too small. I have to actually think about it and make sure I'm pressing correctly. I'd like the buttons to be farther apart and a bit bigger.
3. The wire is kind of stiff, so it doesn't simply lay flat on your shoulders. It kind of stays up and visible. Looks silly. I try not to care :)

EDIT: after a few more weeks using them... I forgot that I had reviewed them and came here to write a positive review. I just love them. That stiff wire is honestly the only problem to think about. When I wear a shirt with a collar sometimes it pulls a bit so that when I turn my head one way or the other I feel it pulling. small price to pay. I think I'm going to buy another pair for use with my PC :)

EDIT again: these lasted almost a year. of being used almost every day. I'm not quite happy with the lifespan (they just died on me yesterday, about 10 months after buying them), but I'm buying more RIGHT NOW.

title: Were These Really $200 or More at One Time
text:
At $88 on cyber Monday I thought I’d found a deal. I’ve never have much luck with anything Sony, but knowing their reputation and others I know being so pleased with Sony products, I figured why not.

I’m going to guess that when these came out, they included a case at a $200+ USD price point. I was shocked when mine didn’t include one. So right away your deal isn’t against the original price anymore I don’t think. While I rarely use the cases provided for their intended use, I don’t travel with any that don’t have a case. And, as I said, I’m betting the original release at top price included a case and if that’s the case we should be seeing an apples to apples comparison.

That’s a guess though because I didn’t but them at that price. But a very experienced guess nonetheless. Since I currently have almost two dozen sets of earbuds and about a dozen sets of headphones. Considering I’m a musician, a B2B/B2C salesman and obsessed with wireless sound, all these companies should be looking for people with my skill set and background to review some of this stuff so they don’t look so bad when their product, or “discount”, doesn’t live up to expectations. Sony is the worst for underestimating their customers. i.e. Last summer they gave a 1% discount on a TV just to get it listed in the July sale. It showed blatantly how Sony undervalues its customers. Trying to call these a deal at $88 follows that pattern.

While I can say the ambient sound control and active noise cancelling are excellent (the yard guys were here when I tried these and I didn’t even realize it until I turned off the noise cancelling. Sony handles that well always) but the build is crap. At first I was impressed how light it all was. Then I opened the box and saw no case so I thought that was it. I was wrong. This has to be by far the cheapest, plastic crap build I’ve ever seen from Sony. And I think they’re mostly overrated to start so I always start with low expectations.

I don’t know if it’s Sony products in general or just those sold here, but I’ve never revived any Sony product that was worth what it costs and that included these headphones at $88.

If you want to give someone a decent sounding headset at a price where you don’t have to worry about how long it’ll last, like a kid that’ll break or lose them anyway, these are probably with it. If you’re an audiophile looking for the best sound and a quality build, probably not for you.

title: Indispensible companion to my Linux workstation
text:
While I cannot comment on the noise cancellation or battery life because I haven't used it enough to feel comfortable rating it, I do like the headset a lot for the way they implemented the technology.

I don't know much about the technical aspect of implementing Bluetooth. Whatever these folks did is amazing though. Some background: I have a late 2019 HP Spectre x360 13t laptop with one of the very latest Intel chipsets. I'm also running Pop_OS 19.10, which is based on Ubuntu 19.10. Linux folks will know, a common problem with using the latest hardware with Linux usually is incompatibilities; drivers that don't exist yet, etc. In this case, the incompatibility I've found is that Ubuntu 19.10 cannot properly support my internal speaker and microphone array to work (internal mic does not work at all, half the speakers work, and this is all after a boot config hack that I have to do for the sound card to show up at all). This may be fixed in Ubuntu 20.04, but I won't test that until its official release. So I bought this in hopes that it would work as a microphone, despite all my other Bluetooth headsets and headphones failing to do so.

In Pop_OS (read: Ubuntu), all of my other Bluetooth headphones would show up as output devices, but never as an input device despite having microphones. This meant I was not able to use them with Skype, Zoom, Hangouts, etc. Bummer. To my joy though, this headset arrived and was a savior. This headset, immediately upon pairing, advertised itself as both a live output AND input device. This meant I could now use any software that makes use of a microphone as long as I use this headset. It's brilliant and I love it! Not only does it work for my own private calls, but I've even set it down flat on the table, used the computer's speakers as output, and this as input, and it picked up the voices of myself and my girlfriend at the same time no problem.

So, technologically, I love this thing and it was a fantastic purchase! Sound quality is also great, or at least I cannot say it's bad because I've never had a problem hearing anyone or anything thing, nor has anyone had a problem hearing me. I love that it comes with a carry case. That's handy.

The only gripe i have with this headset, and it's really minor, is that despite it coming with a plethora of different ear tips, both size and style, I couldn't find a single one that fit my ear in a satisfactory way. They're all loose. The instructions say to find the one that offers a good tight seal and fit, but that does not exist for me. I've never had a problem before getting ear buds to fit and seal perfectly, but I didn't have any luck with these. Having said that, I still use it all the time, I just came to terms with the fact that the fit isn't ideal, but it hasn't affected comfort or quality at all. I imagine if it did fit me properly, then sound quality would be even better, but I'm not complaining about it so it's all good.

I definitely recommend checking this out.

Final thought: I LOVE that it has a mute button right on it that controls the hardware. This is fantastic for video conferencing, as it allows me to mute my end when I'm not at the computer. As a bonus feature, it allows me to mute my end without the other parties on the calling knowing that I'm muted.

text:
These headphones really underwhelmed me. Were they really $200 at one point? If so that’s ridiculous. They are very light and the noise cancelling is very good for the price point and the design is good and they’re quite comfortable because of the light weight. But...

The sound quality is awful. Music sounds muffled - like the highs are pulled back so things tend to not be articulated well with vocals, cymbals, anything that pops really from an instrumental side. They don’t sound like garbage but the sound quality is more in line with what I expect from a $30-$40 over ear headphone set. The buttons aren’t the best for access and in low light knowing L from R when putting these on is a major chore.

I have a pair of Plantronics Backbeat Pro 2s that were $130 and sound quality is noticeably better across the spectrum and those have similar noise cancelling performance. Those are heavier but honestly they feel sturdier than these Sony 710s which feel like they’ll fall apart with one drop. If the sound quality was better and these had a touch more power I’d be really happy with them. But I’m just not there so I’m returning them and sticking with the BackBeat Pro 2 set.

Sony should dump these and get better amplification and better equalization and offer app support. If they could do that I’d pay $20 more for that and be extremely happy. But this is unacceptable for the price. I don’t know if there’s a worse pair of headphones in this price range to be honest.

I do not consider myself an audiophile, but I can discern different qualities of headphones. I typically wear earbuds, which are my preference. With that said, these Crossfade Wireless over the ear headphones have a very good sound quality to them. I dare say that they are excellent.

If you prefer bass in your music, then these are the right headphones for you. These earphones seem to trend toward the bassier side of things.

Generally, I don't like over the ear headphones because others can hear what I am listening to. When I'm in an office environment, this can be an issue because I play my music loud. The sound leaks out of the earcups. This is nothing new, as I have experienced that with other brands as well.

I found these to be quite tight on my head, which after a while is something I could adjust to. They certainly won't be sliding off due to rapid head movements.

I was excited to try these immediately after unboxing them, so I skipped charging the battery (for use with Bluetooth) and went straight to plugging in the included cable. These work fine as wired headphones.

Overall, these are great sounding headphones, that can be wired or wireless, depending on your choice or patience (or lack thereof).

title: BETTER THAN APPLE (no, really :-)
text:
Yes! They are just like iPhone earbuds--but better!

I hate hate HATE the new earbuds, with the rubber condoms that go in your ear. They never fit and they make me feel violated. I missed these and was debating on buying *yet another* set of iPhone earbuds. I am so glad I found these. They are white (just like Apple) and they look, feel, fit, and sound EXACTLY like Apple. But these have a tiny bit more printing on them. Other than that they are virtually identical. They are a bit gummier (2% gummy, not squishy or gooey). They are not "hard plastic" but more "firm plastic." The sound is incredible, possibly even better than the Apple ones I am always paying too much for.

BY THE WAY: There are no volume controls on the cord. Some earbuds come with those. Just so you know this is not what you are getting. They fit your iPod/iPhone, and even my Samsung Galaxy S3 just fine. There is a term for that kind of jack but I don't know (or care) what it is. All I care about is that they work and they are durable. Given that they are built almost identically to Apple's earbuds I am assuming that they will last as long (which is never long enough). Bottom line: for the price these are a steal.

title: I Really Like These!
text:
I'm a professionally trained classical musician. I've been using very high reference end cans for quite a while. I like the separation of sound that I get from a non-forgiving set of earphones...that always tends to make me disappointed in earbuds and I have had a hard time listening to music with any prior to now. Crazy as it sounds, it's just not enjoyable. When I got the chance to review Trelabs XR100 I was mainly hoping for a reasonable set of wireless ear buds for phone calls. I did not expect to actually enjoy listening to them. Was I ever wrong--I like these.
A couple of notable things. They are comfortable for me--that says a lot as most earbuds tend to make my ears hurt after half an hour or so. The other thing that really surprises me is that I have been listening to music at work for 5 days straight now. Next to me sits a pair of Sennheiser pro 380s. I'm listening through the Treblab XR100s. Why? They are gentle and forgiving (but not too much!) on the sound, and most importantly they have enough separation to make the sound enjoyable but not so much that the ears get tired (yes, that's a real thing as any audio engineer can tell you).
So the complaints? The first few seconds of connection while my phone are negotiating a good connection the audio has lots of connection pops...that's Bluetooth...once the handshake is complete the connection stabilizes and the pops disappeared for me. If I walk out of range which for me seems to be about 60 feet and a wall the connection gets dicey...that is completely reasonable to me.
Today I finally made a call using them. Sound was far superior to the wired earbuds that came with the phone. My client heard me with no complaints--and I did not have to hold the mic in front of my mouth (not even an option as the mic is integrated and hidden) like I often have to do with wired buds. There was not a lot of wind so I don't know how that will affect the sound but every mic I have ever used, bar none, has had to deal with wind.
Are they as good as my reference headphones that I use for critical listening? That's the wrong question to ask. The right question is do they provide a realistic soundscape without overly coloring the sound while still being forgiving enough to the music to make general listening enjoyable...hands down, yes! I have to say that I am pleased. I'm listening to some of my favorite recordings and find them very enjoyable with these earbuds.
Battery life is good. I've had to charge them three times in just over five days. Personally I would rather have them just die rather than warn me that the battery is getting low when I am just listening to music, but if I were in a call I would rather be warned...I think they made the right choice there.
The lowdown: comfortable good sounding earbuds. Nice sound separation without being overly harsh. The sound isolation is good (it's passive 'cancellation' which is an engineering principle that goes a bit beyond merely earplugs that have speakers in the middle--I see that as a good thing. I have never heard a headset with active cancellation that I liked (sorry bose). Full disclosure:I was given a discount on these to review them...but if this pair ever dies, at the $70 these seem to be going for, I would buy another pair whether I get a discount or not. After trying these, I simply don't want to go back to what I was using before.

title: Good value, good sound, good battery life
text: We have several sets of Tozo ear buds in our household. We use them for listening to podcasts and audio books, primarily, and they are great for that purpose.  They come with several sets of inserts, so will fit just about anyone. We tend to use just one ear bud at a time, keeping the other in the carrying case that is also the charger - so battery life is not an issue for us.  If you use both, you can expect to get 6 or 7 hours out of a full charge.  I am rating them high for sound quality and noise cancellation but that is a relative rating.  They do not deliver the same quality of audio or noise cancellation as my over-the-ear head phones, but that is to be expected.  The range is about 60 - 70 feet, through walls.  That's can be an issue when I am out and about in the garden and my phone is on a charger.  Also, they don't work well - for me - with hands free phone calls - listeners often complain of distortion on their end and I usually end up switching to speaker phone.  All that said, these are the go-to ear buds for our household.  We find them very well suited to spoken voice content.  If were music lovers, we'd probably spend more to get more.

title: Truly incredible sound, and comfortable too.
text:
After getting irritated with those dang ear buds, I bought my first set of over-the-ear cans in ages – inexpensive ones. The instant I put them on & cranked up some great rock, I was transported back to the days of paying a fortune for a really good stereo – the kind that sounds better when you turn it up. The kind you shell out 5k or so for.

The inexpensive cans were far superior to the wretched buds, but I kept remembering that really superior sound. Figured out that a $300 pair of great cans might replace that outrageous stereo, and was I ever right. I’m no audiophile, so I researched for weeks – V Moda BT won, so I ordered them.

I hear faint bells, children laughing in the distance, just an amazing range of sounds within music, movies & TV shows that I haven’t heard in ages. Better yet, the more I increase the volume, the better these suckers sound! Crystal clear. No raspy blended-together music.

No dang wires either! And, for the capper, I’m blind as a bat & wear thick glasses. These V Moda cans come tighter than ticks, but you simply bend the steel part out – and with the lovely padding on top of the head and on the ear jobs, I literally fall asleep in them AND my glasses most nights.

They sound far better than most stereos, are incredibly comfortable and you’d have to steal them off me dead body to get them away from me! They are gorgeous with it – if you’re in the market for a comparably expensive set of cans, V Moda allows returns so you have nothing to lose trying them.

And a lot to gain - AND nobody gave me nuthin to write this.

title: Worth the wait but don't expect miraculous sound.
text:
A big thing to consider about whether or not to get these ear buds is the shipping. This set is imported from China and with free shipping it took a couple of weeks to get to TX. If you're willing to wait for it you'll be getting a very good sounding set of sub $20 earbuds.
The build quality of these buds does not feel overly cheap nor premium but above average.
Interestingly there's a small metal bead a few inches below each earbud which are supposed to be weights that pull the cable down to straighten it when wearing.
The cables have a strange gummy quality that sort of work out as it sort of feels like silicone. The cables are not stiff but springy in a way that there is less sound when the cord is touched while wearing them.
The storage box these earbuds came in did not impress me much. It was kind of cheap and awkwardly designed.
I really appreciate the memory foam ear tips as they make a better and more comfortable feel than the silicone ones. I have enough space in my ears to wear these comfortably and the memory foam helped out the noise cancellation very much, it's actually doing a good job blocking out noise for me at least.
The body of the earbuds are very unusual. I was wearing them wrong the first couple of times and they are difficult to tell when they are in properly. You have to look for the "L" and "R" markers on each earbud and kind of fit them in your outer ear.
For the sound.. I'll have to disclose that I am not an audiophile so I'll describe it as well as I can.
The sound is easily the best part of these earbuds and the reason to get them.
The bass is strong and full compared to my other sub $20 earbuds. The sound is a bit more dynamic and more pleasing than my other set that has good bass so you get the bass with less muffled sounding vocals.
These bud's have a limit though. A decent pair of large over the ear headphones sound a lot better of course but these earbuds are probably one of the best you can get at this price range.
In my opinion these earbuds are worth the wait but at its price range don't expect miraculous sound.

I bought these earphones at a discount for review purposes thanks for reading.

title: 95 and was very happy with them
text:
hippox vs Iblast audio vs TREBLAB XR100

I originally purchased the TREBLAB XR100 to use because POWERBEATS were not staying charged long enough. I didn’t want to spend another $140.00 so I bought the TREBLAB XR100 for $39.95 and was very happy with them. I then saw the Iblast audio and it seemed to be a step up from the TREBLAB XR100 then I received a LIGHTNING DEAL on the hippox for $25 off, so I bought that one also. So by the time I was done I spent the $140 any way, my bad. I might as well help everyone else out and tell you what I found out.
SIZE AND WEIGHT:
Hippox, Iblast audio and the TREBLAB XR100 all weigh 20 grams or 0.7055 oz. All three are very similar in size and shape the only difference is the face plate on the hippox and the iblast audio have a raised center seam on the face plate and TREBLAB XR100 is flat. The on/off/Home button switch is differently shaped on the hippox and Iblast audio it is tear dropped and round on the TREBLAB XR100.
All three have the same length cord which is approx. 21 ¾ in.
SOUND QUALITY:
I am very impressed with the sound quality of all three of these wireless headsets. I could not notice any difference in the sound quality between any of the three and my PowerBeats. They all produce great bass. The quality on voice calls is exceptional on all three. Clarity of voice on the other end was clear.
WIND NOISE:
I WILL UPDATE WHEN I HAVE HAD A CHANCE TO THOROUGHLY TEST IT UNDER WINDY CONDITIONS.

CASE/CHARGING CORD:
Hippox, Iblast audio and the TREBLAB XR100 all come with a carrying case, which are all very similar to one another. The difference is the TREBLAB XR100 was two-tone color (red zipper black case) as where the iblast audio and the TREBLAB XR100 are all black. All have a mesh holder on the inside of the case which is convenient. These are solid cases and a very nice bonus with the purchase of the headphones. All 3 came with a 12 inch charging cables and 3 different size Earbuds. The TREBLAB XR100 had 6 different Earbuds (3 different sizes and 2 different styles).
PAIRING/BLUETOOTH:
All come with an easy and straight forward pairing process. I have a Nexus 6P phone they all paired the first time in seconds, absolutely no problems.
All demonstrated the same or very similar range on the Bluetooth. They all had an approximately 20 foot (line of sight) range before starting to breaking up. They all lost signal completely at 32 to 35 feet away (line of sight). Going around a corner lost signal quicker, reduced to approximately 10 feet away. But quite honestly how often are you going to leave your device 20 feet away?
I verified that all three were able to connect to at least two devices at the same time. I connected to two different Nexus 6P’s at the same time. Notably, I was able to answer one phone, while listening to music from the other. The music stopped and when I finished the call the music resumed automatically. This was something I wasn’t ever able to accomplish with my PowerBeats.

CHARGE TIME:
WILL UPDATE IN A WEEK OR SO WHEN I HAVE HAD TIME TO TEST CHARGING AND PLAY TIME.
TREBLAB XR100 first charge gave me about approx. 8 hours of music play at mostly high volume. I will continue to test the other two.

PRICE:
hippox $49.99 (I purchased the Hippox on Lightning Deal which was $25 off, my cost was $24.99) vs Iblast audio $49.01 vs TREBLAB XR100 at $39.95, compared to PowerBeats at $140.

WORKOUTS:
I WILL UPDATE THIS POST WHEN I HAVE HAD A CHANCE TO THOROUGHLY TEST IT UNDER A LONG RUN.
I have not had a chance to test for running. At this point, I am a little afraid that the ear loop is not strong enough to keep the earbuds firmly in my ear on a long run.

WATERPROOF/WATER RESISTANT:
Hippox and the iblast audio both claim to be water proof, but the TREBLAB XR100 is only water resistant.

Hippox, Iblast audio, TREBLAB XR100 PROS:
Light Weight
Very Good Sound
Very Good Sound Canceling
Easy to Pair
Pairs to Multiple Devices at the Same Time
Nice Case
Price, Price, Price, Price VS PowerBeats

CONs:
Over the Ear Strap seems to be way too flimsy.

BOTTOM LINE:
First, I have not been paid for nor was I given any discounted price for this review. I did however get the hippox on Lightning Deal which was $25 off. I would not have bought this one for the original price of $49.99 that it sales for, only because I had already bought two others.
It is my opinion that these all are made at the same place and are exactly the same unit just with different names put on them. The difference in the design of the face plate is probably due to older model verses newer model.
With that said, all of these units are very much worth the money. The hippox had the nicest packaging and presentation however there was no mention of a warranty in any of the enclosed information (Buyer Beware). The TREBLAB XR100 was the best priced and came with 6 different earbuds, (most likely last year’s model) a 1 year warranty. The iblast audio had a 90 day replacement and 1 year warranty most concise instructions.
I hope this helps you make your decision. If you think that my review was helpful, please press the YES button below.

I purchased this bluetooth headset after seeing it for sale during the Prime Day 2020 earlier this month. I had been needing one after my old Motorola headset had started dying and was totally unreliable. I had been a Motorola fan for years for headsets, and had definitely paid a high price for those.

When I seen this headset I thought I would take a risk. The price wasn't that expensive and decided that if the sound quality wasn't that good or if it didn't last as long, then I wouldn't be out any major money. When I received the headset, it came in a plastic case that does have a cheaper plastic feel to it. But inside the case contained the headset and several rubber ear pieces to allow for a better fit in the ear.

Once I swapped out the ear pieces to the one for the best fit, I then charged it up for a few hours and finally linked it to my Galaxy Note 8 phone. I immediately started using it for my work-from-home day talking with several staff members and customers. Amazingly, the sound was well beyond average. In fact, the sound was on part with my older Motorola Bluetooth headset. I haven't fully tested the battery as of yet, but it has went part of several business days without being recharged.

Because I work from home and there isn't much background noise, I can't tell how well the noise cancelling feature works, but as soon as I can test all of these various features, i will gladly report back. Overall, I am highly impressed with this headset for the cost, features, and quality of it. I recommend it for anyone wanting to save a little and still have the same quality.

title: Love the TREBLAB XR100 Bluetooth Earbuds
text:
I have had several pairs of Bluetooth earbuds, but never a pair like this! I am in love with my TREBLAB XR100 Bluetooth earbuds. First let’s talk about ALL the different size earbuds they send to you. Normally you get a standard size, small and a larger size. But these come with a rubber set in the 3 sizes as well as a foam set in 3 sizes. So no matter your ear canal opening, there will be a set that works for you. Secondly, I really like the case that they came with. The case feels very sturdy and well-constructed. It doesn’t feel like it will fall apart at all. I also like that it isn’t too big, so I’m able to keep the case in my pocket when I’m out walking or on my bike. I like having the case so I don’t lose my earbuds. Also keeping them in the case prevents dirt from getting in them. Thirdly I really love the sound quality. Normally everything sounds kind of off and far away, but the TREBLAB XR100 earbuds have amazing sound quality. Everything sounded close and clean. There was no static or distortion at all. Also never once did the Bluetooth connection drop. That was a major problem with a few of the other earbuds I had before these. I am a huge fan of having wireless earbuds as well. What I also liked about these is that they came with this little plastic attachment that you could put on the cord to keep the earbuds closer to your head. Sometimes I walk with only 1 earbud in and having the other hang down pulls the other earbud out of my ear. With the plastic attachment, I no longer have that problem. Also having the hooks that wrap over your ear was a bonus for me. I have a Samsung Galaxy S6 and they connected without any problems and never once dropped the connection. These really are worth the money!!
I did receive this product at discounted/free price for my review. The views and opinions are entirely mine and based on my own experience. If my review was helpful to you, please click on the YES button. This will make it easier for others to find the review so that they may be helped as well.

The bass is quite good after customizing Media Player enhancement settings but I would not complain one bit if Jabra really bassed out the next version of the Halo. Of course, like most headphones, the bass is deeper/better if you push the ear pieces against your head but with the Halo the difference is not very significant, which tells me that this headset fits my head very well. I should mention that even at lower volumes the people around you will be able to hear whatever you're listening to, so this is probably not the best headphone to be using in public unless you are content will turning the volume down really low. Not a problem for me though, the Halo should be perfect for my needs. Super comfortable, can even wear glasses with it, the touch volume controls work fine for me, it looks stylish, I love it! (this means alot, I don't like anything and I return most things I buy). The Halo is a pleasant surprise. It helps that I stole a brand new/full retail packaged Halo off ebay for about 40 bucks shipped but I would have gladly paid amazon prices. Let me see a black friday deal on a bulk packaged Halo, I'm in for two, that's how impressed I am.

ps the hinge thing is sort of stupid on Jabra's part. Let's not make the same design mistake next time please, it's just so pointless and makes a very solid headset have a completely unnecessary weak link. I take really good care of my possessions so no biggy for me but it's probably just a matter of time for the heavy handed.

title: A refined M-100 with wireless capabilities? Oh yes!
text:
V-Moda is a brand that has always been very fashion forward. It was until the M80 and M100 in which they were able take traction and gain popularity by merging their designs with respectable acoustics that was generally pleasing to a wide range of people. Now, they have finally taken what made them popular and removed the wires. This is the new Crossfade Wireless.

The box is a bit taller than the M100’s version because there is no longer the click fold hinge that allowed the headphone to collapse in upon self, rendering the new Crossfade wireless not as portable. This may be a deal breaker to some, but the included case is still of quality and attempts to minimize its footprint by molding its shape to the headphone. Included in the box is a spare set of shields usually this will be the custom set you’ve created. You have your quick guide and warranty information especially informing you about V-Moda’s kick ass immortal life program. Inside the specially molded clamshell zipper case you’ll find the micro USB cable to charge your headphones and the 1 button with an in-line microphone cable allowing you to use the Crossfade wireless in passive mode in the event the battery dies or you simply yearn for the best possibly sound quality. And at last you have the clip to mount the case on a bag or your belt.

The Crossfade Wireless retains the same incredibly rugged and sexy design as the M-100 and LP series. What’s even more amazing is that it keeps the same size even despite now housing internal electronics to allow wireless connectivity. I have the XL pads installed and these offer improved cushion depth, a bigger soundstage and a smoother sound as well a wider ear diameter for superior comfort over the stock pads. A much recommended upgrade. The headband offers substantial padding to avoid hot points at the top of the head and remains aesthetically pleasing by not being overly bulky and/or not aligning to the curvature of your head. In summary, these are gorgeous, well-built headphones that can easily withstand everyday wear and tear and if you do break them, the immortal life program is an option.
The location of the wireless controls are fairly intuitive. On the top left we have the volume down button. On the top middle, we have the multi button, play, pause, answer and reject calls as well as activating your voice assistant and on the top right we have the volume up button. Moving down we have a single rocker that when pushed to the middle turns on the headphone and pairs it to the last known device and when pushed and held to the far right for 2-3 seconds puts it in pairing mode. The Crossfade wireless can be connected to 2 devices at once, for example a smart watch and a smart phone or a smart phone and a tablet.

The M-100 was at a time my favorite headphone, but it was until I ventured off into what other high quality portable offerings were available that made me see its flaws. The M-100 is undeniably a pleasing and fun sounding headphone with stunning bass performance, but its resolution and coherency leaved some to be desired. The Crossfade Wireless is a welcoming improvement. By taking the famous M-100 sound and fine tuning the frequency response balance to be more linear as well as brining out more resolving power to allow the subtle textures and harmonic low level details to surface has resulted in being my favorite Bluetooth headphone, period and possibly being my overall “favorite” sounding headphone surpassing the Master & Dynamic MH40. Yes, these are that DAMN good. When in Bluetooth operation, the following said about the sound quality of the Crossfade Wireless is still mostly the same, but it just doesn’t have the same level of detail and overall focus as when it is wired and plugged into a fine setup. Other than that, these are the best sounding Bluetooth headphones I have heard and owned surpassing the Parrot Zik 2, Sennheiser Momentum Wireless, Sony XB950BT, Bang & Olufsen H8, Definitive Technology Symphony 1, Beats Studio Wireless, Beats Solo2 Wireless, Samsung Level Over and Bowers & Wilkins P5 Wireless. The sound of Crossfade wireless is still immediately on the fun sounding side of the spectrum, but still very refined and coherent. No part of the frequency range is absent.

The bass extends endlessly and punches you with no mercy when the song calls for it. This is one of the most downright seductive bass presentations that I have ever heard and it manages to integrate into the midrange quite stupendously well without destroying that whole octave. The midrange is still a bit relaxed, but it’s more neutral sounding than the M100 and sounds clean and proportionally well represented. Vocals sound rich and full even whilst the bass is turning the skin on your face into water waves. The treble seems a bit more present and extended over the M100, but most importantly, it’s a cleaner and more natural sounding treble which really helps clean up the initial transients thus improving imaging and granting the Crossfade Wireless a very, very good soundstage for a closed back and among my best performers in that region.

Now, these aren’t my best sounding portables, but they are not far from it whilst retaining a character that grants them undeniable enjoy ability. I love to be able hear every single thing in the recording, but I more importantly enjoy feeling the emotion in the recording more and this is where the Crossfade Wireless excels.

title: Hands down, the MOST bass you can get out of headphones.
text: I've owned and used several pair of headphones over 25 years and use each pair for different reasons. For super clear hi fidelity listening, I whip out my Bose Quiet Comforts or V-Moda Crossfade headphones. When wanting to travel light or do activities outdoors, I'll use my Beats Powersports or Rockford Fosgate Punch Plugs. (by the way, if I keep a pair of headphones for longer than a few weeks, they are good headphones. otherwise I sell or return them) I bought the Skullcandy Crusher's after demo'ing them in Best Buy. I immediately had to have them after feeling the bass response. I used to have a pair of cheap headphones that had this effect, but they eventually broke and I found out no headphone manufacturer was doing this "trick" any more. Having a driver vibrate the headphones in time to bass frequencies fools your brain into thinking it is hearing massive bass. In car audio competitions, they used to sell vibration "amps" that mount under each seat to fool people into feeling/hearing the bass much harder than the speakers are actually playing. The same thing is happening inside these Crusher headphones. The main reason people keep buying higher and higher end headphones these days is to upgrade the bass response. It is very tough to get massive bass from smaller speakers. Skullcandy has figured out a way to "cheat" and the results are incredible. I'm surprised more companies aren't doing this same trick. I never thought I would say that headphones can have too much bass, but these can hit a ridiculous levels. It isn't ever uncomfortable or too distorted, but you can make these headphones have an over-powering bass response to where songs sound almost comical. These were made for dub-step. Most users I know will play with the novelty of turning the bass slider to max when they first get them, but eventually you will want to hear all of the song and not just the bass end by keeping the slider at 1/2 to 3/4 settings. The mids and highs are very acceptable too. No distortion unless you are blowing up the bass slider to max. The sound you get out of these headphones is worth FAR more than $99. I can't imagine the amount of bass these will have once the speakers reach their prime "break-in" period. To keep this review simple... if you want the most bass you can get from headphones and don't want to spend $500+ to do it, buy these now. The only reason I didn't give this product a 5 star rating was that after an hour or so of listening, it felt like it was crushing my head. They seem a little tight, but that might get better over time. If you have a small/medium head, they might be fine for you. One of the other great features of these headphones are the auto-on/off circuit for the bass driver. Stopping your music or unplugging the cord will turn off the battery powered amplifier circuit. This insures you get the max battery life. I never liked headphones that had a manual on/off switch because you'd always forget. Also, considering what is packed into these headphones, they are rather light. They don't dent your hair like other heavier headphones. If you have a specific question on these, message me. I'd be glad to answer back.

text:

I like the comfort, as my head usually stretches headphones to their extent so they are not always comfortable or headphones of good quality can be heavy after a while. These fit well and are lightweight and comfortable, even though they seem cheaply made with plastic and minimal padding on the ears, but they work well as long as they hold up.

I also like the auto adjusting ambient noise or noise cancellation that senses outside noise and adjusts for it. You can switch between these by touching a button on the headphones. I don't think the noise cancellation is as robust as you might want on some noisy airplanes. It does create a subtle white noise to drown out other noises and reduces noise, too.

I think the sound quality for music is acceptable for average users like me. I have no problem with that and am pleased with it. I can see wearing these for music at my desk and using it for travel.

title: A quality experience from arrival to the day that they will eventually be taken off my head.
text:
This is my first foray into the world of V-Moda and from the first moment I took them out of the box my inner voice said, "What took you so long" referencing my reluctance to take the plunge to try them.

My first impression was how light they are. One would expect these things to weigh a ton (which I think was my original resistance) but they are actually light and feel very balanced. They, in a word are awe-inspiring just to look at in the package. V-Moda seems to pride themselves on the presentation and getting the message across that "We don't just look good, we act good" which is regards to their warranty and service dialogues.

My nephew (a gamer) made almost identical noises as he did when he saw the most recent Star Wars trailer when he saw the empty V-Moda box on the table. A reaction that also let me know that the V-Moda marketing works! But let's take a listen.

The headset is comfortable with a soft by firm squeeze to my head. Pairing was a cinch (iPhone6) and sound was pretty remarkable just listening to mp3's on my phone. It did take me a while to figure out that there is no identifiable microphone (because it's built in) and everyone seemed to hear me fine (nephew interrupted this review to tell me that he would get the sides customized at the V-Moda site but I'll explain that in a minute. The other part of his intrusion was to say HE would purchase the optional external mic that sits in front of your mouth. He said it is more comfortable for him to know where his voice is being sent??). I mention this only to make you aware there are accessories!

The thing the impresses me almost as much as the sound is the comfort of these after wearing them the entire time of writhing this review which is after nearly an hour of TV and Music. I am impressed that it will sync with two devices over bluetooth, like a phone or a laptop (meaning you don't have to unlink one to link to the other).

Sound quality didn't change from wired to wireless (which shocks me) but there was a noticeable drain on battery (nothing you wouldn't expect) so it's good to know that they can be wired without loosing your connection. The sides can be customized very easily through their website, and V-Moda doesn't spare the sense of excitement in that process either. You can make your ear coverings the color of your favorite light saber and have your favorite Empire engraved onto it for around $50 dollars.

The V-Moda, for me, sets high standards that they stand behind with a sense of fearless pride. From their "50% off Immortal Program" to their use of "vegan leather" and cross-fade technology their message is clear - if there was a top, we are over it!

This is a fully immersed company creating a product that allows you to do the same. Now, to figure a safe place to hide them from a certain nephew's longing eye.

title: Wish I could Recommend but I can't
text:
First, I want to note that I purchased these directly from V-moda.

To start, the sound quality and customizability for these is great. I love being able to switch between wired/wireless. The 30min quick charge is also very nice when you run out of juice.

However, there are some striking flaws with these.

1)Simultaneous Device Pairing: One of the main reasons I went with these over other quality headphones, does not work most of the time. I contacted them twice about this issue with no viable help. Jumping from phone to laptop works perfectly, but when going from laptop to phone there is no sound. I've tested multiple times and it takes over 5min for the sound to start working. This obviously isn't simultaneous device pairing. Its faster to completely disconnect from bluetooth and reconnect.

2)Volume Control: While the sound is amazing, the volume control is absolutely atrocious. The lowest you can get the sound is to a medium level. To listen to anything on my phone I have to have the sound to the lowest setting and it is still too loud, even painful at times.

3)Online Documentation: There is none (an old, outdated manual doesn't count in my book)....If I could do more research to find fixes for these issues I would. I've tried. They lack any kind of support or forum presence to help users combat simple issues.

I would love to recommend these headphones based on the sound quality and customizability. Those features are great, but there are just too many disappointments with such a high price tag.

title: **BEWARE: These need more care and maintenance than you think**
text:
I bought these headphones because I needed a "decent" pair of all-purpose noise cancelling headphones. I use them for work, travel and light-medium workouts (walk/jog/weight training). So far they have performed well under those conditions. BEWARE, these headphones require more care than expected (See details below***).

Pros:
Sound quality: These probably won't satisfy the most critical audiophiles but for those of you who are looking for a decent pair of noise cancelling headphones, Look elsewhere.

Build quality: The padding along the top of your head is good and the ear pads are actually quite comfortable. However the inner ear leaves a lot to be desired. There is no padding at all. I bought some $60 headphones to replace these and those came with more inner ear comfort. They need some memory foam or something.

Cons:

App support: Currently there exists no app support for these headphones and Sony does not provide any indication that this is the case. If you are looking to control the intensity of noise cancelling like you can with other flagship models, seek fortune elsewhere. These are not as customizable as the multiple models offered at the $350 price point.

***Water resistance*** ***Crackling and roaring wind noise***
This product is NOT water or sweat resistant. The first couple days I had these headphones, I was very happy with the performance. Then, seemingly out of nowhere, there was a crackling noise that built to a crescendo to a point where they were unsuitable as headphones and more appropriate as torture devices.

That said, I searched reddit and other online forums to try and find a fix for these headphones. There are MANY who have reported the same unbearable crackling noise but there was no consistent fix.

I decided to discontinue use of the headphones for a couple of days then, on a whim, tried them again. To my surprise, the noise was gone. My hypothesis was the moisture build up between my ears and the headphones and caused condensation that filled the cavity where the noise-cancelling microphones are. To confirm this, I removed the ear pads and noticed small water droplets beading up on the inside surface of the pads and after sweating while walking or jogging.

After each workout I take the pads off, wipe and disinfect the headphones and turn them flat to dry so the moisture does not pool inside the headphones. Regardless of whether you are using these headphones to workout or just in a hot office, know that moisture will ruin them and eventually cause a crackling noise. Sony has no fix for this. It has been a problem for years with their headphones.

STEER CLEAR

I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND THESE HEADPHONES

title: Third time's a charm
text:
edit 1/26/16: I couldn't resist the feeling like I gave up on them too soon so I ordered directly from v-moda a white crossfade wireless. I'm going through a second trial. Really loving them so far. Comparing them to my m100 the bass is definitely tighter and in bluetooth mode there's almost more bass. I really prefer the refinements of this sound wired or wireless to the original m100. I still love the m100, but those have gone to my wife and these are mine now. In my original review I mentioned some hiss/sizzle - it turns out these headphones are so clear that they make some recordings' flaws completely apparent. Yes, in low volume there is a bluetooth hiss, but at high volume what I was hearing on many tracks was hiss in the recording. I a/b this back and forth with the m100 and cfw in wired mode and the hiss was there at high volumes. Don't get me wrong, maxed out there might be hiss from the internal amp being pushed, but that's to be expected on any device with its volume maxed. I'm really enjoying them this time around, I have one more headphone to try out but its $550 from master and dynamic - and at that price point it better sound twice as good as these, because if it doesn't i'm sticking with v-moda. I'm leaving my old review up just for comparison's sake. Still leaving it at four stars because theres no 4.5 option. They make my temple and jaw sore after a while in normal use, and almost instantly when lying down. Also, I thougth cliq fold being omitted would be an issue but honestly the carrying case is form fitting and fits in my gym bag just as easily. Its not as short, but its flatter than the m100 case. Plus I found myself not folding my m100 because the earpads would get squished and began to flatten out prematurely. I had to order replacements.

The V-Moda Crossfade wireless is difficult for me to review because ultimately I returned it and kept the m100. The two I received had battle scars from shipping. Both were sealed with the vmoda red ribbon and had the stickers over the earcups so i'm presuming they were brand new. However the first one had scratches on the silver trim between the earcup and earpad. The replacement had a scuff on the earcup and the microphone had shifted in its housing. If you looked inside the pinhole you could see the mic warped to the left. I think there was insufficient packing material in the box and it was bouncing around. Thats not VModas fault. So none of this reflects my rating. Just letting people know to inspect their expensive new toys! Now for the rating.

I loved the wired sound, and really liked the wireless sound. Wired it is very reminiscent of the m100 with slightly tighter bass, and slightly less of it too. Its gives a sense of a more balanced sound than the m100. It is pretty much V-moda sound signature just refined slightly. If you don't A/B them you wouldn't know there's a difference.

Wireless was great unless you turned the volume on the headphone itself up past half, Then there would be this distortion/sizzle/hiss at the top end of the sound regardless of how low the volume was on the music player. Up past half, to me - is where the amp really drove the headphones and made the bass thump, but that's where the sizzle lived. It was hard for me to find a balance between player/headphone volume. The bluetooth was also not dead quiet. I don't listen to music very loudly so I could always hear the signal noise. Its not a "bluetooth" thing in the sense that not every device suffers from this, but I've encountered it before. I have a bluetooth dongle right next to me that doesn't have this line level hiss at all. This was my ultimate reason for not replacing it another time after the second dud. I got my m100 for half the cost of the CFW; I wasn't going to pay double when the main feature was not up to standard. I believe they are almost there. If there's a CFW 2.0 Val will probably address all the signal quality issues with bluetooth. Until then i'm sticking with wired m100.

Minor concerns of mine were the battery life over time (year two and up), sweat/rain damaging the electronics, and falls. The physical build quality is as durable as the m100 but the electronics add more variables that could fail in the event of a minor fall/spill. I know people use bluetooth on the go,so if you're on a train and they fall or it starts to rain, would the destruction be covered under warranty? Too scary for me to take that change.

so why 4 stars? They're excellent headphones wired, if you find the balance in volumes they're very good in wireless mode. I can be objective enough to know that something is good even though its not good for me in particular.

No power indicator, no on chime... nada. Corded up to my phone,iPod they work just fine, but it sucks that the wireless capabilities no longer work which is exactly why I bought the pair.

=================

My only real gripe with these are the push buttons, especially the play/pause, next track (double press) and previous track (triple press). The timing of your button presses has to be very specific. That and it seems inconsistent with my headset. I find myself pausing tracks quite often when trying to advance.

Other than that, I've had these for almost two weeks and have used them daily! The sound quality is great. They definitely have a bit more of a bass signature that I was looking for compared to some others. The highs are pretty well and the mids are decent.

As for comfort? These aren't entirely heavy, but they aren't the lightest headphones either. In all, I've been able to wear these for extended hours without much discomfort. They warm up my ears, but not to the point where it is annoying or unbearable.

Don't forget, these look AWESOME! They're a very sturdy pair of headphones and the leather headband and steel hinges make you feel like you have a quality headset.

For the price, I would have liked some form of Active Noise Cancelling. The Noise Isolation is decent... we'll see how these fair on my next flight but bear in mind I didn't buy these as a comparison to the Bose QC35, for example. I wanted a pair of wireless headphones that sounded great and looked good as well. I listen to a WIDE variety of genres and these balance most of the genres I listen very well. These definitely fit the bill!

title: Not suitable for the purpose, but there's a workaround; moderate noise suppression; too fancy
text:
Review of Sony WHCH710N
Review updated 10-12-2021 after a miserable international flight with this headphone

Noise cancelling headphones should not require you to be listening to music constantly, but this one does. It turns off after 5 minutes if you don't pair it with a Bluetooth device or plug in the cord. If you use it only occasionally, it will almost certainly come to bite you on a 12-hour overseas flight. If you lose your Bluetooth connection or your Bluetooth connection kills your wi-fi connection--which it very well can--then you may be out of luck. I rate this as excessive technology in search of a problem to solve.

But fortunately, there's a workaround. Just plug in the sound cord, and the headphone will stay turned on. I am ordering a 3.5 mm, 3-conductor minipin plug or adapter, which I think will work. I don't see anything about this in the fine-print manual, but if you can somehow figure out the model number and find the online troubleshooting guide, there MAY be an app that you can use to turn this stupid feature off.

Moderate noise suppression, comparable to my Panasonic that was ruined by a battery. This headphone will give some blessed relief, but don't expect all noise to disappear. I just used it on an international flight, and noise reduction seemed not very strong. Noise suppression is not adjustable on this model.

The sound is good but somewhat bright compared to the Panasonic that I prefer.

This has an ambient-sound feature, but it doesn't seem very useful. If you want to hear ambient sound better, it would be far simpler just to take the darned thing off instead of cycling through useless menu options (ambient sound on/off, noise cancelling on/off). All told you have two mostly useless buttons with numerous menu items, plus volume controls. You might find yourself fumbling around for the buttons. A simple on/off switch would work just fine, although some people might find the volume controls handy.

The headphone is comfortable and adjustable. The cups cover the whole ear, and exclude some sound without power. The build quality is fine. It seems sturdy, but like everything else it's made of plastic, and you can probably break it if you try hard enough.

One very bad point from my point of view: The battery is built in, and it requires about 7 hours with a USB charger to recharge, but it's supposed to last about 35 hours. It requires a USB-C cable, which is easily lost because it doesn't come with a case. I manage with a USB phone charger.

The built-in battery may be problematic. If you let it run down, then leave it for weeks or months without a charge, the battery may be damaged. If the battery quits accepting a charge, you might as well throw away the whole headphone.

title: Optimal Compact Charging Unit For Multiple Devices
text:
The vast majority of people today are dependent upon rechargeable devices such as cell phones, tablets, and e-readers. Naturally, along with this comes the mayhem with a multitude of wall plug-in chargers and cables. This can be very unsightly in any kitchen or office, and people can also end up using a charger that was not designed for a specific device. Thus, it follows that a compact multi port charger can help alleviate this problem.
This new Anker five port charger that I received a couple of days ago replaces my four port charger that I generously gave to my grandson. Both units have what Anker calls "PowerIQ Technology" which means that the charger actually identifies the device that is plugged into it and then optimally charges it at full speed safely. It can simultaneously charge at all five ports. While I have no way of objectively measuring charging speed, it is appears that my Samsung Galaxy S5 cell phone charges at the same rate as its supplied charger.
The charger kit includes five cables of varying lengths though they all have the same micro-USB connector. All Anker products that I am familiar with come with a generous 18 month warranty and excellent technical support.

text:
After reading dozens of reviews for over two years, in May 2018, I bought the Sennheiser HD1 headphone. The price then was $224. I was seriously considering the Oppo PM-3, but just about the time I was ready to pull the trigger, Oppo stopped making them. So I've had the HD1 now for a few months, and here are my impressions. Pros: The build quality seems to be good, and it is attractive. It comes with a nice soft bag as well as a very nice semi-hard, zippered travel case. Cons: The ear cups are a bit small for my medium-size ears. The headband is covered in leather, but has almost no padding. It puts pressure on the top of your head and becomes uncomfortable in short order. The cable is removeable, but is very difficult to disconnect. If you're comfortable leaving it connected, that wouldn't be a problem. Oddly, the volume control on the iOS cable is located at the upper end of the cable, only a few inches from the phone. The problem is it is so high you can't see it! You have to operate it by feel only. Bizarre. Lastly, the sound is disappointing. I can't single out any particular flaws--it's just not as good as I hoped it would be. Part of the problem, I'm sure, is that I'm using my iPad to drive it. It would probably sound better with a dedicated digital audio player (DAP) and higher quality audio files.

I didn't have the chance to try the HD1 before I bought it. If I had, I would have discovered some of the cons mentioned above and probably would have kept looking. I would advise anyone considering this headphone to definitely listen to it before you buy.

title: Great Product.  Worth Every Red Cent.
text:
I ordered this product because I was sick and tired of moving my chargers and cables around. I now have one place where I can plug everything in and charge them simultaneously. Everything is always in one spot right where I need it.

I chose the Anker brand because I've had great luck with their 7 port USB 3.0 hub that can be found here:
http://www.amazon.com/Charging-Adapter-Included-VL812-B2-Chipset/dp/B00EYXZI4M/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1417572322&sr=8-1&keywords=anker+usb+hub

and their 2 port DC charger that can be found here:
http://www.amazon.com/Anker%C2%AE-Dual-Port-Charger-PowerIQ-technology/dp/B00DDLYCUW/ref=sr_1_2?ie=UTF8&qid=1417572577&sr=8-2&keywords=anker+usb+car+charger

Anker makes spectacular products that are competitively priced and useful.

I have a Dell Venue 8 Pro and Samsung Galaxy S4 that require 2 amp chargers along with some various consumer electronics that only require 1 amp to charge.

This device can charge at least 3 tablets or 3 cellphones (or a combination of the two) at the same time and still have amperage to spare for something small. I haven't tried 4 because I don't have access to that many power greedy devices yet.

It comes with 5 cables (6 ft, 3 ft, and three 1 ft) that are rated for 2 amps.

6 ft: I use this cable with my cellphone or tablet while I'm using either at my desk.
3 ft: I use this one to charge my tablet while it's propped up on my desk.
1 ft: I use these to charge something that remains stationary or I'm not presently using it.

NOTE: Not all USB cables are created equally. Cheaper cables might not be rated to charge at 2 amps. Using a cable with a lower rating to charge a tablet or newer cellphone will result in LONGER charge times.

The cables that come with this charger have a higher gauge wire for charging allowing you to charge your tablets or newer cellphones at the same rate of speed as a factory charger. If you look at your tablet or phone charger, you will find a UL (Underwriters Laboratories) label. This label will tell you the charger's rating. It will say something like "OUTPUT: 5V 1A" or "OUTPUT 5V 2A" or something similar.

The 120V AC cord is roughly 5 ft in length and can reach from the back of my desk to the power outlet on the wall behind it. There is still enough slack if I need to pull the charger toward the front of the desk.

If you order this product, you will not be disappointed.

title: Took them right back for a refund
text:
Let me start be stating that the audio quality was acceptable, both for calls and music, but overall, the design is seriously lacking in the following respects:

1. The power switch is integrated into the headband hinge -a snap open, fold-and-slide affair that feels rather insubstantial and twice collapsed (inadvertently shutting down the radio) while in the process of taking the unit off my head.

2. Beyond the power switch functionality, the folding configuration provides no significant space savings. It's not as though collapsing these headphones will make them any less bulky in a laptop bag or purse.

3. The earpieces do not pivot or swivel at all -basically, if your head isn't a perfect fit (and mine isn't), they don't sit right on your ears and constanly slide off.

4. The software-based, touch sensitive volume control is a profoundly unreliable, counterintuitive gimmick. A hardware dial or rocker switch would have been much better.

5. The headband and earpieces are lined with some kind of synthetic velour that traps lint and fuzz admirably, but doesn't add to the comfort. And finally,

6. You can't control the tracks on an iPod Touch or iPhone 3G/3Gs with it. I know that's not Jabra's fault -that is a problem with Apple's current version of A2DP, so I don't consider it a knock on this product per se. I just mention it for the benefit of anyone planning to use these with one of those devices.

If you're really in love with the aesthetics of this unit, consider the Jaybird Sportsband. They're $10 cheaper, and they have basically the same features, but the earpieces adjust to the shape of your cabeza and you get real, tactile controls.
