title: You get what you pay for (I didn't pay full price)
text:
I bought these Headphones during the Black Friday 2022 50% off sale (~ $72). What attracted me to these headphones was the promise of noise cancellation, and the price. However, upon receiving them in the mail and putting them through some use, I feel that they are not worth the original price of $140 and wish to share my thoughts.

The noise cancelling feature is flawed. To have good noise cancelling you need to have pads which inherently cancel out noise (passive cancelling) and a good seal so that outside noise doesn't make its way into the cups where your ears are. These headphones do neither. The cups are shallow with very little clasping force. This causes my ears to touch the cloth separator between the cloth and speaker (Not comfortable). Because the cups are shallow, glasses of any real thickness will break the seal and there goes the noise cancellation. Without glasses, the noise cancellation is more effective, but not great because of the lack of passive cancellation. I live in a room next to the washing and drying machines and the headphones fail to block-out the the sounds coming from them (They are in a different room). Overall, the promise of noise cancellation for uninterrupted listening experience will not be found here.

Sound quality is next on the chopping block. These headphones do offer a good dynamic range. However, the overall sound quality is flat and without vibrancy. I am not an audiophile in any way so all I can do is compare the sound to my old V-Moda headphones from 2017.

Overall, as disappointed in the quality as I am. These headphones are worth $70. However, there are better options out the for sound quality, and the noise cancellation does not make up for listening experience. Cheap feeling and sounding, but hey, I got them for cheap.

title: Does the trick and more
text:
I bought these because I was taking my wife and daughter on a long trip from Honolulu to Washington D.C. and wanted to add as much comfort as I could to the flights. Actually, I first bought a pair of sale-priced Maxell NC-II headphones to see what the noise-cancellation was like and whether it was worth it. Yep, it did seem like it would make a difference. There were three of us, so I needed two more. Researching the different models available, I became very curious how much better the more expensive models were, so what I did was buy another sale-priced Maxell, and then succumbed to my curiosity for the third. I figured it might be nice to have a better headphone for home use too. My research pointed at three price levels for noise-canceling headphones, with the Bose at the top, a variety around the $100 price range, and the lower price range with the Maxell and a Sony I found in the stores. The Sony was definitely out of the question because they were not the cup design that covered the complete ear. I wanted to spend money on the lower range of the mid-priced models, and I narrowed it down to either these Jabra C820S or the Logitech Noise Canceling model. The Logitech were cheaper than the Jabra by an amount significant enough that I was close to buying them instead. Reviewers seemed mostly pleased with the Logitech's sound quality. The raves were about equal to the Jabra on that issue. There was one factor that made me go for the more expensive Jabra. Many of the reviewers for the Logitech model complained that the Logitech model could easily break at the swivel joint, and some complained that they even arrived in the package already broken, so why risk that, I thought.

I'm very happy with the Jabras. They do the trick quite nicely. The noise cancellation is noticeably better than the Maxells. I let my daughter use the Jabras on the plane and she fell asleep with them easily. The detachable cord is a significant factor to consider. Fall asleep on the plane, roll over in the wrong way, and you could be putting a strong tug on that cord. Even more so, I used the Jabras while I was on a treadmill at the hotel, and many times my swinging hand came down and knocked the cord right out of its connection to the phones. For what we wanted in the airplane situation, the Maxells worked fine for me and my wife, despite not having detachable cords, but I doubt I'll ever be using them at home. The Jabras have good enough fidelity when the noise canceling feature is on that they also make nice phones for personal stereophonics. With the noise canceling off, the fidelity drops significantly, but you know, so what? If you want to listen to music, you're better off with the outside noises canceled anyway. A true audiophile might complain about a slight hiss from the noise cancellation feature, but it's not noticeable for me.

The case the Jabras come with is nice and sturdy. It's a little nuts in the way it can completely zip apart. I can't think of why they designed it that way. If you zip it completely apart, its a little tedious putting the zipper back together, but if you're conscious of what you're doing, you'll remember not to unzip the whole way. The truth is, though, the Maxells fold up nicer into a smaller ball which I prefer--makes it fast to put them away when you're through with them. The Jabras, though, are definitely a much better headphone. Now I've got one decent set of headphones connected to my computer, and two sets of Maxells in storage waiting to accompany them on our next trip.

Note: At the time I bought these, the Logitechs were everywhere selling cheaper. Right now they're significantly more expensive than the Jabras on Amazon. There are such huge differences in list prices and street prices on these things and prices fluctuate often. Buyer beware.

title: They fit pretty comfortably and don’t make my ears sore like ones ...
text:
Pro: Light weight. They fit pretty comfortably and don’t make my ears sore like ones with harder plastic ear-hooks do. The multiple sizes of ear buds help make sure you get a good fit into the ear.

Pro: Nice build quality. They seem solid and well made, unlike some others I’ve tried that are made from flimsier plastic. I would imagine these can take a bit of abuse before you’d break them. The case they come with is sturdy and I can throw them in my bag confident they won’t get crushed when not in use.

Con: I am not getting anywhere near 9 hours of use on a charge. It’s more like 5 hours. They do charge quickly though, so just make sure you charge them well before you plan to use them for an extended period of time.

Con: As others have mentioned, “Noise Cancellation” is a bit liberally used. There is no active sound dampening system, it is “passive noise cancellation”, which means you have to cram them into your ears like ear-plugs so they block external sound. However, when doing so, you lose most of your treble, and get a nice muffled bass sound, kinda like listening to music with a pillow over your head, while underwater. I have to use the smallest set of buds so that I can get them to fit, yet still allow just enough air to flow to get these to sound good. This allows some outside sound to leak through, but then the sound isn’t muffled. They do sound good when you get that balance just right.
At first I thought I was having the same problem as others, and my phone didn’t have aptX Bluetooth ability, but it does (LG V10). It’s literally just how tight they sit in your ears. Once I got that sorted out I’m satisfied with the sound quality.

Overall I’m happy with the purchase and would recommend it to others, as long as they don’t care about noise cancellation. Honestly though, if you want good noise cancelling headphones, you need over-the-ear cans that cover your ear completely.

title: No Artificial Colors or Flavors
text:
What do I mean by the title? Unlike some other high profile and popular headphones, one with a big B (Bose) and the other with a little b (beats), the M50x's are natural. No modifications for extra bass or treble. That only robs you of hearing things you should be by drowning them out from boosting other things. These give you the pure, unaltered sound as the artist intended. That means a lot to me because as a home theater enthusiast, I want to see and hear things as they were meant to be. I want accuracy in my audio and video devices and these deliver the audio in spades. It reminds me of TV displays in stores. The brightness and contrast are cranked up to get your attention but upon closer inspection, it's not at all realistic. Details are lost, people look sunburned, blacks look grey and it doesn't reflect real life. That's what Bose and Beats are to me. Dial back the settings and you get every detail, accurate colors, levels of shadow and an overall realistic picture. That's the AT M50x's.
When searching for my first pair of expensive headphones (I had never spent more than $50) the M50x's consistently came up as the best or one of the best in the under $200 category. $200 was all I was willing to spend. What always caught my attention was the unaltered clarity these provide and so far, I have been very pleased by how well they deliver on that promise. When listening to music, I can clearly focus in on every instrument, every cymbal, every word, chorus and solo. It's a joy to hear my music so clearly and well defined. If other headphones I've used were good, solid standard definition, these are definitely high definition. If you really listen to your music, these headphones are going to help you do that and will make it a much more enjoyable experience. I've used them for movies as well and they really deliver a convincing movie experience. Dialogue is easy to understand, sound effects pack all the right punches, surrounds come through, putting you in the moment and theres nice thumps and booms substituting for subwoofer action. If there's a need to keep the noise down or your going portable, you can have a great movie watching experience with these.
Speaking of portability, this isn't your practical, walking around town or going to the gym set. They're big but perfect for home, long trips or any other stationary listening. Sure, you could take them out but it's a pretty big set to have on when you're on the move. I'll use my on-ear Noontec Zoro HD's (which I highly recommend) for that.
Build quality is excellent. There's plenty of plastic here but this is a very solid feeling set. The leather on the head band and earpads is soft, comfortable and has an expensive look and feel. The earpads completely cover my ears and form a nice seal, keeping the sound in, preventing excess leaking and keeping outside sounds out. I'm not one of those 8 hour a day wearers but for the duration of a movie, I didn't notice any discomfort. Felt or suede earpads can always be purchased and swapped out if need be. They're also very versatile by how many ways they can contort and collapse for storage. I also like the matching and locking removable cord and spare cords packed in the box. Also packed in was a soft leather pouch in a matching chocolate brown to my set. I bought a hard case to use instead but I could see using it for a short trip or days use elsewhere. I went with the limited edition dark green and brown and they really look nice. The green is a dark forest green, almost black in low light and the brown is a darker chocolate brown, with champagne gold accents on the ear cups and hinges. Aesthetically, this is a very good looking and feeling combination. Like they're more expensive than their price point.
I chose the combo from Beach Camera as you get the free case and mini amp for the same price. Shipping was next day and reasonable and packaged well.
Overall, I'm very satisfied with this purchase. I read a lot and watched a lot of videos before making the decision to buy these. It only took a few listens to know that I made the right choice. I know there are other brands of good sounding and well built headphones in the same price range but this combination of high marks by professional and casual reviewers, numerous appearances on top 5 lists, good brand reputation, warranty, build quality, and physical attractiveness made these the set for me. When I give a 5/5 review, it's not for perfection or best available product, it's for a performance and value combination. These meet that combination easily. Highly recommended for music listeners.
Note: I've since added dbrand skins and Brainwavz earpads to mine for that custom look and feel. Definitely recommended for M50x owners.

title: Why the hate for the ATE?
text:
So if you look at the KZ earbuds generally they get great reviews with 4.5 ish stars. Yet the ATE gets 4 stars why? Some complain that it's tinny. Some complain that the fit is not good. Some complain that the build quality is not great. Let me address these one at a time.

The sound is Tinny: The pair I have sounded good to me. I believe most that get a tinny sound are having "fitment" issues. The foam is not the best quality and earbuds require a really good seal to get a "good" sound. For me the fitment is very good, but everyone has slightly different ears. Let me assure you if they can get a good seal the earbuds will produce a good sound.

The fit is not good: Once again this is the quality of the foam. if your canals can't get a good seal then yes the sound quality will suffer and the earbuds maybe loose. you can try the rubber pieces included, but really it is a matter of finding a manufacturer where you can get a "good" seal. The default foam tips fit me fine.

The build quality s not good: I do have to admit i have low hopes for this. The way the cables are hooked into the earbuds mean they go through some strain in normal operation. This is doubly so if you get a really good seal. The wires are NOT replaceable so after they break you will be replacing the whole set.

So why should you buy this? Well they sound great! If you do get a good seal (many many users do) then you will be rewarded. They are a great budget earbud, but keep in mind that they may not last as long as some others.

title: strong build, tight punchy bass (not overwhelming)
text:
These are my favorite headphones. I switched over from Sony's because their headphones are fragile and cheaply made and I was tired of replacing the pairs every year. I wanted a strong set of headphones with detailed sound and good bass. And these are it. I got them for $128 on a different website though I think for $200, they're not overpriced considering the quality.

Comfort:
The headphones' comfort level is mediocre. I have small ears and they experience fatigue rather quickly when wearing these. They're not uncomfortable upon putting them on, though. Many people can live with them. But definitely go for larger ear-pads if you're going to listen to these for hours on end and comfort is very important to you.

Sound:
I don't think there's much to complain about. Clarity and immersiveness is there. Bass is strong and punchy, though not over-whelming or irritating whatsoever. It's not intense head-rocking bass that you may get from some Sony headphones (if you're looking for that). The sound isn't too bright and shrill, and it's not warm either.

Build Quality:
The build quality of these is truly great. It is as bendy as it promises and the headphones don't use cheap-feeling plastic in their design like other headphones do. The cable is braided and should survive many tugs, though since it's obviously detachable you can replace it when you need to. It will, for sure, survive many drops. I do wish the charging cable went in a bit more easily into the port.

Noise Isolation:
With music playing, the headphones block out outside noise well. Wearing the headphones with no music (testing purposes), I could hear the fan in the background. With music on, I could hear the fan lightly. You won't be disturbed by external noise.

Bluetooth:
There is a slight sound difference between wired and unwired. The wired option provided a more fuller sound with tighter bass. It sounds great either way and it wasn't a big issue for me. You cannot use them while charging. Connectivity is easy enough.

Overall, I would recommend these headphones if you want clarity and strong, tight punchy bass without it sounding muffled or too intense. The sound is fun & immersive. Many people will want to replace the thin earpads since they lack cushioning. The build quality is tough as promised so if you drop these a lot or accidentally step on them, they should still function. If you like deep warm sounds & more "thick" sounding bass, Sony's is a good company for that (though they're not good on durability/longevity).

title: Review from someone that is NOT an audiophile. Just a lover of music, games and movies
text:
Let's get this out of the way first - I am *not* an audiophile. I merely know when what I'm hearing sounds good or not. Long story short, these headphones sound GREAT. I'll break down what I use them with and how they performed:

Gaming - I own a PS4 and play a lot of Destiny, among other games. So like many I tried numerous gaming headsets. Sure, most of them are functional, but they're also almost all universally overpriced on top of only sounding average. So imagine my surprise when I plugged my new Crossfade Wireless into my Dualshock 4's headphone jack and it didn't suck. Not only didn't it suck, but it was actually quite great. I can only imagine how much better it would be if I had a mixamp connected to the optical out on the PS4 and plugged my Crossfades into that. Regardless, if you're getting these headphones to use on the controller, just know that it sounds exceptional. For those of you who are like me that need a microphone to talk to teammates, what I bought was the Boompro. It's also made by V-moda, and it's essentially just a wire that runs from your headphones to your controller and it has a great mic on it. The mic on it is better quality than any I used from Astro, Sony or Turtle Beach.

Music - I use these both in bluetooth or wired(whenever possible because wired sounds much better) on my Macbook and on my Android cellphone. My music sounds so good now. No matter how loud you make them, they never ever distort. The bass is very strong, but unlike the Beats Studio Wireless that I also tried before hearing about V-moda, the bass doesn't overpower everything else. I also tried the M50x headphones, and those are supposedly audiophile headphones, but I got so tired listening to music with them. They're so clear and the individual instruments so pronounced that I ended up focusing more on one thing than the entire arrangement. Everything sounds more cohesive on the Crossfade.

Movies - the main reason I went with the Crossfade Wireless over the V-Moda M100s is because I have an Apple TV 4 that doesn't have an optical out port, but it does support Bluetooth audio. I initially bought a pair of Beats Studio Wireless to watch movies/netflix etc wirelessly on the Apple TV but the audio wasn't very good and any time I hit rewind the headphones lost connection. On top of that the Studios were bad at music and gaming, and used battery even when in wired mode (how dumb is that? The Crossfades shut down all the electronics for Bluetooth when a wire is connected). Pairing was quick and easy and I was incredibly happy to hear that the audio quality was nearly as great wireless as it is wired. To test it out I watched Straight Outa Compton and Mad Max. Wow. You hear everything, and the bass is thundering when explosions etc go off.

On a side note, I had issues with the first pair I got. Amazon took them back and sent me another. The second pair appeared to be used and had numerous issues as well. Instead of dealing with Amazon again, I contacted V-Moda directly and they agreed to take a look and help me out. I sent the headphones to them and they then sent me a new pair. Their support team was great to me. Huge shout out to them (Richard and David). While I waited to have my headphones replaced, I went back to using a pair of Sony Wireless Gold. Talk about night and day. When my new Crossfades arrived the other day, I couldn't wait to start using them again and to stop using the Sony. Once you're used to hearing quality audio, nothing else can suffice. I even stopped watching movies until the new pair had arrived.

Other reviews bring it up, so I'll just concur with what they said - if you buy these headphones, but the XL ear pads. I think V-moda should suck it up and just stop putting the thinner ear pads on by default. Just put the XLs on all new headphones and sell the thin ones as an add-on. The thin ones hurt my ears/head tremendously. The XL pads do not. Eat the loss, V-moda, and start putting the XLs on all of them. You'll earn so much goodwill.

title: Bought on sale and still feel like I paid too much
text:
I have an overwhelming amount of complaints for this headset.

I bought for $88 on a prime day deal but even that feels like too much. These feel cheap, they look cheap, the plastic used is cheap. The cushion against the ear is extremely shallow, even for my small ears my ears are pressing right up against the walls of the ear pieces. The cushions are barely cushioned enough to be comfortable.

The noise canceling is nothing exciting. I had a very inexpensive pair of COWIN headphones that I feel like does a better a better job and those are a quarter of the price. I think my expectations were higher because I figured a pair that normally cost 4x more then my existing headphones would have a noticeable difference. It does not, you can tell that the noise canceling is painfully average. Definetly not near $200 noise canceling.

I'm baffled what exactly makes these headphones so costly. It's definitely not the look and feel as you can tell that the plastic feels extremely low quality as nothing about these headphones scream $200. At most these feel like a $30-40 price ranged headphones.

The button are so shallow that it's extremely difficult to feel what button your pressing.

Anytime you switch modes too, the headphones announce very loudly and without pausing what you are listening to on what mode you just set it on. Even though it's very obvious when you turn on ambient sound, i dont need it announced as it causes me to have to rewind what I'm listening to if I'm listening to a book.

These are cheap and awful budget headphones at a non-budget price. I can see why it went on a deep sale so fast after releasing. Spend your $90 if you buy this on sale with a different brand, or splurge on something you know will be high quality by saving up.

I'm going back to my existing headphones that I paid $50 for. Oddly enough, the cheaper headphones that I have feel higher quality and have better noise canceling.

The only thing it does on my Windows PC is invoke Cortana voice command. As a busy teleworker with multiple things going on at once, this can be frustrating; I bought this item specifically because it included a mute button.

In addition, while the earpiece does allow two Bluetooth connections at a time (e.g. one phone and one PC connection), it does not automatically connect to the second device. I have to manually connect from the second device every time. Again, this is frustrating.

Finally, there does not seem to be any way to determine how much charge is left on the battery; I have resorted to plugging it in every chance I get so that I don't have a mid-meeting surprise.

With a few user interface improvements this could be an outstanding earpiece.

text:
I only had this product for about 12 hours and already love it! My opinion might change a little in future from small little issues but my first impression is highly positive.

First of all, it looks gorgeous. It's very shiny and the ear cuffs look nice as well. It looks like it's worth just as much as some higher end headphones. The headphones are also very light and comfortable. Adjusting for the size of your head is also very simple and it doesn't move out of place.

The sound is also very good considering I got this for $40 on sale. I've had listened to beats headphones before and it's quite not up there in terms of sound quality and volume but it's very close. On max volume, I'm highly satisfied with the sound and bass. I can bump to any song with the best experience.

The Bluetooth worked instantly with no connection problems. The product comes with easy instructions on how to connect and I figured it out in 2 minutes. Once it turns on it also connects to your phone instantly.

30 feet of range? Can't get any better. The fact that I can leave my phone charging, walk to the kitchen with my headphones on and comeback is very satisfying to me. The sound quality didn't seem to change to me either. Maybe once you get near to that 30 feet mark, but my house isn't that big for that to be a problem.

These headphones also come with some useful features as well. It has a built in mic that worked perfectly for me when I ordered pizza last night. The employee had no trouble hearing me and I had no trouble hearing him. Communication was perfect. It also has a pause button and a volume up/down buttons. The pause button also serves as the on/off button, as well as the Bluetooth connection button; and the volume buttons also serve as play next, play previous, and replay button.

So overall, you definitely get the "bang for your buck". If you're just trying to get some good quality headphones without burning a hole in your pocket, this is it. Like I said in the beginning, I only had this for less than a day so I'm not sure if it will have battery issues or charging problems but all I can say is that I'm satisfied enough to be giving a review in such little time. I would recommend this product to anyone.

title: Great headphones for the price!  Maybe a bit too much bass, but well worth the money.
text:
This is my first pair of Bluetooth headphones and I'm pleasantly surprised.

I like to keep things simple and to the point in a review. So, first, the good stuff. These are super comfortable to wear. I wear them almost all day at work, and then to the gym in the evenings and I hardly notice them at all. I've always used the "over the ear" style because generic ear buds fall out and annoy me. These stay put for the most part no matter what I'm doing. They have plenty of power to last throughout the day. I typically charge them overnight and they last for the entire work day (constant use for hours) with battery to spare. I can't compare to other Bluetooth headphones yet, but so far (about 2 weeks) they have never powered down as long as I give them a good charge. They come with a nice case, a few pairs of regular replacement ear inserts of different sizes so you can get the fit you want. They also included black expanding buds for blocking out ambient noise, but I have not tried them yet. The construction is good, they have a good feel in the hand, and seem fairly durable. I'll see how they hold up over time.

The only thing I could possibly dock a half a star for would be the bass. I listen to very heavy music with a lot of double bass drums and deep growling vocals, so I typically like a lot of bass. However, these have even too much for my liking. There's so much bass that sometimes it distorts the sound. I compensate by adjusting the volume control on my phone and on the headphones to find a "sweet spot" and that seems to lessen the effect. But, there is a lot of bass pumped out of these, so keep that in mind.

The price is what made me give this 5 stars. At about $23, they're almost disposable after a few months. I've spent more on corded ones and these sound just as good. Plus it's nice not to have to carry my phone around at the gym. If you're looking for something with better sound quality, then maybe these aren't what you're looking for. But for the price I think this is a great set of headphones. I hope they stand up over time.

title: Great little headphones...especially for working out!
text:
I bought these specifically to use while working out and I could not be happier! I am a fan of good sound quality and was worried these "cheap" headphones would not suffice. I own the Bose QC2's, the Shure E4c earbuds, and an older pair of Sony MDR-CD580's so I know what good headphones/earbuds are supposed to sound like. Now obviously these don't sound as good as the Shure E4c's but at 1/10th the price (literally) these sound phenomenal. The Shure's don't sound 10 times as good (diminishing return on investment with them...but on a side note...the Shure's are simply stunning). They need a snug/airtight fit in your ear canal to ensure good sound quality so be patient and try the different ear pieces they come with until you find one you like. Also, they sound better once you start to workout...I think the sweat helps them make a better seal haha.

The cord is a good length...not too short getting pulled out and not w/feet of extra cord laying around. I have a "SanDisk Sansa Clip+ 4 GB MP3 Player (Black)" and these headphones work great with it.

The "earhook" design holds them in place. ALSO, I was worried that the in-ear design of the earbud would amplify noises like a pair of earplugs...like hearing every thud of your footsteps as you walk...our worse yet it you run. But, much to my delight, these headphones work great with running and that is not an issue.

You can't go wrong with these!

****Update 6/28/2011****

I have been using these for a while and I am even happier with them now than I was when I got them. They sound great and STAY ON YOUR EARS...this can be an issue with headphones while you are working out. I have noticed they have a slight "bass-heavy" bias...which typically I am not a fan of but these pull it off/can get away with it. The way you experience the bass effects from in-ear headphones is different than when listening to a big stereo. The bass is in your ear rather than being felt by your whole body like when a dedicated stereo/subwoofer is playing. The slight increase in perceived bass these headphones provide seems to work great - regular old cheap compressed mp3's still sound great.

Also, these have stood up to many workouts thus far...the rubber ear pieces don't absorb sweat like a cloth covering would. Also, no amount of sweat has affected these. I would think the moisture would damage the internals of the speaker but these have not been affected at all. Just make sure the ear piece size you pick (it comes w/several sizes) fit your ear canals fully. All ear-bud style headphones need to fit snugly to sound good.

title: Modern look, very good noise cancellation, good sound
text:
The WHCH710N headphones are one of the better Sony wireless over ear headphones I've used. The noise cancellation is very good and may be the standout feature on these. The fit is good but some users might not like the plastic feel of the headband. It was actually uncomfortable at first but after wearing them for a few hours, I got used to the feel and now I'm a fan of both the headband and ear cups.

Sonically, these are ok. The audio quality is crisp and clear but bass is lacking, partially due to the smallish 30mm drivers. There is bass, and it's more pronounced with ANC off, which is standard on all NC headphones I've used. These aren't designed as a "maximum bass" headphone so it probably won't be an issue for most users. I've listened to a lot of music genres on these including pop, rock, metal, electronic, jazz, and classical and I'm happy with the relatively balanced sound. For spoken word, audio is clear and easy to understand.

The Bluetooth connectivity on these is good. Standard stuff. Also has an NFC connection if your device supports that. I tested both and it connects right away. Not much to report there, I was expecting that to work well and it does.

Battery life is good and a wired cable is included if your battery runs out or if you need to work in zero latency mode for something like music creation. There's no case included but there are some available as a separate purchase if needed. I have an old Astro headphone case that these fit in that I use for storage and travel.

Overall, a nice set of Bluetooth ANC headphones. I like the over hear closed back design. I like the sound quality and comfort, and I'm a fan of the overall look. These aren't perfect but at this price point they are a reliable, good sounding pair of headphones that should last a long time.

The fit is very tight and comfortable so I can wear them for the entire day without any pain and while still having plenty of battery. The mic is not amazing but it works well enough to where its not a problem. I like the ambient sound mode because a lot of times when I am trying to get work done I need sound but listening to a song will distract me, it acts like white noise at the press of a button. One thing that you will be giving up with this model is the quality, The unit is very light which is nice because it makes it fells better when on, but that lost weight is due to using what fells like a very cheap textured plastic, I would fell uncomfortable traveling around with this in my bag especially since there is no included bag or case to hold them in. The buttons have a bit of a tactile click to them so you can fell when you have pressed them which is nice. The ear-cups and cushion on the top are thin, the light weight makes it so that the lack of much cushioning is fine but the shallow ear-cups make is so that my ears are always touching the inside of the headphones. However in the end I think that a headphone should be judged more by the quality of its sound than the quality of what its made out of, so while I am a bit disappointed in the quality of these headphones I am thoroughly impressed by the quality of the sound and would happily recommend these but would also recommend picking up some type of case along with it.

title: More negatives than positives// UPDATE - Its a Lemon! I'm stuck but save yourselves
text:
[Pseudo Update: Sept 27th, They finally sent in a package to replace my 'lemon' pair... Opened it and found a pair of M100s. The wait continues. The Fugazi is strong with this one]

------(promised) UPDATE September 11th------

So I moved to a new apartment since I last sat dowb to review these. So I have been too busy to give these a shot, but today while unboxing I decided instead of using my Chane Speakers that is hooked to me receiver (...They are amazing by the way), I would use the Wireless headphones. And since I was moving and did not want the cables bothering me, I decided to go wireless. Yes I felt brave!
I decided to play Madeon on spotify, turned bluetooth on my laptop on and then connected to the V-Moda bluetooth headphones.
'Madeon -Imperium' plays... It was awful, really really awful. So bad in fact I ran back to my computer and changed the track.
Next up 'Madeon - Pay no mind'. Muddy, overbearing bass and totally dominates the sound. The lyrics drowned out and did not stand a chance.
I decided to blame spotify (premium by the way so the quality is supposed to be pretty good)
I tried the same tracks on Itunes... 320 KBPS. Same result.
Played 'Madeon - Beings' from my itunes library: Harsh and muddy.

These headphones have ABSOLUTELY RUINED the one thing I like listening to Madeon for...the crispness of his arrangements. As far as dance music goes, Madeon to me has always been a clean production and V-Moda wireless does everything in its power to invert that.

Want a headache... put these wireless cans on and play 'Madeon - Home'.
It sounds like playing an iphone 4 video recording of this track in a club on youtube. Muddy rubbish!

Val Kolton is really selling us a lemon here. If you have your M-100s and were going to trade them in for these....DO NOT!

The reason I really decided to update this review is to warn everyone about how dreadful these are.
Go give Master & Dynamic a shot or even bose, neither are amazing but at least they got it right.

Here is where I stand right now: Got rid of (returned under the lifetime program) perfectly good sounding wired headphones [M100] worth $300 when I picked em up about two years ago. I paid $300 (got a refund of $130 for my M-100s) for the wireless ones instead which are oh so awful at wireless and when wired are pretty much the same as the headphones I gave back. In my head I spent $470 for a pair of wired headphones that pretend to do wireless...

Special Thanks to Apple for putting out Iphone 7 with no headphone Jack, that news is what really triggered this series of events that led me to look into bluetooth. Sigh

[Returned the headphones, awaiting a replacement]
------ORIGINAL REVIEW------
I'll go into the backstory really quick....
I own the M-100s (wired in the shadow) I love the damn thing. I own the LP2, and gave a couple of them as christmas presents.
There was a recent itch to go wireless, it stems from the fact that at the gym the cable alway tangled with the weights or some protruding bar and the tug would project my cell phone into the floor or worse. On a recent trip to NYC I noticed my buddy used beats and I remembered V-Moda came out with a wireless a while back (I was awaiting the reviews and feedback before taking the plunge....the time had come)

I have always read a lot about any thing I think of buying, before I buy it. Understand the factors and variables.
With the idea of buying a bluetooth headphone (was not interested in earbuds, earphones because for the music I like they are nothing to go nuts about) I began looking at the options, I visited stores to demo the popular ones (Ziks, Sony, Senns).... began seeing what features were offered (noise cancelling, apt-x codecs, wireless charging, battery life etc)
While I liked the features and the type of codec involved with others, V-Moda according to many had cracked it....Making the sound almost the same as the wired mode, when used in bluetooth mode.
So knowing all I needed to know I placed my order and even got extra shields and XL pads to go on these.

When they first came in I let them charge to 100%, and also let them burn to tracks and white noise.

I have spent the last couple of days with it now....

Here are my impressions :
--(I will be revisiting this review once I have spend even more time with these to note the changes in my opinion or a possible lack of it)--

Now I listen to dance music, so this is me talking with regard to that genre.
I also indulge in a fair number of podcasts.

So listening to Steve Angello ( I/O, Lights ), Gareth Emery (U, DUI), Eric Prydz (Opus) off spotify and Itunes....
Wireless-
1. The kicks are distinct and pronounced
2. The piano/synths are muddy...awful in fact. The impression I get is the sound is coming from afar...it is lacking.
Same feeling playing Mark Knight – The Return Of Wolfy or Merk & Kremont - Amen. The sounds arent rich at all so the kicks seem to overpower them
3. No hissing sound at low volume that others seem to experience, but anytime there is cymbals in a track....the sound reproduction is hissy and harsh
4. Wireless is NOT a loud as wired. It almost feels like someone has added a layer of cotton to the wired mode. So the claim from some that the wired and wireless are similar, I would not subscribe to that notion.
5. Bass is spot on....good for dance music/bassheads

Wired -
1. Much much louder than the wireless version
2. Sounds are more balanced and richer
3. The flaws of sounds being distant/muddy is eliminated. This sounds so very clear.
4. Sounds way more balanced/less colorful than my M-100s

Other points:
1. The sound fades in and out if I am in the next room...no distinct barriers between rooms.
2. Using the buttons on the headphones changes random applications on my macbook, listening to spotify but it starts up itunes and plays both simultaneously
3. This should have been foldable like the M-100s, now that I see them up close, there is no design restriction that would not allow them to
4. Construction is solid as ever from V-moda and the new box is beautiful. Was not so convinced by the bluetooth toggle button
5. 1 year warranty could have been improved upon
6. The price on these... V-moda nailed that. If you are getting headphones the first time from V-moda, worth getting these over the regular M-100s. But if you have M-100s and do not need wireless option is day to day life for your runs/gym...Id say you can skip this.
7. Connecting to several bluetooth devices is not as seamless, Parrot, Bose and Master & Dynamic do it better
8. Some people reported a lag in playback when used for videos online, not an issue here

Where I stand on these right now....
If I was honest, I would like the wireless mode to sound better, way better.
This pair was a huge let down compared to others I tried.
But I might end up keeping these, so I can hit the gym in wireless mode, but thats probably the only time when I will be going wireless...
otherwise I will be using these wired.
Plus the restocking fee and shipping mess/costs makes it too much of a hassle. And I had some shields made for these too, so there is that.

Like one reviewer said on a tech site, these are solid wired headphones that just also happen to do bluetooth.
Thats how I see it. They do wireless but its not a crisp sound.

I am going to let these play longer, hopefully it gets there...
I'll report back then.

Hope this helps

--I got my pair from V-Moda 's site directly--

title: You Get What You Pay For
text:
If you want/need an inexpensive Bluetooth microphone headset this product fits the bill. I wouldn't recommend it for someone who spends the bulk of their time on the phone or on video conferences. The sound quality (both transmitting and receiving) is simply 'not there'. Sound coming into the headset is muffled and low, and never seems to be quite loud enough. In tests talking into the mic (both recording and speaking with a live person) the quality is (again) low and tinny. On the plus side, I love the ability to pair the headset to two devices (a phone and computer in my case). It means I can use one device for both phones and video conferences.

The build quality of the headset is quite nice. The plastic is nice and sturdy, and there's plenty of plush surfaces for a nice comfortable fit. I do wish the mic could be swiveled down farther, but the flexible arm allows me to position it where desired. Also, I'm not sure why the ear piece collapses/folds. It does nothing to make the headset more portable (i.e. save space), and is actually a little annoying.

Again, if you do a lot of phone/video conference work (more than once a day) then spring for a higher quality headset. However, if you just need something for the occasional call, either professionally or personally, then these should be fine.

text:
Let me start off by saying that my first pair of V-Moda headphones were the [[ASIN:B003BYRGKY V-MODA Crossfade LP Over-the-Ear Headphones (Gunmetal Black)]]. I have had the LPs for a little over a year now with no complaints. These headphones were built like a tank and very bass heavy, which is what I was looking for. I was getting ready to purchase the M-100s then I saw these and with the reviews I had to get them. I ordered the Phantom Chrome from V-Moda's website so I was able to get a free pair of fiber custom shields!

Out of the box, the sounds is tremendously better than my LP's. They are about the same size and have about the same weight to them with the same tank like quality. The sound is crystal clear. I have Spotify with my music downloaded in high quality so I'm sure that helps these headphones get closer to their potential. You'll definitely want to upgrade your music quality to take advantage of what these headphones are capable of. However, from the reviews I read the bass isn't meeting expectations quite yet but neither did the LPs the first couple of days of use so I'm hoping the headphones will open up a bit after I break them in. Don't get me wrong though, these are one of the best headphones I've experienced.

If I had to complain about one thing, and this is with me being extremely picky, it would be about the weight of each side of the headphone. Coming from the LPs, I could tell that right side is a tad heavier than the left when sitting on my head due to the bluetooth technology on the right side. However, the longer they sit on your head the less you'll notice.

Overall these are great headphones and with V-Modas great immortal life program I can't see myself purchasing another pair of headphones. I'm not sure how long V-Moda will be offering the free set of custom fiber shields if you purchase from their website but if they are offering it that's what you should definitely do.

title: Could use improvements
text:
Pros:
It's very lightweight. Great battery life. Amazing range (with my phone, not so much with my Bluetooth adapter on my computer). Easy to set-up, but instructions can be a little confusing. Sleek design and the ability to snap the arms closed is really nice, coupled with the small carry bag. The buttons are relatively stiff, so there's no worry about brushing the headphones against anything and depressing any of the buttons. This includes laying in bed.

Cons:
Not noise-canceling whatsoever. Wearing both headphones with music playing at a moderate level, could easily hear someone talking. For reference, I can clearly hear my computer's fans (which are really quiet). This actually can be either a pro or a con. For me, I like to be able to hear my surroundings while also having music wireless transmitted to my ears. The bass is acceptable, but it's not amazing. If you're an audiophile and you're willing to pay top dollar for good headphones, steer clear. The Bluetooth microphone does NOT work with my Windows 7/Kinivo Bluetooth adapter, which is very unfortunate. I have researched this issue for several hours, and ended up emailing support (support@meelec.com) on 12/16/15. EDIT: Response as of 12/21/15.

The three horizontal buttons are a pain in the ass to use. The top and bottom buttons both have a protruding dot so that you could feel the difference (In theory). But the buttons are all pretty long, and with the power button being in the center, it's almost impossible to tell when your finger is over the power/play button. Which is basically the most important button, so you'd want quick access. Combine that with having to hold the power button for two or so seconds to turn on/off, it becomes a pain in the ass. Some sort of sliding/toggle power button would have been greatly preferred.

The clear smooth plastic finish looks great when it's first unboxed, but it's the same type of material that shows fingerprints/dirt too well, not unlike the face-plate of the Xbox One. You'll find yourself wiping it frequently if it bothers you.

Overall, could use some improvements.

I had a pair of Monster iSport Freedoms I literally worked to retirement (after 2 years and 4 months of excellent service). This time, I wanted over ear (and not over head) so I could take the same pair cycling. My ear canals are pretty small, so I knew it would be a difficult hunt. Last year I bought a pair of Beats (sport) but I ended up feeling that they were uncomfortable so I took them back.

A few weeks before this, I tried some Plantronics, (Backbeat Fit). Great sound, but even their smallest plugs were too big and intrusive for long stays on my ears, and my ears started aching after 30 minutes of use :-( I bought them from BestBuy, so I was just able to take them back and avoid shipping. I then ordered and received these.

I actually like the softer, flexible plastic around this ear piece, it's not hard and crusty like some. Unfortunately, they were just too big, and started slipping and popping out during more rigorous exercises like interval sprints and when I laid down on the bench for chest presses (weights). Even the smallest plugs (both foam and silicone) wouldn't stay in my ears. I typically leave my gym bag at one end of my gym and cycle around doing circuit training. Sometimes the connection would drop, so the wireless range was not as great as my Monsters. Then again, those types of over the head headsets always have better everything including battery life and range so I'm not deducting any stars for that.

Positives: They sound great, and the shipping was fast. I also like the little zippered case they come in. Unfortunately, I am returning them because after three wears at the gym, I couldn't keep them around (or in) my ears. I work out too hard to be distracted by earpieces that won't keep in place :-( Can't comment on the longevity, since I have only had them a short time. But for those of you with bigger ears/ear canals, these just may actually be perfect for you!! I ordered some Epic2's, so I should be receiving them at some point this month. title: Superb headphones!
text:
So why am I giving headphones that I consider to be fantastic only 3 stars? Because I also happen to own the Plantronics Backbeat pros. Those headphones are superior in almost every way for the same price or far less if you get the older version.

I will focus first on these headphones and then the comparison to the Plantronics. The Crossfades scream quality and beauty when unboxing. The materials are the highest quality and they just feel good. The metal construction is top notch and the plastics are solid and substantial. The metal accent shields are beautiful and just make the headphones look good.

Controls are sparse, but effective. There is a power/pairing button on the bottom of the right headphone that functions well and is fairly intuitive. At the top are a series of three button. The center one pauses/starts the music and answers calls. The two surrounding it control volume and skip music forward or backward.

These headphones are very comfortable. I have a large head and they accommodate me with ease and I don't have too much discomfort even after a couple of hours use. They are even more comfortable after adding the XL pads. The pads make the ear opening larger and put more distance between the ear and the speaker. The XL pads are so much better that I think VMODA should have made them standard instead of selling them as an extra. Especially at this price point.

Sound. If I hadn't heard a better set, I would have been completely happy with this headphone. Bass is good and highs are where they should be. Mids are a bit too recessed for my taste so some vocals are lost. They play well at low volumes and can get plenty loud. Sound bleed is minimal and the outside world does not intrude too much. In the end, these really are great sounding headphones. Again, the XL pads improve the sound greatly. They provide a greater depth of sound and a much warmer tone.

This brings me to the reason that I am returning these and why they are only receiving 3 stars from me, despite how much I like them. I happen to own the Plantronics Backbeat Pro and they are superior to the Crossfades in nearly every way. The controls are more intuitive and easier to use. The Plantronics have APTx, active noise cancelling, voice prompts, and longer battery life. Most importantly, they simply sound better. As good as the Crossfades are, the Backbeats are better. Deeper bass, better mids, and they sound far clearer than the Crossfades. The Crossfades are very muddy by comparison. The Vmodas are constructed of better quality materials, are lighter, and look better, but that is not enough to justify buying them when a better alternative exists. Especially since you can get the old version of the Plantronics for far less.

To sum up. Great headphones that you will likely be really happy with, but there are better available for similar or less money. I also think that it is a sin that VMODA charges extra for the XL pads which are a necessity to get the best out of them. I really wanted to keep these and be happily ever after, but I simply can't. Back they go.

I've purchased over a dozen of these headphones, and they've always been great.

Curious as to why the sound quality was so much worse I opened up one of the earbuds and compared it to my aging pair. Sure enough the copper ring around the driver was almost non-existent. Plus it was much more difficult to open my older pair because it had a much sturdier construction.

I love the fit. There's room to hook one earbud to my shirt/tank top/bra strap allowing me to only wear one while conversing with others. I like the longer length of the cord because of that. The louder they are, the better they sound. The 4 star rating is only because the description said super bass, or something to that effect. I don't find the description of bass sound quality to be accurate. Where earbuds are concerned, they are great just the same. Sound quality is clear. The mic does pic up surrounding noises but much less than other pairs I have had. The control buttons are easy to reach and function great. The volume buttons double as forward and back track buttons. The play/pause can be used to call the last number on my phone. I find that the over the ear "hangers" are small enough to keep them in place but not so tight as to make them uncomfortable. I have tried out several different sets of bluetooth earbuds. I wear these everyday from about 7 am to their daily death between 3 or 4 pm. I listen to music almost constantly and make and take phone calls in between. Quality has not diminished in the month or so I've had them. They seem to be holding up well with no signs of falling apart. Another awesome feature is that they are fully charged in about 2 hours. These, as actual earbuds, are my favorite so far. I would recommend them for everyday use. I enjoy using them and expect them to last as long as, if not longer, than previous choices. With all those positives and the decent price, I will most definitely consider replacing these, when worn out, with the same thing...or better if they offer such in the future. The pictures show the earbuds juat over a month later, how I choose to wear the one not used, and the fit around the ear. title: At long last, my quest for my favorite headphones has ended.
text:
I've bought far more headphones than I'd like to admit, and I must say, these V-Modas are probably the best I've purchased at any price point (granted, these are also tied with the most expensive headphones I've ever purchased). The thing that sets them apart is the build quality which is immediately noticeable upon picking up the headphones, they just feel solid, almost indestructible, and with the XL cushions, they're also the most comfortable headphones I own (although, they aren't bad by any stretch of the imagination without the XL cushions).

The sound quality exceeds or is at the very least on-par with other high-end headphones, but even over bluetooth, there's no noticeable loss in audio fidelity vs. using them wired, something I can't say for other wired/wireless headphones.

Finally, as is tradition, after about 8 months of wearing them in the rain, dropping them on concrete, and not taking any special care of the headphones, the right earphone shorted out (this is just a thing that happens, it's happened to every pair of headphones I've ever owned). I loved these enough that I sent them back, and that day they 2 day'd over a brand new pair along with a new pair of cushions with no arguments or questions. Their customer service is some of the best I've ever dealt with.

With this in mind, I can confidently say that I'm now a loyal V-Moda customer, and if you like the way they look, I'm sure you'll be one too.

title: Good light weight neckband-style Bluetooth ear buds - comfortable and rest where they should
text:
I've been needing a new pair of bluetooth earbuds for a while, but I break all earphones eventually so I stick to buying inexpensive ones - I've had decent luck with cheap ones in the past so I wanted to give these a try.

Pairing was simple, once my Android phone got around to scanning the nearby devices, which took a while. The N18s showed up immediately on my Samsung tablet.

These TONEMAC N18 Bluetooth Neckband Earbuds were listed at $29 with a 20% off coupon at the time of the review, which is a fair price for what they are. The last pair of bluetooth earbuds I had were a slightly different style, lighter and more flexible and I could just stick in my pocket. This pair has a stiffer neck band that stays in place better, but they will be a bit harder to pocket. They'll fit in an inside coat pocket, but may be a bit more awkward in my windbreaker hand warmer pockets.

Charging is USB-C, but the instruction manual is old and stills says micro-USB. The magnets on the earbuds to hold them together while you are not using them are pretty strong, which means it will be hard to accidentally loose these, unlike Apple Airpods and other similar earbuds that have no wires connecting them, or even regular wired earbuds which I some times drape around my neck when I'm not wearing them, and have wound up loosing them because they aren't made for that the way these are.

Sound is decent for my needs. Outgoing audio from the microphone is a little bit distorted and output is low, though not any lower than the NoxGear I compared the audio to using the Android audio Recorder app.

Overall, I'm happy with the earbuds. But it will take some time to get feedback from people about the outgoing call quality.

title: Excellent, but with a flaw
text:
These sound great, are comfortable to wear for 10+ hours every day, and the detachable cable works perfectly with switching between commuting and work.

The one big problem I have is that there's a dinky little plastic triangle piece that is critical to keeping each cup from swinging too far out. If it breaks off, that ear piece just flops out sideways instead of pushing up against your head. That happened to me after having them for four years of daily use all day long in and out of a bag, but still it seems weird to have such a weak point when everything else about them had been extremely solid. Looking around online, there's a lot of other people who've had this problem as well.

Luckily, I found the perfect solution that doesn't involve finding replacement parts, drilling bolts, 3d printing bits, or even having to unscrew or disassemble anything: Just straighten out the cup to the correct angle (compare against the other side) and wrap a little hanging wire around the joint, twisting the ends together. It holds it perfectly and doesn't interfere with anything; they fold up just fine and it holds against my ears like when they were new. I just wanted to post this somewhere because I've seen a lot of much more questionable repairs out there.

What I like:
Headphone automatic mute when the microphone is flipped up.

What I don't like:

The cable is also too stiff. 4 days later it is still kinky from the initial packaging foldings, which makes the short cable worse.
I'd have return this if this is mine. Downgrade from 3 to 2 stars.

A few months later:
There's a setting that stop picking environmental noise in the microphone that requires the Jabra software. So that is resolved.

title: Comfortable, high-quality headphones with excellent sound quality
text:
[[VIDEOID:93f3f8e59bcd3a44f877c1bd5e927a25]]Pros:
-Product presentation
-Super comfortable
-Incoming calls and other functions are announced in spoken word
-Noise cancellation is excellent (what lawnmower???)
-Variety of earbud sizes
-Sturdy, compact carrying case
-Same Micro-USB charger as Android phones
-“Bolo tie” style cord manager included

Cons:
-I honestly haven’t found any yet!

I was very pleasantly surprised by these little ear buds. I know Amazon frowns on talking about “packaging” in reviews, but I do like to point out good product presentation when I see it! Unboxing these headphones really feels like you’re digging into a quality product. They did an excellent job there.

The quality doesn’t stop with the unboxing, either. Everything about these seems solid and quality-oriented, from the feel of the materials to the fit of smaller moving components like the charging port cover and the power / pairing button.

I put these to first test of doing all of my yard work this morning and they absolutely exceeded my expectations. The sound quality is unmistakably excellent and the noise cancellation is on-point. Normally when I wear headphones while doing yardwork I have to have the volume on my Galaxy S5 MAXED OUT to be able to hear anything over the lawnmower. With these I was able to listen to podcasts at right around half volume and still hear each and every word clearly. Very impressive.

Another feature I like is the voice which announces different functions and incoming calls identified by numbers. No trying to decipher cryptic beep codes as with some cheaper headsets.

The included accessories are all welcomed additions and of equally respectable quality including the charging cable, different sized earbuds, and carrying case. It is worth noting that the charging cable is pretty short (only a few inches), but this allows for increased portability and it folds nicely up into the netted pocket in the carrying case. The charging port is a standard Micro-USB (same as android phones), so you should have plenty of available longer charger cables if you need them (especially if you’re an Android user).

I really couldn’t find anything I don’t like about these headphones and they’ll be my go-to pair for certain. Please be safe when using earbuds while walking, running, or cycling on public roads and sidewalks – they make it much more difficult to hear what’s going on around you.

I provided an honest and unbiased review of this product which was sold to me at a discount. I strive to stand by the "honest and unbiased" goal. I will always point out what I deem to be negative aspects of the product, and ding stars accordingly. I'm just a regular dude that likes to write and bump NPR while I mow the lawn.

While these are not actively-noise canceling, when I am lifting weights with my boyfriend I have to take one earbud out so I can even hear him talking. In short, I am SO glad I purchased these earphones. My only regret is that I didn't go with the xr500's... I may just end up gifting these to my bohyfriend and buying a new pair for myself because I know I will love them.

Do yourself a favor and buy these! And if you wear glasses, never fear! They are comfortable with those on as well.

The indicator light would come on when the charger was plugged in however there was no change in the flashing status after charging overnight. title: Surprising call clarity on both ends of the call!
text:
I received 2 pair of headphones as gifts, the Runolim Wh301A being one, and the Ankbit E600Pro being the other. I was able to give them a side-by-side comparison, even though at full price, the Ankbit are quite a bit more expensive ($119.99). Even with the Ankbit having CVC8.0 (a feature that is supposed to make calls sound clearer for the person on the other end), everybody that I called while I switched back and forth between the two pair of headphones said that they could hear me clearer when I used the Runolim pair!

The ANC on both worked equally well. Surprisingly, when I tested the passive noise cancellation (how well noise is blocked out simply by how well the ear cups cover the ears and muffle any sound from getting through), the Runolims were a little bit quieter than the Ankbit!

As far as sound quality goes, both headphones sounded great. It was nice to hear that these Runolim's could hold up compared to the Ankbit's in almost every aspect. Where they did fall a little bit short was in total decibel range, because they were a bit quieter at the same volume levels then the Ankbit. Also, I wanted to be able to take these off and wear them on my neck, with the speakers turned upwards so that music could still play while I could hear things around me since these headphones do not come with any kind of transparency mode like the Ankbit's do. The headphone design itself on the Runolim is quite a bit shorter in length than the Ankbit's, so I could not get them all the way around my neck. If these were made with transparency mode, and a slightly larger headband so that it would be the same size as most of the other headphones on the market, I would have given them five stars. I compared these to the headphones that I recently bought for my son, and they were smaller than his as well. I am not sure why Runolim decided to make these a little bit smaller than other brands. Outside of not having transparency mode, and being about 1 to 2 inches shorter in total length than other headphones, these are a great pair of headphones! Definitely 4 out of 5 stars!

title: I've got no strings on me!
text:
I love running with over-ear headphones, and lately my Crossfade M-100s have been my go-to cans for that. The one thing that I've always hated while running with any headphones is dealing with the cords - pulling earbuds out of my ears, rubbing and getting in the way of arm movement with on-ear or over-ear, etc. I can tuck them in my shirt or whatever, but then they're annoying and pull when I turn my head. And let's be honest - most cordless headphones sound like garbage. Been there, done that, returned it. Yeah, first world problems but why not shoot for perfection? The only reason I even gave these a shot is because they're V-MODA and I'm not just surprised, I'm blown away.

V-MODA claims that these sound equivalent to wired headphones. I'm going to disagree for my most common use case - connected directly to my iPhone 6S. In this case, they sound a bit better. The integrated amplified delivers more and cleaner bass presence than my iPhone can. Not as good as with a standalone DAC/amp, but I'd say about 30% better than the iPhone alone - which is not a subtle improvement, and without the distortions introduced by the iPhone's electronic equalizer. You can practically see the strings on a bass guitar vibrating in your mind, and the bass drums have a beautiful kick. Highs and mids still feature V-MODA's trademark clarity and nice, even frequency response. So yes, the sound is wonderful, which is what everyone really cares about. I've seen some complaints in forums, but as far as I can tell these have been narrowed down to devices that just can't send good quality audio over Bluetooth. I haven't personally had any issues yet, but I've only tested with my iPhone and MacBook Pro. Charging is accomplished with a standard micro-USB cable, so most people won't have to worry about carrying extra cords or chargers to keep the Crossfade Wireless topped up while traveling. Battery life hasn't yet been an issue. They come with a typically excellent V-MODA travel case, the sort that puts every other brand to shame but V-MODA buyers have become pleasantly used to.

Minor quibbles:
* No cliq-fold hinges like the M-100s and XS. Sorry, V-MODA, you spoiled us and it's hard to go back.
* A single button for pause / resume / track-forward / track-back. I suck at pressing these fast enough, so I always wind up just pausing it.

I'm pretty nit-picky about things, so that's a pretty short list. I'm loving these so far!

title: It's a little difficult, but I'm keeping mine.
text:
I've shopped around and tried out SOOOO many different stereo bluetooth devices. Most notably have been devices by Motorola and Plantronics. The specific model numbers elude me at the moment. The Motorola was nice, but cumbersome and the battery died after a few months. It had a band that went behind the head and was inflexible making it very uncomfortable to wear while leaning my head against anything such as the headrest in the car, or a pillow in bed. The Plantronics faired better, but the noise canceling wasn't very good.

I typically use my devices for conversations of both a business as well as a personal nature. For talking with my friends it would suffice, but not for clients. I also use my device when I'm working out at the Gym. It doesn't do very well when I work up a sweat, but the Halo device fares better than others.

I had a great deal of difficulty pairing this device the first time and it took me 3 days worth of emails with the technical support department of Jabra. They wouldn't provide me with a phone number and usually returned my emails within a few hours. I still can't figure out how to move forward or backwards through my music. I did it once by accident, and haven't been able to figure it out since.

Overall, the noise canceling is good, and the quality of the sound it produces is very good as well. The only reason I'm not ranking this more than 3 stars is because of how difficult it was to figure out, and the fact that I STILL can't get certain functions to work. Overall, I like this better than other products of this kind.

title: Pretty things don't always perform as expected!!
text:
From the moment I first discovered these online I was in love with this sleek and stylish dream of a perfect headset. Unfortunately actually using them proved much more like a nightmare. While this headset is very visually stunning the performance leaves much to be desired. First and foremost, the headset does have a 30 foot range as advertised, but when you put it in your pocket (as I'm assuming that's where most people plan on putting their phones when they wish to utilize the features of a HANDS-FREE device) it constantly cuts in and out. I usually listen to calming music on my walk to and from school, but the constant blips make it even more frustrating than listening to the homeless people beg for change on the subway. It's a constant reminder of the very disc-man portable CD players that you had to stand stalk still with to use. My experience from the "noise canceling" microphone actually was the opposite, meaning the lovely people on the other end of my phone call could hear my cat breathing from the other side of the apartment!! Whoever wrote this description needs to get their hearing checked. Also IPHONE USERS BEWARE this device is not fully functionally with your iPhones!! The nifty volume control does work, but the track forward/back function is absent, it did however work with my Mac and is pretty nifty. As for the fit, the headset was constantly slipping off of my ears and onto my temples, which wouldn't be a problem if I could hear out of my temples. It would stay put on my head only when I was sitting still at home, but if I was trying to walk or turn my neck ever so slightly the headset would ride my silky smooth hair right off my head. The hinges that turned the device on/off felt very flimsy and kept bending the wrong direction!! YIKES!! Finally the battery life was not all it was cracked up to be, partially because the device would often stay on even when folded. Expect 6 hours period, not 6 hours of actual listening time. If I unplugged this device at 9 they would be dead by 3, only listening to music for the 20 min commute to and from campus. I encountered a stranger on the subway that had recently purchased and returned the Halo just the day before. He asked my humble opinion and completely agreed with almost every complaint.

In conclusion these are beautiful headphones and I received numerous compliments from friends, professors and complete strangers. Unfortunately I listen to music with my ears not my eyes and this experience was painful at best. I've said this about people for years and now I can easily apply it to this headset, when things are good to look at they don't have to perform as well because they're carried by their looks. Perhaps if these were made to function better I would repurchase them in the future, but for the time being I'm going to research a different model. :(

title: Great headphones for some purposes
text:
I don't like writing negative reviews - it makes me feel like I didn't research the product carefully enough. I did like several aspects of this product, but the negatives outweighed the positives for me, so I had to return it.

Here is what I was looking for in a headset:

1. Sufficient volume so that I can hear (I do have a hearing loss and wear hearing aids, so I need some gain!)

This criterion was met, no problem. Its volume is great. I'm not sure that I completely mastered the "touch" volume control in the short time I had it, but it appeared to work. You drag your finger along the front edge of the right ear-piece, and the volume goes up or down. I did NOT have the problem some reviewers have mentioned, that the volume is too high no matter what. If I drag my finger down on the volume control, it gets whisper quiet. But one person's whisper is another person's shout, so there you go.

2. No ear buds (because I wear hearing aids, and there's no place for an ear bud to go)

This criterion was met. The ear pieces definitely do NOT extend into the ear.

3. Compatibility with my Nokia E71x telephone.

This criterion was partially met. I had no problem pairing the Halo with my phone, but its connection would drop mysteriously. I sometimes could not get the connection to re-establish itself without rebooting the phone, which is not fun. This compares negatively to my Sony DR-BT30Q bluetooth headset, which I am currently replacing. The connection between the Sony and my phone was consistent, except when the battery in the Sony was in its death throws. After recharging the Sony battery, it would be fine.

Another compatibility issue was that I was not able to control the phone from the multi-use button on the Halo. I don't do that a lot with my Sony, but the few remote controls that I use (voice dial, answer), work fine.

4. Great sound while listening to audio books

This criterion was met. The sound was great while listening to audio books. I didn't actually use it to listen to music, but that probably would have been OK too. I didn't attempt to use the headset to control the sound playback, so I have no comment on that aspect, which seems to be of great interest to some reviewers.

5. Great sound while communicating on the telephone.

This was the biggest negative for me. The sound during telephone conversations was very bad - for me, and for the people with whom I was talking. It sounded like "being in a tunnel". Volume was fine, but it was just just very hard to understand. This compares very negatively to my experience with the Sony, which had excellent sound (coming and going) during telephone conversations.

6. Comfort while wearing the headset for long periods of time

This was fine. Comfort (and sound quality too, unless you're a sound engineer) is very subjective. I found this headset to be comfortable for a pretty long haul.

7. Ability to use it while exercising

I'm not too sure about this one. The headset worked fine during my exercise session: stayed put, great sound, comfortable. I don't wear my hearing aids during exercise, and the Halo put out enough sound for me to hear the audio book I was listening to.

The problem is that I sweat pretty profusely. I don't know if my perspiration could damage the set, but I do know that it was pretty darn wet - on the ear pieces and also under the "hair-band". The instructions say that limited use in light rain is OK, but that they are NOT waterproof, so one should take care. My perspiration might qualify as more-than-light rain.

8. Ability to use it while charging the battery.

This criterion was met nicely. You can charge the battery with a USB cable (though the one provided is too short to wear the headphone and charge at the same time - one would have to buy a longer cable from a third party. It's a standard mini-mini USB cable). Or you can charge the battery with a "travel" charger that plugs into the wall. Its wire is long enough to wear the headset and charge at the same time, if you're somewhere near an outlet.

You might ask, why am I replacing my Sony headset, if it's so great? That's what my wife asked me! Two reasons:

1) Its two ear pieces are connected with a retractable wire that goes behind the neck. That's fine (and actually gives me clearance to mop my bald pate during the aforementioned perspiration attacks), but my cat knocked the Sony off of my dresser some months ago, and now the retracto-mechanism is balky.

2) The Sony attaches to my ears with some plastic-coated spring-action wires. I find it difficult to attach the ear pieces rapidly, and they are not comfortable for long use.

A less important reason is that I think the Sony looks dorky, as compared to the Jabra Halo, which I felt looked real cool. How these things "look" is pretty subjective, however. And it's not a very important criterion compared to the other ones above.

I have ordered a Nokia BH-503 as a replacement for the Jabra Halo and will try it out. If it doesn't work out I'm going to try the more upscale Nokia BH-905.

I charged these up again last night as usual and watched a Netflix movie on my iPhone -- and around 15 minutes into it I got a "Battery is low" warning. Five minutes later, as usual, it died. Too much battery death! I saved the ear pads for other phones and threw the damn things out this morning.
________
Lots of bang for the buck. Spend some time finding the right set of (included) earpieces that fit your ear canal correctly; so much depends on the proper ear pads. I use the large black soft rubber pliable ones, and they are great for blocking out a lot of outside sound. Sound quality: These sound really good with a slightly muddy bass (which you can adjust with equalizer). Battery life is good enough for a day's listening.
