title: Great Value
text: These over-the-ear headphones are very lightweight and comfortable to wear. They seemed to be designed to be operated while wearing them because they speak to you as you press the buttons, e.g. Power On/Off, Bluetooth Pairing/Connected/Disconnected, Noise Cancelling, Ambient Sound, etc. Press the power button briefly and it tells you the power level, hold the button a few seconds to turn on/off, and hold it for seven seconds to go into Bluetooth pairing mode. If you have Near Field Communications on your device, my cell phone has this capability, the Bluetooth connects and disconnects when held near the device. In the box are the headphones, and two cables: a headphone cable, and USB-A to USB-C cable. The USB cable is less that 8 inches, not sure why so short, it is difficult to plug into my charging transformer or computer. A 5-volt charging transformer is not included and it is not clear the desired wattage. It did take 7 hours to charge initially. It is listed as having a 35-hour playback time on a charge. The sound quality is very good, I play my music at very high fidelity and these headphones are handling the music exceedingly well. One thing that I wish Sony included is a case for the headphones. There are third-party cases available online. These headphones seem to provide many of the features of Sony’s higher end headphones at a more modest price point. I would certainly recommend them for everyday use. I tested the tree modes; Ambient, Noise Cancelling, and Off. We live on a busy street with much traffic, cars and heavy trucks, which was a perfect setting for the test. Noise Cancelling mode did a great job compensating for the exterior noise, the traffic is loud, and I could barely hear it.  As expected in Ambient mode the microphones passed through the street sounds with the music, good if I were walking around and needed to also hear what is going on in the environment and listen to the music. Ambient off turns off the microphones so there is no pass-through sound, so it will depend on the outside volume and your music volume as to how much outside sound you hear. Ambient off also means that Noise Cancelling is off, so if you do not like the compensation that noise cancelling provides, this is your mode. I need to also disclose that I did receive these headphones at a discount in exchange for my honest review. I am pleased with the quality that these headphones provide at a very reasonable price.

I am in the market for some headphones to use for running. Like many others, I find the supplied Apple earbuds to be uncomfortable and prone to falling out with physical activity (such as running). Additionally, I have a set of Sure earbuds but I don't want to run with them because I won't be able to hear anything except my own heavy breathing.

In order for earbuds like these to function well (produce good highs and lows) they need to create a seal with your ear canal. They don't. On the few occasions I was able to get them into a good position and create the seal, the sounds were actually quite good. However, the moment I started walking around they came loose. The earhook potion keeps the bud from falling out completely but without that perfect seal, the sound is not good.

I think I have relatively medium to medium-large ears and for me, these did not work. YMMV.

In a few days I am to leave town on business and asked my wife if she had a charger for her phone while I was away. She calmly told me that the charger was not leaving town with me, that if I wanted a charger while traveling, I would need to purchase another. I bought the newest one with PowerIQ and a complete set of cables. It nicely complements the Anker 10,000 mAh external battery I also purchased to keep all of my devices charged during a 13 hour pair of flights each way.

Pros:
* Quiet and out of the way
* Comes with appropriate cables
* Just works -- with everything I have thrown at it
* Charges everything as fast as the device will take it
* No bling, no flashing lights, no eye-popping graphics, no sirens, no lasers, no logos. Just a charger
* Uses a standard AC cable instead of a wall wart so I never have to worry about losing the power supply

Cons:
* It does not have a battery

Like I said, this is as close to perfect as you can get. The only thing which could possibly improve this is if it had a built in battery so that I could just unplug the AC cable and take it with me to charge stuff on the go.

Every day I use this to charge:
* LG G2 cell phone
* Corporate Blackberry
* Nexus 7 Tablet
* Tablet bluetooth keyboard
* Wireless bluetooth stereo speaker
* E-cigarette battery
* Anker external battery

Yes, that list has seven devices for a five-port charger, but in the real world I never need to charge them all at the same time.

I read somewhere that 1/3 of all USB chargers Amazon sells are made by Anker. Assuming the statistic is true, 2/3 of the people purchasing USB chargers are making a mistake. Don't do the same. Buy this instead.

text:

The sound quality is fine to me, but I use them mostly to listen to audiobooks while doing hands-on chores so I'm not sure how much music would be affected.

Another user said the case wouldn't charge. I also found that to be an issue at first. I was using my own cord in a rapid charge adapter and they wouldn't charge at all. I plugged the tiny 12 inch cord it came with into my desktop port and the case is finally charging. The case is nice, I like the look of it and how easy it is to see the case's remaining charge. My only complaint that took this from 5 to 4 stars is that occasionally the sound will cut out in one or both. It's only a split second, and it isn't very common, maybe 5 or 6 times in an hour. For my purposes, and for $30, I'm okay with it. I will be less so if it gets worse. They don't have too much "noise cancelling" to them but I was able to hear them over the lawn mower so they get loud enough. There is also no way to turn them off. If they are out of the case, they are on, and only putting them back will turn them off. Its a minor inconvenience, more of just something to be aware of for preserving battery life.

title: Excellent and Super Comfortable Premium Headphones!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
text:
After reading various pro and customer reviews about how great these sound, I went ahead and bought myself the Sennheiser HD1 Over-Ear headphones (HPs) in the ivory color. The HD1 is the upgraded version of the Momentum 2.0 headphones by Sennheiser. They feature the exact same award-winning (2017) sound signature of the Momentum 2.0 headphones, but with added comfort. Sennheiser found out a year or so ago that the name "Momentum" was already trademarked, so they decided to rename this line to "HD1" in order to avoid a lawsuit.

Price: I paid $250 for these on Amazon + $25 tax, so a total of $275.

Looks/Design/Features: These are some really nice premium-looking HPs. Though the ear cups are plastic, the rest of the phone is all metal & genuine leather all the way! In between ear cups & the ear pads are gold metallic accents, which give the phone a more luxurious look. They are quite light, not bulky by any means, and so they are also quite portable. A big part of their portability also comes in the form of the "fold-in" feature (see pic below) which the original Momentum 1.0 did not have (though the 2.0 did).

The cable for the phone is a regular (non-braided) cable which features an in-line remote and mic. Though the phone is "Made for iOS", the only thing lost on Android phones with this remote is the volume feature really. The pause/play button works just fine, and I believe the same button can let you take and/or disconnect phone calls as well. The length is 1.4 meters, which is about 4.5 feet. I am happy with anything around 4 feet, so this is just fine with me. The part that connects into the HD1 features a "twist & lock" option as well, and it goes into the right side of the HD1. It takes a BIT of effort to twist and pull it out, but not too much really. I will prob just leave it in most of the time unless traveling long distances.

The HD1 also comes with a suede-like super-soft carrying case AS WELL AS a black hard case! Sennheiser held back nothing here! You usually don't get both, so this was a welcome surprise. The hard case has enough room in it so that you can even leave the cable connected into the HD1 w/o worrying about it (this is how they come actually too).

Comfort: I found these to be one of the most comfortable HPs I've ever worn! They remind me a lot of my old Sony MDR-1A 'phones actually, which were the most comfortable ones I've ever worn, though these may be equal to those or an extremely close second? Due to the HD1 being so light, and because of their smaller size, you don't have much pressure on any part of your head at any given time either. The headband is genuine leather with some padding on it. Not a ton, but the truth is it really doesn't need it IMO. The ear pads feel like giant super soft marshmallows against your ears. They had been enlarged since the Momentum 1.0 due to customer complaints, and it good to see that Sennheiser listened! Even with glasses on, these still felt super comfy to me! I have average-sized ears, and so I never felt my ears touching the speaker driver covering at all either.

The oval shape of these ear pads also have other advantages. One of which has to do with volume and potential hearing loss. Rounded ear pads let more of the sound leak out, which in turn forces the listener to raise the volume up, which can put the listener at increased risk for (unnecessary) hearing damage. But oval-shaped ear pads isolate sound better, and therefore less sound is likely to leak out, and the urge to raise the volume up higher vanishes immediately!

Sound: Many have said the HD1s sound great out of the box and don't need EQ'ing. For the MOST part I agree with this statement. They did sound great out of the box, but I felt they could sound even better, so I tried to come up with a custom EQ for the HD1s. But oddly enough it was the custom EQ I used for my now former Meze 99 Classics that made them sound their best! It opened up the sound to give it more "air" and also less congested (with respect to instrument separation) & less overly bassy on some songs as well. So these comments are based on the use of my Meze 99 Classics WITHOUT the Brainwavz ear pads custom EQs (1st set, 3 total), which can be found here. They were made for use in the Poweramp music app, so make sure to get that for best results! (See HD1 review on Head-Fi by RockStar2005 for these EQs)

But the next day, I tried them again and now they sound just fine! Not an audiophile, so I cant tell if it`s just in my head and I simply got used to them, or if I flipped some setting on my phone without knowing it. I have a much more balanced sound, now.

Some reviewers have complained about comfort, stating the earpads dont cover their ears entirely, leading to sound leakage. If you have big ears, that might be something you should take into consideration when buying these, but I find I can wear these at work all day during an 8-10 hour shift without feeling the need to take them off, something I`ve never been able to do with on-ear styled headphones.

They look and feel fantastic! In fact, part of what motivated me to buy the Crossfade was that it was made out of METAL, not cheapy plastic used in a kid`s toy (I`m looking at YOU, Skullcandy Hesh 3, sitting in a corner of my room with both hinges snapped from daily use!). I needed something that break from something a stupid as removing them from my neck. The Crossfade also looks gorgeous too, having that modern, professional, yet understated look; very sleek, doesn`t give you that "I`m wearing my winter earmuffs indoors" look. I bought the Gumetal look, but one thing V-Moda loves to advertise is that you can order different colored plates for more style; you can even have your plates made with precious metals like platinum, silver and even REAL gold that`s sure to impress absolutely no one.

Battery life is 10-12 hours, a massive step down from 22 hours I got with Hesh3, and it doesn`t charge anywhere near as fast, but the tradeoff is owning headphones not made from brittle plastic.

text:
I bought these headphones primarily for use on the plane. Thus, sound quality was somewhat of secondary importance to me since I already have a nicer pair of Klipsch headphones that I use when I want good sound. The noise cancelling works adequately on the plane, but how well it works varies depending on where you're sitting. The first time I used it, I had a window seat a couple rows behind the engine, and it probably removed 70%-80% of the sound. On my return flight, I sat a few rows in front of the engine, and it performed even better since there isn't as much engine noise towards the front of the aircraft.

Sound quality leaves a lot to be desired. Let's just say that if I had purchased these at the full price of $178, I would have been extremely disappointed and probably returned them. A lot of bass is missing while the mids are adequate but lacking in depth. What saves the headphones in this aspect is the fact that the noise cancellation is not 100% on the plane, so you don't really notice the audio quality while flying. Still, I expect a lot more from headphones that cost almost $200. The good news is that these headphones can be found refurbished for about $50 on that other big e-commerce site where people sell used items (this is where I bought mine). If you can get them for that price, it's definitely worth it. Otherwise, I'd look elsewhere for noise-cancelling headphones.

title: Great sound, but with some quirks
text:
I will be the first to admit I am not a bona fide "audiophile" so so this review will not focus on any technical jargon or specifications, besides those are listed on the skullcandy website. First, These were bought as a replacement to my Sennheiser CX200 earphones that were left in a hotel room. As the package came, the first thing I noticed was not the earphones but the cool ballistic mylon case. It is round, with one side being mesh and the other being nylon, akin to the nylon cases that Oakley sells. the case zips closed, with a small mesh pocket to hold spare ear gels. The earphones also come with two other sets of silicone gels (large and small) and if you look closely they actually have small skulls on the gels themselves.

The earphones themselves look and feel durable. The color is not a pitch black but more of a carbon gray, and the crosshatching on the earbud helps to place and remove the earphones, providing the wearer does not have sausage-fingers. Once fitted, these are less comfortable than the CX200 Sennheisers. The body of the Titans are a bit wider, and that may cause light contact on some wearers ears, as it does mine. That aside, these are still worlds more comfortable than the stock ipod earphones.

The sound on the Titans is superb. I don't have selective enough hearing to tell a noticeable difference between these and my previous pair, but compared to the ipod headphones the bass is deeper and richer, yet the midrange and highs are still very complete. I certainly "hear" subtle musical parts of a song that aren't heard with a basic set of earphones through the entire range of sound. Most of my music selection is made up of 80's and electronic, however I can see where some listeners of hip hop would love this pair for the potential to boom bass. (Maybe different brands of headphones are better for different genres of music, but Im not going to blow out my budget to find out.)

Overall, the Titans get four stars because of the less than perfect fit. Also a cord keeper on the volume bar to help wrangle up some of that extra cord between the earphones and the music player would be nice. As I have not had these long enough to a review durability, my rating may change in the future. Still, a great package and a great pair of headphones, just be cautious for wearers with smaller ear canals.

title: Beats Wish They Sounded This Good
text:
I came to this headphone after having used and loved a pair of Shure SRH-440 for the last few years. Those headphones impressed me with their flat-tuned response, nice sound stage, comfort and durability. After my 440s were stolen from my desk where I work (word of advice: don't leave your headphones out over a weekend for the cleaning crew to steal), I decided to step up and go with the ATH-M50x. I've only had them for 1 day, but they are outstanding right out of the box. They have a more curved eq response overall than the SRH-440s with more defined bass, but certainly not to an obscene degree and not at the expense of any higher frequencies. The sound stage is rich and wide - much moreso than the SRH-440. They are reasonably light and fit comfortably over the ears with very good outside ambient noise isolation. They are a little tight at first, but I know from prior experience that they will loosen up over time a little.

Having previously spent over 10 years working in the consumer electronics industry, I can confirm that these are among the best and definitely a nicer-sounding set of over-the-ears than Beats. These outperform Beats and most other headphones in a similar price range on pretty much every level and, at least to my adult eyes, look classier too. Easily the best pair of over-the-ear headphones I have ever owned!

title: Great Sound Quality for a Low Price
text:
I bought these Sony earbuds as a replacement for the excellent quality wired Klipsch earbuds that I love and have used for years because my last Klipsch pair finally stopped working in one ear and Klipsch no longer makes/sells wired earbuds – they only offer wireless earbuds now. In any case, even though the Klipsch wired earbuds were excellent, they were around 100 bucks for a pair. These Sony earbuds are designed well and feature 9mm drivers that produce really good sound – especially considering that they are literally 1/5 of the price of my previous Klipsch pair.

I am still rocking an 80GB iPod (which I love and which I will shed bitter tears over when it finally dies) that has my entire music library on it, and, being older non-Bluetooth tech, wired earbuds are a must. I was skeptical that low-price earbuds would offer anything better than low quality sound, but I was very pleasantly surprised with these Sony earbuds. I can completely recommend them, and I also recommend that you scoop up a couple of spare pairs if you prefer wired earbuds to wireless ones, since I’m guessing that a lot of big, reputable companies like Sony will also soon retire any wired earbud product lines and only also offer wireless versions in the future.

Anyway, these earbuds are an excellent buy for the price. My only minor complaint is that they aren’t as ergonomically well designed as the Klipsch earbuds that I had and don’t fit in the ears as well or as comfortably (which is why I rated them 4 stars and not 5); but they fit well enough and come with a variety of differently sized silicone earpieces that allow you to adjust to the most comfortable fit. All in all, these are really good all-around quality earbuds at a price that can’t be beat.

title: Great headphones for working out
text:
I bought these headphones so that I could start using Spotify through my iPhone at the gym instead of having to listen to my old iPod nano and the same songs over and over (I'm lazy when it comes to changing songs on devices). Here's a breakdown of the features and my input:
Comfort: They are comfortable and fit securely inside and around the ears, so you should have no trouble with them falling off during your workouts. They also come with multiple sized rubber covers to fit any ear size.
Functionality: Everything you need is located on the right earpiece. You hold down the power button on the right earpiece (Treblab logo) for 2 seconds to turn the unit on. You will hear "Power On" when it turns on and is ready to sync with a bluetooth device. There is a blue light that will blink from time to time during use. Volume can be raised/lowered by the buttons on the right earpiece. The current song selection can be skipped by holding the + sign down for a second (something they don't tell you in the instruction booklet). The charge jack is located at the bottom of the right earpiece and it comes with a charge cable that you can use in a USB port or attach to a wall outlet plug head.
Charge time: I get a good 4-6 workouts with these before I have to recharge. I workout for about 60-75 minutes / 5x a week so that should give you a good sense of charge life. Recharge time takes about 1 hour. A red light shows while it is charging and turns blue when done.
Sound: I have been using earplug style headphones for many years so I have a sense of what I consider good sound. I've used the likes of Sony, Skullcandy among other brands and I have to say that these Treblab headphones are on par with, or better than everything else I have used in the past. Sound is clear, bass is warm, clean and not overwhelming like some earphones can be. The noise cancellation on these is also great. You cant hear any gym grunters or annoying conversations while you enjoy your workout or whatever it is you are doing.
Bottom line: I have had these Treblabs now for over 3 months and can give them this proper review. The only thing I would have liked in these is a microphone, but at this price point, I really cannot complain. You are getting a great set of wireless bluetooth headphones that are probably the same quality as the name brand ones that go for 3x the price or more. Buy these. You will be happy and your wallet will be happy.

title: Excellent!
text:
I will jump straight to the point. Please keep in mind that I am not an audiophile, but do pursue better quality audio products where it matters.

* Size, Weight, Packaging: These full size over-the-ear headphones have moderate weight, a bit on the heavy side comparing to regular headphones but not much different from the weight of noise-cancelling or wireless over-the-ear phones. They are not portable and come with a custom-molded very nice black hard case with a zipper. Two cables are included: male-male 3.5" audio cable and a flat micro-USB cable for charging, as well as an RCA Y-to-3.5" adapter and a small instruction booklet.

* Comfort: The headband is a bit tight, but this keeps the phones tightly and securely positioned on your head. Absolutely no wobbling! The leather (or leather-like -- I am not sure exactly) material of covering the headband and ear cushions is nice and soft. It feels a bit hot around the ears after wearing them for about 1 hour, but not too uncomfortable.

* Sound Quality: I am more than satisfied with the range and the quality of the highs and lows. The sound feels "just right" -- very comfortably soft, not too high or crackling and not too low to the point of being boomy.

* Operation: The headphones hold the charge very well. To turn the power on and off, you will need to slide a switch, which is easy to slide with one finger. The power button is inconspicuously located on the outer side (not along the perimeter, as in some headphones), so it takes getting used to finding it by touch. This multi-function button is the only control element: you use it for pairing with a Bluetooth receiver as well. Every function -- turning on, off, going into pairing mode or having paired is confirmed by a distinct and pleasant sound in the headphones.

Pairing is a breeze. To make these headphones work with my TV and receiver, I have purchased from Amazon.com a Bluetooth transmitter by TaoTronics. Both work very well together, although after a few days of non-operation they needed to be re-paired. Pairing does not require entering any codes: just put both devices in discovery mode and they will magically pair in a few seconds. Pairing with an Android phone and iPad (both up-to-date with their system software) was just as easy and required no codes. If codes are required, a small instruction booklet included with the headphones lists them.

The shields on both sides are metal and come covered with protective film. I have noticed a bit of glue residue one one side after removing this film, and this is the only negative comment that I can make. In other words, I am very satisfied with these headphones.

Still connected via Bluetooth while silent they could turn up or down the volume on the device but no sound would play through the headphones even to say they were powering down. This happened about every 5 minutes and made using the headphones for any length of time impossible. I returned both pairs within a week of owning them after talking with customer service for days trying to reset the headphones numerous ways using unlisted button combinations, trying to update their firmware (there is none on Sony's website), power-cycling, and more. They died on me first thing one morning, and I had them charged enough for a couple weeks before I left for class in the time it took to brush, floss, get dressed, and make a light breakfast.
The sound quality is reasonable for most people, but audiophiles need not waste their money. They’re somewhat balanced, though a bit too light on the treble and bass for my taste. They claim you can use an app to adjust the eq settings but I couldn’t figure that out- the app said it didn’t include this model. They’re light, and don’t provide a lot of passive isolation.
The ANC mode on these is decent for ambient noise but not much else. For ambient, I’d say it is somewhere around an nrr=20, and for other sounds it’s approx 10.
They are reasonably sweatproof- though the pleather ear cushions are less than great when they’re sweaty. That’s not uncommon in this price range though.
I was very disappointed to find that, after less than a year of use, during which they were always on my head or in a hard case, the extendable portions of the band had horizontal cracks. These have not affected the sound quality in any way, but it’s disappointing to see. Sony can do better.

text:
I will say, I only just got these a few hours ago. But I've been through countless headsets trying to find something decent to be on the phone all day with. I've tried every kind out there--the one-sided style with a boom mic, traditional over the ear, tiny ear buds, ear buds that wrapped around the ear, even bone conduction. And I hated all of them. They were uncomfortable within an hour and my ear felt like it was going to fall off. These? I've had them on for 5 hours now and not only has the battery not dropped even a little bit, but I could seriously forget they're in my ear!

So far all the buttons have worked flawlessly, and the neck piece is nice and lightweight, doesn't feel like a collar around my neck. It's really easy to forget the whole thing is there. I love the retractable earbuds too--the last pair I had like this just dangled, and because I only ever use one side (so I can hear myself during phone calls, and my son running around) it was so annoying to have the other side just dangling around getting hung up on things.

The sound quality is okay. I don't know that they'd be the best thing ever for heavy music listening, though that's just personal discretion. It's honestly fine for phone calls, which is what I'll use them for 95% of the time anyways. So far, my girlfriend says the mic quality is fine. It does pick up a lot of background noise, but so did all the other options I tried. She said for some reason they process my toddler crying and being loud weirdly, but that it wasn't necessarily bad, just weird. She's been able to hear my voice super clearly, and in 5 hours they haven't tried to disconnect or do anything weird at all. I struggled with that issue with a lot of the other headphones I tried, and when privacy is important you can't have your headphones disconnecting every 2 seconds. Oh, and the volume is pretty damn good. They get louder than any of the previous pairs I've tried, so I can very clearly hear my phone calls with no issue.

Overall, so far I feel like they're a solid pair of headphones. I have no complaints, really. Pairing was simple, quality is solid. They came with a nice case, they fold down well without feeling like they'll snap apart. They're good headphones, and with the insane battery life I feel like I'll use the heck out of them.

I have only used two of the supplied cables and they were plugged into the same two ports continuously. I charge only cell phones, so there was no high current draw. It is not the sockets that wear out, as I installed the two cables the day it arrived and never unplugged them until they quit working. They just stopped charging. I switched the cables to the remaining ports and found three still functional. It would seem this is a consumable item with a limited lifespan. This is a great idea but I will buy standard chargers from now on that last forever.

***UPDATE*** After contacting customer service, I was advised to disconnect power to the charger for at least 5 minutes. Evidently there is an internal circuit breaker and after a few minutes it will reset. It worked for me. After 2 weeks of inoperable ports, my charger is once again fully functional.

text: I usually do not write negative reviews, unless there is a significant flaw in a product. These headphones only lasted six months before the inner part of the headband (where it should easily bend so as to fit any size heads, or almost) broke. I chatted with the assistance, they asked me if I had always used a case, which I did, despite the fact that these headphones did not come with one (I used one from an old pair of Bose of the same size); then they started blaming it on weather conditions, to which I replied these headphones had never left my home office. Then they just said this kind of damage could not be considered a result of defective material; I asked why and I asked for a list of what should then happen because of defective materials. They said this needed assistance from another team, who would contact me within 24 hours. Of course, nobody has called me. I am a musician and with dozens of headphones I used in my life, never a pair broke in the part in which the material should be the most resistant to make sure headphones fit different head sizes. Not even the pairs that my kids use for their schools ever broke in that spot. I wish a manufacturer of Sony's level would take these things more seriously. title: A closed back headphone that does well, surprised!
text:
As someone who has other headphones such as HD700 and AKG K712 the new addition to the family, M100 Wireless is a pretty decent one, nothing spectacular but why does it get 5 stars?

First, M100 is a closed back headphone and its not like audiophile headphones which are all open back, so in terms of what it does with a closed back, it gets 5.

Design: pretty good actually, sturdy and metallic. If you are one of those who likes form over function then go get one but if you prefer music quality and want to sit down and listen to music for a sessions then visit audiophile forums such as head-fi.org etc.

The sound: Once you get used to wider sound stage, its hard very had to like anything else so m100 is a-o-k to me, now remember, I am saying this from the perspective of open back headphones but for anyone else, specially for those who never had a quality headphone, this will be mind blowing experience. Lows, mids and highs are not all over powering each other. I tested few edm tracks with vocals, and they do amazing. I probably used it about 20 hours and so far its hasn't caused any frequency issues.

Comfort: I did change to XL pad, which gave a deeper and wider sound stage and much more comfort than the original. I recommend the change asap. The original gave my ears lobes some pain, it didn't go around the ear completely and felt too tight. The headband might needs to be stretched out to loosen it a bit. Again, comfort is nothing like the two other headphones I listed, they are miles ahead in comfort.

Bluetooth: Again, I do not recommend using it as it lowers quality of sound. I did notice the drop and just use wired, or maybe my source, note 4.

Last note, I am using this with fiio-e6 portable amp, do you need one? No. Over all, you won't be disappointed, I like mine for what it is, a closed back headphone that does pretty damn good, surprised!

It paired just as it's supposed to, and it was easy for me to interpret the LED activity, which is not always the case for someone with a color deficiency.
Sound quality is very good, but my experience with Bluetooth is that it doesn't provide the same perfect consistency that comes with a direct wired connection. Over the course of 3 hours of MP3 playback, I experienced 3 momentary silences (like a tenth of a second each), which I consider excellent performance.

title: Stylish, Great sound, slightly flimsy, ANC ain't bad
text:
Overall impression: The SoDrop pro is a pretty stylish quality alternative to high end head phones. The main drawbacks I have found is the shallow earcups and a design that feels premium in many ways but is to fragile for me to feel comfortable taking them out and about to much. If you plan on mostly using these at home or during a flight like I do this is very good. The noise cancelation doesnt do well with blocking out sudden sounds like snapping or talking which for the price point is fine to me because while it doesnt block it it does dampen it a bit. With consistent sounds like a laundry machine or an engine it does very well with blocking that out. On top of that there is hardly a hiss at all with the noise cancelation. They do hurt my ears a slight bit after a couple hours of use (I have ears that stick out a bit but a slim head for an adult btw) but it isnt unbearable. The base is pretty good and there is no distortion that I notice. I have used higher end headphones like bose, audio technica, I used the polk striker zx's for years and I can safely say these are worth the cost as long as you're not rough with them.

Sound: the sound is honestly on par with expensive brands like bose. It isnt a pure sound but it is a very enjoyable experience if you're not a purest. I tried a variety of songs with these from rap, pop, rock, chillstep, country, basically anything I could think of even screamo and deathmetal. It never got muddy and the sound staging was always good. Not amazing but I'd say 7 out of 10.

Multi functional: I use these on console and pc with a detachable boom mic and run software like Dolby atmos for surround sound. I got these actually because my steele series and skullcandy crushers got stolen but I'm not noticing any difference in how well I can differentiate where people are. These are very bulky btw. If you're like me and dont mind bulkiness these are stylish as hell!

title: Review Depends on Intended Use
text:
I typically wear just one earbud during the day while I listen to podcasts, and at night while I fall asleep. These earbuds are not a good choice for these purposes for two reasons.
1) There is no way to stabilize the other earbud or affix it to my clothes, so it dangles from my neck, and if I bend over, it attaches to anything metal it comes into contact with. 2) The volume change with each click on the device (including the slider on your device) is in huge increments, so there is no low volume to fall asleep to. When you reach the lowest volume, it is way too loud, even if you pull the earbud out from your ear. And if you click one notch lower, it is silent.
So I can use these to work out, with both in my ears at the same time, but I will revert to my prior brand when it comes to my day-to-day activities and falling asleep.

title: GREAT for active people!!!!
text: 09/06/2016 - I've had these for about 2 weeks, so I'll be sure to post an update in a little while to comment on longevity of this product.  So far, I really like this product.  These were packaged really well and were delivered on time.  I opened them and found that they had a slight charge right out of the box.  I believe in giving all electronic products with Lithium rechargeable batteries a full charge before using.  As advertised, these reach a full charge in around 2 hours.  Each charge so far has got me at least 9 hours of listening.  Primarily, these get used bike commuting back and forth to work and listening intermittently throughout the day.  With this, I get about 2-3 days out of a single charge!  The fit of these is perfect, but like other users, I find that the chord sticks to my neck and pulls on the earpiece.  Although it's recommended that these should be worn with the chord behind the neck, I find that I have much better luck with the wire worn in front, under my chin.  I find that wearing this way and the headphones stay put during workouts with almost zero readjusting.  The real magic with the fit of these things comes when I'm wearing a helmet (either biking, skateboarding, or rollerblading).  The earpieces do not protrude so far from my head that I can comfortably wear them underneath my helmet straps.  The straps give these a little extra staying power which is great when I'm ripping on my bike at 25mph into the wind.  These stay put and sealed!!!  Lastly, the sound quality is solid for these types of headphones.  Yes, I have a pair of Klipsch wired earbuds that sound better overall, but they fall out just sitting at my desk.  These definitely have a low mid-range boost that some may take for being a little muffled, but this actually works perfectly for me because I'm typically battling wind noise with volume.  While boosting the volume to battle wind noise, the highs are not harsh and the lows don't blow your ears out.  Overall, these are perfect for riding!  Oh, and to comment on volume, these have TONS of headroom!  I have yet to turn them up past half way and I like my music loud!  Overall, these are perfect for me and I would recommend them to anyone, especially people who listen while biking, running, skateboarding, rollerblading etc...

text:
Update: June 2017

I've been using this charger and cables for 13 months now, to charge 3 Kindle tablets and 3 Samsung phones. The charger continues to perform as advertised, and the cables have held up well.

The real problem is the connector area. To charge any device, you have to hold the connector in place for many seconds, and when it starts charging, slowly move your hand away. This doesn't always work, so we often spend 5–10 minutes to get a device charging. If multiple devices are charging, approach with caution, as touching one cable tends to wake all the devices up, and they stop charging. The connection is no longer snug after months of use. You simply cannot plug a device in, leave it for a few hours, and return to find it fully charged.

Of the 5 cables, one connector broke off after several months. On two of the cables, when you detach them from a device, the silver head becomes somewhat detached from the rest of the cable, and you have to push it back down.

All the challenges I've had with this product are due to the connectors.

The charging technology works great. My Samsung S5 goes from 5% to 100% in less than an hour. Tablets are fully charged in 2-3 hours. We received two incorrect cables (product description was wrong) and Anker quickly sent two additional cables. Initially the cables fit snugly/firmly in the ports with no wiggle. After a few months, they wiggle a bit but still get the job done.

title: Blah sound quality / slightly better anc / loss of app support
text:
Purchased these as an “upgrade” from their predecessor (700n) which I love, in the hopes that they’d add more to those headphones in the price range.
Well, there’s some pros and some cons — but ultimately returning them and sticking with my 700n’s. Also want to mention I’ve tried the 900n, the xm3 and xm4 as well — all of those were simply too big for my small head, and created too much of the “cabin pressure” feel and heat that they were not comfortable to wear and just not worth the cost for me.

Anyway, back to the 710n’s in comparison to the 700n’s:
Pros: lighter, maybe very slightly more comfortable to wear with a slightly better overall build quality, slimmer profile, better anc and a good ambient mode to let in outside sounds while listening to music.
The anc feel here does seem to be improved overall. If I was to rank the xm3/xm4 at a
10, I’d give these a 6, while the 700n’s would be a 5. Technically, it’s eANC which is more virtual and is supposed to constantly adapt to the surroundings to +/- on its own. Didn’t seem to change for me, or if was not noticeable if so. However, it did block out more sounds in comparison to the 700n’s where it was definitely noticeable.
The ambient mode is pretty good too — it lets in outside sounds enough to hear what’s going on. Finally we get usb-c, but they don’t seem to charge faster. Battery life is the same at 35 hrs. Call quality/mic sounded just about the same too, maybe a bit muddier but not worse enough to really note as either a pro or a con.

That’s about all the pros here: better and and the ambient mode itself.

Now, ahem —
Cons: sadly, there’s way too many trade offs here. The plastic feels really cheap, especially the buttons. I found them to be not pronounced enough that I would have to feel around to find them if that makes sense. They removed the rocker from 700n (which was perfect with form and function to me).
The sound quality — wow what a let down. I don’t know what they were thinking, but the audio profile is completely muddy and bass heavy to the point that mids and highs are not clear at all. Compared to the 700ns which sounded brilliantly clear and balanced to me — these are just awful.
Sony dropped app support for the 710ns which baffles me, so there’s no way to adjust eq to try and fix the sound eq or adjust anc/ambient levels/ update firmware. The 700ns have app support and the sound was fully customizable — even though it didn’t need changes for me. Again — why?!

I don’t know why there so many trade offs here. I was really hoping they’d build on the 700n to add what could be improved.

For me, ultimately the slightly better anc and ambient sound was just not enough to cover for the truly “blah” sound quality and loss of app support — especially from having a reference point against the 700n predecessor.

title: Still my favorite after 6 years and dozens of earbuds.
text:
These are still my favorite earbuds after all these years.
I've owned every model of this line, MDEX58, MDRX61, MDRX100, and MDRX110 is the current generation model of the "$30 MSRP" Sony earbud.
They sound spectacular. No other earbud that I've tried under $100 comes close to providing the highs that these do. The sound quality is relatively flat from the lowest bass to the highest highs. They aren't bass enhanced, but they do provide adequate deep, mid, and high bass as well as even mids and highs. They come with 3 different sizes of silicone earpieces and 3 sets of memory foam earpieces as well. I like how each set changes the tonality of the music. They do a very good job with noise cancellation but put out a bit of noise that people around me can hear with the volume up. Not a big deal in my world but something to mention. Haven't pushed the battery time fully as they are advertised with having around 9 hours possible on a charge. I've worn them for 6 hours once and the fit and comfort was outstanding with not a drop of performance during that time or a reduction in volume level.

Overall I'm super happy with my purchase and highly recommend these to anyone looking for an inexpensive set of earbuds (but you don't get cheap quality) because I think you'll be pleasantly surprised with your purchase. text:
I’ve been holding out for a set of new earbuds for a while, and I’m glad I found this set. Last month I nearly jumped for a pair of Apple EarPods when this very site had them on special, but many review sites consistently mentioned Earpod’s mediocre sound (even for earbuds). So I found myself taking a chance on this set, which lets be honest, could pass for the Apple product based on appearance, and I am glad that I did.

The earbuds arrived wrapped well and in a sturdy, attractive box that should hold up to reasonable bumps and bangs. The box contained the earbuds, silicone covers x 1 pair, a charger/storage case, instructions, and a USB-A to USB-C charger cord. I was impressed that the earbuds case/charger used an USB-C plug, as most newer rechargeable devices now utilize this connection to allow for faster charging, and Android has had Apple on the ropes for years with their chargers.

The earbuds arrived partially charged, and when I placed them in the charger, they were at full capacity within half an hour. The case can be recharged without the earbuds inside, and based on my first couple of recharges, it seems to hold enough power for 3-4 recharges.

The headphones were lightweight and comfortable but here’s the kicker - they stayed in place. I put on some metal and did as much head banging as my 47 year old neck would allow, which wasn’t much, but these things stayed put.

The sound. (!) I know next to nothing about earbud speaker technology, but I know when music sounds clear and crisp. They handled the continuum of sound from base on up really well, and vocals weren’t drowned out by instruments. Now, these are not over the head earphones that completely cup the ears, but they deliver as good a sound as any earbuds I’ve tried, and some headphone sets. Operation was intuitive and commands are given by gentle touches to the earbud itself (no buttons). Well worth the price. 10/10. Would head bang with these again.

title: Great for the Price
text:
Overall verdict - Even with my sensitive hearing, I feel these are very good for the money, especially if on sale or discounted in some way. The sound stage is very good, though maybe slightly exaggerated, and the instruments are reproduced well. These earphones sound best with less-dense music. When there are several layers, you lose some detail and bass, and sometimes get some faint distortions. They will not replace more expensive wired options or proper headphones, but they are good for on-the-go, a workout, or an inexpensive backup.

My review is going to follow the same format as if you were opening this package for yourself. I’ll be sure to bring up any concerns that I have as we walk through the packaging and use of the product.

Packaging:

These headphones come with fairly minimalistic packaging. The box is shrink-wrapped. Once removed, the thin cardboard sleeve slides away to reveal the case with molded plastic packaging sitting inside a thicker, sturdier cardboard. The packaging seems nice enough, however I did notice the light weight.

Contents
Ear buds in charging case

These items are under the molded plastic packaging:
Extra small and large tips (1 set of each)
Charging cable
Instructions
FAQ sheet

The case with the headphones inside is incredibly light, so it is not the most expensive-feeling set. The ear buds sit inside the case with the help of a magnet, which helps to align them properly with the charging prongs.

I tested the power upon opening the package and the left bud powered on while the right one did not. The recommended charging voltage is 5 volts. I plugged the charging cable in to a standard iPhone charging brick (5v) to charge. The charging cable ends in a USB cable, so most standard charging bricks should work, but just mind the voltage. The charging cable is extremely short, so you will need to be close to an outlet for charging purposes.

While charging, there is a separate LED for each bud that illuminates red while charging. There is also a center LED that illuminates green once fully charged. At the brick-end, the charging brick stayed cool while the case-end of the cable became warm to the touch, though not too hot. I always recommend being careful with cheaper electronics, as cheaper electrical components inside the devices can be a potential fire risk.

The packaging claims that these earphones have about 4 hours of playing time and a range of 10m, or approximately 33 feet. The product is made in China. The packaging shows the CE marking, which, according to Wikipedia, “is the manufacturer's declaration that the product meets EU standards for health, safety, and environmental protection.” The packaging also claims RoHS certification, which means that the product does not contain or use hazardous materials listed by the European Union. If true, these would all be good product attributes.

After approximately 30 minutes, the LEDs turned green and then went turned off. I removed the earphone from the case and the LED on the right earphone began to illuminate in blue and red. On the bluetooth devices setting in my iPhone, T20 showed up immediately and paired without an issue.

Spotify played without an issue or any sort of lag. I was pleasantly surprised by the sound quality. While listening to music at an extremely low volume (about 25%), I was unable to hear my typing on my laptop or the air conditioning, so there seems to be a good measure of sound isolation here. The stock tips fit in my ear quite well, so be sure to try different sizes if you do not feel like there is adequate isolation.

Walking through my house, the bluetooth stayed connected. I had zero issues.

I next ran the headphones through a few different genres.

Folk/Acoustic - For Elliott Smiths’ “Either/Or,” the bass presence of the acoustic guitars came across a bit more than the treble when compared to my flatter-EQed (and much more expensive) Audio Technica M150x wired headphones. I think this sort of quieter music is where these earphones shine, as the music came across clear and I felt like the songs sounded quite detailed.

Alternative Rock - On Radiohead’s “Electioneering,” these earphones reproduced the stereo image quite successfully. It felt a little muddier in the midrange with two guitars, vocals, drums, and bass going on.

Indie - Cloud Tapes “Beyond Innocence.” This is my own band, so I know a lot more about how the track was mixed and produced. The album overall had a higher bass presence, which I hear reproduced in these ear phones. This was also one of the tracks that sounded quite good in these earphones.

Classic Rock - On Led Zeppelin’s “Rock and Roll,” I felt like the bass was actually a bit quiet while the other instruments and vocals were very present. The drums sounded slightly distorted in the chorus, however, once again, the panned guitars in the solo sounded great.

Hip-Hop/Rap - On Eyedea’s “Smile,” the music sounded pretty good, and I could notice the sort of “lo-fi” static sounds produced in the track that I hadn’t noticed before. The instrumentation came across fairly well, though I felt like the bass was a bit lacking.

Hip-Hop/Rap - On Scarface’s “No Tears,” the bass sounded more balanced, and the track sounded very good overall. No issues at all here.

Country - On Gram Parsons' “Return of the Grievous Angel," the instruments all came through quite clearly. Gram and Emmy Lou’s harmonies sounded great. I felt like I lost the bass a bit once the other instruments came in. These headphones reproduced the high end of slide guitar quite well.

Oldies/Jazz - On Billie Holiday’s “I’ll Be Seeing You,” I could hear some of the artifacts of the track’s age, as I could certainly tell it had been ripped from a vinyl source. The track sounded a bit heavier on bass.

Metal - On “Scream Aim Fire” by Bullet For My Valentine, the guitars sounded very good, though I did feel like I lost the bass in the mix. To be fair, metal bass can be a bit more on the treble side in terms of tone. The vocals were reproduced well and weren’t distorted when the vocals were screamed. But I came here for the guitar solo, and it sounds GREAT! The sound stage reproduced the panned guitar harmonies as well.

Classical - Well, this is more of an organ piece, but it is one of my favorites—Julius Reubke’s “Sonata on the 94th Psalm.” These earphones reproduced the dynamics of the organ quite well.

Electronic - On Joy Electric’s “Drum Machine Joy” sort of synth-pop track, I felt the electronic instrumentation was reproduced pretty accurately. Some of the track’s high-end came through a bit more than I’d generally prefer, and I felt like there was a bit of a loss of detail when the track became very layered.

Overall, I was quite impressed with the sound quality of these earphones. I felt that the spacing in the sound stage was possibly a bit exaggerated, and there were moments in dense instrumentation where I felt I could hear some distortions of the drivers, but if I was in the middle of running or working, I most likely wouldn’t notice it. For an inexpensive option or backup, I would definitely recommend these.

Just a moment to talk about SAR Ratings and Radiation….

One thing that is always of concern to me with products such as these is the SAR, or Specific Absorption Rate. This is the rate at which the body will absorb energy when exposed to an electromagnetic field. Over the years, various sources have claimed that wireless products such as bluetooth headphones can cause illness within the body (namely cancer) due to the way in which the body absorbs allegedly DNA-damaging energies from the electromagnetic fields produced by the wireless technology.

I did have a professor once tell me that the waves produced by these fields are generally too large to penetrate cells and cause damage. This is the difference between ionizing and non-ionizing radiation.

In addition, scientific research does not support the idea that cell phone has caused an increase in illness. One would expect that the massive growth of cell phones would lead two massive increases in irregular cell growth. The data, however, does not show this.

Evidence has been incredibly inconsistent with various studies claiming that high exposure can cause cancer, cell damage, or other issues while others are unable to reproduce these effects. When this occurs, it can suggest there are numerous other factors at play—environment, individual health, etc.

I did contact the manufacturer regarding this product’s SAR rating, but I have not yet heard back as of the time of writing. In short, good practice is to avoid extended listening times with devices such as these. For me, I intend to use them while working out, or maybe in moments where it’s more convenient than a wired device. Generally, both due to sound quality and concerns about radiation exposure, I tend to stick to wired options.

title: Went through a dozen headphones before crowning the HD1/Momentum 2.0 king...
text:
First, the HD1 headphones are simply the newer renamed version of the Momentum 2.0. Beginning in 2017, Sennheiser was forced to market the Momentum 2.0 under a new name, because it was found out that somebody else held the copyright to the name Momentum in the U.S. So, the Momentum 2.0 that is still for sale as "new" on Amazon is an older production run that ended in 2016, with some as old as 2014! If you're wondering what year your headphones were produced, look at the first four numbers of your serial number on the box. For example, 0445xxxxxx would indicate that your headphones were manufactured the 44th week of 2015.

I've tried or owned A LOT of other competitor headphones: Bang & Olufsen H6 (2nd gen), Bowers and Wilkins P7 and P9, Beyerdynamic DT-770 and Custom One Pro, V-Moda Crossfade M100, ATH-MSR7, Sony MDR-1A, etc... With the HD1 you finally have a pair of headphones that has clear, prominent and detailed MIDRANGE, while also having a fantastic bass response, crisp treble presence, clarity, and imaging. With the midrange response on the HD1, vocals and other instruments sound more immediate and clear. Literally all other headphones I tried annoyingly scoop out the midrange response (usually around 1k) a few dB, with V-shaped EQs endeavoring to make the bass and treble response SEEM more impressive than it is. As a result vocals and instruments in that frequency range (like guitars) sound more distant and undefined on other headphones.

Lastly, you absolutely don't need an EQ or preamp with these headphones. Some audiophile types use pre-amps, DACs, and EQ to get the most out of high-end headphones, but I don't like to involve that kind of complexity. I want to just plug a great-sounding pair of headphones into ANY device (like my phone) and get an outstanding frequency response, fullness, and resolution. The HD1 does this all brilliantly. All while being very comfortable, providing outstanding passive sound-isolation, using genuine leather and looking very cool.

User jerake summed up the characteristics of these headphones quite well, so I won't rehash what he said. His review is what took me to take a chance on these headphones and I am super pleased, so I just want to add my experience.

These are sport headphones so I am looking for good fit and durability first. I was getting frustrated after wearing out my third set of $100 Sennheisers. After about 12-14 months one side would stop working properly and I'd have to replace them again. Remembered some indestructible Philips headphones I still have from 10 years ago, so I gave these a shot.

I wear them for an hour a day at the gym and have been super impressed with the fit, comfort, and sound of these headphones. Liked them so much I've already got a second pair on order to keep in my motorcycle saddlebag. The highs sound almost as good as the Senns costing 5x as much, and the bass response on the Philips is much better. Can't imagine buying anything different for rugged use after my experience so far. Go for it.

title: They are a good option for the price
text:
Recently I have been testing out different Bluetooth options for use with my phone. Up until recently I was happy with my cheap, wired headphones, but they tend to get caught on things when exercising which all I need them for.
I gave the Tozo T10S just three stars across the board simply because in every measurement they were average. However, compared to the other's at this price point I have tested this set compared quite well.
Starting with the case they come in it was the easiest to hold and open to get the 'phones out. The other's were too rounded, or small, making them difficult to grip when trying to access the contents. the latch was also easy to use while others required a either a great deal more effort or force to open them.
The design of the 'phones are not much different than the others in that they are relatively easy to grasp and have a familiar shape. The shape is the oval type with a flat control face that sits in the ear comfortably. I was I was able to use these for almost two hours without feeling pain in my average sized ears. If you have large ears they might feel loose, which is a big issue, and if you have smaller ears than it's likely these will be uncomfortably tight, perhaps painful.
The control face for pairing, music controls, etc. is too sensitive. Any time I brushed across them accidently, or while adjusting their fit, they would pause or change the music, or book I was listening to. Since the entire face is a control panel it's difficult to grasp these without touching that control area.
One thing that surprised me was the audio quality. Definitely not high quality, but it was decent. I tested them against my cheap and expensive wired headphones as well as the other inexpensive Bluetooth sets I have. While they don't reach the same level as the wired 'phones they sounded better than the other three wireless sets I've been testing which all seem to have a dull, muffled quality to them.
The thing I didn't like about the Tozo T10S is stability in the ear. After only a day of cycling these almost fell out of my ear three times. The fourth time they did and I lost one of them. It's a shame since I had started to use them around the house to listen to my music and books when doing chores or cooking.
I would have like to have spent more time with these, but since one part is lost I can only give my impression based on a couple of days use. In that short time I did grow to like them and wish the design fit better and didn't fall out of my ear so easily.

Update:
Forgot these were in the pocket of my safety vest I wear when cycling and put them in the wash.
They still work. :| Washed, dried and still work. That's impressive.

title: They Are Now Sweat Resistant!
text:
[[VIDEOID:4a481846ce6582e770f2f3c90c96ed87]] I bought these headphones specifically for using at the gym, as they are the only ANC BT Over-Ear headphones that I could find with an IPX rating of any sort (even if it's only a 4). The first day, they worked fantastic for the whole 2.5 hours I was at the gym. The noise canceling kills all but the sound of people slamming weight stacks or dropping weights. When I first turned them on, with no music playing, it's as if someone hit "Mute" on the world. The sound quality was great... for the price. Think, better than my $100 earbuds, but not as good as my $250 over-ear cans.
The second day I used them, the right side started crackling and popping after about an hour or so. I thought that it was an issue with sweat and the ANC microphones, because turning the ANC off would stop the noise. I used them a few more times to see if it would persist, and it did. Last night I used them for the first time outside of the gym; dry, if you will. After about an hour it started crackling and popping again. I'm sending this set back to get a replacement from Amazon and if they have any issues after a week or two, I'll return them and get back to my search for some Over-Ear ANC BT headphones that are gym-safe.
A couple of side notes:
- I've used them for about 11hrs, altogether, in the 2 weeks I've had them and they still say "Battery High" when prompted.
- The touch controls are sporadic, at best. Sometimes they will pause with a tap. SOMETIMES, they will volume up or down with a vertical swipe. SOMETIMES, they will skip songs. If you aren't prepared to use your phone for controls, steer clear.

I'll update this review in a couple weeks, as to whether or not the replacements worked properly. I hope so, because I genuinely like these... when they work right.

Update - 5/3/2022:
So the second set worked fine for the 2 hours I worked out yesterday... until I was standing at the entrance of the gym to leave. The right side started crackling and popping again. :(
Today, they started doing it again after about 25 minutes. As, with the first pair, turning off the ANC stops the noises. I remembered to record a quick clip of them popping this time, and that they stop, when the ANC is turned off.
This sucks; I really like these headphones, but for $150 I can get something better without the ANC that I can't even use.

Update - 12/20/2022
I randomly got an email from the Treblab customer support yesterday telling me that they found and fixed the issue that was causing my problems with these headphones. They are sending me another pair to try and I will post up later whether they WORK OUT (😂sorry, I had to) or not. Always a nice rarity to see good customer service. 👍🏻

Update:
I spent 2 hours in the gym Tuesday and 2 hours tonight, sweating like a pig in the Hormel parking lot. They are fixed! The hole that the CS rep mentioned being fixed, by the ANC mics, apparently was the problem after all. The new set I have hasn't had any issues yet. That's with 5-6 hours around the house and 4 hours sweating like crazy. Actually It was also pouring down rain when I went in and out of the Gym Tuesday, with them around my neck. I gave back the 2 stars. Good stuff! 👍🏻

title: Nice headphones but a lousy unboxing experience
text:
These Sony WHCH710N noise-cancelling over-the-ear headphones boast a 35-hour battery life with quick charging, 30mm drivers with active noise-cancellation and Bluetooth with NFC connectivity.

What I liked most about these Sony WHCH710N noise-cancelling over-the-ear headphones was:
- The sound. I admit to being initially skeptical of these cans because of the 30mm drivers as most of my favorite over-ear-headphones have 40mm+ drivers but the sound coming out of these is big and immersive. While not the richest or most nuanced sound you can find for 200 dollars this headset has a nice separation of mids and highs with deep, punchy bass. There's even a hint of soundstage, but this is much more muted with these cans than others in this product line.
- Battery life. Opting for 30mm drivers allows Sony to give users longer battery life. While 35 hours might be possible if you keep your headset at 50% volume without ANC activated, I was able to get 25-27 consistently with the cans cranked up to 75% most of the time. I used ANC roughly a third of the time I had my cans on.
- Active noise-cancelling and sound isolation. These cans have sufficient clamping force to drown out a good deal of background noise without activating noise-cancelling. Once you activate noise-cancelling you have the choice of allowing some sound in or toning it out at this headset's maximum capacity with Sony suggests is about 75%.
- Easy NFC pairing. Once you've paired a headset via NFC you'll never, ever want to do it the old fashioned way again. With NFC pairing, even if the headset is off, aligning your source device's NFC chip with the NFC insignia on these headphones will turn them on and automatically pair them.

What I liked least about these Sony WHCH710N noise-cancelling over-the-ear headphones was:
- The unboxing experience. These headphones were boxed in a brown cardboard box and wrapped in cheap plastic. They included cheap charging and audio cables, nothing else. I was quite underwhelmed at what Sony offers customers who 'only' spend $200.00 with them. I felt almost as if the company wanted me to thank them for letting me buy their tech for such a low price.
- No app support. A key way Sony intentionally detracts from this headset is by not supporting it within its app. This means there are no granular controls to access for ANC, acoustic settings, and the like.
- No carrying case. Amazon sells hundreds of headphones for less than 200 bucks with many of them having active noise-cancelling onboard and some have cases. No excuse for a 200 dollar headset to ship without one.

Overall, while I was pleased with the sound quality, noise-cancelling, and battery life of these Sony WHCH710N, I was somewhat disappointed by the pauper treatment you get in the unboxing experience. Combine that with glaring omissions to app support and a carrying case and I am left conflicted about these cans. If you want a jack-of-all-trades headset that is just good enough in every area to warrant regular usage, the Sony WHCH710N should make your list. However, I think you'll find offerings within this price range that exceed expectations in areas that might be most important to you and don't offer the compromises Sony seemingly built into this model to keep it from cannibalizing sales of their flagship cans. 3.5 out of 5.0 stars.

title: Lasted 7 months
text:
The headphones lasted from when i purchased them in July 2018 until March 2019 when they just stopped working. This did not include any type of drop or anything that imparted any force on the headset. They simply were charged overnight and the next morning died within about a half hour of use. After charging them again, they never went back into a functioning state. I am assuming this was due to an issue with the circuit board of the system as the power button stopped being responsive and the orange switch light is on at all times, even with the switch in the off position.

This pair of headphones was taken pretty good care of and was mainly used for conference calls, so outside of being at my desk, they didn't see much action. Unfortunately, if these are purchased (even new) from any non-authorized reseller, the product is not covered by their warranty. The warranty center was fast and courteous to receive and correspond to me about this, and even provided the option of purchasing a new product from their site at a 50% discount via their immortal life program. They did not provide the option of repairing the product for a fee though, so the only option was to purchase a new set. This was my second pair of V-Moda headphones, and while the older ones are not wireless, they have held up for several years. They will also be the last V-Moda product I purchase for obvious reasons.

The headphones were actually comfortable to use and delivered good sound for daily use. They weren't really noise cancelling, but did do a good job of muffling most of the noise i would hear on a daily basis. They were also comfortable to have on for about 2-3 hours before i did end up having to take a break. The only real drawback was that the microphone was not great and made my voice sound a bit muffled.

title: Lower Your Expectations!
text:
I got these on sale and was pretty stunned when I opened the box and held them in my hands. They felt and looked very cheap. Really cheap. If I'd paid full price, I probably would have boxed them up and sent them back without even trying them. That's how flimsy they felt. But as I said, they were on sale (even at that moment I still felt overcharged), I decided to give them a fair try.

The first thing that surprised me was they felt very comfortable. Very light weight and I thought I could wear them comfortably for a long while. Okay, that's nice.

But things broke down quickly after that. They sound was not very sharp and the noise canceling seemed very minimal. I know these are not top of the line, but I'd think the noise canceling would at least be superior to my Corwin headphones that cost a 3rd less then the regular price.

Still, I wanted to give them a fair try and I did like the feel. But it never they never grew on me. In fact, I liked them less as time went on. I wore them on while walking my dog and more then once I heard them squeak as I turned my head or leaned down. And that was pretty much it. If headphones themselves make noise, what is the point of having noise canceling headphones?

I'm not saying these are the worst headphones out there, but I think a realistic (and more fair) price is around $50, not nearly $200

Sony, if you're going to make real budget headphones, price them at what they're really worth.

One point for comfort, one point for ease of use.

title: Very good for the price I got them for
text:
My wife got these for me for Father's Day. I've had a pair of Bose AE2 (wired only, no noise cancelling) since 2014, so that's what I'll be comparing these to.

The Sony headphones have a more satisfying, deeper bass, so unlike with the Bose, I can actually use the default graphic equalizer setting on my DAP. With the Bose I found myself having to reset the equalizer setting to maximize bass. The highs are not as bright as on the Bose. Besides that, my ears can't detect any other differences in sound quality.

I got the blue tooth to work, but the volume levels were super low compared to when they were wired. I actually listen to them wired most of the time, so not a big deal. However, the aux cable that came with these headphones was a foot too short for my liking.

The headphones themselves are bulkier on the ears than the Bose, and I can't sleep with them on, which is a bummer because I fall asleep faster with music playing.

As with the Bose, these headphones get very warm when worn outside at temperatures in the 70s or more, especially in direct sunlight.

The noise cancelling feature could be better. As has already been noted, it gets rid of low frequencies pretty well, but other frequencies not so well. The sound quality with noise cancelling off is just as good as when it's on, which I like a lot.

Overall, at $140, I'd say these are an upgrade

title: Two Words - Value and Quality
text:
If you have 3-5 devices that need charging, this hub will be perfect for you!
I purchased this hub, needing a way to manage an increasingly cluttered desk area filled with hungry devices. With multiple devices that needed charging, each with a different level of attention needed while charging, I thought I would take a chance and buy one of these hubs. With the price and quality of Micro-USB cords being wildly different from company to company, the added "pack" of cables made this a good deal from the get-go.
The product is packaged in a simple, no-nonsense way that isn't cheap, but doesn't make you have to break out a pocket knife to get at the goods. I have found this to be the case with most Anker products. The hub itself is substantial and solid, but can stand on its side to take up minimal space on the desk top.
The thing that makes me really love this package is the varying lengths of cables. I am lucky enough to have a phone, a tablet, and a watch that need charging at virtually the same time. However, having access to my charging phone (being able to pick it up and not yank the hub off the desk) is important, whereas the watch and the tablet can generally stay on the surface and mind their own business. The 1 foot cables are great for the little things that can stay out of the way, while the longer cables are for the workhorses. It doesn't seem like much, but an organizer like me will totally dig the choice.
The Power IQ technology is something that I haven't seen before in charging stations, and it's a cool feature. Some devices take a heavier "draw" on a power supply, and can charge much more quickly with a higher amperage. The hub knows essentially what it is charging and powers heavy draw devices with more amps, while giving the little guys less juice. I don't know if this will save me money in the long run, but I know that when I plug my phone in, it charges fully in minutes.
One last thing that a person that fiddles with devices all day would appreciate. The Micro-USB connectors FIT THE DEVICES. They click into place and stay there. I've had OEM parts from Samsung that are wiggling in the port when connected and making my phone chirp over and over when it gets moved on my desk. The Anker plugs snap right in and hold on for dear life. You'll pull the hub off the table before the plug will pop out.
All in all, my five-star rating is for a solid, affordable product with a lot of thoughtful features. Good price, good quality, and good design. Worth every penny, and indicative of the Anker brand.
Enjoy!

title: Was a bit worried with the reviews, but they've worked great so far
text:
This product is a prime example of when the consumer is not always right. To me, it's also a lesson, that you cannot always put full trust in these reviews.
They might not be the most "neutral" headphones, but there are plenty of choices for that route around this price point. Ive owned a pair of AKG K701's since 2013, and I find music incredibly neutral with an enormous sound stage, so I will opt to use them if that's what I'm looking for at the time. Just like these Sony headphones, although maybe moreso with the AKG's, you'll have best results driving them both with a competent amplifier.

It strikes me as a bit odd that so many reviews complain about the sound quality, when the headphones are likely driven by their phone and nothing else. As with most speaker/headphones, the more you're able to drive these below the point of distortion, the more you
will likely hear better sound . My Yamaha a-s501 integrated amp does very well with these, and they absolutely serve the purpose (playing drums along to music) that they were intended for.

Just wanted to write this up, because I do like these headphones a great deal, and I think tech ignorance on behalf of the average consumer is largely responsible for the bulk of the bad reviews for this product. People are quick to jump in and say tHeSe sOuNd liKE cRaP. It couldn't have anything to do with the fact that the power being fed to them from your smartphone is mediocre, at best. Reviewers take no responsibility in the fact that many of their issues are at least partially due to good old user error.

EDIT: for the past few months, I've also started using these when my dog and I go for walks. I've had him for about 3 months now,and try to walk him everyday. And the headphones have been on the same charge. What's more, the talking lady says the battery is still fully charged! The picture was taken during one of said walks.During this time, I've also taken a few calls. Upon asking if I sounded okay, they responded in the affirmative. I haven't seen much difference in the ambient/noise canceling modes, but I also haven't tried very hard. I suspect that it will probably be more noticeable when they are driven properly.

title: Can The T10S Take Out The TOZO NC2?
text:
[[VIDEOID:cc75227daed0095b2ab609f43bee89f3]] I am very new to the world of wireless earbuds, and I needed something for a plane trip. After a brief bit of research, I decided on the TOZO NC2 earbuds, which I purchased on August 17. I absolutely fell in love with the NC2 and their snug fit, crisp and clear sound, deep bass, and amazing ANC that completely blocked all the ambient noises in the plane cabin. So, two weeks later I saw the T10S available as a Vine product and immediately jumped on them. But, in my haste, I didn’t catch the fact that the T10S utilizes ENC (Environmental Noise Canceling) technology, not ANC (Active Noise Canceling). A simplistic way of explaining the differences in these two technologies is that ENC removes ambient noises from signals being transmitted by the microphone (outgoing), and ANC removes ambient noises from signals being heard through the speakers (incoming).

Even without ANC, the T10S still does an admirable job of blocking ambient noises due to the tight seal of the comfortable and soft silicone earpieces, and they performed very well in my “leaf blower” test. My “test” is to simply fire up my cordless leaf blower while listening to some music, preferably while my ground AC unit is also running. The music was plenty loud and very clear without the need to max out the volume, and they were a lot closer to the NC2 in keeping all this racket out of my ears than I expected. Unlike the bass-heavy sound of the NC2, the T10S puts more emphasis on the high and mid ranges. For those that want more bass (like me), the sound can be easily tweaked through the 10-channel equalizer in the simple and user-friendly TOZO app. There are 16 presets to chose from, and, of course, any of them can be customized to the listener’s personal preferences. Unfortunately, I found that no amount of tweaking can get the T10S to output anywhere near the levels of highly gratifying deep bass that the NC2 does. A feature that is missing from the T10S that I really like in the NC2 is the pause feature when one of the earbuds is removed. I know that a single tap will pause the T10S, but “pull out to pause” is just so convenient.

The T10S is tough to recommend when they are currently $3 more than the NC2. They have a nice style, great and comfortable fit, solid and high-quality case, and a great equalizer app. But, price, low bass levels, and no ANC make it a no-brainer to get the NC2. If someone just wanted basic, but good quality earbuds, and the T10S was $20 or less, then that’s a pretty good buy. But, as it currently stands, it’s NC2 all the way. Be impressed, or for $3 less, be REALLY impressed.
