title: Nice Headset!
text:
I have had an opportunity to use the Icomtofit Bluetooth headset for a few weeks now. I have used it during many activities, exercising, in the car, at home, and while teleconferencing. Overall, my experience has been very good. It is comfortable, easily pairs with two devices at once, has a long battery life, has clear loud audio output and a sensitive microphone.
Details:
It comes with 6 different sized silicone ear gels. After trying all the inserts, I found the smallest felt the most secure. It inserted the deepest into my ear canal and did not feel too loose, and held the microphone in one position. I adjusted the retractable section on the ear piece frame and this improved the comfort level by 10x! I was able to do a strenuous 40-minute workout on my elliptical with no issues. It held in place, and I was able to clearly heard my music through the ear piece
I was concerned about the sound level, but the level was more than adequate. The quality of the sound was very good in the G3 stereo mode. It has a balanced sound with good bass response and clear upper frequencies. It plays loud without much distortion or being overly shrill.
My in-car experience was satisfactory. I was able to hear phone calls better than with my Alpine car stereo interface. The Icomtofit microphone was clear with much less ambient noise than the in-car microphone.
The button ergonomics were very good. The buttons are easily accessed, without touching the wrong buttons. The volume, mute and MFB (Multi Function Button) worked as designed. The volume control had good level granularity, so it was easy to set a comfortable sound level.
The Bluetooth Pairing is straightforward. It easily pairs with both of my Apple Iphone 8 and Iphone Xs max and my Lenovo desktop computer. No Drama there. Having the ability to dual pair is great, as often I carry my personal phone and my work phone. The Bluetooth range is good. At my home, I can walk around 20-30 ft without any issues. Considering I have a myriad of other BT devices, keyboards, mice, speakers, this is more than adequate.
The battery life is very good. I ran various tests for about a week, before I finally got the charge beep reminder. On my Iphone, there is a battery level indicator. Nice feature.
Cons:
After using this for a week, I can find very few items that really need to change. Maybe a verbal announcement that battery needs charging would be nicer instead of a beep.
All in all, it is a super nice headphone with a very attractive price and great customer service.

I have an original pair of T10 earbuds and the sound quality has been great and the touch controls have been responsive. The T10S pair is no different, but have been updated to work with Tozo's new app which finally lets me tweak the EQ to my liking, so now I can push lows or highs a little when needed depending on my environment. I've only had these for a couple days now, so can't speak to battery life, but I suspect they'll be just as good as the original T10 pair.

My single minor complaint is the size of the charging case. It is about twice the size as one of my other favorite tozo earbuds - the NC2. That's not enough to take off a star as I suspect battery life of the charging case will be an advantage with the size. So, when I want a pair that will live in my pocket all day when I'm on the go, the NC2 will probably still be my go to set, but the T10S will take over for my normal T10 and will be my go to for wearing around the house now and my old T10 pair will be passed on to my daughter.

They also come with a wide assortment of silicone ear pieces so you can be sure to get a proper fit which is necessary to get the best sound quality and isolation from external sounds. Another nice feature is the cover of the charging case is a semi transparent so you can easily see the charging status as well. Overall, very pleased and highly recommend!

title: Extremely cheap components for large amounts of money
text:
I really really really wanted to love these headphones. I really did. I have been looking for the perfect pair of Sleeping headphones, and these are very far from the best.

Take note; I have tried every type of these, the wired ones, the wireless ones, and now these "effortless" ones.

The wired ones were probably the best, as there is no battery to worry about. The issue is that the cable broke within a few months. I'm not sure what they expect, as you move around when you sleep, that cable is going to get bent. Bulk up that cheap cable.

The wireless one was awful because taking out the component to charge it was an incredible hassle. Most cheap wireless headbands just have a cable that pokes out and you plug it in there, the sleephones you have to take the entire wireless unit out, unplug it from the headphones, and plug it in to a cable.

So after not wishing to deal with that, I decided to go with the "effortless" ones. And oh boy was that a mistake. They advertise these to last 12 hours on one charge. And they did! The first couple of nights, I didn't exactly sleep for that long, but one night I decided to sleep a bit early, and they lasted an entire 13 hour bed session. Awesome! Then, a few days later, I tried sleeping early again, and they died in the middle of my sleep, within about 8 hours. Now, the next night, as I'm writing this, they did not even last 6 hours. They don't even last a proper amount of sleep, and I think I know why.

Induction charging is notoriously bad. It wastes a ton of energy, and gets very hot. I decided to check the unit while it was charging, and it was incredibly hot. This thing is burning its poor battery to smithereens. Clearly they did not test this at all. I don't even know how anyone can give this a positive review. Sleep headphones should last AS LONG as a normal sleep schedule. This was an extreme waste of $150

The sound quality is fine. They are comfortable tho I do wish they covered your eyes, you can spin them around tho and you can put the larger part over your eyes. However battery life is an absolute joke. I bought these like 2 weeks ago and they already don't even last 6 hours. This is pretty much a scam.

title: I Use Them Daily but they Make me Crazy
text:
I wanted some bluetooth head phones for use with my iPad around the house so that I don't have to subject the rest of my family to my tech podcasts. These headphones have been great to fill that bill. However, for a few minutes after they connect they seem to be out of sync and the audio drops out for about 10 seconds at random times. This causes me a lot of frustration in rewinding so that I don't miss anything. After a while the dropouts cease but every once in a while they creep back in. It is not enough to brand the headphones unusable but it is annoying. Many times the press to pause command from the headphones won't work either and I have to close the headphones and reopen them forcing a reconnect so that it will.

Also, I want to note that I sent my first pair back thinking they were defective. The instructions do not tell you that you have to open the headphones and snap them into place before they will even charge.

I gave them a three because I do like them but there is plenty of room for improvement.

title: Not my jam...
text:
I bought these headphones primarily for the gym, I was looking for an over-the-ear headphone that would block out the annoying gym radios and would provide the kick to really pump me up during my workout for around $100. And I did my research, months and months of research watching reviews and testing headphones. I narrowed it down to the V-Moda Crossfades and to the Skullcandy Skullcrushers. I bought and tried both and here is what I found...

These headphones have a crisp clear sound and appear to be more durable than most, however, there biggest drawback is I could not wear them for much more than an hour. The pads don't fit completely around my (average-sized) ears, they pressed tight on my head and they also hold in heat and caused my ears to sweat quite a bit. I don't know if I couldn't find the sweet spot or what but the headband also began to dig in, probably due to the weight. My aux cable didn't work either which they probably would've replaced but I had already decided to return them for some Skullcrusher 360's and have been a happy camper ever since! People say that Skullcrushers have a "bassy" inferior sound quality but I could not disagree more, in fact, I would say that the opposite is actually true. I listen to a lot of different genres of music which is what makes the bass slider on the Skullcrushers so nice. I can just turn down the bass when I'm listening to some of my favorite blues, rock, or bluegrass tracks. I spent months researching and I would say try the Skullcrushers!

title: Great reference headphones with a great form factor, comfort could be made better.
text:
The sound is great for people who know the audio profile theyve selected. Its a non-bass heavy reference sorted sound geared towards comfort and soft layered clarity.

The audio has a great layering, but if youre a normal human that just wants a quick immediate solution to your audio needs then this probably isnt the product for you.

The construction leaves a little to be desired and the cups could use slightly more foam and a less thick liner.

Those caveats having been said you wont get the soft layering produced from these drivers elsewhere.
I recommend having good enough headphones that youre more happy with before purchasing these as theyre non punchy but great cloudy subtle layering of sound in which youll find new clarity in your music.

The pads could also be built better. But the rest of the plastic parts, the cups have a fantastic soft smooth finish. Also steelor aluminum around the headband. Maybe it could be cheaper? As an audio lover this still passes as a 5/5 product just not for those who want a thump or thumping in the sound.

title: Nice idea, poor implementation
text:
This is a headphone that has a nice sound and a good design concept, but it's impaired by cheap materials and poor execution of the concept. I would not recommend buying this unit.

I have two grievances with it:
1. The plastics used in its construction are inadequate for the loads placed upon the hinges in normal operation. I like the folding aspect of the headset: it's why I originally selected it. However, it depends upon the strength of the plastic to stay "locked" in the "on" or operational position. After a month of use, the plastic is cracking and broken away so the unit does not stay locked open. It still works, kindof... see the next note.
2. It has developed an internal short. I'm not sure where, but it results in my having to fiddle with it for the first five or ten minutes of use to get it to stay on. This is unacceptable. It's for this reason that I don't recommend it.

In fairness when it works, it works well. The unit does have a microphone and I do use it with my iphone 3GS as a headset. It's amazing to me that the microphone which is up in the speakers is able to pick up my voice even when the ambient noise is very high.

title: Unit has worked great for everything I have plugged into it
text:
USB chargers kind of sketch me out a bit since not all are created equal. Not only do they provide different amounts of current output, but apparently the quality of the power provided can also be widely varying.

There are a lot of "cheap" units out there that are very difficult for a consumer to understand how they differ from high quality units, and how to tell which is which. Think of all the units given away at trade shows... These are optimized for absolute lowest cost with minimum functionality.

So while I am not an electronics expert, I will say that the first thing I did with my Anker 5 port unit was I went and plugged every device I could find (that was needing a charge) into it simultaneously to see what would happen. To my pleasure, I found it charged every one of them without any issues and did not even get very hot doing it (this is one sign of a quality piece of electronics - the less power lost to heat likely means a better design with better components).

I have been using it for weeks/months now every night without a single issue. Just last night my sister-in-law was having issues charging her iPod using my wife's cell phone charger. After trying several chargers to no avail I came up to my bedroom and tried the Anker unit. No problem whatsoever. ;-)

If I was to ding anything about this product, I guess I would call out that it kind of results in wire spaghetti with everything hooking to it. Though that is really the nature of this kind of product and I don't know what you could really do about that.

-Eric

title: Comfy, but Lackluster Sound
text:
I purchased these as a replacement for a pair of Sony MDR-XB9501n that cracked after a few years of pretty much living in them 24/7. Despite previously owning headphones whose primary feature was EXTRA BASS, I'm not a huge fan of bass - so naturally I was looking for something with less of it. Sadly, these are still too skewed toward lower frequencies for my liking. Not only that, but the mid-range is dull at best, and while the higher frequencies have their moments, I was immediately disappointed by how lackluster my overall listening experience was right off the bat. I will say that the quality improved significantly when using the provided cable, which is to be expected - but as that's not going to be my primary mode of listening, it's not enough to convince me to stick with these.

Before I even put them on, I was surprised by how cheap the construction seems to be compared to my previous Sony headphones. That being said, these are much lighter and significantly more comfortable. I could easily see myself wearing them for hours at a time without issue. The button controls are pretty standard, and everything is more or less in the same place as it had been on my other pair. To be honest, I'm weird and usually forget that I even have the option of using the controls, so they're more of a bonus than a priority for me. My only problem is the noise cancelling option. I prefer to do much of my listening with noise cancelling switched off, so on these, every time I turn the headset on and off, I have to cycle through two options just to listen without it. A minor gripe, but it makes the apparent lack of app support (or maybe I'm just unlucky?) that much more frustrating. After doing a little searching, I'm still unclear whether this particular model is supported by Sony's Headphones Connect app, as my MDR-9501n model was. If it is, then I had no luck getting my headphones to do what the app's name implies they should: connect. They connected to both my PC and my phone with a few minor issues; I just couldn't get them to show up in the app for some reason.

Speaking of noise cancelling, this feature seems markedly less effective than what my previous 'phones had to offer, and there's an obvious hiss that occurs when it's active. I definitely wouldn't be relying on these to perform well in an environment where noise is an issue. I haven't played around with the ambient sound option, so I can't really speak to its effectiveness either way.

They're certainly not bad headphones - although, in my opinion, you can get better sound for the price. Ultimately, between the merely mediocre noise cancelling and a sound profile which just isn't for me, I think I'll continue searching for a pair that better suits my needs.

title: Pleasantly Surprised and Loving Every Minute
text:
So...it took a couple of days for me to make a decision on these. I am huge on OEM prestige and have been a loyal Sony headphone audiophile for years now (had studio monitor cans as well as the XBRs which I loved). Have also owned high-end Klipsch and Sennheiser earbuds, as well as countless other borderline disposables. It was a leap for me to go with an unknown manufacturer.

In short...these are GREAT. Not great...GREAT. Every bit as solid as any of the buds/phones I mentioned above. At first they sounded a bit muffled and bass heavy to me (and I love bass), but after about a week they have burned in a bit and all music sounds phenomenal. I listen to hip-hop, jazz, blues, rock, and lots of live music and these are extraordinarily versatile. I also watched Game of Thrones last week with these bad boys and could hear amazing details in the murmurs and dogs barking in the background of a scene in Braavos (yes, I am a nerd).

For those considering making their first foray into wireless headphones, let me say there is zero drop-off from wired phones and having your hands free when you're active (i.e. lifting weights, running, biking, etc.) is a priceless value-add. They run out of batteries about once a day with heavy use. I would guess the battery life is about 6-7 hours (advertised at 9) and the distance you can be from the source with flawless connection is about 15 feet (the 38 feet advertised is a bit ridiculous...not sure who would want/need that anyway). They also charge INCREDIBLY fast. I would say it has taken on average about 20 minutes to get a full charge.

Lastly they are super comfortable. There are six different sized buds and you should take your time to find the best one. Once you do, you will be very happy.

The biggest drawback has been the charging cable that came stock. It got CRAZY hot the one and only time I've used it to the point where my Macbook actually warned me that it had to shut off the usb port. Weird. But yeah...a VERY SMALL fly in the ointment.

Especially for the price (I paid about thirty-five) these are WELL worth it.

title: Good construction, mediocre sound.
text:
I bough these headphones after my Creative EP-630 broke. These seemed to be much more durable, and got good reviews in terms of sound. Here are my thoughts:

Sound: Compared to the EP-630's, these are actually pretty bad. The sound is just not that clean and clear. It always feels like there is a little bit of interference, almost like white noise in the background. The bass is nice and strong, but the rest of the range is mediocre. Not as bad as the Marshmallow earbuds, but nowhere near as good as the Creative EP-630.

Construction: This is one thing I really liked about these. The buds themselves seem to be metal, and look pretty good, and feel solid. Everything is made in a simple style, but high quality. The chord seems to be rather strong, and does not tangle easily at all. I think these will definitely outlast my previous earbuds. The silicone tips fit pretty well: not too soft or too rigid.

Price: The construction of the earbuds fits the price. A lot of higher end models are not made as well as these are. The sound definitely does not. EP-630's, which are in the same range offer much better sound quality. Or you could go for the Sennheiser CX-300 (basically the same as EP-630, but they are the ones who actually own that design).

Overall, I think I will stick with these for now, despite the not-so-good sound. However, I would not consider buying them again in the future. Unless you just want something very robust, there are other better alternatives out there.

Sound quality is good. I felt like they didn't get as loud as my ear pods, but everything sounded good while I was running outside with them. I honestly don't have super high standards for sound quality, though, so if you're a real audiophile, you can probably discount/ignore that feedback.

They are very comfortable and light weight. On a 16 mile run, I never felt the need to adjust them- they stayed in place and felt comfortable the whole time. The upside of losing the smart on/off is that you can take one out without having to do anything to keep listening. This is great for times when you need a little more awareness of your surroundings, but also want to keep listening.

title: Amazing for gaming and music!
text:
I was doing research on a new pair of headphones for over 2 weeks. Initially I was looking for a new gaming headset, but nothing really "blew me away". It always seemed like the manufacturer was cutting corners somewhere for costs. Almost every product I looked at had pictures of people breaking them at the head band from normal daily use, cheap sounding mics, or their inability to function as normal headphones without a massive base station. After 2 weeks of research, and constant questioning (harassment) to my audiophile buddies, I stumbled upon these. I was worried they would be "too good to be true" from all the claims (durability, sound, style), that was until I watched a couple people on YouTube literally bend these things in every way like Gumby's yoga instructor, and then pop right back into shape. I was sold! The claims are true (for me anyway), the build quality is awesome. Some say that the bass can be a little heavy, but I found it to be perfect. I frequently listen to hip-hop, I've heard the crap that has come from "beats by dre" and these are not in any way as muddied and cheap sounding. Truly a class of its own. The only "negative" I have is that they're slightly more immersive than my last headphones, they block out a surprising amount of noise around you. So if you like to hear all the noise in the room around you, these might not be for you. Also, after about 3 hours of continued use they did start to feel slightly heavy (I have a 7 3/4 hat size) but you shift the headband forward or back and inch, problem solved. I use them for gaming mostly, the optional "boom mic" was incredible, the usual gaming crew could tell the difference and the clarity was crisp. But the true beauty of these is the Bluetooth. Being able to have them connected to my computer and phone simultaneously enabled me to wear them around the house blasting music without missing texts or calls. Charge time is fast and even if it dies, you can pop the cable in and continue rocking out. Absolutely love these and I'm thankful that a company like this exists. They truly take pride in their product, all the way from the build quality to the insanely polished packaging (I actually kept the box it was that nice!) And if you do manage to break these puppies, they have a lifetime 50% discount for the replacement. 1st class product.

I purchased these headphones from their website directly because they offered the ability to choose an extra ear shield of any color with a laser etched design for free (and a choice of screw color as well). Not sure if Amazon offers the same thing, but for a difference of $5 I thought it was a safe bet to customize it a little. After 2 weeks of constant use, I’m confident to say they are well worth the money and will the only headphones I wear for many years to come.

I have two Samsung Galaxy S3's with Kit Kat 4.4.2 O/S that are charging nightmares. Many Galaxy S series owners have had the "red x" charging issues since this O/S was installed and these two phones are no exception. You can read all about it on the Verizon Community support site if you are bored... Google: "Galaxy S3 red x"

None of the cables would work with my S3's at all and I wasn't sure that the charger was actually working until I used a known, good, micro-USB cable. Then it was evident that the included cables may have been the issue as the charger started working somewhat.

I was getting the infamous "red X" in the charging icon on the phone. That "usually" means an under-voltage situation which means the charger wasn't at 4.9-5.1 Vdc as required for charging, an inferior connection, or it isn't receiving enough current. However a 2.1A charger should have plenty to charge a phone that came with a 1A original charger.

Unfortunately, I had to return it because I need cables that work 100% with the phone or it's kind of pointless to have non-working cables and charging issues.

text:
I really, really, really wanted to like these headphones I really did. They look really sleek and for the price sound really good! But unfortunately if you're thinking of getting these for long distance runs beware. They would always work fine for a short 3 mile run but any longer and one headphone would always stop working for a few seconds or minutes and then would start working again. And then on my latest long run I got to mile 9 and they just disconnected all together and would not repair. Such a bummer and buzz kill for my run. I brought them back home and tried troubleshooting them as instructed in the product manual. After a hard reset they reconnected but then they just started having a mine of their own literally and started pressing their own commands (pause, play, skip, voice assistant) without me even touching them. I attempted 3 more hard resets and still no luck as it continued to press commands on it's own. Could I have gotten a lemon? Possibly. But with so many others out on the marketplace I would look elsewhere. If you're looking for something for podcasts or audio books these could work but if you're thinking of getting these for running or working out I would pass.

**Update**
The customer service I received exceeded my expectations! The seller reached out to me and agreed that I may have purchased a defective product and sent me a replacement ASAP! So far so good. No disconnections or issues when running long distances with the replacement.

title: Unbelievable experience
text:
Unbelievable over-ear wireless headphones. These V-Moda Crossfade Wireless headphones are very visually appealing. They arrived very fast and were brand spanking new. I bought the Sennheiser Momentum 2.0 Over-Ear wireless headphones and returned them right away after I got my V-Moda Wireless headphones. I did this for a number of reasons: the sennheisers are fairly expensive cans ($500+!), the sennheisers are also bigger and I believe they look slightly more distasteful when they are over your head. By no means does it look bad however, I prefer the sleeker design of the V-modas. I also love the customizability of the V-modas. I was slightly disappointed hearing that the V-Moda wireless model will not be having the folding/clicking mechanism that the M-100's had but the V-moda wireless already leaves such a small footprint that it doesn't suffer much from the lack of this folding mechanism. Now lets get into the sound:

The V-Moda Crossfade wireless offers superb sound - especially at its price point. The highlight of it being its very noticeable bass (by no means jaw-rattling, but indeed felt when compared to the Sennheiser momentum line up). Although the bass is much more pronounced and heart-felt the V-moda team did a remarkable job in fine-tuning the bass so that it doesn't leak into the mids and highs and disturb those ends of the musical spectrum. In other words, the highs and mids are still present and do not suffer from the blossoming bass (great job V-Moda!). The ear cups encompassed my ears perfectly and were very comfortable. If they happen to not work for you, you can buy the XL versions which are sold separately (around 20 bucks). Another amazing aspect of these headphones is the build quality. These feel substantial when you hold onto them without being heavy. These metals are built with some plastic and a lot of metal which really improves its structural integrity. In other words they are very strong cans which will last you a good amount of time. The clamping pressure of these headphones is perfect (on the snug side but by no means uncomfortable). I use them while I workout and so far they are amazing. However they are probably not the best option if you run a lot. Bluetooth connectivity is amazing. I tested them out and the range is around 30ft. These are wired too so you get the best of both worlds. Personally I listen to a lot of rap, rock and hip hop genres of music and I believe these headphones are tailored towards that spectrum of electronic/modern music. If you listen to classical I think there are better headphone options out there like the Sennheiser momentum line up. These V-Moda's will do a good job with classical music but I believe it's tailored towards more modern and younger crowd of individuals.

IN CONCLUSION: These headphones are by far my favorite headphones to date. They are exceptional in the sound, portability, visual appeal and comfortability aspects and for $300 you are getting much more than you paid for. If anything, I wish they update this version and add the folding mechanism which will manage to make this headphone EVEN better. I hope you pick one of these up because they will most definitely not disappoint.

text: I bought these headphones after using my Sony headphones from Costco for 7 years. I absolutely love these headphones because I use two phones with my headphones and I don't have to turn the bluetooth on and off on each phone every time I want to switch the phone that I am using. I also really liked that it tells you when you power on, power off, and turn the ANC on/off. My other headphones didn't do that. The only down side is that you have to hold it for a long time to power off but at least the lady tells me when the headphones are off. The huge plus with these headphones is that the battery lasts a very long time and my android tells me the battery percentage on the top bar. My other headphones didn't do that so that is extremely convenient! On top of that, the battery lasts a really long time. I've had them for two and a half weeks and I used the headphones for approximately 20 hrs at the gym(with ANC), 30 hrs while working on my car(without ANC), and 15 hrs (without ANC) while doing chores around the house and I still have about 25% battery life left. With my last headphones I never knew when it was going to run out of battery and they would just randomly shut off so knowing the percentage and having it connected to two sources is extremely convenient for these headphones. The only down side to them is the sound quality. They are not better than my last headphones but they are very close. The ANC absolutely works and I'm able to work out at the gym without hearing anybody else. My last pair cost $150 so I would absolutely pick these over the last pair I had. For the price of these headphones they are absolutely worth it!

text: There are some inconvenient features to these headphones.  They are big and bulky and compensate for this by exerting too much clamping force.  Though they clamp down hard enough to make the region below your ears sore, I would not try them in the gym because I am convinced any rapid movement would cause them to wiggle on my head.  Yet since I bought these headphones a few weeks ago I find myself coming back to them more than any other set I own, especially when I just want to shut the world out.  The ANC does a good job of canceling out regularly recurring noise, so it filters out the sound of the air conditioner, washing machine and refrigerator.  Have not tried on a plane yet, though I bought them for that purpose.  They do not do as great a job of canceling the sounds of the television in the next room.  These sounds bleed through as a low clatter.  The best thing about these headphones is how they frame the music you hear.  There is almost a dreamy, trippy quality to the sound.  They are great for reading and writing and any kind of work where you want to just tune out the world and concentrate.  Be warned though.  The least attractive feature of these headphones is that if you use them regularly, say two - three hours a day, they will need to be recharged every third day.  This weakness makes them problematic for travel.  But as a set of headphones to keep near your easy chair, they may be perfect.

title: Relaxed sound, forward mids, but bass and comfort have issues.
text:
Sennheiser HD1 Over Ear Headphones

Sound Quality:
· Bass is slightly emphasized over neutral, but nothing like the portable headphones offered by V-Moda or Beats. It's somewhat punchy, but could use more character and presence.
· Midrange is noticeably forward compared to other closed backs at this price. The midrange is clear, authentic, and spacious.
· Treble is very recessed and makes these a very easy listen and relaxing headphone, albeit not the most detailed. This lets the midrange shine even more.
· Soundstage is better than most closed backs I've tried, but still not great.

Comfort:
· The earpads are quite comfortable at first, but over time they become much less comfortable due to the memory foam getting compressed and losing it's shape. My ears ended up touching the drivers and the pads never felt secure and stable over my ears over time.
· Headphone is very lightweight and headband isn't even noticeable once these are on your head.

Build:
· Build is adequate. Lots of leather and stainless steel. The sliding mechanism does seem like it could come loose over time and the lightweightedness of these could make them more susceptible to drops. The build isn't a deterrent or a negative, but not a highlight either.

Overall, these are pretty good and better than M50x which are similar price on Amazon. I personally prefer more bass punch and more lower treble energy for a fun and vshaped headphone, but these definitely have a very specific sound that some people will love.

PROS:

· Lightweight, solid build
· Authentic, forward midrange
· Relaxing treble

CONS

· Bass could use more character
· Comfort degrades over time

[[VIDEOID:19213d6fddf7c389e0fcdc2ab8b608b0]] I had high expectations for this newer TOZO product and was not disappointed. Right out of the box it connects via Bluetooth. Out of all the earphones I have had in the past, these earphones have touch actions that make the MOST sense. Double tapping for the next/previous track and long presses for volume. As expected, the Bluetooth connection does not cut out nor does the music while connected.

The case is a bit larger than other earbud cases but I LOVE the loop for attaching! Many times, I come across a great set of earbuds and they refuse to add a loop. These do not disappoint.

The only gripe I have about this product is the app they advertise that works with earphones. The moment I connected my earbuds to the app, the app crashed and refuses to stay open. That is why I docked a star off for the value of money and sound quality because in this case, I did not COMPLETELY get what I paid for.

As with many new things (especially software) they never really work like their supposed to even after testing the first time, so I'm positive in the future the app will get a rework and start working again. If I'm correct this is TOZO's first attempt at implementing an EQ so I understand.

TLDR: Overall, the sound quality is amazing. Can hear individual instruments clearly. A great amount of bass. Fit comfortably. Touch controls are intuitive. The case is a little big (pictures for reference). App does not work but is not needed (for me anyways)!

title: Good overall, but painfully tight for big heads
text:
These look really slick and I wish they had fit me. They fit my wife fine and they seem to be intended to keep all the pressure on your head and little to none on your ears. This works well for someone with an average to small sized head, but on my big head they were painfully tight over my ears even when extended all the way. They were particularly painful while wearing glasses.

Regarding the touch interface, it worked decently well for controlling the volume, but I could almost never get it to change tracks. Play/pause is controlled by a conventional button which worked well.

I liked the battery indicator on the inside of the head band. The mechanism for locking out the hinges was odd and felt fragile. The inside of the band is lined with a felt like material which picks up lint easily. Dandruff suffers and heavy hair gel users need not apply.

My house is in a densely packed subdivision with neighbors close on either side and we all use a lot of wireless tech, so I have a higher than normal amount of interference to contend with. These did ok with the interference, but not great. They suffered some minor interruptions (skipping and crackling) in the heaviest interference areas, but were generally usable with my iPhone 4.

Speaking of which, the iPhone 4 shows a battery meter for the headphones when they are on. Really slick. I wish all the blue tooth headphones would do that.

title: My new go to headset.
text:
I decided to give these a try after years of wearing LG Tone products. I have been a fan of Bluetooth devices since before Bluetooth was cool. I started with a clipon device from Plantronics that had too many wires that were too short. Then I tried a Jabra device that looked like dog tags, really liked how they worked and thought they were cool till someone asked me if it was that medic-alert thing. You know the one where you fall and can't get up.

Finally I found the LG Tone and it's successors. It's a quality device and what I compare everything else to. I keep looking for other devices because of two issues. One, it's a collar and a little bulky to transport. Two, I have gained weight since I started wearing them and find that when I turn my head the Bluetooth cuts out.

Now I am using the TREBLAB Earbuds. They so far are excellent. No signal drop whatsoever. I wear them for hours comfortably. The ear hooks are very soft yet hold the device in place very well.

Sound quality. I prefer the sound of the LG, but this is very close.

Battery life is as rated if not better. Shorter than the LGs, but to be expected. It's a lot smaller and lighter. The only negative is that the device only warns you about thirty seconds before the battery dies that the battery is low. The LG devices gave a battery level indication every time you turned it on so you were prepared. This means it's easy to have a dead device on a long walk.

This device recommends not leaving it charging. Which means it doesn't have the circuitry to prolong the battery life.

Still these are minor issues and the combination of wearing style and overall quality has won me over.

title: Very good value-priced true-wireless earbuds.
text:
To get this out of the way first, I did receive this as a promotional item, and am exchanging an unbiased review.

I "needed" a new set of earbuds, and figured that this would be a good time to go with a true-wireless set. These came up on my Amazon recommendations, so I figured that I'd give `em a shot. I had previously owned a set of the older T6s, which had held up pretty well and had overall good quality.

These are pretty nice, and paired with my iPhone almost immediately. From there, I put the earbuds through the paces. I listen to a lot of audiobooks, and my music tastes are fairly varied. There's the Tozo app that is suggested. I found the basic sound to be pretty good, but did like the variety provided by the app, which gives 16 different sound modes aligned mostly by music styles. I pinged between them, but ultimately settled on the "Rock" preset, which seemed to me to be the best "all around" preset for my taste.

Audiobooks (currently listening to "Three Body Problem") are crisp and clear.
Music - I'm actually listening to these as I'm writing the review, and I'm listening to Amon Amarth's "Great Heathen Army," and am very pleased with the robustness of the sound. Again, the sound is crisp and clear and of very high quality. I've also listened to other music, such as classical, various classic rock (mainly Queen Led Zeppelin, and Pink Floyd), and Sarah McLachlan - all of which sounded great.

Call quality wasn't the best. It sounded like the call would go from being on both earbuds, then it shifts about a half second to one ear, then to the other, then back to both earbuds. This happened several times in a 20 minute span, and the other person that I was talking with would complain about the quality the call. But that's OK!

Overall, a solid performer. 4.5 of 5 stars!

text:
Arrived on time as indicated. Great quality packaging and easy unboxing. The following is in the box; Wireless earbud pair, 2 types of earbud inserts in 3 sizes (Silicone and spongy foam in SM-M-LG). A short charging cord (USB to Micro USB), a handy storage case, and an instruction pamphlet. The finish and build/material quality of the earbuds are of a high quality product. My earbuds arrived charged but I only tested it for a couple minutes and then I charged it for 2 hours noticed the indicator L.E.D. was blue shortly after. The charging port is smartly sealed by a tethered cover cleverly located underneath the RH earbud unit (perhaps to prevent moisture intrusion). A low profile volume rocker switch is on top of RH earbud unit. The RH earbud unit also features the On/Off switch and call answer button (Red circle). Built in MIC.
PRO's: ease of Bluetooth connectivity, user friendly, long battery life, comfort, run-weight lifting-trail run-MT biking friendly (never worked its way out of my ear), and the sound is AMAZING!
I have not tested the call quality/experience as I have not yet received or made a call. The only issue I encountered is with initially inserting the RH earbud securely into my ear. I believe the fault lies within the shape of my ear canal. I have to gently pinch the top of my ear and lift it while inserting the earbud for it to stay in properly. Purchased a 2nd set for my wife and she loves it too! She really looks forward to her daily run/workouts!

(I love a deep, strong, punchy bass) they were up by 20$ but luckily for me they went down to 59.99$ just a few bucks more than my two first choices, so I got them right away.

Now, after I got them and tested them, I have some pros and cons about them:
+Great sound, very high volume, both wired and wireless. Good bass. (Warning: they're really loud, and the sound isn't isolated, so beware while using in public space or office space, those at full volume could pass by a small speaker, lol)
+Comes with a neat carry bag and cables.
+Wired&Wireless function (you can also use the wired without battery or while charging)
+Looks like good battery life, but I'll have to use them more to see how that goes. Will update if necessary.
+Incredible range, with my Moto G I can walk around the house almost from an entire side to another and just aaalmost at the end they start to lose signal, still, I'm really impressed in a good way.
+- (again, a pro and a con), even though they're not entirely over-the-ear, more like on-ear, they are comfortable and because they're on-ear, they hang tight in there, you can use them at the top or hanging at the back, and they will stay in position.
-Only three buttons for basically almost everything you can imagine, while you have the other side totally free to add at least three more buttons, they decided to add a bunch of ways to press the buttons so you have every possible option in one side, bad choice imho.
-Foldable, not a fan of that (for me, the less things they have to potentially broke, the better)

Even though there are some cons, they're 5 star worth for me.

Edit: I recently had some issues related to the bluetooth drivers and I contacted MEElectronics for support, they were quick in responding and did a great job assisting me. Another good thing for them, since I value customer service a lot!

text:

The indicator lights are a nice and the UC buttons are a handy feature and work best with Zoom in my experience. I had less success with GoTo and Teams.

My biggest issue: When using Evolve2 40 with Windows and UC soft codecs, audio does not remain reliable throughout the day. When jumping between multiple conferencing platforms and local computer audio (music and computer notifications), audio becomes modulated and distorted requiring disconnection and reconnection of the headset multiple times a day, even during a conference. UC buttons also stop working after a while, especially when hopping between conference platforms. Additionally, there appears to be interference with cellular devices indicating shielding is not sufficient as static and audio artifacts are introduced to the audio signal.

Other issues: The passive noise canceling feature primarily relies on the earpads squeezing your head to create a tight fit to your ears, keeping room noise out. Over time, this becomes uncomfortable. If you want proper isolation, go with in-ears or full muff headphones.

Overall, when it works it works beautifully and sounds great - but I'm displeased with the quality and reliability for the price paid.

title: Lemon or Unmarked Refurb?
text: Honestly, I wonder if I received a pair of unmarked refurbished headphones; they don't meet any of the expectations of this brand.  Prior to ordering, I watched countless videos, read plenty of reviews, and even tested the M-100s against which the Crossfade Wireless' were referred to as more mature sounding (CNET's review).  Most reviews said they were well-built premium headphones.  Most said they sounded nearly identical in passive and Bluetooth mode.  Most said they were fun to listen to.  Wrong wrong wrong.  First, while exceptionally comfortable, the fit/finish on the left ear cup allowed it to slide laterally within the swivel like the swivel was built to a larger tolerance or bent.  Second, the upper midrange distorts on certain notes and there is too much bass when using the Bluetooth to power the speakers; when listening in passive mode with the included cable connection, they have a decent sound and a really good sound stage, but did not sound as crisp as the M100s I listened to at the Best Buy Magnolia display (the only V-Moda retailer near me).  However, I didn't buy them for their corded capabilities, but rather for their wireless capability and they just don't work for me under that use case.  Lastly, they're no more fun than my $25 Panasonic wired earbuds which reproduce higher bass than one would expect, but muddies the rest of the sound spectrum.  For comparison, I have the Jaybird X2 earbuds and they blow these V-Moda's away.............with the X2s I hear things I missed like the piano and violin on System of a Down's Chop Suey, but they're recessed on the V-Moda's in wired mode and barely audible in wireless mode.  BTW, I was really excited for these and returned a pair of JBL Everest Elite 700s (poor headband design which was cracked and a bad cable) in order to get the V-Moda Crossfade Wireless.  Utterly disappointed and returning them.  Given all the hype around this brand and these headphones, I honestly wonder if I got shipped a pair of refurbished/returned headphones instead of a pair fresh off the assembly line; if so, they weren't advertised or priced as such.

text: I bought these for running because they were the least expensive "active" bluetooth headphones I could find at the big electronics store I was at. My review is mixed. I have relatively small ears and a small head and these fit me very well. The sound/volume is fine for me when running, but I'm not someone who cares about great sound and probably wouldn't notice if the sound wasn't great. They typically have a brief, nearly unnoticeable sound drop about once or twice in my hour long run. I have run in the rain with no problems, and they keep working. The challenge is that the volume control/power piece bounces all over the place when I run and pulls the normally well-fitting earpieces out of my ears. I tried clipping it to my shirt, but the cord to the right ear isn't quite long enough and it pulled when I turned my head. Instead, I now clip it (and the extra cord length) to my hat. I use two sewing clips (my mom is a quilter and gave me some), which work perfectly when I use one on each side of the bulky control piece. I just can't take my hat off without pulling out the headphones, but that's not a problem for me. I don't regret the purchase given the low price and the fact that I figured something out, but I'll probably pay more next time to get something without a control piece that bounces.

They have slightly recessed mids, and pronounced highs/lows. They sure can go low, but not that digital low crap like Beats by Dre. The 50mm driver makes them never run out of breathe, even for those incredibly low hits you get from EDM. They also connect to my apple watch amazingly well. The bluetooth receiver has been modified to account for the small antennas in smart watches. Val himself ran over 1000 km with his watch. What a way to remove yourself from the world a little bit. If you are looking at these headphones, it means you have done some research and have a good head on your shoulders. You're already this far, just do yourself the favor and buy them... YOU WON'T REGRET IT!!!! You will fall in love at first hearing. The XL cushions increase the sound stage and make long listening even more comfortable. They are a must! text:
I’m personally not a huge fan of these headphones. Now I realize they are currently priced at $25 and at that price, you have to curb your expectations a little (which I did), but they are advertising that these are typically $60 headphones - which they are absolutely not worth. There are better headphones out there for even $30 (ie Skullcandy).

First off, these earbuds default to what is presumably Chinese, which I haven’t been able to figure out how to change and don’t care enough to try to research…so I suppose on the plus side, I am improving my Chinese vocabulary every time I turn these on. It doesn’t bother me THAT bad, but it definitely gives a slightly “cheap” feeling to the headphones.

The sound quality isn’t bad, but it isn’t great either. Honestly, the aforementioned Skull Candy headphones for almost the same price have a higher quality sound. I think what bothers me the most about these headphones is their overall design. Yeah the touch feature sounds cool on paper, but any time you adjust the position of these headphones in your ear or bump them, the touch feature is so sensitive it’s inevitably going to pause, skip, or do something else funky. I run with these a lot and the overall fit isn’t great (even with different size ear buds), so my music is constantly getting interrupted every time I adjust their position.

Finally, whenever I take a phone call on these headphones, the person on the other line tells me they can barely hear me and, worse, the phone call randomly gets dropped most of the time.

In conclusion…I would say you get what you pay for, but the problem is there are far superior headphones out there for almost the same price. These aren’t HORRIBLE, but they ain’t great. Cheers.

title: Well, the 2nd one works great......
text:
O.K., I have a HTC Fuze, and I wanted a Bluetooth stereo headset to listen to my music player, and to take calls. So I went out and bought this one, because I hate ear buds, and I liked the design of it. Well the when I got home, and started syncing it up and using it, it acted really touchy and wierd. It wouldn't stay synced up to my phone and trying to adjust it to fit my head it would turn off and unsync. And it kept saying the battery was dead and shutting off.(I did get to work for a couple of hours,though.) So I took it back a couple of days later after playing with it. Making sure it was the headphones, and not me or my phone.

So now I got my second pair and they WORK GREAT!!! You can't beat the sound quality( I listen to drum and bass, old school rap, heavy metal.) And no matter what type of music it is, all of the channels are clear. And even if you have the volume turned all the way up there's no distortion of the bass. They also seem to hng my head pretty well, after fine tuning the sliders. Going between calls and your music it effortlessly, it pauses the music so you can take the call, and when you end the call goes right back and unpauses the music. Clarity on a call is once agaian awsome, can hear the person on the other side crisp and clear. And it has dual microphone so you can be heard without effort. You can sync up different devices at once with it too.

Now the bad,(which isn't much.)First it the volume control/ song skip buttons(or lack there of?)they're touch sensitive, meaning that there it really no physical buttons, you kinda touch/tap the area marked on the side of the right earphone. And the volume up, shares the same area for the song skip,(tap it once to increase the volume and double tap to skip the song.)this doubles for the decrease/song back area. Which can be a steep learning curve. I kinda of got it down, but there is plenty of times that I'll turn it all the way up trying to skip a song. Or I will be trying to turn it up only to toggle back and forth between turning it up and down. Some time I get no response from tapping it twice. So I end up pausing then unpausing the song(it the only physical button-the send/end call button.) Then double tapping, and that seems to do the trick. Once I turn off the headset( by closing them at the hinges,) and reopening them to turn on the headset my phone only reconizes that they're handfree bluetooth and not handsfree stereo bluetooth. So I have to manually go into my settings, and turn that on. They are also lined with crushed velvet on the inside, which can get a little hot. But I work in a building with no air conditioning in the summer, and the boilers makes feel like summer in the winter. And I must say that to some people this also might be a deal breaker, but I have worn many over the ear headphones,or ear protection in some really hot enviroments, and these really don't get all that hot.

In my opinion this is a great bluethooth stereo headset. There are some minor issues, but if you can get past the volume/song skip issue, and the crushed velvet making you hot, you will come to like this headset.

title: Excellent music audio, average phone audio
text:
I've owned many Bluetooth headsets, mainly because I'm very hard on them. I have several hours of commuter train rides each working day and any Bluetooth headset I buy will get constant usage. I bought a Jabra Halo about three months ago and so far, I'm extremely happy with this product.

There are several thing I really like about the Halo:

1) They fit my head very well, snug but comfy. The problem is, not everyone has my head's dimensions but for me, they're perfect.
2) Audio quality for music is excellent...much better than the Plantronics/Altec-Lansing Backbeat headphones I was previously using. Specifically, the bass response is much better and the mid range sounds have much more punch.
3) These headphones are able to connect to more than one device at a time, two at a time to be precise. Hence, I can switch from my iPhone, laptop or iPad without explicitly disconnecting from one unit and reattaching to another. This is an extremely convenient and helpful feature.
4) The Jabra Halo connects much more quickly and with less fuss than any other Bluetooth headset I've owned. Other Bluetooth headsets seemed to connect sometimes but not others, and invariably, I end up fiddling with them, turning them off and on, turning the Bluetooth functions on the source device off and on...etc...etc to get a stable connection. The Halo connects just about every time on the first shot to all my devices.
5) The quality of materials is high and feels substantial.

About the only thing I don't think is truly excellent about the Jabra Halo is the phone functions. While the headset works decently with my iPhone, it's not as amazing as it's stereo audio performance for music. The Halo works but it's preyty average where the phone calls are concerned. Hence, I give the Jabra Halo only four stars but that's much more out of consideration of the needs of others than my own.

Indeed, I like this product so much that I just ordered a second set, which I'll keep on my shelf in case my first unit fails. As I said, I use my Bluetooth headphones heavily and eventually, they will die...no reason to think that day is coming soon however, when it does arrive, I'm going to want another set of these headphones. Jabra might discontinue them and replace them with something worse and hence, my second set are an insurance policy against future screwups on the company's part. For right now, these are the best Bluetooth headphones I've found...and I've had a few.

title: Control buttons are Awful
text:
The first thing to note is that there is basically no bass on this thing. However, the reason for the one-star review is the touch controls are horrible. The instructions refer to tapping and pressing. Actually, tapping or pressing, for whatever combination of seconds they tell you to simply results in some random action that you cannot figure out. There's literally no rhyme or reason whatsoever in what these buttons are going to do.

Case in point: I have a music app on my phone, and I was playing a playlist where the shuffle was turned off. So, in theory, if I use the touch control on the earbud and tap once, the playback should either pause or play. In real life, it may or may not do anything. It may also pretend that you've given it a double tap and then you get some kind of mysterious voice assistant.

Let's move around in a playlist. Let's say I've listened to song A and I moved on to song B. If I press the button for three seconds, I should be back listening to song A. Yeah, good luck with that. You're going to hear something, but it sure isn't going to be the previous song. If you somehow manually go back to song A in your app, and you press the button for one second, it should go back to song B. It won't. I can go into the music app on my phone and press forward and backwards all day and it goes to the correct song. These earbuds, in effect, have no discernible way to control what song comes up next. No matter what you do, the next song you hear will be some completely random thing pulled out of your music app that may or may not be from the playlist that you're in.

I have had these earbuds for an hour to charge them, and have been working for an hour to get them to work. In the next 5 minutes, they are going to be packaged up and going BACK.

Just don't waste your time. If you want random results, just go buy a Magic 8 ball.

title: Easy to Use, Good Sound Quality, Decent Battery Life, Great Value
text:
These ear buds are wonderful! First off, they feel very nicely made and don't feel cheap. They come with a nice compact hard case that provides more then enough protection while travelling or in your pocket. This case also charges them as well. The charging uses a USB-Type C connection and they do include a cable in the box.

The sound quality is really good and they have a good bit of bass to them, too. I was really impressed and they allowed for a great experience gaming, listening to music, watching movies and TV shows, and making phone calls. During a call, the people on the other end were able to hear me just fine.

Charging is simple and once charged, I averaged quite a few days of use with them being recharged in the case (keep in mind I didn't use them all day). Battery life will differ depending on how much or how little you use them. They don't take that long to charge from a completely drained battery as well.

Once fully charged they are very easy to setup and pair. No worrying about them unpairing each other and then doing some complicated hold this and that button to pair. Put them in the case and pull them back out, it's that simple.

They are very comfortable in the ear and easy to wear for an extended period of time. They come with extra tips as well. They stayed in my ear while running and working out. The touch controls were very easy to learn and worked exactly as they should.

All things considered, I really love these ear buds and to me, they sound just as good, if not somewhat better, than more expensive ear buds out there.

title: Incredible. Just wonderful. Best I've owned so far.
text:
The best I've owned so far (upgrading from Crusher Wireless). There's audio details I've never heard before in some songs, and the bass response is way more balanced than a lot of critics like to say about these headphones. Wired and wireless sound amazing, and for the average ear you'll be hard-pressed to hear the difference between the two modes. Blocks out sound surprisingly well for not having ANC, and did I mention they sound amazing?

I only have two complaints:
1. The ear cushions are much too shallow for my ears. Not sure if my ears are too big for the default cushions (which are exceptionally soft and honestly among the nicest feeling leather I've felt in a while), or if they were made for small ears, but my ears were pressed up against the drivers and it was a bit irritating until my XL cushions came a few days later. Once I put the XLs on, it was night and day on comfort. I've been wearing them for 3 hours straight, and they're on right now actually. The XL cushions should be default in my opinion, and I recommend buying them with these cans just in case.
2. The Bluetooth *call* quality is atrocious. FaceTime audio calls are incredibly clear and beautiful, but for some reason they sound worse than normal phone calls on these, until I use them in wired mode for calls. I may contact customer service about it, but that's my experience right now. Not too big a deal though since I bought these to listen to music, not make calls, and I keep these in wired mode most of the time (they were designed to be wired headphones with the wireless mode as an added feature, not the other way around, and it shows in very good ways.)

For $90 this holiday of 2019, it's an absolute steal. Go to V-Moda's website for free customization options and in-stock models for the same price if they're out of stock here.

My journey into the audio appreciation world began a few years ago and has led me to obtain some nice hi-fi quality gear such as the Highly Acclaimed Sennheiser HD600 open-back headphones, as well as the Hifiman HE-400i, Massdrop AKG K7XX, and most notably my prized Beyerdynamic DT-1770 closed-back headphones. These, paired with the excellent Schiit Jotunheim have given me a modest perspective into the amazing world of high-fidelity audio. Although I am a relative newcomer in this arena, I feel proficient enough to provide a fair and honest review.

PROS / BENEFITS
Low Frequency Response: First off, let's get one thing out of the way: The KZ-ATE IEMs have BASS FOR DAYS!!! Woa!! I was not expecting this when I first put them on. When I first saw them on Amazon, I thought "oh how cute". Let me be CLEAR when I say that I bought them solely on price and aethetics, and because I wanted a cheap pair of IEMs and thought "what's the worst I can lose out on?" Well, it's a good thing that I did because I'm not joking when I say that these IEMs have EARTH-SHATTERING bass and so I now have a entry-level unit that I can recommend to my "bass heads" friends, lol.

Sound Isolation: The KZ-ATE IEMs have very good sound isolation. I found that even at low volumes, the KZ-ATE IEMs were able to drown out most of the noise in my office where I work. Now, keep in mind that I work in a very quiet office setting (about 32-37 dB). Still, the KZ-ATE IEMs produced a good seal inside of my ear with one of the included ear tips.

Detail / Resolution: At a current price tag of $12-15 on Amazon, the KZ-ATE IEMs aren't the cleanest or most detailed IEMs around, but FOR THE PRICE boy do you get a bang for your buck! You would think that such a cheap IEM with such powerful bass response would be SEVERELY lacking in the mid-to-high audio spectrum, but in my case I was surprised by the relative clarity that these IEMs are able to achieve. For example, listening to Lindsey Stirling's "Crystallize" on Tidal with Master Quality Settings is quite a joy. Again, these by far are NOT the most balanced IEMs out there, but for the price you will be amazed at how they sound.

Portability: IEMs by default are designed to be portable, and that is also the case with the KZ-ATE IEMs. With a low impedance of 16 ohms and a Sensitivity Rating of 106 dB, you won't need to pair them up with an external amplifier, but of course you will always benefit from having one.

CONS / DOWNSIDES
There are some downsides that we should discuss.

Audio Quality: First off, there has to be a trade-off when producing cheap products. There is a reason why high-end audio gear costs so much, but that gap significantly gotten smaller in recent years. These IEMs are proof of that!! Still, I don't want to mislead you. What you will NOT get from these IEMs is high-fidelity audio. This is most noticeable in their lack of clarity and separation. While you do get detail and bass response that you would not expect at this price range, you will NOT be blown away by pristine highs and mids. Instead, what you will get is a very fun and enjoyable listening experience if you can learn to live with the IEM's shortcomings in the middle-to-high ranges.

Comfort Factor: Overall, I found the KZ-ATE IEMs to be much more comfortable that I had expected. If you check out my recent review of the Klipsch R6i In-Ear Headphones, you will see how I tear those apart for their lack of comfort. Well, I am pleased to say that the KZ-ATE is much more comfortable in my ears when compared to the R6i, and those are much more expensive headphones, so price is not always an indication of how good or comfortable an IEM will be.

CONCLUSION
The KZ-ATE IEMs are now my go-to IEMs when I want a fun and punchy sound on the go, that is, until my new Sennheiser IE80 arrives in the mail. Of course, the Senn's are much more expensive, and so if you want a cheap alternative to hi-fidelity IEMs with Earth-Shattering Bass, don't give it a second thought: The KZ-ATE is for you!! However, if you aren't a "bass head" and don't want to lose out on a whole $12, stay away from these.

title: A true powerhouse for your house!
text:
First, I would like to state that I was supplied a sample from Anker for testing and evaluation, and I promised them detailed, fair, and honest feedback on the product listed. This is my eighth review for Anker and these are my honest impressions of this product, for which I used to type this entire review.

Packaging
I would like to start with the first impression, the packaging. Anker is constantly striving to become very green and they are maintaining this to the fullest as I have outlined in prior reviews. The packaging is still a recycled brown box with a white sleeve that has a picture of the charger on the top along with the Anker logo and a prominent PowerIQ Specification badge. The front also includes badging that there are also 5 cables included in the package. The bottom of the sleeve has a QR code to direct you to ianker.com and their offerings. One side of the sleeve has contact information for Anker and the other side has a label with the serial number of the device. The box itself is rather simple, after sliding off the sleeve you are met with a plain recycled box and just the Anker logo on the top. My box did not have a security seal and it opens from the side. Once opened, you are greeted with the PowerIQ pull-out leaflet and under it is the 40W 8.0A Desktop charger in its plastic bag. Next to that is a pull-out section with the supplied power cord. Under the charger is another pull-out section which contains the 5 different Micro-USB Cables and they are bundled by size: 2 cables 1 foot long end-to-end, 1 cable just under 3 feet end-to-end, and 1 cable just under 6 feet end-to-end. Also, a Welcome Guide and a Happy/Not Happy card that has Anker’s contact information. Those cards seem to be the standard with all Anker products lately.

Impressions
There is little that can be said in relation to this product as Anker has completely nailed it in regards to the PowerIQ technology. It is simple, you plug in your device and the charger will charge it in the fastest means possible. There are 5 ports that does this so you can charge 5 different devices simultaneously at their maximum speed. The device measures in at 3 ½” L by 2 ¼” W by 1” H roughly the size of a deck of cards albeit a little thick and weighs in at 5.2 oz. Other than the fact that you have a separate power cord, this is one powerful little charger and the power cord is actually a benefit as you can place this anywhere on your desk or night stand and have easy access to your USB ports. The exterior of the device has a soft-touch coating that really gives it a striking feel to it and the face of the device where the USB Ports are located does have a shiny plastic surface that is prone to fingerprints and really makes the device stand out when placed atop a desk. The cables are of really high quality for aftermarket cables with a plastic over mold and rubber stress relievers that are very stiff. Only time will tell how well these cables stand up to wear but at this point they seem like they will take some abuse. The beauty of it all is that Anker backs these with an 18-month warranty. My only gripe is the advertised lengths, the 1 footers do seem to be 1’ exactly from end to end but the 3 and 6 footers are both a couple inches shy of their advertised lengths so keep that in mind when you are trying to map out their reach, personally I like the lengths to match the advertisements as I am an exact kind of guy but these will be fine for most users.

Charging Performance
This charger is UL certified safe and at 40W 8.0A output power, rest assured that there is enough juice to go around for all your devices. My desk normally charges an iPad 2, iPad Mini, an iPhone 5S, HTC One, and even a Pebble Steel Smartwatch all with relative ease. I also charge many Anker products on my desk including the Portable Bluetooth Speaker (MP141), 2nd Generation Astro 3, and an Astro Mini all without a hitch so this product definitely delivers. The performance from PowerIQ technology is definitely much faster than its stock counterparts, all of my Apple devices charge much faster on this than the supplied chargers by almost 50%, the same applies to the Android devices that are being charged with even faster charge times.

Summary
Overall, I personally love this device and has been my daily driver quite some time as I purchased one when they first came out. The quality of the product is second to none and the fact that it is $49.99 MSRP is a steal for this much power from something no bigger than a pack of cigarettes. Trust me on this one, you cannot go wrong with this combo and I would rate this product as 5 stars out of 5.

text:
Ive tried Wireless Dre Beats, These (trelab), and the Bluetooth Wireless Headset With Mic By The Dreaminex Private Collection. Out of these three wireless headsets, I place this in second, dreaminex in first, and dre beats last.

Where dreaminex wins:
Overall Sound quality, loudness, sound frequency balance (great trebles with bass- not muddy), ear snugness (these snug into your actual lobes and then the ear lobe wraps around so even if you tuga little, they wont come out like the others will)

Where trelab wins:
Bass, bass, bass (maybe too much bass? Even iphone equalizers have trouble bringing it down), loudness, ease of comfort to take on and put back on the ear again (in case someone is talking to you and you need to hear them)

Where dre beats wins:
Ear lobe support brace is hardened on the inside so it can be molded around the ears a bit. Trelab and dreaminex ear lobe supports are the flimsy kind (but that’s because they have more inner ear support)

Overall, the sound quality to trelab is absolutely awesome, and so is dreaminex, but in their own ways.
They both have that master quality sound but trelab emphasizes more mid/lower bass frequencies and dreaminex emphasizes low and high frequencies, with less mid tones (less muddiness); ie: the plucks from an acoustic guitar on the dreaminex would sound crystal clear, where as a low long bassy sub sound would sound like king kong jumping on the ground with the trelabs. That’s not to say either one good in one frequency and not the other, but its just what they emphasize, that’s all, because all around they both sound awesome. I just chose to use dreaminex bc the sound frequency for them is more pleasant to my ears than trelabs, but I love them both. Overall, trelab is LOUD, so you wanna turn up at the gym- BOOM- these will do it- you’ll feel like you’’re in a club!
Dre beats are getting killed by these new no-names in sound quality now so I guess they are just still popular because they came first but people haven’t done their updated research yet with competitors. Don’t get them. Trelab murders drebeats by far. Trelab is a winner and you will not be disappointed, gym rats and EDM heads!

title: These earbuds survived nearly 5 years of constant torture!
text:
I've been working for nearly ten years at a factory, and have been using an iPod for about 7 of those. My original earbuds wore out within the first two years of use, and I was looking for some cheap replacements that weren't crap. I found a package of these at Wal-Mart or something, and I've used them ever since.

Last night, after five years of nearly daily use, one of the earbuds stopped working due to the cord catching on something and snapping off. A year ago, the left-side earbud was damaged by a piece of work equipment and cracked a bit, but continued working perfectly even with a chunk missing and the gummy bit partially ripped off. With the gummy bit damaged, earwax easily built up over time inside it, and even with my best efforts, still collected in the inner workings of it. The man section of the cord was cut in multiple spots, and part of the rubber rubbed away through constant friction on my clothes/me. It dealt with extremely hot summers and swam in sweat for hours on end, day in day out, sometimes would get caught on things and yanked out, all sorts of damaging instances.

Throughout that whole five years, they never stopped working properly. Not even losing sound for an instant in any of the above cases. It took getting ripped off the cord itself for the earbud to stop working. These are top-quality products. What I'm saying is, there is no better earbud for your money. Thirty dollars for official iPod earbuds when these are what amounts to The Little Earbuds That Could for at most 10 dollars a pair, to pick the former is sheer LUNACY. The Apple ones didn't even last two years.

BUY THESE EARBUDS IF YOU NEED EARBUDS. It's foolish to pay more for crappier ones than these!

title: Bass Amplifier cuts out unless volume is extremely high
text: I really had high hopes for these headphones.  When the bass amplifier is on, they sound great.  The bass amplifier has an auto-shut off that turns itself off when there is no audio, or at least that is the theory.  The problem is that the auto-shut off circuitry is not nearly sensitive enough which means it shuts itself off at all but the highest volume levels.  In order to keep it from shutting off, you have to keep the volume at a level that is not comfortable at all for listening.  To make matters worse, their customer support is absolutely horrible.  I tried to send them a message using their website, but it complained about me not passing their 'captcha' test, the problem is, there was no captcha test on the page, and yes, I disabled all ad-blockers.  Then I sent them a private FB message as well as posted on their FB page (which got deleted).  No answers at all.  Then I tried their live chat option, sat at queue position #1 for 45 minutes and then was told to contact the seller on Amazon.  Bottom line, stay away from these unless you want to listen to your music extremely loud just to have the bass kick in.

title: Comfortable with Great Sound, but some strange distractions
text:
Very comfortable. I wear glasses and over the ear headphones can be very painful for me. No problem whatsoever wearing these for long periods of time, so far.

The noise cancellation is moderate. Some reviewers claim that noise cancellation introduces a whistle noise. That’s not very bad as far as I can tell, and is also - to some degree or other - standard. When listening to music is goes away. However, when not listening to music the headphones, while connected to a device, make a lot of noise. There are clicks and other garbled sounds, whether noise cancellation is on or off. It’s very distracting.

The sound quality is great, but there is occasionally a connection blip which can take me out of my music - a split second stagger here and there. Not a huge deal I guess, but if you want to really get into it, it can take you out.

The battery life seems a bit better so far for me than some other reviews have stated. I haven’t used them for extremely long times yet, but some reviews state that it dies quickly when not in use, recommending that you charge every day; this hasn’t been my experience.
