text:
Nearly the perfect headphone. With the XL pads I bought it's extremely comfy, sounds great, 12 hours is a good playtime amount, very sturdy, excellent warranty, free shield from ordering at vmoda.com, the list goes on and on.

Why the 4 stars?

It's a small gripe from me but it's big enough of an issue for me to not want to give this headphone a 5 star.

When you connect the device and it plays the startup/connection audio, or any time it stops playing audio either when you pause the music/end the video or there's a small period of silence, you will hear a distinct and somewhat loud static in the background for about a second while the headphones wait for potential new audio, then they fully go into quiet standby mode after that second of static. I know there's probably nothing that can be done about this because that's just how wireless headphones are, but it's still annoying to hear nonetheless as I do sometimes either pause my songs or after I finish watching a Youtube video I can hear it for that second.

Don't at all let this detract you from wanting this headphone, once the audio starts playing and while it's playing it sounds awesome, and like I said in the first sentence of the review it's an amazing pair of headphones and I'll never go to another brand, V-moda all the way for their sound, build quality, comfort, and service.

title: Great cans for your average young adult
text:
Alright. I picked these up for $100 at Best Buy. I went around testing all the available models they had and these stood out with the price point and sound. (They easily beat all of the Beat's in sound quality, AND comfort)

Comfort was a big deal to me, I spend a lot of time studying and playing games with my friends, so lasting comfort was a must, especially with me wearing glasses. These feel great. I can get into a study/game session for 6 or more hours and sometimes forget they're even on. They don't seal great, which is fine with me because I want to be able to hear how loud I'm talking while gaming or if someone calls me.
One small problem is that the headband isn't the softest and can begin to make the top of your head sore. Simply elongate the headphones, and move the pads to have your ears support them more, taking some weight off of the band. Problem solved!

Comfort - 9.5/10 even with my glasses on

Admittedly I'm somewhat of a basshead. I love electronic music and alternative rock. These things are super versatile. I usually keep the bass adjuster around 25%, and that works great for subtle rumbling and great sounding bass. Whenever I'm in the mood, I can turn the bass all the way up and enjoy my music for a bit. Also sounds great for movies and games, being around or inside a tank in Battlefield is an experience not like any other headphone has offered me

Sound - 9/10, pair these up with an EQ and they will sound great.

While they don't feel too expensive, I'm not worried because Skullcandy headphones come with a lifetime warranty, so I'm covered! Definitely stylish enough for me to wear around college and get compliments!

I didn't really have a lot of respect for Skullcandy years ago around 2009, but I was Wowed by the new Crushers, completely blew away the old trashy Skullcrushers.
Skullcandy is stepping their game up, and I'm quite impressed with them.

title: I like to listen to music with a great beat to ...
text:
I've been using Skullcandy headphones and earbuds for some time, and have always been impressed by the quality in comfort and sound, at the fraction of the cost from the competition. I like to listen to music with a great beat to it, so I decided to give the Skullcandy Crusher a shot for the added bass.

Out of the box, the adjustable headset was extremely comfortable around my noggin. The cushioned ear cups felt good around the ears. Construction overall felt solid. The headphones required one AA-battery which installs within the right ear cup. The adjustable slider for bass control can be found behind the left ear cup. Now on to the sound...

I really was impressed with the bass through these headphones, providing deep hitting lows. However, the more I listened to other music tracks, I noticed something I wasn't a fan of. I felt the sound quality was lacking in the mids and highs. And no matter how much I adjusted the equalizer, I just couldn't find that right combination I was looking for.

About a week after using the headsphones, I started running into an issue where the bass would kick on and off while listening to music. At first I thought that maybe the battery just needed replacing. But that wasn't the case. The control slider had nothing to do with the issue either. It eventually got too annoying I ended up discontinuing use of the headphones.

Overall, these headphones were....somewhat okay. I expected more for what I paid for them. Comfort-wise, they were awesome. But sound quality could use more tweaking. And I hope the bass issue was an isolated one.

title: Skull Candy Delivers...and it's Delicious
text:
I did a few months of research for headphones for my budget under $200. These are hands down the best bang for your buck and for your ear drums. They fit comfortably over my big ears and the head band is nicely padded as well. The bass drivers are amazing and produce face massaging bass! I bought these to listen to while at work as a web developer and for online school work. On average I'll have them on my skull for 10 hours per day.

I have only had to change the battery one time since I got them for Christmas...and I've listened to them heavily! If I'm going to spend the majority of my waking hours with Headphones on, #1 they better be comfortable and #2 they better be quality. The build is mostly hard plastic but that does not detract from the sound at all. My cube farm neighbor just bought the Beats Studio headphones for three times as much $$ as the Crushers and they I hear sound leaks all day long! Crushers leak very little and the volume has to be up quite a bit.

The sound quality of the bass is really amazing for the price you pay. Perks of the headphones is the detachable cord and the long battery life of the bass driver. My neighbor that has the Beats Studio requires two batteries and they require to be changed twice as much. Crushers battery power is turned off when you unplug them or when you turn the bass adjuster all the way down so you don't have to worry about dead batteries in the morning if you forget to turn them off.

The other day I forgot my Crushers at home and my day wasn't the same...I had to use ear buds...gak. I am thrilled with these every day and consider them part of the family. Ha. Go try them out at a Best Buy near you side by side with the other way more expensive competitors...you won't be disappointed. My ONLY gripe with these is that I haven't been able to find a hard case that will fit these. I sent them an email and they said they do not know of any manufactures that make Hard cases to fit and they won't be making any for the next foreseeable future. At any rate...Make your face and hears happy...GO BUY THEM!

But ignore reviews which say that the bass is too much. when you enable the additional bass it somehow balances out and in the end while the headset is going to "rattle" ( no joke - its vibrating ) it wont hurt your ears, although it can be loud. Despite the rigidity it is quite comfortable, it holds on nicely and the pods can be extended as you wish with a few too many length options, not that this is a bad thing. In the end this is pretty good headset where its weak around other frequencies that arent bass but if doesnt bother you go ahead an order this beast.

title: Good choice for noisy shop environments
text:
I am pleased with these earplug headphones. They are comfortable to wear for extended periods and they are very good at reducing the noise from my woodworking tools.

The sound is quite good and the bass is better than I expected. The volume is limited for a reason; it's a safety feature to prevent you from damaging you hearing. If you want to have the volume really loud in your ear then you will not be happy with these. But they are so good at cancelling the noise that you just don't need the volume very high to hear your music, or whatever you listen to.

Once you find the tip that you like, it's just a matter of learning how to properly put them your ear. There is a right and wrong way. The directions that are included explain the correct way to insert them to get the best noise reduction benefit.

The noise cancelling mike does a good job of allowing a caller to hear you over the noise in your environment. But they will have some trouble hearing you if you are standing very close to a very loud machine. I would never take or make a call while I was operating one of my tools, but I wanted to see how much noise these could actually block. So I turned on my loudest tool and made a call. I stood at various distances from the tool to see how well I could be heard. I could not be heard while standing right next to the tool, but when I took a couple of steps back from the tool, I could be heard much better, and the tool could not be heard at all. So I believe you could carry on a normal conversation while mowing the grass.

One additional tip: when you remove them from your ear, grasp the bottom of the foam plug. Otherwise you may cause it to be left in you ear. The tips are threaded but the insert that screws onto the post is only plastic.

title: My 2nd Set of V-Moda Headphones did not Disappoint!
text:
I've been a professional DJ for many years, eventually switching from my trusty Sure cans over to V-Moda Crossfade LP (non wireless) for my DJ gigs about 4 years ago. I put the original Crossfade LP headphones through a lot of abuse including long nights at high volumes, being knocked around, thrown in boxes with equipment, loaned to other DJs and dropped. The old ones started to show their wear by the plastics eventually getting hairline cracks and the earpads getting small cracks in the vinyl but they still sound and fit great and the original cable is still perfect.

I'd been wanting a pair of the wireless versions for a couple years but the price point kept me away. I finally got a set when they were on sale and they're wonderful. They remind me of my old crossfades in many ways but with a key difference- they're bluetooth!

Sound Quality:
Very good, clear sound and a little bassy depending on the music. I've seen reviews that say these have too much bass or not enough. I think that's pretty subjective on the part of the listener. I have a recording studio and these sound great for mixing and mastering as well as just listening to podcasts in bed. I have no criticism on the audio quality. I love it.

Call Quality:
One of the reasons I wanted these was the ability to take calls wirelessly when I'm listening to music. The audio coming into the headphones is fantastic, but the audio going out is not that great. I've had callers tell me that they had trouble understanding me and there was too much background noise. I believe this is due to the placement of the mic which is on the right side facing forward. Don't expect these to be your go-to for phone calls. They work in a pinch but they're really designed for music. That's the reason for 4 stars on sound quality. Purely because of the mic for calls, not because of the actual speakers.

My favorite feature:
The fact that you can plug them in and use them wired. This is awesome. I can plug them in and use them for DJing, or just unplug the cable and bluetooth them to my iPhone when I want to listen to music or podcasts. This makes these headphones incredibly versatile.

Durability:
These will last for years. The included case is a bit large but very durable and holds all the cables that are included. The headband will not lose its shape and the fit is consistent. Perfect to go in your backpack or large purse.

Tips:
Get the XL ear cushions for extended listening comfort. I didn't have these on my old V-Modas and my ears would start to hurt after about 45minutes. The larger cushions eliminate this and they're very easy to change.

title: Jabra Halo:  The most underrated wireless headphone set!
text:
This won't be long, but to the point. I only tend to write reviews when I feel strongly one way or another (good or bad), and by the amount of stars for this item, I think you can foreshadow what this will be.

Previously I was using the Sony DR-BT101 wireless headphones, which are good but not fantastic like the Jabra Halo. The Halo seems to just fit better (albeit not recommended for overly large heads...might be an issue), it has a much smaller profile which I think many people would prefer from a wireless headphone set, and the aesthetics and options are plentiful being just enough to satisfy even the savvy tech connoisseur. But one of the major differences between this set and others (I mean this is after all the main reason for them) is the sound coming out of them. I'm a bit of an audiophile, and while these are certainly not the absolute best sound I've ever heard, they are definitely the best sound I've heard from sub-$60 headphones, and better ANY wireless headset that doesn't have Bose written on it. The highs and mids are comfortably set, and the bass is most certainly classified as surprisingly good. I can't see anyone not satisfied with this pair at least sound wise.

The only con I can think of is their folding mechanism seems to be a little weak, and a person might think that with some stress on the joints when folding that they will break. This doesn't seem to be the case for me, but I wonder how it will be later on. My recommendation is not necessarily to come at them with kid gloves, but just take care to pay attention to what you're doing and I'm sure all will be fine. In any case this "con" certainly is outweighed by the "pros" listed above, so much that I don't even pay attention anymore.

Lets just say that I was pleasantly surprised at the quality of the Jabra Halo wireless headphones. Now back to some music...

title: Probably the best bluetooth headphones out there so far, but not perfect yet.
text:
To be completely honest here, I'm a pretty big V-Moda fan when it comes to their crossfade line. I've owned the LP, the LP2, the M-100, and now these. I've had the chance to see just what V-Moda can do with their sounds.

The crossfade wireless is advertised, more or less, an M-100 with bluetooth and re-tuned drivers. Unfortunately, the only thing it truly retains from the M-100 is the way it looks.

Looking at the outside of the headphones, they're the same beautiful V-Moda crossfades that we've seen throughout their line--with buttons. The buttons look nice. They aren't obtrusive and they don't make you stand out like a lighthouse should you walk around with these in the middle of the night. The only light on the headphone is a fairly dim power light on the power switch. With that being said, I dislike the buttons. On the bottom of the headphone, we have the switch. Nothing wrong here, very sturdy feel to it. But at the top, we have the three buttons we will be using the most--Multi-Function (Play/Pause/Command), Volume up, and volume down. These three buttons feel flimsy to me and for worse, they are kind of hard to press, for some reason presenting resistance particularly when I try to turn the volume down. Perhaps they made it this way to avoid accidental pressing, but these buttons are right underneath the metal clip that holds the band to the cans so I'd imagine it would be somewhat difficult to bump into something that would hit the buttons here.

On the inside, we have a whole new story. If you're coming from the M-100, these are supposed to sound the same. Even after burn-in, the sound felt almost hollow to me, compared to the M-100. The bass was lacking, both on bluetooth and wireless, which is what most seem to buy V-Modas for. The mids were recessed, but this is no change from the M-100. The highs were also present, so no change here. Somewhere along the line, V-Moda tweaked these headphones and dropped (upped?) the bass from the M-100s. These headphones also lack aptX lossless/low-latency codec which is a major disappointment in this price range. The Sony MDR10BT has it and costs less. What gives, V-Moda?

The other thing to note in regards to the bluetooth is that if you listen to softer music, you may notice a near-silent static playing along with your music. This seems to be the standard for bluetooth headphones.

Other notes:
- The micro USB charging port is on the LEFT cup, while the 3.5mm plug is on the RIGHT cup. I prefer my wire on the left side, so this is entirely up to user preference.
- These lose the cliquefold mechanism that was so popular with the M-100. Bluetooth is intended for mobility, so it's strange that this would get removed, but it may be a design limitation here. If you're coming from the M-100, expect the larger LP case.
- These can be paired and connected with more than one device at a time, but can only play one at a time. This is pretty interesting, since the M-100s had two ports so that you could either listen to two sources at once or daisy chain your headphones. Unfortunately you can not stream to the cans and use the 3.5mm port as an audio-out.
- If you have the M-100s, or really any headphones that have a removable audio-in cable and want wireless, I'd check out these: [[ASIN:B0134DTP9Q BTunes VXB-35 (3.5mm Model) To Make Wired Headphones Wireless for Beats, Monster, Sony, V-Moda, Marshalls and more]]. I'm ended up returning my Crossfade Wireless and buying this instead.

title: Poor design and cheap feeling materials
text:
I recommend that you handle these headphones in person before purchase. They're much smaller than you'd expect (maybe a good thing or a bad thing). This is great for traveling, as they're fairly compact and lightweight. The downside is they look circumaural in photos, but in reality they crowd your outer ear and the drivers end up resting on your ears like a supra aural design. There is virtually zero clearance, and I have average-sized ears. The end result is: they're uncomfortable.

All headphones use plastic in their design but these feel rather cheap. When you pick up the headphones they do not feel high quality. Lightweight can be a good thing, and maybe that is the upside to this material, but other Sony headphones do not give me this impression.

Sony, like most manufacturers, use a synthetic pseudo-leather, very thin material on the ear pads. This is fine if you don't have a beard or don't have a shaved head. If you DO have a beard or a shaved head (or even just sideburns), your ear pads will get chewed up in very short order and you end up with dark bits of material clinging to your skull. I HATE this. Sennheiser and Beyer Dynamic use a velour material that wears much better. I wish manufacturers understood how bad this material wears and stop using it.

My primary complaint is with the physical user interface controls. It is impossible to operate the buttons to control these headphones when they're on your head. There is no tactile feedback because there is nothing to physically distinguish the buttons from one another by feel. Worse, on the right side, there is an array of buttons in a undifferentiated field. You absolutely can not feel with your fingers which button is which. To add to this, the tac switches have such a small amount of travel, that you can't tell if you've pressed a button or not. On top of that, there are user interface gestures that require you to hold a button down for several seconds. How can you do that if you can't feel which button you've pressed or if you are even pressing a button at all?

Power is arguably the most important function to control on any piece of gear. If you have an engineer who suggests you have to hold a button down for three to five seconds to power something off, you need to fire that engineer. I put the headphones on and off countless times a day. I switch them on and off over and over constantly and every time I do that with these I swear because I'm fumbling around for a tac switch I can't feel and pressing for seconds until I hear a confirmation. It's maddening. Power is a binary choice, it is either off or it is on. A switch is the proper user interface for a binary function. Software needlessly complicates this because it is assumed that users prefer to have the headphones power themselves down when they lose bluetooth connection. That argument can't be made for the active noise canceling. A switch is obviously better here. I have other (cheaper!) noise canceling headphones that use a physical switch (with an LED!) for ANC and it's glorious. Why can't Sony do the same here? Yes, I use ANC without a bluetooth connection. It's actually my primary use case.

Sound quality is actually ok. They sound like an $80 pair of headphones. Definitely not $150 headphones. Noise canceling is average to below average.

Also, the V-MODA site has chat support, which makes contacting them with questions or issues extremely easy. Even with my phone's issues with the wireless side, I'd recommend this headset.

title: Not perfect, but definitely solid
text:
Before I review the actual product, I want to preface it with this: ask yourself why you're buying these before you place your order. Knowing what you want before you buy something makes the purchase worthwhile.

This is why I think the SHS8100/98 are solid headphones: unobtrusive design, decent build quality, moderate price tag, and effective (for me).

I was searching for a pair of headphones that would stay in my ears and on my head while I exercise and play basketball. I've tried the Earbudi Apple ear-bud clips (that attach to the 5th gen Apple ear-buds) a year and a half ago and quickly realized that they were a waste of time due to poor build quality and being largely ineffective.

My Sennheiser/Adidas ear-buds sound fantastic but they barely stay in my ears with the 'fins' so I opted to find another pair with hooks that went around the ears. The Senns sound amazing, but the price tag was also easily almost twice the amount of these Philips SHS8100/98.

I just received the SHS8100/98 in the mail today and immediately took them to the gym. They stayed on my head, only slipping out a little bit while running my warm-up mile (I sweat A LOT and pretty much no ear-buds designed on this earth can stay in my ears, so don't take that as a slight to these ear-buds). All I had to do was gently tap the buds back in and it was fine. I've come to terms that my ears are probably slightly different from the average ear so your experience will obviously vary.

I am currently 'burning in' these ear-buds overnight with an old iPhone at full volume playing various genres of music to get the most out of the drivers. Yes, burning in your headphones is a good idea regardless of what you buy. All headphones sound better with time and being broken in for all of you non-audiophiles.

The ear-buds get loud and block out a lot of external noise. If you're an outside runner, these will not be good for you in terms of hearing cyclists, cars, sirens, etc. These are GREAT if you're running on treadmills or you want to block out THAT dude who's grunting at the gym. These ear-buds are also extremely comfortable on the ears where some other brands and models can become quite uncomfortable after extended use. The material is soft and pliable (good or bad? Depends on your priorities).

As with all ear-buds, you must find the right size to fit your ear as this will greatly affect your sound quality and how well they stay in your ears. Some ear-buds actually require you to read the product manual in order to learn how to properly put the ear-buds in. Luckily, these Philips are not like that because it is pretty straightforward.

With all of this being said, here is what I think can make this pair better. I believe all headphones / ear-buds should start incorporating flat cables to reduce cord tangle and overall durability. The SHS8100/98 does not feature any type of filter between the buds and your ears, so you can potentially get the insides a bit dirty depending on where you're putting them and how often you clean your ears (hygiene, people).

The sound is so-so, but that is precisely what I was anticipating. For the price these were being sold at, I wasn't about to expect the same sound that my Senns would give me. That's why I have a Klipsch Reference One and a Sennheiser HD280 Pro on top of the Sennheiser ear-buds I referred to earlier.

**NOTE: the Amazon product information is misleading. The frequency range is NOT the actual range. Refer to a Google search on these ear-buds, but I believe the actual range is 18hz-23khz if my memory serves me correctly. Double check for yourself if you feel inclined to do so.**

If you're looking for a (mostly) affordable pair of headphones to work out in the gym and stay on your head, these will work wonderfully. These are not so great for outside runners or for people who are extremely picky about sound quality because you'll end up kicking yourself for ever considering buying these. I think the price could have been a few dollars less seeing as though these didn't even feature a remote toggle or microphone, but I was desperate for a new pair as soon as possible and these beat out many other pairs that I was researching.

These ear-buds are comfortable and seem like they could potentially last for quite a while if you take proper care of them. So don't go off tightening the cord to high hell around your fingers (extremely bad for the wire's integrity). The cord itself is pretty decent and the length is adequate. These will definitely reach down to your pockets without pulling down on your ears. That being said, you may need to seek a way to shorten the cord if you're using an armband for your music device. Luckily I have an old little gadget that allows me to wrap the cord around it to make the overall length shorter.

I gave this product 4 stars because it was exactly as I was expecting it. I definitely like it, but it didn't wow me in a way I hadn't expected which would have warranted an extra star. These are solid, but not perfect. Again, ask yourself why you want these and the answer to whether you should buy them will present itself to you.

I may update this review once they have been burnt in and I have used them for an extended period of time to see how well they hold up to normal wear and tear.

End of novel.

Story time. I go through headphones like tic-tacs, this is from a person who's owned these headphones for over 5 years now. If you have a massive head like me, and wear glasses, don't buy these for 10-12 hour workdays at the computer, go look for a nice and comfortable Bose set or open backed Sennheisers (600 series). The cable is amazing (and you get TWO). You could probably tow a truck with it. Cable is short (which isn't great) but is crazy durable. Anywhosers, enough jibber jabber. title: VERY good sound for reasonable money!
text: These earbuds have great sound quality, if worn properly.  Pay no attention to those who say that they have no bass or that they sound tinny or have too much treble.  They, most likely, are having trouble getting a good seal in their ears with the medium sized gel tips that came on the earbuds.  They may have missed the little package that has the larger or smaller gels in it.  If you don't hear good bass, try the larger gels, if they hurt, try a smaller gel.  These earbuds have great sound with punchy bass and balanced mids and high tones.  If you like more bass than you get with a correct fitting to your ears, try playing with your phone's music player equalizer settings.  I haven't had a problem with them falling out of my ears (possibly another fitment issue for some) but I don't do a lot of bouncing around, either.  Any trouble keeping them in the ear could be cured with a set of Comply Sport T200 foam tips if you know the correct size of tip you need (find the correct size gel and you have the right size foam tip.)  These earbuds don't have complete sound isolation, meaning that depending on your music volume, you can still hear most things that go on around you, which can be good or bad depending on your particular situation.  The isolation foam tips by Comply can fix this, also.  The button will pause/play your music, answer/hang up a call, and can select the previous or next track when using the Smart Key app available in your app store for Iphone or Android phones. There is no volume control on the earbuds, but there IS one on your phone or music player, so what's the big deal?  These are great earbuds for the price.  I am a musician and audiophile.  You can pay a LOT more and not get better sound than with these Sony MDREX 110AP earbuds.  Better sound CAN be had, but I don't have that kind of money!  Believe me when I say that these will do the trick!

title: These are definitely the best headphones I've ever had the pleasure of owning.
text:
I have owned multiple sets of headphones including some very well known name brands. These blow those out of the water. I was honestly not expecting the level of quality that I'm getting from this pair.
I've recently taken up walking/jogging on the trails near my house and I did not have a set of wireless headphones that would stay on while out there. I was ordering a few other small things from Amazon anyway, so I just threw these in with the rest of the order on a whim. I figured that they would be decent enough that I could use them for a while, but wasn't expecting much in the way of sound quality.
The first time I put these on, I was amazed by the clarity/quality of sound. Not only that, but they stay on/in my ears no matter how much I sweat or jostle them. I was even caught in a heavy downpour one evening and these things weren't even phased. I also love the way the controls are built right onto the earpiece. I've had other pairs where controls are built into the cable and to change any settings you had to take a moment to figure out where the stupid thing shifted to. With these, I don't even have to break stride. Battery life is excellent. My excursions typically last at least a couple hours and I don't usually remember to charge things in between. So far, I haven't even gotten a low level warning despite going multiple days in between charges.
Also, customer care is superb. I registered the warranty on these as soon as I received them and I've gotten a few emails checking to be sure that I'm satisfied.
If I need to get any more headphones, I will definitely be checking out TREBLAB first

They have a great metal housing (It feels really sturdy and can easily take some hits without much issue) and a double layer of plastic around the wiring (Making it really difficult for the wires to take damage).

The volume control slider is surprisingly useful and well-built, unlike most headphones that use buttons and get damaged with ease. All in all, these are excellent mid to high end headphones. Beware however, that the new version of these headphones is actually of a lower quality (Aluminum housing and single layered wire wrapping) and doesn't have volume control (Which might be a plus for you)

I have chronic tension headaches and as soon as I tried these on, I knew that the headband would exacerbate my headaches. It seems that the arms are too short for my head and make the headband dig into my scalp. Not to mention the fact that the headphones themselves are quite heavy.
After some more testing, I decided that I should return the headphones. Normally when you buy something online, the company will be kind enough to offer a return label for your purchase. Apparently not V-Moda. They constantly talk about their "six star" customer service. If their customer service was truly "six stars" you would expect the bare minimum from a brand, perhaps a return label for their heavy headphones. I don't know, just spit balling here. Anyways, I guess I'm paying the nearly $20 to return the headphones and get a refund for 85% of what I actually paid for them, after shipping and handling.
If you're going to buy these headphones and you aren't sure how they're going to work for you, just buy them from Amazon. At least their return policy is well-established and fair. I don't expect to be doing business with V-Moda anytime soon, which is a shame because I loved other products of theirs that I had gotten for Christmas a couple of years ago.

title: I can hear how low quality my music is
text:
At first, I thought that the sound quality was awful when I was listening to music on YouTube over my phone. Then I listened to music I downloaded onto my phone and the sound was fantastic!!!

So my one complaint is that I can actually tell how compressed a lot of my music is, and it's like nails on a chalkboard.

Noise cancelation works well. The louder and more constant the noise is, the better it works. FYI: Active Noise Cancelation works by a microphone picking up the sounds around you, inverting the sound waves, and feeding you the inverse waves. The inverted waves clash with the ambient noise around you and cancel out. So the noise needs to be loud enough to be picked up by the microphone.

To give you a good guage of the capabilities of these headphones, if your TV is on and you have these on WITH music or something playing through them, you won't hear the TV. If you're in a Costco or a store, you won't hear the ambient noise, either. If you have a fan going, it will eliminate MOST of the noise, depending on how loud the fan is. If it's a relatively quiet fan, then the mic won't pick it up enough to cancel ALL of the noise out, just most of it. Also, conversations between you and others won't be constant enough to be canceled out, which is good in case people need to get your attention.

Battery Life has been really good on these, too.

Overall, I enjoy these headphones. I recommend them.

Designers have to choose to do either 1) support only 1 devices at a time OR 2) headphones have to seamless switch devices, with priority given to any requesting device. THIS IS NOT THE CASE. And if you turn off the headphones while this is happening, the off-chime SCREECHES with static too! So you HAVE to take them off. And sadly that's the way they stay a lot of the times which sucks cause they $$$. I CANT EVEN leave my laptop open upstairs while I go to get laundry downstairs and listen to music on my phone because it starts skipping and pausing and playing and SCREECHING and POPPING and I CANNOT DISCONNECT until I get upstairs because AGAIN the headphones done care if you are crying or if need to drown out the sounds of your own sobs with music, THEY WILL NOT disconnect!!! I WISH I COULD JUST RETURN EVERYTHING NOW but it's only been now that I've had the courage to write this critical review because usually I am a very kind, soft, cheerful person. title: I'll be in my bunk.........
text:
I did a LOT of research on headphones before buying the V-Moda Crossfade Wireless Headphones. I mean $300 ($270 purchase price with some free extras like custom shields and boom mic) for a pair of headphones was REALLY pushing my budget, but the more I researched the more I kept coming back to the V-Modas. V-Moda offered a sixty day no questions asked test drive so I finally decided to go for these. I am very glad I did. I can tell you that I honestly have no complaints about these headphones. If I HAD to find one thing to complain about, I would say that I really wish they would have included the cliq-fold hinges from the M-100s on these as the Crossfades do take up quite a bit of real estate in a back pack, but this is a small complaint. The main considerations that led me to buying the Crossfade Wireless headphones are as follows.

Durability - These are built like a tool. The metal headband was one of the major selling points for me. I had previously had the Bohm ANC bluetooth headphones and liked them, but there was a serious weak spot in the (plastic) headband that eventually broke. These feel like they are built for working DJs. In other words, these REALLY feel like they are built to last.

Warranty - Speaking of being built to last, V-Moda's "Immortal Life" program is unique among headphones and was a MAJOR selling point for me to justify spending this much money on a set of headphones. That plus a one year warranty and the sixty day no question return policy told me that V-Moda is going to stand behind their product for a long time. I really like that!

The Looks! - I'm not afraid to admit it, I care about what headphones look like, they can sound great, but if I would want to be seen wearing them then I'm probably not going to buy them. Style is subjective and while these may not fit everyone's style, they really work for me. As V-Moda was having a sale when I got mine, I was able to get a set of matte green shields with chrome bolts which to me is a really nice combination.

The Sound! - Before spending the money on these, I went to Best Buy and tried the headphones they had there. The BT selection was very slim, but they did have a pair of M-100s to try. I was really impressed with the sound of those. The Crossfades have a 50mm driver and it really punches. Not to the point of being obnoxious, but they are really fun. Bjork's "Dull Flame of Desire - Modeselektor Remix for Boys" will rattle your head a little and is a bassheads delight, but the headphones are quite versatile. Matthew Sweet's classic Girlfriend album sounded clean and fresh and while this is an album I've literally heard 100's of times, I was able to pick up details on some of the tracks I had never noticed before. As Val likes to say, "We didn't just build a pair of wireless headphones, we built the best wired headphones we've ever made that have the option of being wireless."

The comfort - While most reviews say the XL pads are needed, I have not experienced this. Granted I have a smaller head and smaller ears, but the included pads seem just fine for me.

The Details! - V-moda (and Val Kolton) has a passion for audio and it is plainly clear when you purchase one of their products. Even after watching countless reviews and unboxing videos of these headphones before I got them I was still really, REALLY impressed with the attention to detail shown with this purchase. They really seem to want to earn your business and keep you as a customer. They are a family run business, not a mega corporation and this appealed to me to.

Anyway, if you can swing the price I would without hesitation recommend these Crossfade Wireless headphones. Also, when considering the price, consider how long a cheaper pair of headphones might last. What is their warranty like? What happens if the cheaper set breaks from regular use, or is run over by a lawn mower? Both of these circumstances are covered by V-Moda's Immortal Life program! How long will they last before I have to buy another pair? Yes, there may be an upfront higher cost with the V-Mods, but I think the long term cost will be much lower.

title: Mic is very unreliable
text:
I bought these to replace an older Sony model that I used for years before the battery/charging system failed.

I've used these headphones with two different iPhones. Just for listening, they're completely fine. They don't have studio quality audio or anything but they're not unpleasant to listen to.

But, about 3 out of 4 times that I turn the headphones on and they connect to my phone, the mic delivers garbled audio, and no one can understand me.

If I'm just going to listen, I don't have to do anything special. But, if I want to talk to a human or give a command to Siri: (1) Turn on the headphones and let them connect to the phone. (1) Hold down the command button until the little Siri blob shows up on the phone, indicating Siri is listening for a command (3) give a simple audio command, like, "What time is it?" (4) If Siri understands and responds, then the connection is fine for two-way communication; if Siri doesn't understand and doesn't respond, turn off the headphones and repeat steps 1-4.

Sometimes I have to repeat this four times to be able to use my mic. I'm giving up on the headphones and giving them to my kid, who never uses the mic. I guess I won't buy any more Sony bluetooth headphones.

title: Extremely bass heavy but otherwise amazing
text:
Pros:
* Metal headband (As opposed to cheap plastic that tends to break one way or another)
* Sound great after a bit of EQ adjustment
* Decent battery life on wireless
* Wireless sound quality is good
* Has option to use in wired mode without draining the battery
* They don't fold (might be a con depending on who you are I guess)
* They completely enclose your ears
* Easy to operate in wired and wireless mode
* Comfortable with XL ear pads. Can wear them for several hours minimal discomfort.

Cons:
* Extremely bass heavy (Not a con if all you care about is bass)
* Fits a tad tight but can be made more comfortable with the XL ear pads. They definitely won't come off accidentally though so it is sort of a pro too.
* This headset is not great if you are planning on depending on the bluetooth functionality. While the battery life is pretty decent, the battery itself is not the best, and will cease to hold a charge after a short while of ownership.

Additional Thoughts:

I have been looking for a headset that would last longer than 6 months before cracking, snapping, and breaking at the ear piece/headband and I am hoping that these are "The One". I have only had these for a couple days but overall I am happy with them. The fact that these have a metal head band (Instead of cheap brittle plastic) is mostly what sold me on these.

My biggest gripe with this headset is that it is way too bass heavy for me to enjoy listening to genres with an emphasis on the sound dynamics of the music as a whole rather than just an emphasis on the beat. It tends to flood out the mids and highs; so it probably won't be for people who are audiophiles or who like to enjoy music that doesn't have an emphasis on bass (Such as rock, metal, classical, etc). That said though, utilizing a 3rd party software EQ to bring the low frequencies way down, boost up the mids a bit, and the highs just a tad, and the headphones are actually more pleasant to listen to now. Some frequencies still get lost in the bass but it still sounds much better than my old headphones.

As a side note to the above, it would be really great if the headset was configurable via an app, especially to let people adjust EQ directly in the headset itself so that they sound the same no matter what you plug them into, and whether or not said device has capability to make EQ adjustments on its own sound. For instance, XBox One doesn't have a configurable EQ (that I can find whether native, app, or otherwise) so I'm stuck listening to everything in my games with super deep bass. Perhaps even have configurable profiles too so you can quickly switch between your favorite settings for different songs or genres.

The bluetooth wireless functionality is easy to use and works fine with my PC and mobile devices. I notice very little if any audio quality differences between blue tooth and wired mode. There can be occasional pops or crackling on blue tooth but I am chalking that up to it just being the nature of wireless devices and interference. It isn't frequent enough for it to be an issue for me. Battery life in wireless mode has so far been stellar. I charged it to full capacity the first day I got it and haven't had to charge it again yet.

As mentioned above, while the charge capacity and use time before needing a charge is good; the battery itself is apparently not so great. My headset ceased holding a charge after very short term ownership (About 6 months), and I didn't actually even use the wireless all that often. I've charged it perhaps maybe 5 times since I've had it. I have since sent it in for warranty repair, the warranty process went smoothly, and customer support was really good about the whole process. Just be aware that the turn around time is a bit lengthy, it took almost a month to get my repaired headset back.

Although the stock ear cushions are by no means uncomfortable; the XL memory foam ear cushions definitely make the headset much more comfortable if you're a long term wearer of headphones.

The ear pieces are a lot smaller than I imagined they'd be. I thought that they would be more the size of studio headphones, and I didn't think they would fully enclose my ear, but I was pleasantly surprised to find that they enclose my ear just fine.

I've seen some reviews complaining that the noise cancellation isn't all that great. I didn't buy these for noise cancellation so I don't really have an opinion on it one way or another, but I will say that it's okay, not great, not bad either.

Overall, aside from the minor things here and there, I like this headset a lot. I am hoping to get at least 3 years use out of these (I didn't think that was asking too much of the previous headsets I owned but apparently I was wrong...) If this headset can last a reasonable amount of time (with proper care and handling of course) then I think I will call these my new favorite.

title: Excellent earbud in the low price category
text: I purchased all of these and compared them with each other: [[ASIN:B004Y3A3ZQ JVC HA-F150W Gumy Headphones, White]],  [[ASIN:B003EM8008 Panasonic RPHJE120K In-Ear Headphone, Black]],  [[ASIN:B007FRYDWM JBL Tempo High-Performance Earbud Headphones (Black)]],  [[ASIN:B0054L4AD8 AKG K311 In-Ear Headphones (Arctic Blue)]].  All sounded good for inexpensive earbuds, however the JBL and AKG were standouts, with Panasonic next and JVC last.  JBL and AKG sounded very realistic with good, crisp treble and audible/realistic but not overpowering bass.  JVC treble was harsh.  All were comfortable in my medium size ears.  AKG and JVC stayed in well while jogging, as did JBL when worn with the removable foam covers.  I'd rate the AKG and JBL as tied for best sound.  The AKG at about half the JBL price is the winner.  I plan to use the AKG, JBL, and Panasonic but will give the JVC's to my daughter!  Note that I have heard that these earbuds are often copied by cheap counterfeits from China so buy from a reputable seller like Amazon (some Amazon marketplace or ebay sellers may not be!).  Also, individual hearing and sound tastes vary so your review may not be the same as mine.  Good luck with your earbud search, hope this review helps!

title: bluetooth / qc is very bad
text:
I'm very dissapointed with these headphones. I cannot recommend them.

I spent weeks researching headphones to try to find a pair that would give me superior sound and was hoping to find a pair that also had bluetooth. In the past, I've kept my headphone budget around $50. Most have lasted me 1-2 years. My most recent pairs were Jam Transit and Nakamitchi Bluetooth.

I did not purchase on amazon because I wanted to try them out at a local store before I bought. I tried a bunch of headphones and of all the wireless ones, these were towards the top in sound quality. I tried one wires pair with a built in amp in the same price range that was clearly superior but I really wanted wireless so I went with these.

Fast forward a few weeks- I can't stand the pads- I could bear wearing these for an hour max until my ears started hurting. Went out and got the XL pads- not much better- these buy me an extra half hour. My nakamitch headphones I could wear all day with discomfort.

My first impression was that these were good headphones (outside of the comfort issue). I could care less about no case and about the buttons being hard to find without taking the phones off. What matters to me is sound.

I started wearing these commuting and noticed the bluetooth would cut out once in a while. I found that walking around NYC the bluetooth would cut out a lot. With my half mile walk, BT would cut out 5-10 times.

A few weeks later it got worse. Eventually (2 months after purchase) the blutooth stopped working.

I called up the 6 star service and tried to get them to send me a new pair immediately (rather than me have to wait for them to ship across county + get inspected +and shipped back = 2 weeks) but they would not honor this request.

I'm on my second pair now and on my 3rd day of using them for my commute, I'm having serious bluetooth issues again. BT cut out no less than 15 times on my walk to the train. I'm guessing I either have a defective pair, again, or the bluetooth gets killed by NYC. I don't know enough about bluetooth to know the different technology used, but perhaps whatever bluetooth Vmoda uses can't handle major cities? I don't know- I like to theorize and thats my theory. If my theory is false then we know the Quality Control for this product is awful. I can't think of on product I've purchase in my life where it took more than two tries to get a non-defective product.

Anyways, that's all the time I have today. Hopefully vmoda sees this and is working on improving QC or their blutooth technology because they have a problem in one of those departments.

title: Treblab customer service saves the day. Originally: Don't believe the hype
text:
UPDATE 7/9/16
Treblab contacted me only a few hours after posting this review, I have to commend them on their excellent customer service. They agreed to a refund and I told them I would amend my review in return. I still am unhappy with the product, but due to the prompt customer service and willingness to rectify the situation I am raising my review from 1 star to 3 stars. Good job guys, I wish more manufacturers would stand behind their product to this degree.

ORIGINAL REVIEW
I bought these to run with, I was tired of cords flopping around and yanking the earbud out. These don't work for me very well. The ear loops won't keep them in place while running and I constantly have to stop and put them back on. There is WAY too much bass, all of my music sounds terrible. I'm forced to use the equalizer settings on Spotify to have any semblance of sound quality. Then have to turn off the equalizer any time I play music on another device because the treble has to be turned up so high to make anything sound good with these. The cord comes out of the front of the earbuds, causing them to be "torqued" forward when the cord is worn around the back of the neck.

Lastly, after looking at more of the earbuds for sale on Amazon, I see that there are numerous versions of this product that have been rebranded with different names. Which leads me to believe that these are just another example of chinese-made junk. I wish I would have bought the Bose and been done with it...

Unfortunately, I waited too long hoping to find a redeeming quality with these earbuds and now I can no longer return them. So, if anyone at Amazon is reading this, PLEASE let me return these and recover my wasted money.

title: A quality experience from arrival to the day that they will eventually be taken off my head.
text:
This is my first foray into the world of V-Moda and from the first moment I took them out of the box my inner voice said, "What took you so long" referencing my reluctance to take the plunge to try them.

My first impression was how light they are. One would expect these things to weigh a ton (which I think was my original resistance) but they are actually light and feel very balanced. They, in a word are awe-inspiring just to look at in the package. V-Moda seems to pride themselves on the presentation and getting the message across that "We don't just look good, we act good" which is regards to their warranty and service dialogues.

My nephew (a gamer) made almost identical noises as he did when he saw the most recent Star Wars trailer when he saw the empty V-Moda box on the table. A reaction that also let me know that the V-Moda marketing works! But let's take a listen.

The headset is comfortable with a soft by firm squeeze to my head. Pairing was a cinch (iPhone6) and sound was pretty remarkable just listening to mp3's on my phone. It did take me a while to figure out that there is no identifiable microphone (because it's built in) and everyone seemed to hear me fine (nephew interrupted this review to tell me that he would get the sides customized at the V-Moda site but I'll explain that in a minute. The other part of his intrusion was to say HE would purchase the optional external mic that sits in front of your mouth. He said it is more comfortable for him to know where his voice is being sent??). I mention this only to make you aware there are accessories!

The thing the impresses me almost as much as the sound is the comfort of these after wearing them the entire time of writhing this review which is after nearly an hour of TV and Music. I am impressed that it will sync with two devices over bluetooth, like a phone or a laptop (meaning you don't have to unlink one to link to the other).

Sound quality didn't change from wired to wireless (which shocks me) but there was a noticeable drain on battery (nothing you wouldn't expect) so it's good to know that they can be wired without loosing your connection. The sides can be customized very easily through their website, and V-Moda doesn't spare the sense of excitement in that process either. You can make your ear coverings the color of your favorite light saber and have your favorite Empire engraved onto it for around $50 dollars.

The V-Moda, for me, sets high standards that they stand behind with a sense of fearless pride. From their "50% off Immortal Program" to their use of "vegan leather" and cross-fade technology their message is clear - if there was a top, we are over it!

This is a fully immersed company creating a product that allows you to do the same. Now, to figure a safe place to hide them from a certain nephew's longing eye.

text:
I purchased these to use with my Mac Mini and have had mixed results. I think they have perfect ergonomics, they're comfortable, light, controls are even good IMHO (I had no problems with the volume control). Not critical, but when they were connected, any alert sounds had a strange crackling noise just before the actual alert sound played. Listening to audio or video was good quality though. However, it was difficult getting them to link each day for sound upon turning them on. It took several minutes of fiddling to get them working.
Finally, I've found the trick: After you unfold them sometimes their is a bit of a gap in the seam where they fold. You need to push them together to close that gap and then they come alive and pairing works.

After about a month I'm just sick and tired of these things. They are constantly problematic and finicky. Some days the battery is dead (or they won't come on which I think is because of battery) and some times they just loose signal. I'm sick and tired of goofing around with them.

My intention on purchasing this product was to reduce the amount of wires I seem to be surrounded by, especially now that I have a cat that seems to want to chew all these wires.

I like the product appearance, how it fits around my ears, how long a charge lasts and how it sounds.

Two problems areas I have noticed are the plastic on the headband (broke easily from daily usage right at the outset) and the static on the outgoing voice on calls (incoming is clear) - I am not sure if both are related.
My handling of the phone is gentle and thus the plastic breaking is a deficiency as I see it.
The static on outgoing voice (my voice as heard by others) is a pain as, with each call, I have to ask if people hear static and if they do, I have to turn the headphone off and then back on which has resolved the problem each time.

The noise cancellation is not great, but that is not the primary reason why I bought these.

title: The best headphone in the market. Don't spend your money on high priced headphones.
text:
I have tried audiophile phones with the recommendations of my friends although I thought this earphones were already top-notch. I purchased Sony Z7 and Sony Bluetooth WH-1000. I got a DAC device, too. I tried them side by side on my DAC LG cellphone with the same synchronized song. Believe me save your hundreds of dollars and get these earphones for $20.

In my opinion, 110AP on my right ear, Z7 on my left ear, both playing the same song which EQs with the best way I enjoyed, the bass on 110AP hits in your head, highs are more crisp (I listened to drum cymbals especially since I am drummer). Z7 had lots of mid level, not a bad headphone at all but it is $500 for pete sake. (I purchased it for $339 but returned it after the test showed that 110AP is better IMO with a price of $20.

Several years ago, I purchased several 110APs worrying that they might go out of production because everybody buying high end headphones without even knowing what they are missing with these low prices earphones.

I also tried it with Sony WH1000 wireless bluetooh one. WH1000 has a little better bass than Z7 and it has incredible noise cancelling however if you move your head a little bit and the headphone moves around your ear, it disturbs the air insolation around your ear and distorts the sound. However, while walking and listening to TV, it is great. So I kept it. But it still could not beat the sound quality of Sony MDR110AP.

This earphone has awesome sound quality. That is why I purchased it over and over again in the last 15 years when their cable break or something.

MDR15 is similar to MDR110 with a little bass. But if you adjust to lows higher in the EQ a little higher, it keeps the same bass quality definitely. So it is like a version of 110 with a different color of sound. I liked that one, too.

title: Muddy sound - unacceptable.
text:
I purchased 5 different models, here is my opinion ranking them by absolute performance:
1. Tribit QuietPlus - One of the best sounding headsets out there, beats the Sony WHCH710N hands down while costing less. A little tighter on the head than others. Good noise cancellation. Comes with hard case. Great value.
2. TaoTronics TT-BH085 - Perhaps the best headset for the money. Decent bass, balanced mids and highs too, good passive and active noise reduction, light and comfortable. The power button is between the up and down volume - not easy to find. Comes with a soft bag.
3. Mpow H19 IPO - Good highs and mids, a bit weak on bass. Comfortable. Great value.
4. Tribit XFree Tune - Not an ANC model and not very good passive noise reduction, decent bass, mids OK, highs are little weak - safer for young ears at higher volumes. Overall balanced. Confortable. Tribits come with a hard case. Good value.
5. Sony Noise Cancelling Headphones WHCH710N - Nice built quality, disappointing muddy sound, good active noise cancellation, the TaoTronics TT-BH085 sounds so much better for half the cost. The Sonys come without a bag or case.
As for reliability and longevity it's too early to tell.

Good charger, terrible cables.

I simply don't understand why any company would pair an excellent product together with a terrible one. In this case, the charger is great and the cables are pretty worthless. By pretty worthless, I mean the cables at the dollar store are far superior.

I've had the charger for about 8 months now, of which I use 2 ports of regularly. I don't use the other 3 ports, but they work fine without issues.

As far as the cables goes, I didn't use any of them until recently since i had other cables to use anyways. However, recently I decided to switch one of my old cable for ones of these new ones since I liked the length of the Anker one slightly more. In a matter of a couple months the cable already feels loose on my devices that i'm charging. The Samsung cable it replaced was used for more than 5 years and doesn't feel as loose. Similarly the cables by my bed that have been used for between 1-2 years aren't loose either.

They charge at the same speed as every other cable I own, so the wiring inside seems fine. Just the part that connects to the phone/tablet is pretty much as bad it it gets.

Pretty much a 5 star charger + 0 star cables. I would suggest buying one of the chargers that doesn't include cables.

title: I love these headphones for what they are! Perfect for iPhone 7!
text:
I love these headphones. I was skeptical about the whole Bluetooth concept. I am not an audiophile in that I want everything to sound perfect, but I want everything to be a pleasure to listen too. I want listening to music to be fun. I want equipment to make me want to listen to music.

For reference, I love my AT-M50's and my 1960 audio 4 driver custom in ears are a joy and when I am playing drums, nothing is more pure, full or accurate. I wouldn't wear my Crossfade Wireless for mixing or for monitoring while playing live music. That being said, if I am in bed, in a chair, on a plane, or at work, I want to listen to these Crossfade wireless headphones. They are the type of headphones you go hunting for your favorite songs to listen to again.

For a disclosure, I am a drummer and I want a kick drum to sound like a kick and and a bass guitar to sound like a bass. I also listen for the vocals, guitar, keys, cymbals etc. but strong clear bass seems to be the thoughest quality to find. My Shure 5s and 425 in-ears didn't have it, my Weston in-ears didn't have it. The AT-M50s have it and my 1964 Qi's have it. These Crossfade Wireless have it too. Full disclosure, the 1964's have more sub bass and the Crossfade more upper bass (100-250) than the sub bass, but the 1964s are also $600 in ear monitors. The 1964's are incredible and nothing compares, but I don't want to bring them out every time I listen to music! The $600 1964's better have more than my $269 Bluetooth headphones anyways!

In all, I bought these because I got a new iPhone 7 plus, I got frustrated with the whole lack of a headphone jack, and looked for the best Bluetooth headphones for the price. The Crossfade Wireless have exceeded my expectations, and now I can't go back. I am a big fan and listen to these more than all my other Headphones combined. These may not be best for everyone, but for me they fit the bill perfectly.

title: I'm not picky but I'm pretty disappointed
text:
All I wanted was something that worked half decently. I guess I should not have been so literal because that's basically what I got. Got these for a prime day deal because I wanted to have some over the ear headphones that wouldn't cost me an arm and a leg. I switched to an iPhone recently and now have no headphone jack so... that sucks. but it inspired me to look into some wireless alternatives and when I saw these at such a discount I figured what the heck? I'm not picky and these look perfect!

Unfortunately this is the very first day I have really tried them and I will be returning them. If they didn't have Sony written on the side I honestly would not even believe this was made by them as they feel more like a really bad knock off. I honestly am still not sure if they aren't some really bad ripoff posing as the real thing. While the plastic they are made of feels more flimsy than I have come to expect out of quality headphones, I like that they are light weight so I feel like I can wear them for a long time without neck strain which is a problem I have with my husband's Bose. They also are smaller than what he has so they fit comfortably on my head and over my ears without the inner pad touching my ear. His are so big on me that at their smallest they are sliding and pulling the tops of my ears down whereas these fit snuggly but not uncomfortably so.

So why am I returning them? Well the noise cancelling isn't the best which really wasn't high on my list of importance and was something I was expecting at this price range and okay with. When I take the headphones off though, the ear pieces pick up whatever frequency the headphones are using for the noice cancelling and start squealing with feedback. That I absolutely did not expect. I either have to turn the noise cancelling off or turn the headphones entirely off. I tried turning the earpieces away from eachother and while it lessens the squeal it doesn't stop completely. Also while I am listening to anything with the noise cancelling on, it has this slight ringing sound in the background and then if there is any external noise at all it gets significantly louder. To the point that I don't want to use them. And what is the point of headphones if you don't use them? They also had problems connecting to both my phone and my laptop and when we tried to do volume controls with an app on my phone (my husband is a tech guy and he was trying to figure it out so I don't know what he was using) it just would not connect for the longest time and continued to have issues.

Really disappointed. My bar wasn't even set all that high and it's just disappointing with how they poorly they performed.

title: After years of cords, I am finally free
text:
I purchased these headphones a couple months ago, and not once have I regretted doing so.

I would describe my music taste as anything that isn't country or rap (and yes, there are of course exceptions to the rule) with a preference towards dubstep (Lindsey Stirling and the like). They perform admirably in every way possible to my untrained ears. The bass hits hard, but is also still pleasantly warm and not boomy, which is in stark contrast to many cheaper pairs of headphones I have run into over the years. Mids are crispy and clear, and I personally turned down the high end stuff with an EQ, but that's just my preference.

I am coming from a dearly loved pair of the legendary ATH-M50x's that served me well for a good couple of years. Nothing happened to them, but I wanted something with a little more bass and without a cord. These most certainly delivered. I can get a full week of use out of them walking around the university with them on at 30% volume and about 2-3 hours of use a day. Going from someone who had to deal with a clunky cord all the time to having a completely wireless pair of headphones is a transformative experience, one that I recommend experiencing in some capacity or another.

I have never used the included cord with them, though I did purchase the boom-pro mic that they sell so I can use it as a gaming headset, and I am also quite impressed with the quality of that. The mic is a little quiet, but that can be dealt with on the software side quite easily.

As for comfort, the ATH-M50x's (with velour earpads) win by a landslide, though that is mitigated by purchasing the XL pads. They help a ton, as the included pads are far too shallow, and frankly hurt to use for more than a couple minutes.

Regarding the default volume, I quite agree with a few of the other reviewers in that it defaults to an uncomfortably high volume when you first turn it on. This is more of a gripe than anything, as it is just as easy to turn them on, bump the volume down, and then put them on.

TL;DR: Fantastic sounding, great battery life, durable, spectacular aesthetics, make sure to buy the XL pads, and turn them on before you put them on your head because they default to an uncomfortably loud volume.

title: Headphones Shouldn't Be This Fussy
text:
I've held off on writing a review for these hoping they'd get better. Unfortunately they haven't. I'll start with the positives. They're relatively comfortable. They have decent range (IMO) and the noise cancellation is pretty good. I also think the sound is pretty decent.

As for why I want to tear my hair out at least once a week because of them: it's because the slightest thing will interrupt the blue tooth signal. I never know when or what will cause the sound to go out or mess up, but it happens at the very least once a week. Sometimes the sound will go out completely and I'll have to turn them off and then turn them back on to fix. That's the simplest remedy. Other times the sound will get messed up (it'll sound muffled or like it's coming from a tin can) and then my options change. Occasionally I can do a "reset" and that will fix the issue. Other times I can delete the headphone information, reset, and re pair the headphones to my device and that'll work. Still other times I have to restart my computer entirely to fix the problem.

There's also another level of "mess up" where none of the above will work and I''ll have to go deep into some of my computer settings (after looking up a tutorial) and check off options that somehow got unchecked. I've lost track of the number of times I've thought the headphones were just broke because they stopped producing sound. I've also lost track of the number of times I've had to fix a sound issue with them.

For as much as these cost and for what they're supposed to do (i.e. work as a blue tooth device), this level of frustration is unacceptable. I would have saved myself so much grief if I had purchased wired headphones instead and cannot believe a device made by a big time electronics brand malfunctions so often. It really makes me hesitant to purchase wireless headphones again because I don't known if it's a Sony issue, a model issue, or a blue tooth issue.

title: Better sound quality than others that I've tried
text:
Love these headphones!!! Just bought my 2nd pair.

First pair was *very* beat up after using heavily for 2 years, but amazingly they still work just like new.

I much prefer the sound quality of these over the LG Tone (HBS-700) that I just tried. The Halos have much clearer, cleaner highs. I cannot stress enough how the difference makes the listening experience so much better for me:
with Halo: true bliss
with LG Tone: blah, boring.

Negatives for Halo:
- Must admit that the Halo has an extremely fiddly volume control. But I now just set it to the max and adjust volume on my iPhone.
- Seating onto my ears could be tighter. When at the gym, I put a sweat band over the headphones. That's seats them better to my ears, solving most of this problem.
- And if seating were tighter, they's be less likely to fall off when I bend my head down.
- More obtrusive than ear bud type. But the better sound quality is worth it.

Plus for Halo: battery life is very long. Unless I forget and leave them on between listening sessions, they seem to never run down.

You can get used to fiddly issues that aren't that great (like the volume control). But you can never "work around" sound quality. That's why sound quality needs to be the highest priority in reviewing an audio product.

Pros: Good sound, product stays comfortably in ears, and there are a variety of different earbud sizes to suit your size. The earbuds do not love tap your eardrum either, they rest just inside the canal.

As soon as I brought a barbell or piece of metal like iron or aluminum near it, the music would jitter. I charged the device again using the provided charging USB, still nothing.

Conclusion: This brand gives you some pretty good quality earbuds, but its wireless products (as well as other brands, I'm sure) are just "not there" when it comes from high quality, wireless earphones. title: Extremely convenient charger for multi-device households, but the cables SUCK
text:
This charger is easily the most convenient charging solution for a household with multitudes of devices. I've had all five ports in use on more than one occasion, and saving the room on the outlet strip for laptop cords and other non-USB charging plugs is extremely useful. Instead of constantly shuffling chargers on and off or finding different outlets around the house, this one keeps everything convenient. It also comes in handy when travelling. Outlets just aren't as common as power-hungry devices seem to need these days, so only using a single outlet is very useful.

The biggest downside to this charger is that the cables it comes with are downright flimsy. Anker has their own "premium" cables they sell separately that are 100x more durable and reliable. The 6ft cable that came with this died in a month, and the 3ft cable only made it another month or so longer. The shorties are too short to really be useful for active use, so they hold up, but only because the device plugged in usually just sits on the table while it charges. If this shipped with Anker's own premium cables, it would easily be a better product. If those cables weren't so cheap to purchase on their own, I'd probably dock another star off of this review...what good is a charger if you can't use it?

title: A great pair of headphones.
text:
First of all I want to start by saying I am a casual listener. I enjoy listening to music but couldn’t get into the technical aspect of the quality of sound produced from these headphones. This will be a review of my experience with the Audio-Technica ATH-M50x’s compared to past headphones I have encountered.
These are the first overhead headphones I have personally owned (apart from my Astro A-50’s for gaming) but I have used others in the past; however, I have used and owned many in-ear headphones. These have varied in price range and brands with a pair of Bose in-ear headphones being the most expensive (can’t recall what they are called now) at around the same price range as this headset (around $170 while I write this).

Sound-
I personally enjoy this headset due to the clarity of sound. I listen to a variety of music so I wanted a headset that would do well at many ranges. These do well in that aspect. The vocals always sound amazing and clear (blues sound great!) as well as instruments such as in classical music. The only thing as far as sound goes where I wish these headphones produced a bit more of would be bass. Although it’s there and it still sounds good within pop songs or house music it seems to lack a bit of punch. This seems to take a bit from the drums in rock music to me but this is an ever so slight complaint seeing as everything else sounds so much better. There is also a way to get more bass from what I’ve read by getting an amplifier for the headset. So if it doesn’t have enough bass for you there is a way to get more!
The M50x’s due let out sound if you play music loud enough and if you play them at higher volumes people will be able to clearly hear what you are listening to.

Physical Goods and Quality/Durability-
From the box, my M50x Limited Edition (dark green and brown ones) came with, the headphones (which fold into the band, adjustable), three audio cables (a curly one, a three meter straight cable, and a 1.2 meter cable) all detachable, a 3.5mm adapter, and a nice little brown carrying case (probably faux leather but still looks nice).
The headphones seem to made of mostly plastic which seem light but somehow don’t feel cheap to me, seem fairly light overall and are definitely comfortable for me. The headband is cushioned with the same material on the ear cups which during use do get warm after a while but nothing like my Astro A-50’s (again for gaming).
Although I have only owned this headset for a few months these headphones seem very durable. I am a student and stuff these in my bag with just the cloth bag and I am not afraid of these breaking at all.

Verdict-
I do not regret my purchase, I personally got these on sale for about $120 and think it has been well worth the purchase and would recommend them to anyone as they produce great sound (that’s well rounded), a good simple styling (debated on black vs my green/brown at first but now wouldn’t consider changing them), and seem plenty durable where I don’t feel I have to worry about babying them at all. Great buy!

title: but certainly not bad. Lower frequencies sound a little muffled or hard ...
text:
PROs:
- Sound is adequate while on the move. Not ground-breaking, but certainly not bad. Lower frequencies sound a little muffled or hard for the phones to render appropriately
- Very easy to pair/set up. I pulled these out of the box and turned them on, paired them up, and was ready within 5 mins
- Volume control on the headset itself is nice. The power button works as a pause/play button in addition to being the power button

CONs:
- The power button on the right earpiece is in an annoying place. If I go to readjust the earpiece in any way, I inevitably hit the power button, because it's right in the best place for pushing the earpiece in your ear
- There are volume controls, but no other playback controls. There is an "autoredial" function, which I found by accident after hitting the power button too many times while readjusting
- When the battery gets low, a woman's voice comes over the headset and loudly proclaims "Battery low." She does this maybe every minute as the battery gets low. I would much rather it be a semi-quiet beep

Other comments:
- I guess I have small ears, but these things just don't sit right in them... that tends to go for all of these rubber earbud types, so this isn't a fault on the device
- The "around the ear" piece is actually floppy rubber, and not a harder plastic. Part of the reason I got these was because I thought they would stay in my ears better than say, the Jaybird headphones, but that rubber piece doesn't seem to do much
- Overall, I was looking for something wireless that fits in my ear and plays my music while I run and/or lift, and these do a good job of it. There are definitely better things out there, but for the price, these things are pretty solid

title: Great quality, doesn't drop connection, didn't break the bank.
text:
I purchased this on an Amazon deal of the day and got it to try until I could find another, better one. My Bose bluetooth headset broke (plastic ear piece cracked) and couldn't replace. Bose no longer makes it.

I got this expecting it to work ok, but the setup was simple like all bluetooth devices and the sound quality far surpassed what I expected. It was comparable to the Bose for noise cancelling ability and far exceeded (!) the Bose headset battery life. I have used this all day and still have enough charge for another day's use or longer. The case that came with it is handy and has enough of the rubber pieces included to fit any ear. This is a little heavier that others I have owned, but at the same time, you get used to it and forget it is there after a while. For me, the fit does inflict some discomfort where the ear piece fits inside my ear, but is probably more around my ear shape than the headset. It is sensitive and will pick up noise from anything else you are doing too...

It is rugged and even accidentally sent it through a full wash and dry cycle where it was in the pocket of a pair of shorts. It came out clean and 100% functional and still charged. I had turned it off before placing in my pocket but doesn't appear to have affected anything, verified with extensive use in the week and a half since.

I highly recommend this headset. If I lost this or broke it, I would purchase another of these without considering others. I also saved a lot of $ compared to the cost of my Bose or something similar high-end too.... No issues with dropped connections or disconnects and put together well.
