title: Review from a professor teaching remotely
text:
I'm a college professor in 2020, and I've had a web-meeting almost every hour on the hour 5 times a day for almost the entire summer, with a full class load to teach online right around the corner. I've gone through 4 different headphone/microphone experiments, and this headset wins hands down. Very comfortable, it just sits on my ear, as opposed to sticking in the ear like a typical earbud, so it doesn't get itchy or uncomfortable. The sound is almost too loud and clear as a bell. I've had to turn down my settings rather than go full blast as I have with prior headsets. As far as I can tell the microphone works well. Clear and crisp, no 'crunchy' clips or blips like I was getting with other headsets.

I literally just took it out of the box in the middle of a meeting, paired it, and went straight to work. The only warning I'd give people is that it will be loud, by comparison, initially, but otherwise a seamless integration. I'm writing this review after sitting through my second meeting with it, so I can't speak to the battery life, but I'm impressed enough to write this review immediately upon use.

title: Best Value Earbuds for 2023
text:
Are you an audiophile?
Get eShures, Phaizon, or whichever wired version you fancy.

Do you constantly need to take calls?
Get a proper speaker audio.

Do you glue you ears to headsets every waking min?
Get a wired headset

Do you want a Vinyl, 1028 bit audio for $25?
Jus cut off your ears, everything will sound the same by then.

Is $25 too expensive for you?
Try and make World Class audio for $25 or less. (I will be the first to try it).

————-

Barring these expectations, the sound quality is MUCH better than my previous ACIL headphones (which already have decent sound - not an audiophile). You can hear the separation between Tweeter n bass w some mids (nothing like Grammys but above standard $1 earbuds).

Mic while true is kinda weak. ~50% of volume (try making a headset wo a proper speaker mic), you will NOT get the same fidelity as a regular landline. But is decent enough talking in a quiet room.

Pairing. BTv5.3 is fast, stable and longer range ~10m (I noticed I can walk to corridor without losing signal. Previous ACIL could not).

Noise cancellation. Forget it. I actually want some background noise cancellation but able to hear traffic. (Works for me). But if you absolutely need to close out outside noise, get a proper headset.

Battery. MILD to moderate use (not all day), I was able to stretch this for almost a week (casual use). AMAZING battery. (20hrs claimed. Lasts forever!!)

Controls. Forget it. If you don’t like using your phone, it’s difficult to control this as the menu is behind your neck (try reaching for it while wearing a scarf during the winter). Any other location will unbalance the headset.

Fit. Excellent doesn’t fall off is almost any position. (Don’t use it while bungee jumping pls).

Magnets. Excellent. This is the bane of most headsets. These one come w powerful (maybe) neodymium magnets. Strong and holds on when not in use.
(Pls don’t put it in your pocket, it will destroy any headset).

Charge over usb-C (next gen charging). Fantastic. Didn’t test charge time. it does claim to have fast charging. (I jus use spare headsets)

I would never spend above $20-$30 for good quality earbuds. If you want more then spend more for professional music/ wired headsets.

Other that that. It’s as good as it gets. I read a little bit about the company. They are Engineers and truly care about their product.

Happy to support the smaller-medium size Businesses.

Keep Rocking!

Thank you

However, I wound up returning these headphones for one specific reason: the audio circuitry in the earmuff is sharp-edged and quite obtrusive, with only the thinnest of fabric as the covering. No matter how I situated the headphones on my head, my ears pressed directly against this hardware. I was constantly aware of the pressure and it caused a lot of discomfort after only a few minutes of wear. My ears are not particularly large, so for $200, that is an unacceptable flaw to me.

I have since given in and purchased a pair of Bose QC 35s and absolutely love them. App support, superior controls, and unmatched comfort...they are worth the extra money. title: Definitely not worth full price
text:
Alright, really, it's tough to say that this headset does anything correctly all the time. I'm a tech savvy guy (guru, this is my job, etc), but this headset is really just inconsistent. The best use I've found for it is to use it as a pair of wireless headphones with my laptop for listening to music while working. However, it's not my top choice simply because it's not padded like a headset I would normally use. I've also used it for watching videos, which isn't too big a problem except that there is a fraction of a second delay. Your brain can adjust to it pretty easy for movies, but you can't use this as a gaming headset. Where reaction time and positional audio are important, this is simply unusable. Granted, this is probably true for any bluetooth device, but I'm just confirming it.

Now, the complaints about using it for music/movies. Sometimes, the wireless connection just flakes out and all you hear is static. It usually works itself out after maybe 10 minutes, but it still happens occasionally after that (maybe once every 5-10 minutes). These instances usually last 10-15 seconds too, which is annoyingly long. Also, sometimes the headphones just make a connection that sounds like garbage. I've tried with 2 laptops, and with both it seems to be random. Sometimes the headset will sound great, other times, I can't even begin to describe how terrible it sounds. Not that I have high standards for audio quality but it brings it to a completely un-enjoyable level similar to people talking across a 2-way radio. Sometimes turning off the headset and re-pairing will fix it, sometimes it doesn't work until after the laptop is rebooted. It's really just annoying and I can't ever just trust that it'll work.

Surely this works as a headset for your phone at least... Just for the record, I never had any trouble pairing it with any of my devices. I originally dropped money on this because my phone's earpiece was broken (some loose wiring, didn't feel like fixing it) so I thought this would allow me to make voice calls without having to use the speakerphone again. I thought it sounded fine for hearing music from my phone and the call recipient's voice, but I made 2 calls to my own mother and 1 call to a friend and both kept asking me to just put them on speakerphone because apparently my voice quality was terrible and full of static.

If this were a cheap bluetooth headset, I'd figure I got what I paid for. But this is supposed to retail for over 100 apparently, and I honestly wouldn't say it's even worth 50. I got it for 30 and I was still considering returning it. It's just too unreliable. When it's behaving, it's a neat little toy, but that's really the only credit I can give it.

Oh, also, the hinges everyone complains about... yeah, I feel it was stupid to make that the only means of turning the device on/off. It really does feel like it'll break at some point, being all plastic and requiring some amount of force. If you really think this is a device you're interested in, I'd urge you to try one first and see if it magically doesn't have any of the flaws I described and be sure it'll work for you.

title: One of the best pair of headphones iv'e heard to date.
text:
Take note that these are my first pair headphones that goes over $150 , so lets get started .

(BUILD QUALITY)
These headphones by far are the most durable pair of headphones iv'e ever owned and held, taken that they're $300 i wouldn't expect less ,just by holding them makes me feel like they can survive a three story drop to the ground and i bet they can . Everything from the headband down just screams quality in such a way that your money is being worth of and that applies to the sound as well, but we'll get into that in a bit.

(COMFORT)
All i can say is that these headphones are quite comfortable not the most comfortable iv'e tried but still to the average consumer they well very much find them satisfying to wear. No wearing fatigue at all overtime even though the clamping force is kinda strong, it makes me feel like they're telling me "i got you ", like they're never gonna let go and i like that in a way and it's all because of the headband , because of it's compact shape to give it a low profile it kinda conforms to your head and it really adds to the comfort ,but they will start to fall if you're head knocking like a possessed person to some heavy dubstep i can tell ya that . On to the ear pads , even though the ear pads are not too plush they're really comfortable ,but the comfort varies on the size of your ears , my experience with them is that my ears fit perfectly not too big or not too small and it has been great experience for me , my ears don't even touch the divers but that's just me , if you know that you're ears are big i suggest getting the XL pads i am myself are planning on purchasing them because who doesn't want 2X the comfort .

(BLUETOOTH CONNECTIVITY & BUTTON FUNCTIONALITY)
Not much to say here but when it comes to Bluetooth it's no joke, i can hardly tell the difference between when it's connected via Bluetooth or wired, yes it's that good and also they can go really far without braking up ,i can literally walk around some parts of my house with them on while my phone is in my room and nothing , i can say the max range can be up to about 50 feet or so . The buttons on these headphones i can say is that the placement is adequate and the feel of when you press on them are not really rouged but is enough to satisfy anyone. When it come to the functionality of the buttons it's really easy to operate [middle button : one tap = play/pause , two taps = skip track , three taps = previous track] and there's just the volume up and volume down, when using these buttons i find them very responsive but not too responsive where it's instant but over over all they're really good .

(SOUND QUALITY)
Now taken that these are my first headphones over $150 you'd expect me to say that these are the best iv'e heard and you're right ,the fidelity in this masterpiece of an headphone are insane , The highs are very present ,the mids are in a position where i can say that they are slightly less present but still has a strong influence and now the lows , i can say that they are as present as the mids but yet it doesn't distort the mids at all ,it actually blends with it really well also it's so strong that the headphone literally shake ,kinda like the sony pulse. Now on to the volume levels , i can tell ya that these headphones get way louder than the average headphone wired or non wired , when it's on Bluetooth mode the volume levels to me are way louder than wired ,that's because of the mini vamp inside the headphones to push that extra volume that normal Bluetooth headphones don't provide.

Ratings
BUILD QUALITY : 10/10
COMFORT : 7.5/10
BLUETOOTH : 10/10
BUTTON FUNCTIONALITY : 9/10
SOUND QUALITY: 10?10

OVERALL : 9.5/10

title: Great Sounding Headphone at a Great Price
text:
I'll start by stating that this is my first set of over ear headphones, but what sold me on these was being wired with the in-line mic. More on that towards the end, but I did NOT want a headphone that would be useless once the battery died.

I've had these about two weeks now and I am overly satisfied! Mixed purpose use between listening to music during work/gym and taking conference calls. These work very well for both uses.

Sound::: fantastic! Gone are the days of endlessly tweaking the equalizer to make music sound good to my ear, these are brilliant with just a flat EQ! Some may say (and have said in other reviews) that these are a little bass heavy and I think that is slightly true. It definitely packs a good punch but hits very clear in my opinion, not boomy. I like my music to have a nice, full and rich sound which to me means having strong low frequency output. The highs are also extremely clear, making listening to great female vocalists that much more enjoyable. Smaller, lesser heard background sounds can definitely be heard with these.

It probably depends on your source but I didn't experience tooooo much difference between wired and bluetooth mode. I first tried them in bluetooth mode and I was awed with how well they sounded! So regardless you are going to get a great sound.

Battery::: I can't speak to battery life as I almost never use them in wireless mode.

Comfort::: This is the only drawback to the Crossfade Wireless. My initial impression was "these are really comfortable!" But then after a couple days use I literally could not go 10 minutes without wanting to take these off. I made the very quick decision to upgrade to the XL pads and it's worth every penny. These give a sturdy hold on your head which makes them good for moving about, workouts, etc.

Value::: Excellent value, in my opinion. These actually were not on my radar at first because I kept searching "top headphones under $100, then under $150, then under $200" and was struggling to find a good pair that met my needs but didn't break the bank. Well, at the time of release these were $300 headphones, so they did not show up on any "best under $200" lists. Easily worth every dollar of the ~$100 I think I paid. You get great functionality with exceptional sound quality.

Noise Isolation/Cancellation::: This wasn't a high priority for me but noise isolation is okay. After upgrading to the XL pads the noise isolation became very good, but still don't expect to be in silence. These do not have noise cancellation.

I couldn't believe how difficult it was to find a well rated over-ear headphone with an in-line mic. They all had mics that only worked in bluetooth mode, and my work machine does not have bluetooth where I take all my calls so bluetooth only mics got me nowhere. The Crossfade Wireless has both an in-line mic that I use frequently as well as a built in bluetooth mic for running in bluetooth mode. I'm not certain of voice quality, but I asked 5 or so of my colleagues if I sound okay and they all said yes.

Only reason for 4 stars, as others have mentioned as well, is after 5 or 6 days of owning these I HAD to upgrade the earpads to the XL cushions. The XLs seriously saved this headphone and my ear pain from being crushed against the drivers. After the XL cushion swap the sound did alter slightly, making the overall sound much more balanced. I think I noticed increased noise isolation with the XL pads as well.

Overall recommend!

text:
I am not a fan of reviews right after or during an unboxing, I do believe that in order to review most items objectively, you need some time to really use them every day.

I've had this pair for two months now so let's try to separate this review into some categories:
- Sound: Warm, heavy on the bass and, as other user and critics review said, it sounds equally great with or without the cable. You can use these for ALL kind of music and expect great detail and differentiation of frequencies
- Battery life: 13 solid hours
- Price: 299 as of Feb 2016, which is extremely competitive, particularly because V-Moda's previous model, the M-100 was introduced at that same price point. Compared with other brands, it is also pretty competitive but you have to consider that these do not have active noise cancellation
- Noise cancellation/Sound leaking: As previously said, these come with passive noise cancellation, meaning no ultrasonic sound blocking external sounds, but thanks to that, it adds to a better clarity and no head aches. In terms of sound leakage, these isolate your music pretty well, you will be able to use them on commute trips without disturbing people around you
- Comfort: Great but not superb, I suggest you get the XL cushions to make this category Excellent. The head band is not too tight, you can wear these for 3 hours or more with the XL cushions. Out of the box, the original ear pads are a little small so you will be able to continually use these only for some time before your ears get extremely hot or start hurting
- Design: The design carries from the M-100, while timeless, at this point this category is probably the lowest point of this product. Do not get me wrong, the headphones have a beautiful design and with a terrific construction and the ability to replace the side shields is a really clever idea that got enhanced with the support for 3D ones, V-Moda has used the same look for a few good years now. Imagine if the most beautiful cars stayed with the same look over many, many years
- Support: One of the best things about this company is its commitment to an outstanding customer service, so this category needs to be mentioned. For example, they have a 30-day satisfaction guaranteed when purchasing these (not sure if that is applicable to Amazon's purchases), second example: they allow you to keep up with new products for a significant discount thanks to the Immortal Life Program, if you have not heard about it, it is basically a trade-in program which is much, much better to use than selling your old headphones via Craigslist to get the latest product
- Cons: The only downsize of these is that for some odd reason the minimum volume is a bit high

If you are considering a good pair, look no further, get these, make sure to get the XL ear pads and start customizing them with new shields, 3D printed or not

title: Stop looking for headphones and buy these. These are "the one."
text:
I bought these headphones based on reviews I've seen scattered on the internet. On recommendation, I bought these - slightly scared I spent $300 on headphones that are subpar. Once I received the package itself, I knew I wasn't dealing with any middle-of-the-mall pair of headphones. The packaging was nice; you could immediately tell that the gods presented you with a musical gift based on packaging alone. The headphones came with x1 micro-USB cable & x1 analog audio cable. They sync'ed to my phone without any problem what-so-ever but I have not had the opportunity to sync these headphones with another device while simultaneously playing music. These are over-the-ear headphones and they ISOLATE noise; they do not cancel noise. However when you're jamming out to your favorite tracks...you can't hear anything at all.

The sound quality is the main selling point here. Sound quality is superb and will surpass just about any pair of headphones that seemed worthy enough to cling to your ears. The high & lows are incredibly powerful. I was able to pickup partitions of my favorite music that I've never heard before; the clarity the VMODA Crossfade provide is unmatched. This, in no way, distorted mids. The Crossfade wireless perfectly ties highs mids & lows together like the Holy Trinity. Unlike some headphones I've experienced, you can FEEL the bass resonating from them. This makes the music you're listening much more enjoyable.

A concern many have had would be the quality of music with Bluetooth compared to a wired connection. Fear not! These bad boys sound almost exactly alike when compared to a wired connection. There is a very, very small difference between the two. You would be incredibly surprised how similar the 2 connections are. These are, without a doubt, the best sounding Bluetooth headphones you will listen to.

Overall durability? You're not breaking these headphones any time soon. The headband is made of steel yet provides a lot of flexibility. I purposely tried to bend the steel bands connected to the drivers and couldn't. You will have to put in serious effort in order to bend these beasts. There are kevlar wrapped wires hanging above each driver; they do not get in the way in any fashion. Some have complained about getting this wire caught when taking the headphones off but I do not see how this is possible. To protect your favorite headphones, you will also receive a nice case to store your headphones & accessories into; the case has a decent amount of durability behind it so you can store your jam boxes and be on your way. The battery life is also something to be remembered. These have latest almost 8 hours before needing to be charged again. Need a quick charge before heading to the gym? Thankfully these babies are equipped with quick charge. 15 minutes of charging will get you 2 hours of listening!

While these sleek pair of headphones scream superb quality - it does come with a few cons. One major con are the 'memory foam' ear pads. Since I use these headphones throughout a majority of my day...my ears would begin to hurt and I'd have to take my headphones off. My ears were pressing against the drivers which made them more & more uncomfortable to wear. I solved this problem by spending the extra money on a pair of XL ear pads. Installing these XL ear pads was incredibly easy. Some have said the earpads 'increase' sound quality but I don't find this to be true however they also did not take AWAY from my music experience. The ear pads are a comfort upgrade only.

Want to use these headphones for gaming on your Xbox One? These are excellent gaming headphones; Don't expect something similar to a 5.1/7.1 surround sound though - remember...these aren't designed for gaming but make an excellent alternative regardless. If you plan on chatting while gaming: do yourself a favor - buy the BoomPro microphone. The stock analog cable DOES transmit voice however you may sound incredibly muffled to a point where no one can hear you. You CANNOT sync these headphones via Bluetooth to an Xbox one. You will need to plug these headphones directly into the Xbox one controller.

Verdict? Buy. Buy. Buy. Take the $300 and spend it. Once you encapsalte yourself into the music with these beastly headphones you will become a V-MODA enthusiest. I sure am now and will recommend these to ANYBODY in search for new headphones. While the price is steep...you absolutely cannot deny the overall music quality & headphone durability.

TL;DR
PROs:
Highs & lows sound incredibly superb.
Bass so distinct it can be felt while simtaneously not distorting any highs, mids or lows.
Bluetooth vs Analog connection sound incredibly similar and the difference can go unnoticed.

title: Awesome SQ; the fact that it's wireless in icing on the cake!
text:
Just recently received the V-MODA Crossfade Wireless and I got to say, I think the team at V-MODA hit this one out of the park. Just a little on my background -- I have owned the M-80 (which I have since gifted), and I own the XS as well as the M-100 so I have a sense of the V-MODA house sound. I also have owned a bunch of other portable headphones (you can check my profile to see which ones), mostly because I appreciate a lot of different sound signatures and certain unique characteristics of each headphone I own. Which could also mean I can't make up my mind lol but I love them all for different reasons and wish I could just be the one-headphone kind of person but alas, I cannot. I also listen to all genres, mainly rock/alternative. I listen to most of my music on-the-go, being that I live in NYC and I am always on the move. So portability, great sound quality, and isolation are all paramount. I also appreciate style and comfort but not as much as SQ.

For a long time, I would be skeptical about BT headphones. Although every once in a while I'd see someone with a set of BT cans from well-known companies, and I'd think there must be a certain kind of liberty I am missing out on, not having to deal with cables. I thought to myself, I would love to try that and have that freedom on the go. But like I said SQ, is above and beyond, necessary for me as now my ears have been spoiled by good SQ. I don't claim to be an expert and don't have 'golden ears'. But I do go by what I hear and how I feel hearing it. And I'd like to think that I know what crappy, murky sound, sounds like. On that note...

I know I might be hyping these up, but I really really dig these cans and feel like they might be the ultimate portable solution for me. Because of the convenience of no cables as well as the awesome SQ, I am afraid it may make all my other cans a bit... obsolete. Only time will tell and there are some cans that I own that are staples in collection but some others could be on their way out soon (as I would hope to simplify and thin out the herd at some point) I do love different sound signatures and different characteristics that headphones have to offer this CFW takes the cake for my needs. To my ears, they are detailed, warm, pleasant, lively and enjoyable on the move or even at home. They are on the warm side and the low end boasts a full bodied beautiful clean bass. Compared to the M-100 I feel the CFW sounds a bit cleaner across the spectrum TBH. In wireless mode, they are very very similar, almost identical. In wired mode, it is slightly more improved with tighter bass and airier highs. Otherwise not a huge difference to the point where I would want to use these in wired mode. They sound too good in wireless mode! It's great however that they sound so good in wired mode, and that I have the option to use them and know I'm getting great SQ whenever the battery runs out, on the go. So being that I had been thinking about getting a BT headphone for a while but concerned about SQ and also any possible BT technology malfunctions that I read were happening with other cans recently, I was intrigued upon learning that V-MODA was coming out with a wireless headphone and keeping tabs on it. Count me a fan of the V-MODA house sound (as well as the beautiful aesthetics and BQ) and I was just hoping that the SQ was going to be up to snuff. I am happy to say that the CFW exceeded my expectations.

So let's get into the sound:

Bass: The bass hits hard with plenty of impact, remains tight, and reaches deep. I have a deep appreciation for lower sub bass detail and can't stand anything that has that one-note bass. Anyone who has heard the M-100 knows how deep it reaches and these deliver all the same. It's definitely north of neutral but there is plenty of detail and texture, and for portable applications, it's the perfect amount of bass as the low end is the first part of the frequency to go when in a loud environment. The lows give the overall sound plenty of body and warmth, without sounding slow at the least. Good sense of PRaT and energy as well. Very tight and clean IMHO.

Mids: The mids align nicely with the rest of the spectrum. They are not in your face or pushed forward in any way, but they're not recessed in the least. To my ears, this is great because if the mids were any more forward they would be fatiguing, yet I don't feel like I am missing out on the detail with instruments and vocals at all. Male vocals sound deep and smooth and female vocals sound very natural and not overly bright. There is a great clarity and instruments have a nice sense of decay without ever sounding slow. Very smooth and natural-sounding overall. Feels like you're in the orchestra-section at a concert.

Highs: The highs are sparkly without harshness! They are smooth but not overly smooth and nicely extended. This is a great feat because you have to have some sparkle for high hats, trumpets, and brush strokes to sound accurate with the right timbre. At the same time, especially when if I am in a loud setting and want to increase the volume by a notch or so, these haven't fatigued my ears with the treble. Nice and smooth yet sparkly.

Soundstage and imaging: I would say soundstage and imaging are about average. Good width and height. The M-100 sounds slightly deeper in comparison but for me, made things sound a little too far away. I like that these sound a bit more intimate yet still having the out-of-your-head experience. While the M-100 sounds like a deep hall, I'd say these sound like a deep and wide chamber orchestra room. Sounds like I'm at an intimate, unplugged (no pun intended) jam session with my favorite band. It's a delight to my ears, warm and sweet.

Isolation: Isolation is about average, not bad for a circumaural portable, better than the XS, not as good as my HD25 or DT-1350 which isolate a bit more.

If I could characterize these headphones in a few words, I would say they are musical, detailed, euphonic, natural with a "fun" sound that any audiophile can enjoy. These, being wireless is incredible icing on the cake, as that is never at the expense of SQ to my ears. I have these on my head and still can't believe I am not connected to my DAP by a wire (using these with my iPhone 6 listening to ALAC and Spotify). They are highly convenient and if my fiancee doesn't permanently kidnap these from me, I can see myself using this headphone as my predominant headphone, only using the others that I have in case I miss a certain headphone's sonic sig/characteristics.

This is my first BT headphone so I'm happy to see how easy and intuitive it's been to use. Also the buttons are well-placed while being nicely discreet. I love that there is no obvious, bright blue flashing light that tells the world this is a BT can. The small v-light that lights up on the bottom is nice and discreet. So far so good with the BT connection to my phone. I haven't heard any clipping or anything. I am very impressed. It appears V-MODA has taken a lot of time testing these out, which I expect no less. Build quality is great. Battery life is also great, I have only charged these once when I received them in the last few days (about a couple of hours a day) and they still have a full charge. I know some people which that these had the clip-fold but frankly I am quite ok with it. This way I am a little more ginger with these cans -- I tend to be rough with the M-100 when I would fold them up throw them in my bag. I would rather less moving parts and so far they have been quite the travel buddy. The M-100 will be my beater, slightly more portable back-up.

Lastly, these are at an amazing price-point. Glad that V-MODA did not boost up the price to way more because of its BT capabilities, like a lot of other companies have. I think for anyone who have come to appreciate the V-MODA house sound with the M-100 and XS, these are a no-brainer. Plus it's great to know that V-MODA always has your back in case there is a problem with your gear and has outstanding warranty and customer service. All in all, I am a happy camper and these will be a permanent staple in my stable of cans. Happy listening and thanks for reading!

title: From the Perspective of an Athlete
text:
I'm generally not one to write any reviews on any products, but after owning a set of V-MODA Crossfade Wireless (1) headphones for about 2- years and using them almost everyday, I just had to express my satisfaction with them. To make it clear, I am no sound aficionado and when it comes to sound quality, I'm not the one to be asking how it sounds compared to other headphones of similar caliber. To me, I just know the volume is loud enough and the bass is delightfully bassy.

Rather, I'm pretty familiar with their durability as I use these headphones whenever I workout or run. Granted, there are most definitely better headphones to be running with and maybe specific sports earbuds fit the runner's niche but I've never had any issues while running with these.

Before owning a Crossfade Wireless, I always used wired headphones and earbuds during my workouts. As you would guess, the wires would always get tangled with the weights, sometimes trapped under them and snapped, and they would also become extremely annoying on runs. With the V-MODAs, the "Wireless" part of the name eliminated all of those issues. On the rare but inevitable days that I forget to charge my headphones and am forced to plug them in, I’ve still not issues with their durability. Sure, it’ll be annoying and still get caught between my body and the bench or some weights, but they have yet to snap like previous wires.

In terms of durability of the headphones themselves, there was one particular incident (out of many), that colored me impressed and inspired this review. I will start with this: Don’t ask me how my headphones got into this predicament.

A few weeks ago, at the gym again, I was minding my business, enjoying the workout with my V-MODAs. My friend comes over and asks me to spot him while he squats 405lb (~183kg) for a few reps. As you should when you spot, I took off my headphones but put them on the ground behind me (you should never put you’re prized $300 headphones on the floor in the first place). I spot him a few reps and his last one, he gets stuck at the bottom of the squat. The hotel we’re at doesn’t have safety rails to drop the bar on. Not thinking about my headphones behind me, I pull the bar off his back and the weights on one side of the barbell land on my headphones.

Needless to say, because I’m writing this review, my headphones survived the incident and still work like new (knock on wood that delayed issues don’t appear). There are a few cracks on the silver lining beside the earpads but no major damages.

Overall, I am extremely pleased with these headphones and would not trade them for anything in the world except maybe the Crossfade Wireless 2. Maybe when the ones I have now die but may that never happen.

My only complaint with the headphones were that the stock earpads would crimp my ears during long gaming sessions, and commutes, especially on plane trips. It really wasn’t a terribly big issue but I decided to invest $20 on some XL earpads that arrived yesterday morning. As soon as I installed them (easy as pie to do so) and put them on, it was instant satisfaction. I then put them through two intense workouts in the same day and my love for the earpads and headphones increased tenfold.

Absolutely amazing, if you’re willing to spend $300+ on headphones, look into these, especially if you need a set of gym headphones and don’t want the run-of-the-mill look and sound of Beats lifters.

title: One of the best over-ear headphones available
text:
I don't normally leave reviews for products, but after trying out a few pairs, I felt compelled to write one for anyone trying to decide which pair they should get.

I've tried a bunch of over-ear headphones with wireless capability, and the top three contenders are the Sennheiser Momentum 2.0 Wireless, Sony H.ear on wireless NC, and the V-Moda Crossfade Wireless.

They are all in a similar price range, so here are my opinions regarding the build quality, design, sound, comfort and functionality.

Build/Design/Comfort:
The V-Moda's win in this category, feeling the most sturdy, They feel like you could drop them off of your roof and they'll still be intact. It comes with braided cords and a great case. Unfortunately, they do not fold up which can make portability a bit more difficult, but they more than make up for that fact with their durability. Plus out of the three, they are the best looking when you put them on. Their design is stylish and sleek without looking gigantic or weird. I was able to wear them for hours at a time without any complaints. For added comfort, you can get the XL pads which improve them comfort even further.

The Sennheiser's are a close second. They are the lightest and definitely most comfortable, but the design is industrial looking, which may not be for everyone. I found them quite ugly to be honest. If you have a small head, the ends will stick out past the ear pads, making it just look weird. The cords attached to the headphones through the headband are also very noticeable and curl up, which makes their design look kind of messy. They do fold up though. Build quality is average.

I tried the Sony's but found myself not being able to tolerate them for more than an hour, leaving my head and ears sore. They come in a chic array of bright colors and are definitely the most streamlined looking, with no loose cords visible. They also have the best controls, separate ones for volume and track control on the right side. The other two have only volume and a multi function button to rewind/skip tracks (double click to advance, triple click to advance). However, they feel somewhat cheap like they may break. And I did not like the bulky drive units, they stick out way too much to the side and look extremely weird. For a headphone that is as much as a fashion statement as it is for Hi-fi music, I found this a major drawback.

V-Moda: 4.5/5
Sennheiser: 4.25/5
Sony: 4/5

Sound:
I'm gonna keep this short because I am no audiophile and I think you probably won't go wrong with any of the three choices above. I use them for daily listening when traveling to and from work since I take public transportation

V-moda: Has the loudest bass, but other sounds are still noticeable and appreciable. It doesn't drown out the rest of the song, but if you don't like bass then these are not the headphones for you. Does not offer any active noise cancellation (ANC), but has passive noise isolation that drowned out most ambient sounds, but still allows you to hear something loud/close by.

Sennheiser: I thought these had the best sound (but not by much over the V-moda). Bass is there but not as loud as the V-moda, and the mids and highs are bright and clear. They give your music that special quality that really makes you want to listen to everything over again. Has ANC but isn't the best for that. You could also hear yourself walking which I did not like.

Sony: These had the worst sound out of the three for me, but that doesn't mean they are bad. Bass was tight, treble was controlled but the mids seemed muffled to me. There were parts in songs that seemed muted compared to the other two. ANC was slightly better than the Sennheisers. Their price is high and I don't think it's worth $350 for the sound that you get.

For all three wired was better than wireless, offering a fuller sound. I think this would be true of all headphones. You could listen to all of them in either mode if you prefer. I wouldn't get any of them for the noise cancellation because it's honestly not that great (I felt like I was able to hear the same amount of ambient sounds on all three). If that is your prime factor in deciding which pair you should get, then I recommend the Bose QC 35, which has amazing ANC but average sound.

Sennheiser: 5/5
V-Moda: 4.75/5
Sony: 4.5/5

In the end, I chose the V-Moda because I liked the design much more than the other two. They just look sleek and fashionable, are not gigantic looking and sound is great. If you don't like loud bass then I would recommend the Sennheisers. If you are solely concerned with the look and colors, then try the Sony's. Plus they are cheaper (because there is no ANC).

Minor gripes with the V-Moda that I can easily look past but may be annoying:
In line control on wire does not offer volume controls
When wired, if you have the headphones extended the wire may brush against you clothes causing a bit of a weird sound
Do not fold up.

Noise cancellation is fantastic. The sound quality is pretty good but honestly i expected a bit more from headphones that normally cost $200. I got them for $98 so they’re satisfactory at that reduced price but by no means would i have purchased these headphones for the full retail price.

Sound quality is great with the headphones straight out of the box but it took some time for me to adjust to the isolation of the noise cancellation since my old headphones don’t do much in terms of noise cancellation.

After the adjustment period i can say that im happy with the headphones and the fact that they charge through USB-C is great, however the included cable is embarrassingly short.

The headphones don’t feel particularly premium in terms of build quality but the matte plastic does offer a nice feel. The ambient noise mode is a nice addition but I don’t feel like ill get much use out of it due to the fact that i mainly use over ear headphones at home and i usually use Airpods when i go outdoors.

It is also important to note that Sony’s more expensive $300-$400 headphones seem to come with a case for protection when carrying the headphones in a bag but these do not come with a case for those who are curious about that. It makes no real difference for me though.

Lastly I tested these through various styles of music. These headphones are okay with dubstep and offer a decent amount of bass. Pop music sounds okay but the bass can be overbearing and can feel like it’s competing with the acoustics. I tried listening to classical music such as Handel’s messiah and the great gate of Kiev but i can safely say that i wouldn’t recommend these headphones for classical music fans. title: Bluetooth interferes with Wifi. Good sound over quality connection is a no contest.
text:
When i first got these they felt cheap all of literally a single day They was really light weight which can be a good thing you don't want something weighing you down. But you want something that will make it through the day to day for a reasonable amount of time. Mind you about 2yrs ago I bought "Sony WH-CH700N Wireless Noise Cancelling Black Bluetooth Headphones" for the same $200 price for most people that kind of pricey for a set. But as they say you get what you pay for. To my surprise they ended up being solid. Infact i still use them when I work out and still hold up pretty well. The reason i picked these wasn't to replace that pair. but for a set of Beats that I kind of mishandled but also pretty solid. So why not get a more recent version of Noise Cancelling Sony's they have to be better right?
Wrong!
*Cons*
*Noise cancelling I believe should be considered more of a noise suppressant and for both sets felt more like suction cups being placed on my ears. but this pair felt more of an annoyance

*Second as I mention the durableness of the WH-CH700N set was great, plenty of times I've dropped them and still worked just fine. I felt if I put these on the wrong way or even looked at them wrong they would snap.

*Lastly the previous night I paired them with my Bluetooth and suddenly it was a noticeable different in speed. I'm no stranger to decreases of speed, I do sometimes have more windows/programs than necessary opened. but not as glaring as this issue. It didn't hit me until the following day. So I disconnected and boom everything loaded fine. I looked up that bluetooth and Wifi run on the same GHz. But I never knew that it was the first time I have had it interfere with me. Good sound over quality connection is a no contest.

Pros
*The sound was pretty good not amazing enough to out weigh the cons but solid enough I could hear everything clear from the highs to the lows. And No hiss when talking like with some of the cheaper sets

*The Bass was very good all things considering as well.

*Having the option for the 3.5mm jack fixed the blue tooth issue

So if you can look past the physical appearance of this headset for decent sound it might be for you. But for me this could sell for maybe a quality $60 price tag, but $200 is way too overpriced

title: High quality headset for a reasonable price!
text: This headset is a must buy if your in the market for one. Many years ago I bought a cheap bluetooth headset thinking there couldn't be much of a difference in them as they're were so many on the market. It was horrible. The sound quality was bad, people couldn't hear me, it hurt to wear; all in all just a terrible experience. From that point on I've only used expensive headsets from companies like Jabra and Plantronics, and always paying upwards of hundreds of dollars a pop. That was until a month ago. My last headset finally gave up the ghost and I found myself in the market for another one. After reading many reviews I thought I'd give the Icomtofit G3 a try, and boy was I impressed. The sound quality is great, the battery will last me almost an entire week on a single charge (I use it while I'm driving, so about an hour a day), and it's super comfortable. It comes with a handful of different ear gels so you can get the right fit. It also comes in a hinged plastic case to protect it when you're not wearing it. And not that it should ever be an issue, as most people keep their phone near them when using a headset, but the range on the G3 is incredible. I was talking to a friend one evening and ran into a store, completely forgetting that I had dropped my phone into the cupholder in the truck. I was almost to the back of the store (probably 50-70 ft. away) before I started experiencing issues with the call quality. It never disconnected and once I got back outside the store, the audio quality was immediately repaired. All that to say that if you're looking for a new bluetooth headset, look no further.

title: Comfortable little headset with great speaker/sound quality and connectivy range.
text: I am a pediatric Speech Language Pathologist working in the school system. I work across 5 schools with very different COVID19 protocols in place; however, all 5 schools conduct ARD meetings via Zoom, but due to FERPA regulations we are required to use headsets to ensure students privacy. I ordered another company's over the ear headset which worked great for the first 2 weeks, but it was uncomfortable and then I would get complaints from meeting participants stating "you sound like a robot", "you're fading in/out", and "we can't hear you". That's so unprofessional & embarrassing.  I average 15-25 ARDs a week so I returned that headset and researched comments on Amazon until coming across this Bluetooth headset. The comments alone gave me hope so I placed my order and just used my husband's big, bulky gaming headset in the interim. I looked like an astronaut or a pilot during the meetings, BUT they could hear me. The morning after I placed my order the headset arrived in a cut little case with a charger and replacement ear pads. This little device is a game changer. It's small, easy to wear (I hate things in my ear, hence the reason for originally ordering over the ear style, but this doesn't go IN your ear but instead has a flat ear pad that rests ON your ear and I can easily reposition it higher/lower outside of my eardrum). It's not big/bulky and is wireless!!!! No need to unplug anything while I run and take bathroom breaks or grab snacks/food between meetings. The connectivity range and speaker/sound quality are amazing. I've been able to check my mail and water my plants in the backyard while still connected to Pandora. All 5 schools immediately noticed the difference and complimented the headset's speaker and sleek, unnoticeable look. The battery life is great also and has lasted upward to 7+ hours on one full charge. I'd definitely recommend this headset to others.

title: Great Bluetooth Headset
text:
Packaging was easy to deal with and protected the product well. Packaging is all cardboard (no plastic) so recycles easily which I like. Inside the package was a warranty card, instruction booklet, and the headset in a plastic case. The hard plastic case holds the headset well and protects it from damage. It doesn't snap shut but the hinge is spring loaded and keeps it closed. Also included are two other ear cushions to adjust to the inside of your ear (three total).

The ear hook pivots in two directions (around the earpiece and where the chrome ring is) to adjust the headset to your ear and face. It can be worn on either ear. It will need to be folded flat to fit in the storage case.

It comes partially charged. Connection is micro USB. Single LED on arm indicates red for charging and blue when charged. To charge fully took about 20-30 minutes.

Four buttons on headset control all functions; these are explained very well in the included instructions.

Pairing was easy and without issue, displays as "G3" on your device. After initial pairing all future connections were quick and automatic (tested with a Android smartphone). Can be connected to two devices at the same time. Voice prompts in earpiece indicates power and connection status, which is clearer than beeps that some other devices have.

Call quality is excellent, people I have called have told me they can hear me clearly with minimal if any background noise. You can also listen to music with this headset from your device, but with only being in one ear it understandably won't sound as good as with a stereo headset.

I am very happy with this headset and would recommend it to others.

P.S. Don't forget to look under the cover in the bottom of the box - you will find more ear cushions and a short USB charging cord. I just happened to notice it just before I went to recycle the box.

As for the sound, for a guy who used to work on fighter jets and may be not the best of hearing, the volume is GREAT.  The bass is definitely noticeable and everything is clear.  I guess since I want to be as honest as possible, the only complaint might be that when I'm tinkering with my phone and playing around with different apps with audio, the headset activates and there's a low buzzing sounds.  Presumably, the buzz continues, but is drowned out by the actual audio. Bottom line, I'm considering buying another set so I can have them in multiple places. text:
I'm a big fan of Apple's Earpods since they fit in my ears great. The Kimwood headphones fit just as well.

They make a great alternative since they are a lot cheaper than the original Apple product and they don't look exactly the same so we are able to tell different pairs of headphones apart in our house.

I do feel like the headphones lack some bass that the Apple version has, but I'm primarily using them as a headset for phone calls so for my purposes they are great. In fact, in some situations I think I can hear a little better with them since there isn't as much background bass to drown out the voice I'm trying to hear.

A nice surprise was they also include a silver carrying bag so they don't get tangled with other items in my luggage.

Overall, for the price, these are a great, less expensive, alternative to Apple Earpods

title: Works well until it doesn't, but replacement is an improvement
text:
I bought this to replace a pair of Samsung with a damaged cord (an accident that was my fault). The Apple earphones were overpriced, in my opinion. The black color and the design of the ear pieces are what drew me to the Kimwood, But in less than two months, the cord near the jack became faulty. There is no visible damage, but there seems to be an internal problem that is creating a weak flow of energy. It started with an occasional hum that sounded like it needed a loop (or whatever the correct name is). A few days later, it sounded as though the voice was muffled, while the background music was at a normal level, which overpowered the voice perhaps someone can explain better than I what I was experiencing). This is all disappointing because I was initially impressed with the increased volume over the previous pair of Samsung earphones. Now I have some new, nice-looking trash.

Update:
The seller was on top of this and tried to make things right. I now have a replacement that has been working better. The volume is still superior than other earbuds I've tried, but there's an occasional low-pitched hum that occurs, which is rectified after I jiggle the jack or change the position of the cord (away from other electronic interference). I'm going from 2 stars to 4 (almost a 5, if it weren't for the aforementioned situation).

title: Great, but fragile headphones
text:
I got these headphones when they were at about 70 USD, and at that price they are great, but there are compromises to make them so good at 70 USD.

For the pros, they have decent ANC, ambient mode, fairly flat sound, and good connectivity (Bluetooth and a 3.5mm jack, and a usb-c charge-only port).

For the cons, looking at the other reviews, these headphones tend to have issues with the plastic breaking on the headband, so be cautious buying these at anything above what i paid for them. Although, if you are careful with them and fine using some duct tape to fix it, they are still usable and versatile. They also have a weird dip in their sound profile at the high end which makes some music with plenty of treble sound at best off, and at worse completely different.

If you are willing to deal with the durability issues, and they are discounted, these headphones are absolutely a great deal, but if you can't, look either up sony's lineup or around at other comparable headphones.

title: Amazing on many fronts... except battery life.
text:
I'll keep it succinct. And by the way, I'm comparing these earbuds to others in the same price range. If you're looking for a competitor to $200 earbuds, these aren't it. But anyway.

Pros:
- It has a very good distance for broadcasting. I can put my phone in my room, walk all the way downstairs, go into the laundry room, shut the door, and it still stays connected. This has the best connection I've ever had for headphones this cheap.

- The volume is amazing. You don't have to turn it up that loud at all. I can have it almost completely off and still hear just enough.

- It's hard to accidentally stop or start the audio by touching it. You have to give it a firm tap. Other wireless earbuds I had were ay too sensitive in this regard. A gnat could breathe on them and they'd turn off/on. These don't do that which is a perfect for when I'm dancing and I tilt my head.

- I like the hooks on these. They help the earbuds stay in my ears and keep them from threatening to pop out (for the most part).

- When the battery dies, it doesn't play a jump scare sound bite or hideous beeping noise. It's pleasant and I like it.

Cons:
- The main reason I'm giving it 3 stars (and I may be returning these) is because the battery life. The left earbud drains significantly faster than the right. It even charges slower. I'll leave the earbuds in their case overnight and when I put the on in the morning to exercise, the right bud is at 100% and the left is at 97%. Every time. Then, literally a minute later, the left is at 95% but the right is still at 100%. I've never had earbuds do this before and it's aggravating.

- If you wear glasses, the ear hooks will be competing for space on your ears. You might have to settle with either wearing contacts or having to rotate the earbuds so that they can rest in an acceptable manner. I have done the latter and it's fine but this may be a turn off to people.

All in all, I do recommend these but make sure to test the battery life beforehand. If the battery is wonky, return it and get a new one cuz it's worth it!

text:
I've been using these headphones for a few days and let me tell you, they are fantastic. I am not an 'expert' on headphones, but I can say that the sound quality blows away any other headphones I've had. Whilst these are billed as studio headphones and are very detailed in mids highs and lows, they have a somewhat warm sound which makes them very enjoyable for simply listening to music. I was concerned that these were going to be geared more towards studio work than casual listening, but these will do both quite well. There is plenty of bass, dubstep and electronic music sounds great. The dark green edition looks fantastic. The green parts appear dark grey unless in direct sunlight, then they appear an olive color. They are also very comfortable. The band fits a bit snug, just enough so that they won't fall off or slide when bending over, but not so much as to cause discomfort. The extra cables are also very nice to have. Keep in mind that these are closed-back headphones.

Overall I think that these are quite possibly the best all-around studio headphones for under $200. You would be remiss to not give these ample consideration if you are looking for a pair of great sounding headphones at this price point.

text: The Treblab XR100 Sport headphones are a wonderful edition to my Bluetooth earbud collection.  I just don't understand why people pay more for Power Beats.  I come from a background of sound engineering and music production so quality sound is a must for my ears.  With that being said for $21.00 (about what I paid for these at the time) these are damn good earbuds.  They have a very good sound stage and they get loud.  The lows are deep and have a nice thump and rumble.  The highs and mids at first were slightly muffled but after a couple days of break in they started to open up a bit.  I still bump up the mids slightly in my EQ to bring the vocals out a tad.  The thing with sound is it's purely a subjective subject, some people like more highs and little bass, others like more bass and less highs.  For me it depends on what I'm listening to, My music selection is very diverse, these are more for Hip-hop, Pop, RnB, Electronic, etc (my go to set for the gym)... I use my QCY-Q11's for other styles of music those are a more balanced set of earbuds (probably my favorites).

title: Audio quality is good, but you may find the user interface annoying.
text:
I wanted physically robust Bluetooth headphones with good range and good sound, and I was excited to find these on sale for $100. The good news is that the V-Moda Crossfade delivered on robustness, range, and sound; battery life was great, too. The bad news is that this unit had a defect, but, more importantly, I don't like the user interface.

I am returning this pair because of an intermittent problem with the volume-up button: unpredictably it gets very hard to press and/or makes a creaking sound, maybe more often when the narrow part of the button is pressed. This does not happen with the other two buttons. This seems like a one-off that won't happen to other people, so I could have returned for replacement, but I didn't.

The reason why I am trying something different (Pioneer SE-MS9BN-B) is because I found the user interface of the Crossfade headphones disappointing. For me the biggest disappointment is that when the Crossfade makes a Bluetooth connection it plays a surprisingly long and quite exuberant sound clip -- loudly. In fact, every time it makes a connection it resets the volume to a level I find high (5 steps above minimum) just so that it can play the exuberant sound clip loudly. I guess I could live with that, but I didn't like the rest of the user interface either--and I don't mean only that I didn't like the rest of the sound clips (though honestly I don't).

The three buttons are located at the very top of the right ear cup, next to or even partly obscured by the metal cage connecting the cup to the headband. Other headbands put the controls on the lower edge of the head cup, not up at the top next to moving parts. Also, the power switch is a slider rather than a button, which means that the device can't turn its own power off when it's idle for a while the way other headphones do: the user must remember to physically slide the switch.

Obviously these user-interface issues don't rise to the level of criminality, but this is a $200 pair of headphones. In addition to being physically robust, sounding great, having good range, and having great battery life, I think $200 headphones should be a pleasure to interact with, not just to listen to. BTW, it appears that the Crossfade user interface (including cranking up the volume for each act of exuberance) persists in the Crossfade 2 line.

For a straightforward user interface I like the JBL E50BT, which has a four-way rocker plate on one ear cup: you can press the top or bottom of the plate for volume-up or volume-down, and the forward/backward edges for call control and other functions. Power-on/off is by a brief press of a convenient button on the edge of an ear cup. That user interface unobtrusively does what it needs to do, without unnecessary machinations such as gesture pads. Sadly, I can't keep using those headphones because the plastic parts of the ear-cup sliders are crumbling into dust, hence my quest for solidly-built headphones.

title: Great sound-quality headphones, very low comfortability for me
text:
I'd like to start this off by saying that these headphones were purchased in 2015. I used them for about 3 years and have since removed them from use, though I still have them if I ever needed any noise-cancelling headphones.

Speaking of the noise cancellation, it works VERY well. Almost too well! I ran into myself getting yelled at by my parents because I couldn't hear them at all while wearing these. The sound itself was my first introduction into a good quality pair of headphones though, and I was very happy with what I got in that aspect. It captured the sounds I was looking for while not being too expensive.

Now for the not so great part of it for me. The materials of the headphones combined with it being a closed-back pair left me getting rather warm where they sat, and eventually the headphones loosened up enough to where it was only sitting on my head by the headband and absolutely no grab was happening from the earcups themselves. This may sound nice, but it actually caused the volume to not be as loud as they had originally been. This also gave me headaches at each use. I'm sure there are people who have had a better wearing experience than I, especially with that happening after a couple years and I know many have had these headphones much longer with minimal problems.

TLDR;
Pros:
-Sound Cancellation
-Overall Sound

Cons:
-Made me sweat where the headphones would touch
-Eventually loosens and causes volume loss and (in my personal case) headaches

I'm still giving the product 4 stars despite my own issues. Maybe these same things didn't happen with others, but I was happy with the sound that came from these headphones while I was able to wear them.

title: I was very excited to try these because of the good reviews about the sound quality
text:
Just... no. I'm editing my original review after finding cushions to fit my ears to test out the sound and range. I was very excited to try these because of the good reviews about the sound qualit. I might have kept these despite the growing list of cons because the bass was better than other buds I have tried. But then I saw that these are suspiciously similar to another Bluetooth earbud sold on Amazon for $22.09 (at the time of writing this). Same labels, same design, same buttons, same colors. Just a different logo printed on the home button. I wouldn't be surprised if these were made in the same factory with the same tech. If you have larger ears and want a bass heavy (muddy) sound and don't mind tinny treble, and want to keep your device within 2 ft of you while using these, go for the $22 version.

Fit: Not for small ears. These headphones came with six pairs of cushions, 3 silicone and 3 from a squishy earplug material. Would not stay in my ear for even a couple of seconds because the the clips were not even close to fitting snugly and the Bluetooth receivers weighed them down significantly.

Range: About 2ft. At 3ft. I lost connection completely after the sound got choppy. So the advantage is that you don't have a cord dangling around, but other than that, your device will need to be just as near to you if you were using corded headphones.

Sound: yes, the bass is strong, but muddy. It squashes out the rest of the range. The treble is quite tinny.

*For reference, Apple headphones are too large to fit in my ears. I use Sony MDR-XB950BT over-the-ear headphones or the smallest cushions when using Sony or Philips earbuds.

However, I will hold down the power button and the earbuds will say "powering on, connected" and then I will hit play on my phone and the music will come from the phone speaker. So I press down the power button on the headphones again and it says, yet again "powering on, connected." But I never received the information that they had disconnected. The earbuds simply turn themselves off and I can turn them on over and over and over but they always shut off within the first 3 seconds of being on. Was very happy up until this and would love a replacement pair if possible because they were not cheap headphone either.

I received a message from TreLab customer support about a day after I posted this above review. text:
I've been dealing with wired headphones for a while in a fairly active work environment so I'll try to filter out my joy at not having to deal with wires getting tangled with machinery. Also, being able to plug in my phone to charge and wander around a lab area and still have music/comedy/news playing in my ear is fantastic so if you're on the fence about getting bluetooth ear buds, do it.

That being said, should you get these? They're very easy to use, the signal strength is excellent, they'll get me through an entire work day on one charge, they charge in an hour, the mic is clear as a bell for calls, and the sound is very high quality. I like them a lot. Getting them to fit comfortably is a bit of a challenge (they do provide multiple ear inserts, you just have to try them until you find the ones that fit) but that will differ from person to person. I'm sure some of you might think they feel awful, and others will love them. All in all, a good buy. The only reasons they don't get 5 stars is because there are much higher quality buds from Bose and such places that blow these out of the water and I didn't pay anywhere near suggested retail price for them. At my pricepoint, they're good, at the retail point, there are many more options. That, and the volume button rattles, but I don't hear it in when they're in my ear.

title: The TREBLAB over the ear wireless earbuds are perfect for any type of person that enjoys running indoors ...
text:
TREBLAB XR100 Bluetooth Wireless Earbuds

Working out 4-5 times a week I needed to find a pair of wireless earbuds that work well for me. After going through numerous different cheap and expensive pairs, I finally have found the right pair for me. The TREBLAB over the ear wireless earbuds are perfect for any type of person that enjoys running indoors as well as lifting weights. With the around the ear ear-strap the earbuds stay in place throughout your entire workout, alleviating the stress that comes with always having to adjust your earbuds during any type of workout. Getting the perfect ear fit is easy with this earbud. It comes with three different ear bud sizes that are interchangeable. There is a small medium and large. Compared to the other ear buds that I have purchased this pair easily has the best sound. The music is loud and clear. The bass is incredible. I recently had Beats wireless earbuds and I prefer the bass on these $20 ear buds compared to the $150 Beats ear buds I used to have. These earbuds have great noise cancelation. It is great for when you are working out and want to block out all your distractions. The built-in-microphone allows you to have complete control over your phone calls. You can adjust the volume while on the phone or listening to music with the built-in-volume buttons that are located on the right ear piece. The Bluetooth capability is easy to set up right out of the box. Anyone who has ever used Bluetooth on their phone will be able to set these up with ease. Other wireless earbuds that I have had in the past lack Bluetooth connectivity. I had some pairs where my phone would be in my pocket and it would connect in and out. It was such a hassle. That hassle is eliminated with the TREBLAB XR100 earbuds. I can leave my phone on the ground during a workout walk around the gym and not have any issues with connectivity within about a 40 yard range. If you are on your treadmill, you can set your phone down on the treadmill and not have to worry about it connecting in and out. If you are looking for a great pair of wireless earbuds that are at an extremely reasonable price, I believe that this pair is one of the best on the market for sound, Bluetooth capability, fit, and comfort. If you are considering a different pair I would highly suggest you take your time to heavily consider this pair, I have owned pairs that are 5 times the price of these but that don't have near the sound or capability that this pair has.

title: Bluetooth Earbuds TREBLAB XR100 just OK
text:
I've had these headphones for about 3 weeks now. I bought these due to the many high reviews and relatively low price for noise cancelling Bluetooth headphones. Pairing to my IPhone was fairly simple. I'll start with the positives. The sound is not bad. I'm not an audiophile so these sound decent to me. Fit is ok after I changed out the earbud piece. I wear these on my hour and half train commute each day comfortably. Battery life seems to be as advertised.

I do not like the hook that goes around your ear. It is rubbery and very flimsy with no adjustability what so ever. You have to position the headphone just right so the hook rest on the back of your ear and doesn't flop around all over the place. As for noise cancelling, it’s non-existent unless sticking headphones in your ear is the noise cancellation.

Bluetooth connectivity strength is not the greatest on these headphones. I can be walking with my phone in my hand and will get intermittent connection between my phone and headphones. Don't even think about putting your phone in your pocket because the intermittent connection gets worse and cuts in and out. Sitting on the train with my phone in my lap is the only time these do not cut in and out.

I don't know if I got a bad pair of headphones but I can only give these headphones 3 stars and I’m thinking I’m being generous at that.

title: Never Write Reviews
text:
Never Write Reviews.

These headphones are nice! Depending on the music that you listen too your experience may be better than other. As for me I listen to a fair amount of rap with a heavy beat. I wouldn't consider myself an audiophile but I do have experience with Bose, Etomotic and Klipsch. This being my first pair of "in ear" Bluetooth headphones (own Outdoor Research Chips).

One of the biggest things I look for when I purchase new headphones is comfort. These are great in that aspect, they are lightweight and more or less "rest" in your ears while staying secure.

Are they noise isolating? Kinda, but not really, they do block out some ambient noise but not like my Etomotic HF5's or the Klipsch earbuds I owned years ago. The battery life on these is congruent with that in the description.

Some very minor problems I have with the headphones..
With Bluetooth your sound quality isn't(yet) up to par with a wired connection. Not these headphones fault, but they are bass heavy regardless. Some people enjoy their bass a lot but I prefer even tones. I did set the EQ on my iPhone to bass reducer and found that to make them in my opinion, better.

The charging/Bluetooth light doesn't have the ability to turn off when on. So it blinks every few seconds. Like I said minor problem.

Other than those two things I absolutely love these headphones. I go to the gym daily and these are now my go to. I don't have to deal with cords which makes life easier at the gym for sure. Controls are simple for pausing and changing songs, and I sweat(a lot) and they have yet to have any problems.

As for the company Productech, they certainly care about customer satisfaction, and reply readily with any questions you may have.

text:
Tired of my well-worn Plantronics Edge bubbling through calls, and the fully in-ear design that I thought I'd love pulling at the inside of my ear, I went shopping for something different. All the pro review sites have that brand listed at the top - best noise-canceling, best connectivity etc.

But most of the consumer reviews are less favorable - and many pan those same features. And they're all pretty expensive.

So I gave this far less known brand a try. It has great reviews on Amazon, has a boom, specs out nicely, and was half the price of the name brand models with fewer stars.

I'm glad I did.

It is not the most cutting-edge BT set here. It isn't super-chic, and is a bit chunkier than most of the newest high price models. But it checks all the boxes a phone headset should:

Incoming audio is good. 4 out of 5. There are 2 styles of ear tip, neither of which is noise isolating. Makes it comfortable in your ear canal, but allows some (or a lot) of ambient noise. Quality is good, but would be difficult to hear in noisier environments. And the volume only gets to "pretty loud".

Mic quality 4 of 5. Good noise canceling here - very similar to my Voyager Edge (which the pro reviews say was excellent...) Medium volume music in the background is heavily muffled, while speech into the mic is still clear. You may not be able to use this while driving with the windows down, but normal road noise should be suppressed well. On the other end, it sounds like a BT headset - no HD audio claims here, but I have yet to really experience that at any price point. Nobody complained.

Comfort 5 of 5. While a little chunky, it wears comfortably and stays in place very well. The ear tip is loose in your ear, but the hook keeps it in place. There are enough adjustments to make it fit well and still put the mic where you want it. For the daring, the ear hook actually hangs on the front of your shirt without feeling like it will fly off. If you're like me, you want the headset right there all the time, but not always IN your ear.

Functions 4.5 of 5 for having all the requirements covered. Volume and track control, separate Mute function, Assistant activation and the big MFB for answer/hang up/play/pause. Pressing that MFB does push the speaker firmly into your ear - and results in a solid Click sound when it triggers. A softer touch button would have been nice.

Battery 5 of 5. I've had it on Stand-by for days with frequent short calls (and PC audio) without any level warnings.

Connectivity t of 5. Seems to reach as far as BT v4 does. Volume drops as you get further away, but no issues with the phone nearby. And unlike some headsets, it doesn't drop out when the phone is in the wrong pocket. Nothing amazing here, but no letdown either.

title: Audio aficionados really need this item
text:
After some intermittent problems with my bluetooth adapter (see other review) I bound the unit to my computer and my Android phone. It exceeded my expectations. First, the audio is great and you can control the next/previous with the headset. The mic is excellent and works quite well in windy conditions. The bass and high notes are clear and crisp, volume goes to dead quiet to beyond anyone's comfort level. From a sound quality standpoint, I would ask for nothing more. After over 30 charges, the battery still lasts more than 8 hours. I have only had it run down once, this was on the third day after a charge. No indication, just would not stay bound to a device for more than 15 seconds or so.

Here are the issues I have with this unit.
The inner foam rubs off. It doesn't effect the quality of the device but it definitely looks like I have had it for years. I use it every day (listen at work) and the foam is very cheap. The next/previous function is by tapping the + or - on the headset. There should be a raise/recessed area so that this location can be easily found. If not, then you will have your volume go too high for comfort. (next function).

Last, While you can see if you are connected via bluetooth, (blue light flashing) there needs to be some indication of battery level while the unit is open. The battery seems to last as long as I need, but it would be good to know this with some positive feedback from the headset.

text:
First of all, let me say that Amazon rocks! I just ordered these yesterday afternoon and got them this morning. I've been reading reviews on all types of BT stereo headets, and I was liking the overall response on these. Out of the box, it paired immediately with my Galaxy Note. I also paired them with my Motorola Xoom. Here's my report:

1. Sound (Music)
These suckers has got some deep bass. Rich. I listen to primary house music and sound great! No crackling, distortion, hiss, etc. Nice and clean. I can also play music from my Xoom or my Galaxy, I just hit play on either device and it will stop the other one automatically. No disconnecting needed. Nice touch. Also track Forward/Back works fine from both of my devices.

2. Comfort. I can confirm that these things are total comfort. They do leak some sound, but they do sit on my ear fine. I was looking at Dr. Dre's beats wireless BT, but I couldn't justify spending 300.00. For 79.00, you are definitely getting your money's worth!

3. 3.5 inch cord. This was a bonus for me. I'm a DJ, so I can use these by plugging them into my mixer and go! NOTE: In this mode, BT is disabled, so you cannot take calls. Also, you do need to have your battery charged to use the cord or they won't produce sound. (I don't like this, but I am pretty good about charging my gadgets and if push comes to shove, I can plug my set into my laptop for a quick charge between my Dj sets.)

4. Calls. I can hear my callers loud and clear. They can hear me loud and clear. No complaints here.

5. Design/Durability. These are lightweight and sexy. The padded felt is definitely a lint magnet. I personally would not wear these to the gym if you are a heavy sweater. I could see moisture damaging the felt and possibly the earbuds. I use my Backbeat (Plantronics) for the gym. The Jabra blows the Backbeat away when it comes to sound, though. The hinges may pose a problem from wear and tear, so I would baby these, but for now they seem pretty secure.

So, if you are on the fence about these, I would say get them. I read reviews on the first version Jabra Halo and they were not good. Apparently, they made some major improvements to Halo 2. I didn't have the first ones, so I can't compare them to these. But I will say that I really like these and I have had at least 6 different pairs of BT stereo headsets...these could very well be my favorite pair of out of all of them. I hope this helps.
