title: Design Flaws Destroy its Value
text:
The Jabra HALO is a very nice looking set of headphones. The sound quality is fine (I'm not picky though), but there are a number of design flaws that really make it a no-buy for me.

1. The only way to turn the headphones on and off is by folding in their right side. The power mechanism is built into the hinge. For someone who does a lot of on-and-off listening, it's really annoying to not be able to just turn the headphones off.

2. The folding arms are weak. After about a month of regular use, small cracks started to form around the hinges where the headphones fold. Now, after about three months, shards of plastic are constantly splitting off, and the hinges no longer stay open on their own. I have to carefully put the headphones on, and then the pressure from resting against my head keeps them in place. A moving part like this should have been designed to withstand much more wear and tear.

3. The touch-sensitive area on the right earpiece that does volume and next/previous track is terrible. It is sluggish and slow to respond. You'll also find that you accidentally change the volume a lot of the time when you're trying to reach the play/pause button, or trying to change tracks. Using a touch sensor here is pure gimmick, I would definitely prefer physical buttons.

4. If you have glasses, you'll be miserable. The headphones, although sleek, are really uncomfortable to wear for more than a few minutes if you're wearing glasses.

If these headphones cost $10.00, I wouldn't mind just buying a new pair every couple of months, but at over $50.00 I can't recommend them.

I bought this in January to replace wired headsets for my iPhone, and it worked very well. I read all the reviews about flimsy hinges and the indicator lights not working as described, and yes - they are correct. The call quality on phone calls was excellent and worked flawlessly from audio to call. Volume control was a little iffy because you can't see your right ear to know exactly where you are going to touch it - you might accidentally do something you didn't intend. But generally I had little trouble with volume.

I loved this headset - really - and I was as gentle as I could be with it. But eventually the right hinge lost a piece of plastic, even though it continued to work. The headset also loosened a little, so that it became harder to keep it over my ears. Then, last week, it stopped sending a bluetooth signal (which you can see as the blue indicator light). I imagine the connector wire is probably damaged, and I'm looking for my warranty info now. I won't be surprised if they say I damaged it, since that piece of plastic broke off, so I'm not hopeful they'll repair or replace it.

I give it 3 stars - I loved it and want to give it 5 but hey, it costs too much, especially for only 8 months of service. That being said, don't buy it - it's too fragile.

They are almost the most comfortable pair I have ever wore around my ears while wearing hearing aids. They are as comfortable if not more than the QC35. title: Worked great with Mobile, but not so much with Laptop
text:
Firstly, I am just an average user of headphones and I am not super picky on the features/tech.

I purchased this for work as my prior headset (of 4 years) broke! I must say this product wasn't in my list of options (it wasn't intentionally left out); however when a friend alerted me to the ongoing deal I looked this one up and didn't think twice to get one! I am on calls almost all day and my current headband of the one that I using for 4 years, broke!

(a) Worked well with my iPhone. Apple's Spatial Audio Songs sounded awesome through these headphones.
(b) The wireless connectivity worked as expected.
(c) The Ambient and NC Feature was more than satisfactory. I did not use this to take any calls.
(d) Headband was sturdy and the ear cushions sat quite well over my ears.

What's NOT SO great about the Headphones I received?
I gave the headphones two full days at work.
a) Every 10mins or so the I lost the audio/microphone. I had to switch it off/on again to get back the audio/microphone.
b) Along with (a) I experienced a lot of interference and it was unbearable. Similar to (a) I had to switch it off and on again to get back to normal.
(c) Lastly, (I know I got this on a deal), but what's up with a Headset costing $178 not coming with a Case?!! My last one came with a case!

I had to contact the Customer Care - as things go - tried few Trouble Shooting tips and did a factory reset as well. Just disappointed that this didn't workout for me.

Thank You.

title: My daily drivers
text:
I've had these things since February, and have been using them on the daily! These are fantastic headphones for the price. Definitely an improvement if you're still using muddy-sounding or tinny headphones. The sound is clear, with good highs as well as bass. The sound in general is pretty flat, though, and not in the bad way. These ARE studio monitor headphones, so they're don't have any bass boost. I'm sure if you like your music extra bass-y you can toy with your EQ to get it sounding fine.
They're quite comfortable to wear, and have nice padded ear cups and a padded band. They're perfectly fine for wearing for extended periods, but do get a little warm around the ears. It could be the Floridian heat, but I notice my ears get a little sweaty after extended use.
The headphones are also pretty portable! They fold up quite nicely, and will fit in most medium sized bags. The baggy and three cords included are very nice as well! My favorite is the coiled, but the smaller straight cable is probably the best to use on-the-go. Still, I took the coiled cable with me on a couple of flights, and it felt fine. :-)
The only problem I've had with these is that they're not good for gaming, as they don't really have much of a sound stage. I really don't think that warrants me taking away a star, though, because I love these things way too much. Other than that, I'd recommend these! They're definitely worth the money, and a lot better than some of the other models you find out there.

title: Good Sound Quality, But Poor Build Quality
text:
After using this headset for only 15 months with very little usage, I noticed that the earpiece sponge started peeling, as shown in the attached image. Although the sound quality is good, I must say that the overall build of the headset could have been better.

In terms of sound, this headset delivers clear audio and provides an enjoyable listening experience. However, I was disappointed to find that the sponge on the earpiece started deteriorating so quickly. It's a shame because the headset itself feels comfortable and fits well on my ears.

The peeling sponge is not only aesthetically unappealing, but it also raises concerns about the long-term durability of the product. I expected the headset to withstand regular usage without experiencing such issues. It seems that the materials used for the sponge were not of the highest quality.

While the sound quality remains satisfactory, I would caution potential buyers about the durability of this headset. If you prioritize audio performance over build quality, then this might still be a suitable option for you. However, if you're looking for a headset that will last longer without any cosmetic flaws, I would suggest considering other alternatives.

I hope this review helps potential buyers make an informed decision.

title: Comfort and Quality Exceed Most
text:
The comfort of the headphones is great, even when wearing them over long periods. The batteries last a long time. However, the power indicator is not obvious and you have a difficult time discerning if they are left on, or turn themselves off over time. If utilizing the microphone as well, it is critical that the left muff goes on the left ear so the microphone points forward. There is no obvious difference between the left and the right muff and is easy to put them on backwards. When charging, these headphones turn themselves off. So when unplugging them in preparation for a video conference, you not only need to turn them on, but also wait for bluetoooth to connect to your laptop. Then you can switch your audio source on the computer to the headphones. Seems like a big hassle to reconnect and reconnect time after time. The range on these is great. I seem to be able to walk more than 100 feet and stay connected.

Needed improvements: 1) an easy/visual way to tell the difference between Left and Right on these. 2) larger more obvious power indicator. 3) option to charge while in use would be nice 4) reduce or eliminate the need to switch audio source when they power up, or connect to your computer.

text:
If you are looking for BASS HEAVY headphones on the cheap (let's say, for the gym, running, school), get these!

Decided to give these a try and I am super happy. I don't understand how they managed to kick so much bass out of these. My EQ is back to where I like it: bass is all the way up.

One caveat though: I noticed that I need to crank the volume all the way up (as opposed to the Sony, which managed about 60% volume). And at about 70% volume, increasing the volume will do nothing. Not sure if this is my phone's dac limitation or the Jib themselves.

title: These are exactly what I need for my 8 hour work days.
text:
I want to preface this review by stating every pair of Earbud I owned before. Was either an uncomfortable painful torture to my ears to wear. And/Or had MAYBE 3 hours of battery life, at half volume, (And an important note, as I work in Retail) Looked like the ugly apple airpods. Big, clunky, the little stem that hands out of your ear. Not easily obscurable unless you wear a beaning pulled low over your ears. Anyway. Thats what my experience was BEFORE these Earbuds.

THESE Earbuds... I have to have to have one ear clear always incase I am paged on the PA, or a customer needs assistance. I listen to podcasts all day to pass the time. One earbud, like mentioned above, at half volume. Lasted the ENTIRE 8 HOUR SHIFT!!! And still has battery left!! I never have EVER had that from any Bluetooth earpod I ever owned. I wasted more money on various wireless Earpods than what my gaming PC costs. Hell my Motorola Edge+ was cheaper than all the money combined on earpods. And not a single one of them could last a full day. I would previously have to resort to putting one earbud in, running that till it died, then finishing the remainder of the day with the other earbud. I bought a 5000mah battery bank because I was convinced no earbud was ever capable of lasting more than 3 hours per bud. I now own a battery bank, for emergencies I guess, and a pair of heavenly Earbuds. They fit. They never feel like they would get loose of fall off if I turn my head slightly toooo fast or sneeze.

The sound for an Earbud is on the pretty good side. (At least from listening to podcasts that is.) They lasted the whole day with a full charge. And they are not as obscenely obvious as a normal clunky earbud. And for someone like me that has torturous tinnitus. Certain sounds, or shapes of earbud will flare the tinnitus up. Not these. My tinnitus is put in check by just the sound of podcast. I will never buy a earbud from any other company.

title: Poor sound quality and battery life
text:
Comfortable to wear. Looks inconspicuous. Charges fast. Those are the only pros.

The sound quality is lackluster. It sounds low-quality. Of course, this product is cheap, and I didn't expect much, but it seems worse than I would have hoped. Not rich at all. Very "tinny". There is also way too much bass, which works well if your song is bass-heavy, but leaves other genres sounding pretty horrible.

The battery life on mine, at-least, is horrible. It does charge fast, but it loses that charge faster. Some reviews talk about the battery lasting for "days". I don't have that. Instead, the battery dies after a little over an hour of use. Since I intended to use these for upwards of 8 hours a day, they miss the mark.

Perhaps indicative of a faulty product, the little control module on the right-hand side gets pretty hot. In the summer heat, it gets even hotter. It hasn't caused me any issues, but I could see someone taking issue with that. What does it say about how long the product will last too?

When the battery gets low, perhaps like 10%, it repeatedly plays a voice clip that says "Battery low!" that constantly interrupts your last few minutes of listening. When the battery starts to die, the product plays a loud, obnoxious, hissing/static "alarm" sound, like something out of an emergency broadcast, that honestly scared me the first time I heard it.

Sound quality and battery life are the two biggest factors for a product like this, and it fails to deliver.

title: Perfect for small ears and exercising
text:
I purchased these headphones specifically after reading another reviewer who called out the fact that these buds are ideal for small ears. Those of us with tiny ears have a hard time finding earbuds that fit properly. Over-the-ear headphones are great but not that great for exercising, hence earbuds make a better option, theoretically. Unfortunately most earbuds just fall out of my tiny ears.

In an effort to get a better fit than the standard Apple iPod ear buds, I purchased a set of expensive SHURE earbuds. Unfortunately, the SHURE buds were just too tight in my ear canal, regardless of the type of bud cover I used (and SHURE provided several fit options). The SHURE bud cover materials were too stiff and simply not small enough, so I ended up going back to the old Apple earbuds as 30 minutes with the SHURE buds left my ears aching. This is most unfortunate because the SHURE earbuds had phenomenal sound quality.

I recently discovered this pair of Philips buds and the above-mentioned review after throwing in the towel while running stairs one afternoon --as my Apple buds kept falling out, every dozen steps. The Philips buds utilize an over-the-ear wrap that is extremely flexible and ultra lightweight, so it fits perfectly on each ear, regardless of your ear shape. What's more, the cables are super thin, so they don't drag down the buds. The less-than robust cables certainly call durability into question, but I'll have to see how they hold up over time before commenting further. Whatever the case, the wrap is fantastic. Additionally, the look of these buds is very slick, and their overall size and shape makes for a discreet package.

The next great feature is the bud itself, which comes with three different sizes of soft, super-pliable bud covers. I used the smallest size cover and they fit perfectly. What's more, the bud covers don't completely filter outside noise like the SHURE buds --which can be great in some instances (e.g., noisy buses and trains). The Philips buds offer a nice compromise in this regard, offering the ability to have excessive noise dampened, yet still enabling you to hear your surroundings enough to get by.

The next great benefit of these buds is the quality of sound. I am very impressed at the overall frequency response and reproduction of sound. From Jack Johnson to the Pet Shop Boys, the highs are accurate and the bass is encompassing (tested with my iPod's EQ turned off). I am very pleased with the sound quality, especially at this price range. It's not as perfect as the SHURE buds, but it's darned close.

I want to mention that I received the buds from Amazon new and instantly noticed that the left bud had greater bass response than the right. After testing to confirm that the buds weren't performing correctly, I used the simple exchange procedure online and a new pair showed up at my doorstep the very next day. The UPS driver even handed over a delivery label for my defective pair, which he delivered back to Amazon. The Amazon exchange procedure is fantastic and painless, with new product delivered overnight.

Yes, this technical issue with the first pair also calls their durability into question, but again, I am willing to wait until I've had them for a while before issuing further judgement --especially at this price point.

The fact remains that these buds fit my almost impossible to fit tiny ears while staying put through intense exercise and offering excellent sound. I'm willing to risk durability when all these other conditions have been met.

title: Build quality is a joke
text:
This review is for the Sony WHCH710N headphones.

I ordered the Philips PH805 headphones first, which were very comfortable, but I returned them because I didn't like the controls.

When I put these on, my first thought was that they must be counterfeit -- but the box had been sealed. The pleather is thin and itchy, similar to what you'd expect to be given out for free on an airplane. The cushioning makes a crinkling noise when you press against it, like cheap foam. I have small ears, but they don't fit inside the ear cups, so the tips of my ears get irritated as they scrape against the drivers. The only way I could tolerate wearing these for more than a few minutes was to fold my ears forward so that the drivers contact a less sensitive part of my skin.

Pros: good ANC, good audio quality, intuitive controls, USB-C port
Cons: uncomfortable, thin cushions, poor build quality, no case included

Sound quality was good, and noise cancelling was good. But so are other headphones in this price range, and those come with a case included! I guess you pay for the Sony brand name.

I could pay $15 to replace the ear cushions and another $15 for a case, but I think I'll order a different pair instead.

text:
I pulled the AirPod Max out of their oddly shaped cover and they automatically tried to connect to my phone, but I was immediately greeted with this message “The owner of this item will be able to see its location.
You are connecting to an item that's
paired to someone else's Apple ID.”
The headphones are in excellent shape and I don’t see a single blemish. The noise cancellation and spatial audio work amazingly well, but I’m definitely not going to connect them to my phone with them being traceable and no way of removing it without contacting whoever owned them previously. I feel like this should be one of the very first things they check for when receiving a return product for refurbishment. 1 star for now, will update review when I get a pair that doesn’t belong to someone else.

:::UPDATE:::
I left a message with customer service and was called back the next day. They told me how to factory reset the headphones [hold the Digital Crown and the spatial audio button down simultaneously for 15 seconds until the LED flashes amber then white] and it paired to my Apple ID and was no longer associated with someone else’s. Wow, that was easy. Great product and great customer service experience. Would have been nice to not have to deal with that scary experience, but it all worked out well!

title: and for that price these are a fantastic value. The Bluetooth sound is good enough for ...
text:
Got these on sale for $180, and for that price these are a fantastic value.

The Bluetooth sound is good enough for commuting, but as you'd expect they shine when the cable is plugged in and you are running them through an amp.

The bass is fantastic, smooth, accurate, low, but not bloated. It is, however, ever present so if you prefer a flat sound, these are not that. That said, unless you EQ with the bass sliders to 11 (which will sound great if you want your ears to rattle) I never found the bass to get 'in the way'. I was still able to make out a lot of nuance despite the growl.

Midrange is a bit recessed, but you generally won't notice unless you compare it to a headphone like the NAD VISO HP50, which has lovely (read: better) midrange for vocals.

Highs are bright, but not fatiguing (for me anyway). I think the emphasis on highs and lows of these cans is what leads to the recess of the midrange.

Isolation isn't amazing, but it's ok. The three chevron slits on the sides do let in a bit of sound, but generally don't let it out unless you listen at really high volumes. This is probably ok for general commuting awareness, but less great on planes.

I like the style, and love the customization options.

The package value is fantastic, because these are built like a tank, sound great (and fun), and come with a great carry case and the cable/adapter you need.

TIP: buy the XL pads. It makes all the difference in the world for comfort, and I think it improves the sound a bit as well. (a bit more spacious).

title: Super comfy and sound great!
text:
Old ear buds died, time to get new ones, these seemed highly rated and cheap so gave them a shot. They've got a lot going for them -- I really like the size and weight of the case (a lot smaller than my last ones) and the quick charge. They sound great -- I use them primarily for podcasts so it's important they aren't too muddy, and they definitely check that box -- really balanced tone. They are definitely comfy (I strongly prefer this type of ear bud over an apple style, I figure you kinda either like this type or don't).

The quick charge is of course balanced with not unbelievable battery life, but I can deal with that. There's a convenient graphic telling you how much life you have left, so I know ahead of time when I'll need to charge them. My one quibble is that when the charger case is dead but the headphones still have charge, they do not power off and disconnect when put back in the case. A couple times I'll get into my car and be connected to my car via bluetooth and then all of a sudden I'm back connected to ear buds because they didn't shut off when I put them in the case.

That said, that happens very rarely so if you're looking for affordable, comfy ear buds with good audio quality and a convenient charging case, these fit the bill!

text:
The 13mm drivers in these tiny buds are incredible! I've tested approximately 30 Bluetooth earbuds from high end to low end and these surprisingly provide similar sound quality compared to many of the higher end models like Jabra 75t/ 85t, Liberty Pro 3, Soundpeats H1. Also, the small form factor is amazing and the surprisingly fit well in my large ears. They of course come with a variety of ear tips and it’s crucial you find the right size so you have a snug fit. If you don’t have the proper fit even the highest end earbuds will sound awful. The touch controls also work like a charm.

With the proper ear tips these earbuds do offer good noise isolation. However, I wish they had ANC (Active Noise Cancellation). I’d pay at least $20 more to have ANC/ transparency mode on these. I’ve searched everywhere and can’t seem to find a similar size/ form earbuds with these features. Despite not having ANC I highly recommend them. If you're a bass head like me you'll be in love!

One thing I don’t necessarily care for it the glossy finish on the charge base. It seems like it would be very easy to scratch. This is a very minor thing so take that con with a grain of salt.

title: I found a new best headphone in the sub-$50 range
text: For a long time I considered the Skullcandy Ink'd Buds the best headphones around for under $50, but when my pair broke on me a few months back (after three years of abuse), I decided to step up to these because the difference was only $10. I wasn't sure if they would be worth the money (the versions Skullcandy sells that fall between these and the Ink'd Buds have majorly disappointed in the past), but they are more than worth it. These quite literally blow my $130 Shure phones right out of the water, and are a considerable improvement on the already excellent Ink'd Buds. With the Ink'd Buds you always need a good break-in period (usually 20+ hours) before the highs loosen up and the sound becomes really enjoyable. These sounded smooth and rich right out of the packaging, and have only improved in the month since I got them. The bass is strong and solid but never overpowering, the highs are rich and clear, and the soundstage has excellent depth. The buds are comfortable, even though I got the plastic rather than foam tips, and the construction is rock solid. A coating on the cord cuts down some of the incident noise that all buds have on contact, and the inline volume control is excellent. Sometimes I wish for a little more sensitivity at the low end of the volume control (these phones are sensitive, and therefore I usually keep them at a very low volume so I don't blow out my hearing), but they sound great throughout the range regardless. If you're currently in the market for a new pair of headphones (and don't want to spend over $100), these should definitely be on your shortlist.

title: 3 ports failed
text:
I bought this over a year ago. However, I hardly used it because I mainly used the original charger that came with my smartphone. I used the charging cables, but not a single one of them lasted. All 5 went bad after several weeks. That is to be expected.
What I did not expect is for the ports on the chargers to fail after a very light use. I only charge one item at a time, but when I tried to charge a tablet and a smartphone at the same time, I noticed that one port was not charging. I did more testing and figured out that port 1, 3, and 5 were not charging at all. There must be a connection between them, but I tried different cables and switching ports.
Very disappointed in this product since it was recommended online.

Update: Customer service is awesome!!! As soon as my original review was published, I received an email from Anker. They apologize for having a product that failed and offer me a replacement free of charge. Got it today...Thanks Anker.

title: Best headphones for video editing and relaxing!
text:
I am a video editor and need great sounding headphones for audio mixing. I need to be able to hear the lowest of the lows along with the highest of the highs and everything in between. To get right to it, I have absolutely nothing bad to say about these headphones. I used to own a pair of the m-100's and decided to try the wireless after reading many reviews about how great these headphones were. I also have cats at home that tend to chew on and destroy cords, so I decided to hunt down the best sounding wireless headphones.

One thing I am kind of sad about is that they don't retract like the m-100's do but it actually worked out better for me because the case stays strapped onto my backpack better with the bigger case. I have yet to experience any lag with the audio. The transition from going between wireless and wired is seamless, the is no break in the audio playback if you need to plug in and charge them. It was a little confusing trying to connect my the headphones to my iMac at work because I also have bluetooth desktop speakers, I realized that those had to be unpaired and completely disconnected before I could pair my v-moda's, then I could pair the other speakers. I switch between using headphones and speakers often to show the producer what I've been working on. After the initial pairing, they just connect when you turn them on, easy peasy. The battery life lasts quite a long time, a couple days of video editing for me. The sound quality is just perfect. They are super comfortable and durable. I'm not afraid to take these on a film set to record audio. I can hear every little detail when listening to music or when I'm mixing audio. I also use the FiiO portable amp with my phone when I want a little more rumble in the bass.

Ok actually there may be one thing that I noticed when I was charging them via USB through my computer, I also had them plugged into the same computer so I could keep editing but I got some static and that I couldn't work with, so as a work around, I plugged them into an outlet nearby so they could continue charging as I was editing and the static went away. So for that I would give these headphones a 9 out of 10 score but still a 5 out of 5 stars.

If you're looking for stylish, great sounding headphones for listening to music or mixing audio or both, I recommend the V-MODA Wireless 100%!
